these ingredients at a final complete type and constructs the uncolored
envelope required in the arithmetic lower bound.

The remaining subsections make the constants explicit. Their order
reflects the proof dependencies: the rank coupling and its wall action;
the exact middle tube; the Gaussian endpoint and wall bounds; the flat
preparation and relative coupling errors; and the separate ordinary
bridge construction. Large numerical constants serve only to give a
uniform fixed length threshold.

\subsection{Auxiliary probability estimates}\label{app:probability}

We begin with the association inequality used both to join adjacent
Gaussian segments and to compare environmental tilts. All conditioning
in its applications is specified separately; the inequality itself
concerns the unconditioned finite Gaussian law.

\begin{lemma}[Finite Gaussian association]\label{pr:association}
Let $Z$ be a centered nondegenerate Gaussian vector whose covariance
matrix $\Sigma$ has nonnegative entries. For bounded coordinatewise
nondecreasing Borel functions $f,g$,
\[
 \mathbb E[f(Z)g(Z)]\ge\mathbb Ef(Z)\,\mathbb Eg(Z).
\]
The assertion also holds whenever truncation makes both sides converge.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For smooth bounded functions with bounded derivatives, let $(X_t,Y_t)$
have diagonal covariance blocks $\Sigma$ and cross block $t\Sigma$,
$0\le t\le1$. This is a positive semidefinite covariance: one may take
$X_t=Z$ and $Y_t=tZ+\sqrt{1-t^2}Z'$ with $Z'$ an independent copy.
Gaussian integration by parts gives
\[
 \frac d{dt}\mathbb E[f(X_t)g(Y_t)]
 =\sum_{i,j}\Sigma_{ij}
       \mathbb E[\partial_i f(X_t)\partial_jg(Y_t)]\ge0.
\]
The two off-diagonal covariance blocks account for the absence of a
factor $1/2$. The covariance derivative identity follows by
differentiating $\exp(-\langle\xi,C(t)\xi\rangle/2)$ and integrating
twice by parts, first for smooth compactly supported test functions;
cutoff approximation and covariance regularization give the displayed
form. At $t=0$ the two vectors are independent; at $t=1$ they coincide.
Integration proves the claim for smooth functions.

Convolution with a positive smooth product kernel preserves
monotonicity. Bounded coordinatewise monotone functions have a
Lebesgue-null discontinuity set, so the convolutions converge almost
everywhere for the nonsingular Gaussian law. Dominated convergence
proves the Borel assertion. At distinct finite Ornstein--Uhlenbeck
times the covariance is positive definite; coincident times can simply
be deleted. Applying this finite result on nested dense time grids and
using path continuity proves its survival applications. The continuous survival applications therefore follow from the
unconditioned finite-grid inequalities. Any conditioned association
used elsewhere is established through the stated MTP$_2$ structure.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{Joint exact-total comparisons and small tubes}

Exposing two ends of an exact bridge leaves a common residual total
and a common residual type. A single likelihood ratio handles those
constraints jointly and compares the exposed variables with independent
reference coordinates. On central exposed totals it also gives the
lower comparison needed for the middle-tube construction.

Let $f_{r,\tau}$ denote the density of a sum of $r$ independent
exponentials of mean $\tau$. If $n$ marks have exact low count $k$,
$\pi=k/n$, and their $n+1$ gaps have total $P=(n+1)\tau$, exposing
$m$ specified marks and $m$ distinct specified gaps has joint density
\begin{equation}
 \frac{f_{n+1-m,\tau}(P-T)}{f_{n+1,\tau}(P)}
 \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(n-m,\pi)=k-K\}}
      {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(n,\pi)=k\}}
 \label{bridge:prefix-density}
\end{equation}
relative to independent reference gaps and marks. Here $T,K$ are the
exposed totals, and the ratio is zero outside its support. Independence
of the two unobserved sums proves the identity. The same formula
with $m$ replaced by $2m$ applies jointly to the first $m$ and last $m$
marks and to the distinct gap sets
\[
 E_1,\ldots,E_m;\qquad E_{n-m+2},\ldots,E_{n+1}.
\]
There are $n-2m$ residual marks and $n+1-2m$ residual gaps.

For $m\le n/4$, or for $m=\lfloor n/8\rfloor$ at each end, this
ratio is bounded above on its entire support, uniformly on compact
positive $\tau$ and interior $\pi$. On each fixed central box
\[
 |T-m\tau|+|K-m\pi|\le C\sqrt n
\]
it is bounded below positively for sufficiently large $n$; in the
two-end formula replace $m$ by $2m$. Indeed the Gamma maximum density
is $O((1+r)^{-1/2})$, its density at the reference mean is
$\asymp(1+r)^{-1/2}$, and the corresponding binomial bounds have
the same order. Central Stirling bounds give the lowers after the
remaining totals are inside their support. These denominators are
at their exact reference means. Near-central variants require the
large-total hypotheses of Lemma~\ref{pr:gamma}.

\begin{lemma}[Exact multicolor small tube]\label{bridge:small-tube}
Fix $r$, $\epsilon>0$, $0<\tau_-\le\tau_+<\infty$, and $a>0$.
Let a word of length $n$ be uniform of exact type
$v=(v_1,\ldots,v_r)$, $\pi_c=v_c/n\ge\epsilon$. Independently let
$n$ exponential gaps be conditioned to have total $n\tau$,
$\tau\in[\tau_-,\tau_+]$. For all sufficiently large $n$,
\[
 \mathbb P\left\{
 \max_{j\le n}|T_j-j\tau|\le a\sqrt n,
 \quad\max_{c,j}|N_c(j)-j\pi_c|\le a\sqrt n
 \right\}\ge c_a>0.
\]
The threshold depends on the fixed data and $a$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
We first obtain a maximal tail estimate by comparison on each half
with independent coordinates. We then retain central subblock totals
and use that estimate inside shorter bridges to obtain a small tube
of any prescribed fixed scaled radius.

For both exact bridges,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\{\max_j|T_j-j\tau|>u\}
 +\sum_c\mathbb P\{\max_j|N_c(j)-j\pi_c|>u\}
 \le C\exp\{-c\min(u^2/n,u)\}.\label{bridge:maximal}
\end{equation}
To see this, expose at most $3n/4$ coordinates. Their likelihood
relative to independent reference coordinates is the product of
\[
 \frac{f_{n-m,\tau}(n\tau-\sum_I E_j)}{f_{n,\tau}(n\tau)},
 \qquad
 \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Mult}(n-m,\pi)=v-N_I\}}
      {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Mult}(n,\pi)=v\}}.
\]
Gamma and multinomial maximum-density and central-density Stirling
bounds make both ratios bounded above. The bounded ratios compare the entire selected set with its independent
reference law; the selected coordinates remain dependent under the
exact bridge law. Independent centered gaps and centered color
indicators have moment generating functions bounded by
$\exp(C\theta^2)$ for $|\theta|\le\theta_0$. The exponential
supermartingale maximal inequality gives the right side of
\eqref{bridge:maximal} on the first half. Reverse the second half,
using exchangeability and the zero centered complete total. This
proves \eqref{bridge:maximal}; $n=1$ is immediate.

Choose a fixed integer $J\ge2$, and split the coordinates into $J$
blocks of lengths between $n/(2J)$ and $2n/J$. In the first $J-1$
blocks, let the first $r-1$ color counts vary in integer intervals of
width $\delta\sqrt n$ about their means. Determine the remaining
color count by the block length and the last block by the full type.
All deviations are $O_r(J\delta\sqrt n)$ and all counts are
nonnegative for sufficiently large $n$. The exact conditional atom is
\[
 \frac{\prod_{b=1}^J
       \mathbb P\{\operatorname{Mult}(n_b,\pi)=v_b\}}
      {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Mult}(n,\pi)=v\}}.
\]
Central Stirling gives a lower bound
$c_{J,\delta}n^{-(J-1)(r-1)/2}$ for each choice. There are at least
$c_{J,\delta}n^{(J-1)(r-1)/2}$ choices. Thus this event has positive
constant probability, including $r=1$.

Likewise prescribe the first $J-1$ block gap totals in real intervals
of width $\delta\sqrt n$ about $n_b\tau$, with the last determined by
the full total. Their density is
$\prod_b f_{n_b,\tau}(A_b)/f_{n,\tau}(n\tau)$, bounded below by
$c_{J,\delta}n^{-(J-1)/2}$ on a box of volume
$\asymp n^{(J-1)/2}$. Its probability is positive, and the gap and
color channels remain independent.

After $J$ is fixed, choose $\delta$ small enough that all cumulative
boundary deviations are at most $a\sqrt n/4$. Conditional on these
block totals, the blocks are independent exact bridges with compact
new parameters. By \eqref{bridge:maximal}, their combined failure
probability for tubes of radius $a\sqrt n/2$ about their own linear
interpolants is at most $CJ\exp(-ca^2J)$ for sufficiently large $n$.
Choose $J$ to make this at most $1/2$, and then choose $\delta$ and
the length threshold. Boundary and internal deviations sum to less
than $a\sqrt n$. All choices precede $n$.
\end{proof}

Apply the gap and color conclusions separately at $n+1$ and $n$,
respectively, to obtain the small tube for a bridge with $n$ marks
and all $n+1$ gaps. The prescribed tube radius determines its
large-length threshold.

\subsubsection{Positive drift under exact conditioning}

In the asymmetric endpoint regime, the effective prefix ends at a
height comparable to the inverse remaining drift. The following
continuation estimate converts that height into a constant success
probability on the entire remaining exact bridge, however long it is.

\begin{lemma}[Ordinary positive-drift continuation]
\label{bridge:continuation}
Fix compact positive ranges for two marks $w_0,w_1$ (which may be equal),
a speed $c$, and $\tau=P/(n+1)$, with $k/n$ in a fixed compact
subinterval of $(0,1)$. On $[0,P]$ take $n$ uniform points and,
independently, a uniform $k$-subset bearing mark $w_1$; the others bear
$w_0$. For $\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}$ put
\[
 Z(t)=x+\varepsilon\{w_0N_0(t)+w_1N_1(t)-ct\},\qquad
 v=\varepsilon\left(\frac{(n-k)w_0+kw_1}{P}-c\right).
\]
Suppose $0<v\le v_{\max}$. For every fixed $a>0$ there are
$R(a)<\infty$ and $b(a)>0$ such that
\[
 x\ge a/v,\quad Pv^2\ge R(a)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathbb P\{Z(t)\ge0\ (0\le t\le P)\}\ge b(a).
\]
This probability averages both the exact clock and exact type.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Section~\ref{supp:exact-type-continuation} proves the two-color
continuation directly. Its first half compares the exact clock and
exact type jointly with two independent Poisson processes. An
exponential supermartingale gives a positive first-half survival
probability; a central count window retains a fixed fraction of it.
The reversed half-density has a uniform upper bound, and its
maximal inequality bounds late failure by
$C_{\rm den}e^{-\kappa Pv^2/4}$. Choosing $R(a)$ as specified there
leaves a positive fraction of the first-half mass. This argument
uses the given exact type and both marks, including the case of equal
marks.
\end{proof}

The reference rank drift is
$\varepsilon(\mathbb EW-c\tau)=(y-x+\varepsilon c\tau)/n$.
The terminal unmarked gap accounts for its difference from the
physical drift $(y-x)/P$. It is retained in both the density and the
path calculations.


\subsection{Uniform scalar estimates at final complete types}
\label{supp:single-block-source}

We assemble the binary bridge estimate in the form used after the
arithmetic count adjustment. The complete type is fixed before the
spatial clock is read. We choose a legal common endpoint pair, obtain
its strong fractional survival moment, and then bound every admitted
type by one uncolored envelope. This separates the lower family at a
specified type from the upper envelope that must work uniformly over
all types and reveal assignments.

\subsubsection{Count types and endpoint pairs}

Condition on one original uncolored total \(n\). The physical block
has length \(P\), with \(n / P\) in a fixed positive compact interval. Its
fine word at any final feasible complete type is a uniform multiset
permutation, as proved in Section~\ref{supp:joint-count-source}. A fixed
binary bundle has exact size \(k\), so its mark word is a uniform
\(k\)-subset of the \(n\) original slots, independently of the uniform
uncolored clock. All \(n + 1\) gaps are retained.

Write its local risk as

\[
 R(t)=ct-aN(t)+bN_B(t),\quad a>b>0,
 \qquad \Delta=cP-an+bk,
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

with \(c , b , a - b , n / P\) in fixed positive compact intervals. Its final
binary fraction \(\pi = k / n\) is in a fixed interior interval; adjusting
exterior counts changes it by a fixed multiple of \(n^{- 1 / 2}\), not
by an order-one fraction. For the selected edge assume the actual
intrinsic endpoint minima, at every final admitted type, satisfy

\[
 a_*X\le x_{\rm act}\le b_*X,\quad
 a_*Y\le y_{\rm act}\le b_*Y,\quad
 y_{\rm act}-x_{\rm act}=\Delta,
 \qquad X,Y\ge h_*.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

Here the scores \(X , Y\) are fixed before the unread spatial clock.
The common local pair is

\[
 x^- =\max\{a_*X,a_*Y-\Delta\},\qquad y^-=x^-+\Delta.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

It obeys the same positive lower bounds and the upper bounds in
(2), and is below every actual endpoint minimum. Its chord is
therefore below every actual intrinsic chord with the same local
increment. Keeping the increment fixed is what makes this common pair legal;
its endpoints are chosen together.

Set

\[
 T=\frac{(1+X)(1+Y)}n,\quad p_0=\frac{a-cP/n}{b},\quad
 \rho_0=\frac{(cP/(n+1))^2}
              {(cP/(n+1))^2+b^2p_0(1-p_0)}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

On a fixed rare branch \(T < t_{0}\), (1)--(3) give exactly

\[
 |\pi-p_0|=|\Delta|/(bn)\le C(X+Y)/n\le CT.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

Take \(t_{0}\) small so \(p_{0}\) is uniformly interior. The resulting interior bound verifies feasibility at the actual
binary type as well as at the uncolored total.

\subsubsection{Gaussian estimates}

The Gaussian input consists of three comparisons: endpoint tails under
the survival tilt, constant-factor multiplicativity, and bounded-action
walls after Brownian time change. We collect them here so that the
relative discrete transfer below has a fixed reference lower constant.

We apply the estimates of Section~\ref{pr:section} with $\eta$ in
place of $\lambda$. For the private endpoint distribution $\mu$,
with mode $m$, Lemma~\ref{pr:filter} gives
\[
 |W-m|\preceq_{\rm st}|N(0,1)|,
 \qquad |\mathbb EW-m|\le\sqrt{2/\pi}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]
Its proof also gives the decreasing environmental majorant
\[
 m_t(E)\le M_t(E)=C\left[1+\sum_{l\ge0}e^{-l/2}
       \sup_{s\in I_l}(-\sqrt{\rho/(1-\rho)}E_s)_+\right],
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]
where each interval $I_l$ has length at most two, and
$\sup_t\mathbb E\exp(cM_t^2)<\infty$ for some $c>0$.
In particular,
\[
 \mathbb E_E\left[e^{aE_t^2}
       \bigl(\mathbb E_W[1_{\rm survive}e^{aW_t^2}\mid E]\bigr)^\eta\right]
       \le CF(t)
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]
for a sufficiently small fixed $a>0$, also simultaneously at both
endpoints. Theorem~\ref{pr:gaussian} supplies
\[
 F(s)F(t)\le F(s+t)\le CF(s)F(t),\qquad
 C^{-1}e^{-\chi t}\le F(t)\le e^{-\chi t}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]
Together with the bounded-action wall comparison, this yields
\[
 \mathbb E q_{\rm Brownian}^{\eta}\asymp
        \min\{1,((1+h)/\sqrt n)^{2\chi(\eta,\rho)}\}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]
when $|\delta|\sqrt n\le D$ and the two channel variances lie in
fixed positive compact intervals; see Corollary~\ref{pr:brownian}.
The endpoint boxes and strong curves in that corollary can be retained.
Proposition~\ref{pr:lipschitz} controls changes in the parameters.
Quantitative constants for these estimates are given in
Section~\ref{supp:explicit-ou-construction}.

\subsubsection{The relative discrete-to-Gaussian comparison}

For iid exponential gaps and iid binary marks, the reference
one-end risk is a sum of two independent centered channels plus
drift. Couple the channels separately on independent successive
dyadic blocks. Section~\ref{supp:explicit-rank-coupling} derives the
required numerical coupling from
\cite[Theorem~2.2(ii), equation~(2.4)]{CastelleLaurent1998}.
On a block of length $L$, its error is at most
$1000M^2(A+4)^2\log^3(L\vee e)$ and its failure probability is at
most $5L^{-A}$, for every fixed $A\ge1$. The environmental and
private channels use independent copies. Summing successive dyadic
errors gives a fourth-degree logarithmic majorant; its normalized
Cameron--Martin action and variation are bounded in
Section~\ref{threshold:coupling-action}.

The coupling error must be paid at the scale of survival. We obtain
that relative estimate from flat preparation and reserve comparisons,
before using the Gaussian exponent.
For either risk sign let \(F_{n} ( h )\) first mean its flat-wall
fractional one-end survival moment. Optional stopping at a fixed lower reserve
or upper height \(B\), followed by a scaled positive tube, prepares
height \(u\) in time \(O ( ( 1 + u )^{2} )\) with ordinary probability
\(\ge c / ( 1 + u )\). The walk and both channel sums can be kept central:
their stopped second moments are \(O ( B )\), so exclusion beyond \(RB\)
costs \(O ( 1 / ( R^{2} B ) )\), a small fraction of the \(B^{- 1}\) preparation.
Exponential overshoots and bounded opposite overshoots justify
optional stopping by truncation. Bounded scaled drift is paid by
an exponential-mean likelihood ratio on that central preparation.
Concatenate independent survival from \(h + u\). Time monotonicity,
\(\mathbb{E} p^{\eta} \ge \mathbb{E} p\), and the same tube prove

\[
 F_n(h)\ge c n^{-1/2},\quad
 F_n(h+u)\le C(1+u)^C F_n(h),\quad
 F_{2n}(h)\ge cF_n(h).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

For doubling, first remove environments whose unfavorable centered
gap sum exceeds \(R \sqrt{n}\). The unfavorable event has monotonicity
opposite to survival, so association pays its weighted loss by its
ordinary loss. On the retained environments, a favorable private
centered endpoint of size \(C \sqrt{n}\) has constant probability.
Its monotonicity agrees with survival, so their intersection retains
that fraction of the conditional mass.

The resulting reserve permits an independent future interval with
constant ordinary success probability. For its completed private mass,
\(0 \le U \le q\) and \(\mathbb{E} U \ge cq\) imply
\(\mathbb{E} U^{\eta} \ge c q^{\eta}\). Averaging the future in this
order proves the last part of (11).

The flat preparation also proves the reserve comparison for a negative
soft wall \(- g j^{\gamma}\). After preparation at time \(m\), the
future condition at \(- g j^{\gamma}\) is stronger than the shifted
global condition at \(- g ( m + j )^{\gamma}\). For a positive strong
wall we instead use flat-survival domination below. The flat and
negative-wall comparisons hold for Gaussian increments as well.

If a bad event \(D\) reads the first \(b \le n / 2\) slots and their coupling
auxiliaries, discard initial survival and bin the positive prefix
height in unit bins. It has Gaussian/exponential tails, and each
bin's probability is at most both \(\mathbb{P}( D )\) and its height-tail
probability. Apply (11) to the remaining reserve, use the geometric
mean of those two probability bounds, and sum the bins. This gives

\[
 E\mathbb P_{\rm private}(\text{survival},D\mid
       \text{extended environment})^\eta
       \le C(1+b)^2\mathbb P(D)^{\eta/4}F_n(h).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.12}
\]

If \(D\) begins after \(n / 4\), retain necessary survival on the first
\(n / 8\) slots, independent of \(D\), and use Jensen and finitely many
doublings in (11). Its relative cost is at most
\(C \mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta} F_{n} ( h )\). The argument applies on each marginal of the
coupling; the environmental coupling stays outside the private
conditional probability and the private coupling stays inside.
All independent reference increments belong to the original coupling
space; survival remains inside the conditional private integral.

By (12), all dyadic coupling failures after a fixed scale \(L_{0}\)
have total relative fractional cost at most

\[
 C F_n(h)\sum_{L\ge L_0,\ L\ {\rm dyadic}}L^{2-A\eta/4}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.13}
\]

Choose \(A\), then \(L_{0}\), so this coefficient is below the fixed
Gaussian lower constant from (10). The first finite block has
an exponentially decaying maximum-path tail. Choose its reserve
threshold last; (12) then also makes its bad relative cost small.
On the good coupling event, the accumulated discrepancy at rank time
$t\ge L_0$, including the within-block interpolation, is at most
$C(1+\log t)^4$.  Indeed the error on a block of length $L$ is
$O(\log^3(L\vee e))$, and there are $O(1+\log(t/L_0))$ completed
or partly read dyadic blocks before $t$.  In Lamperti time
$u=\log(t/L_0)$ a smooth majorant for the normalized discrepancy is
\[
 w(u)=\frac{C}{\sqrt{L_0}}
          (1+\log L_0+u)^4e^{-u/2}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{couplingwall:lemma}, with $m=4$, bounds its
Cameron--Martin action and the square of its variation uniformly in
the final horizon.  The explicit calculation in
Section~\ref{threshold:coupling-action} gives
$A(w)+V(w)^2<M^{-100}$ at the stated starting scale.
The first finite coupling block is treated separately and consumes
a fixed fraction, for example $h/8$, of the reserve.
Path inclusions and fractional subadditivity therefore first give
the discrete flat-wall upper and lower comparisons from (10), with
each failure absorbed against the corresponding flat marginal
moment in (13).
This proves flat discrete/Gaussian comparability before a
positive strong curve is imposed. Positive strong-wall survival is
a subset of flat survival, so its bad-event moment is bounded by
(12) for the flat experiment. The Gaussian strong-wall lower with
compatible central separate endpoint boxes is at least a fixed
positive multiple of the Gaussian flat moment by the bounded-action
comparison above. The already proved flat comparability now
absorbs that error. Choose the failure coefficient smaller than
this fixed multiple divided by the flat comparison constant. Thus
strong curves and their compatible boxes survive, without any
linear reserve comparison for a positive wall. A negative weak
wall, when needed for an upper path inclusion, uses its valid
negative-wall version of (12); its bounded-action Gaussian upper
and an error coefficient below \(1 / 2\) absorb its own error first.
These choices use the fixed Gaussian comparison and the already
proved flat relative bounds, so they precede the strong discrete
normalization.

\emph{Retaining regularity.} Before exact conditioning, interval tails
and the same relative early/late decomposition permit local REG to be
added at a fixed fraction of the survival moment. A failure
on a rank interval of length \(l\) and endpoint depths \(d_{1} , d_{2}\)
has probability at most
\(C \exp [ - c l - cK ( 1 + d_{1}^{\zeta} + d_{2}^{\zeta} ) ]\). For early intervals apply
(12); for late intervals retain independent early necessary
survival; intervals joining the two regions have length a fixed
fraction of the horizon and their length tail pays the reciprocal
of the crude polynomial lower (11). Summing the fixed-grid pairs
and using fractional subadditivity deletes at most
\(C \exp ( - cK ) F_{n} ( h )\) of the moment. Gap REG converts rank depths to
physical depths; the discrepancy in a strong \(\gamma\) curve is a
small multiple of rank depth to \(\gamma\) plus a fixed intercept,
because \(\zeta < \gamma\). Choose curve amplitude before the intercept
and final minimum reserve. Thus the discrete one-end
theorem holds with physical strong curve, binary REG, and
compatible central boxes of the separate channels.

\subsubsection{Joint conditioning on the total and type}

The uniform clock is \(n + 1\) independent exponential gaps conditioned
on their sum \(P = ( n + 1 ) \tau\); the marks are iid Bernoulli \(\pi = k / n\)
conditioned on their exact count. Exposing \(m\) marks and \(m\)
distinct gaps has joint reference density

\[
 \frac{f_{n+1-m,\tau}(P-T_m)}{f_{n+1,\tau}(P)}
 \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(n-m,\pi)=k-K_m\}}
      {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(n,\pi)=k\}}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.14}
\]

Its upper is constant on the whole support for \(m \le n / 4\); its
lower is constant on fixed central exposed totals, above a fixed
length threshold. This follows directly from Gamma/binomial
maximum atoms and central Stirling bounds. The two-end formula
uses \(2 m\) jointly, including the final unmarked gap at the reversed
end. Thus both exposed ends are compared in one density, retaining their
common residual total and type.

Suppose the legal reserves \(x , y\) are both of order at most
\(\sqrt{n}\), and expose \(m = \lfloor n / 8 \rfloor\) slots at each
end. Their reference drift is
\(\epsilon ( w_{+} - b \pi - c \tau ) = ( y - x + \epsilon c \tau ) / n\),
with bounded scaled magnitude. The density upper in (14) bounds
the moment by the product of independent reference one-end moments.

For the lower, retain the compatible positive central inner heights
and the separate central totals from the relative coupling. The
remaining exact clock and type have compact parameters. Their mean
path joins heights at least \(a \sqrt{n}\), with an \(O ( 1 )\)
pre-jump correction. A tube of radius \(a \sqrt{n} / 2\) therefore
gives constant ordinary success probability.

To obtain this tube, split each exact bridge into a fixed number
\(J\) of subblocks. Central Stirling bounds give constant probability
that their totals lie in intervals of width \(\delta \sqrt{n}\).
Conditional on these totals, exponential maximal tails control the
internal fluctuations. Choose \(J\) large enough to make the combined
failure at most \(1 / 2\), and then choose \(\delta\) small. The gap
and binary channels remain independent. Finally, interval Bernstein
bounds and the depth summation give ordinary middle REG failure at
most \(C \exp ( - cK )\), which can be paid against this fixed tube
probability.

For each fixed outer clock let \(q = q_{L} q_{R}\). The full private mass
\(U\), as a function of the remaining clock, obeys \(0 \le U \le Cq\) and
\(\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{middle}} U \ge cq\). Hence

\[
 E_{\rm middle}U^\eta\ge(Cq)^{\eta-1}E_{\rm middle}U
                                    \ge c'q^\eta.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.15}
\]

Use the central lower in the single joint outer density (14),
then average the independent reference ends. Thus the exact-type
strong-wall/REG fractional moment is comparable to

\[
 Q_n(x,y)=\min\{1,[(1+x)(1+y)/n]^{2\chi(\eta,\rho)}\},
 \quad \rho=(c\tau)^2/[(c\tau)^2+b^2\pi(1-\pi)].
 \tag{\papertagprefix.16}
\]

For the remaining endpoint regimes, two large reserves are treated
by a whole-bridge tube and unequal reserves by an effective prefix.
If both exceed \(\sqrt{n}\), a
whole-bridge small tube has constant ordinary probability. If one
is smaller and the other much larger, expose only an effective
prefix of length \(m\) comparable to \(n^{2} / ( 1 + y )^{2}\). Its bounded
scaled drift gives the one-end factor in (16). For the lower its
retained height is \(H\) comparable to \(\sqrt{m}\) and remaining drift
\(v\) comparable to \(y / n\), so \(Hv \ge a_{0} > 0\) and the remaining horizon
times \(v^{2}\) is as large as needed after fixing the asymmetry cutoff.
For the remaining exact bridge, compare its first half to two
independent color Poisson clocks. Their joint density is bounded
above everywhere and below on central half totals. The exponential
supermartingale \(\exp ( - \kappa v Z )\) gives ordinary survival from
\(a_{0} / v\) with positive constant probability on that first half.
On the reversed half, a centered maximal inequality bounds failure
by \(C \exp ( - cPv^{2} )\). Choose its fixed threshold to make this smaller
than half the retained first-half mass. A half-chord version stays
above \(( H + vt ) / 2\), which dominates the sub-square-root curve uniformly
in the remaining horizon. The same REG deletion applies. Integrate
this remaining clock by (15). When the effective \(m\) is bounded,
the physical drift is bounded below; one fixed minimum reserve
pays the curve and the same continuation gives the constant factor.

This proves Theorem~\ref{bridge:all-reserves} with the relative marked
fractional moment, the feasible remaining exact type, and all
\(n + 1\) gaps. The middle and tail clocks are integrated before the
fractional power. One fixed large reserve and regularity intercept
cover the bounded supported experiments. Deterministic marks use the
separate ordinary bridge argument.

\subsubsection{Contracted actual-type chord and the required persistence factor}

We now return to the endpoint scores fixed by the arithmetic type.
Contracting their legal chord spends only a constant fraction of the
reserve budget. The same-word identity below changes the speed by a
small amount on the rare branch, and parameter stability gives the
required canonical persistence factor.

Write the original exact bridge as \(\ell ( t ) + E ( t )\). For a fixed
\(\theta \ge \theta_{0} > 0\), its contracted chord has the same word identity

\[
 \theta\ell(t)+E(t)=\theta x+\varepsilon\{S(t)-c_\theta t\},
 \quad c_\theta=\theta c+(1-\theta)M/P.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.17}
\]

The speed remains in a fixed positive compact interval. On the
rare branch, \(| c_{\theta} - c | \le C ( X + Y ) / n \le CT\). Together with (5) and
the \(n / ( n + 1 )\) gap correction, local Lipschitz continuity gives

\[
 |\chi(\eta,\rho_{\rm contracted,type})-
              \chi(\eta,\rho_0)|\le CT.
\]

The contracted endpoint product is comparable to \(T\). Changing
the exponent therefore costs at most \(\exp [ C T | \log T | ]\), bounded
uniformly. Equation (16), with (3), proves that the contracted
curved binary path and binary REG have fractional moment at least

\[
 c\Psi,\qquad
 \Psi=T^{2\chi(\eta,\rho_0)}\ (T<t_0),
 \qquad \Psi=1\ (T\ge t_0).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.18}
\]

The constants are uniform over every final complete type in (2).
We can now impose fine-name regularity pointwise on each retained
binary word. At a fixed fine refinement type, the two parent lists
have uniform multiset refinements. An interval containing \(m\)
parent positions has hypergeometric named count with mean
\(( k_{c} / n_{\mathrm{parent}} ) m\) and tail
\(2 \exp [ - c u^{2} / ( m + u ) ]\).

Parent binary regularity bounds \(m\) and the difference between
this mean and the physical empirical rate. Choose the parent slope
below the prescribed named slope, then choose the named intercept
large. A named failure has bound
\(C \exp [ - c l - cK ( 1 + d_{1}^{\zeta} + d_{2}^{\zeta} ) ]\),
whose grid-pair sum is uniformly finite. Thus at every retained binary
word and complete fine type the refinement succeeds with probability
at least \(1 - \epsilon\). The named restriction retains
\(( 1 - \epsilon )^{\eta}\) of the binary fractional moment before the
rare path is averaged. Only the uniform multiset laws inside the
parent lists are needed.

Macroscopic recoloring banks can also be admitted. At a central
complete fine type and fixed interior interval of length comparable
to the block, its uncolored occupancy is binomial and its fine
counts are hypergeometric. Failure of the broad bank window has
ordinary probability at most \(C \exp [ - c n / \log^{2} ( 2 + n ) ]\), uniformly in
the type. If \(q_{\mathrm{bad}}\) is the already restricted conditional mass
lost to this failure, Jensen gives

\[
 E q_{\rm bad}^\eta\le(E q_{\rm bad})^\eta
            \le C e^{-c\eta n/\log^2(2+n)}.
\]

Since \(\Psi \ge c ( 2 + n )^{- 1}\) from \(\chi \le 1 / 2\) and the endpoint floor,
this is smaller than a fixed fraction of (18), above one fixed
length threshold. Fractional subadditivity
\(( q - q_{\mathrm{bad}} )^{\eta} \ge q^{\eta} - q_{\mathrm{bad}}^{\eta}\) proves the broad bank retention.

\subsubsection{The type-uniform uncolored envelope and its matching moment}

The lower family just constructed is type-dependent. For the reveal
argument we also need an upper envelope depending only on the
uncolored clock. At each reveal depth, two unread intervals give
necessary one-end tests. Their lengths adapt to the larger reserve,
and a summable depth weight combines their private masses into a
single envelope with the same fractional scale.

On the saturated branch $T\ge t_0$, set $q_d=D=1$ at every reveal
depth. Then $\Psi=1$ and the envelope upper bounds are immediate.
The source retains the separate fixed positive lower bound established
above. The construction below therefore concerns $T<t_0$, as in
Appendix~\ref{appendix:counts}.

Binary REG implies the endpoint occupancy bound
\(N ( [ 0 , t ] ) + N ( [ P - t , P ] ) \le C_{\mathrm{occ}} ( 1 + t )\). At a prescribed reveal depth
\(d\), leave strips of width \(C_{s} ( 1 + d )\) and use two disjoint original
free intervals of length

\[
 L_d=\epsilon_0\min\{P,(n/M_d)^2\},\quad
 U_d=1+X+d,\quad V_d=1+Y+d,\quad M_d=\max(U_d,V_d).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.19}
\]

On active depths \(d \le [ C_{\mathrm{cut}} \log ( 2 + n ) ]^{1 / \gamma}\), a fixed large
length threshold and small \(\epsilon_{0}\) ensure their combined
occupancy is at most half of the unread slots. Fix the complete
type and every actually revealed label. If their counts are \(m , e\),
the remaining binary word is an exact \(( k - e )\)-subset of \(n - m\)
slots. Its fraction differs from \(p_{0}\) by at most
\(C ( X + Y + 1 + d ) / n\). The joint exact subset density on both free
intervals, relative to iid Bernoulli of that remaining fraction,
is bounded by a constant: its numerator is a maximum binomial
atom on at least half the slots and its denominator is a central
atom on all unread slots.

Use Bernoulli probabilities
\(p_{+} = p_{0} + C_{1} ( X + Y + 1 + d ) / n\) for the increasing left necessary test,
and \(p_{-} = p_{0} - C_{1} ( X + Y + 1 + d ) / n\) for the decreasing reversed right
test. Coupling uniforms coordinatewise gives the necessary path
upper \(Cq_{d} ( G ) = Cq_{L} ( G ) q_{R} ( G )\) at every supported type and reveal
assignment. These coordinatewise couplings bound necessary tests under the
original exact type; their reference Bernoulli laws define the upper
experiment only.

The uniform exact-total clock on both fixed intervals has joint
density relative to a rate \(n / P\) Poisson clock

\[
 \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Pois}(n(1-2L_d/P))=n-N_J\}}
      {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Pois}(n)=n\}}\le C.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.20}
\]

Only after this one density comparison are the reference intervals
independent. Their physical drifts times \(\sqrt{L_{d}}\) are bounded.
The physical one-end upper (proved by a rank prefix and the same
Gamma conditioning/relative comparison above) gives

\[
 E q_d^\eta\le C
 \min\{1,(U_d/\sqrt{1+L_d})^{2\chi_+}\}
 \min\{1,(V_d/\sqrt{1+L_d})^{2\chi_-}\}
                   \le C(1+d)^C\Psi.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.21}
\]

To compare the right side with the canonical factor, separate the
two length regimes. If \(M_{d} \le \sqrt{n}\), then \(L_{d}\) is
comparable to \(n\). Otherwise the larger-reserve factor is saturated,
and the smaller reserve ratio is comparable to \(U_{d} V_{d} / n\).
The exponent changes by \(O ( T + ( 1 + d ) / n )\). Every nontrivial
reserve ratio is at least a fixed multiple of \(\min ( 1 , T )\), so
the logarithmic exponent-change costs are uniformly bounded.
The remaining depth loss follows from
\(U_{d} V_{d} \le ( 1 + d )^{2} ( 1 + X ) ( 1 + Y )\).

If a free interval lies below the scalar threshold, take \(q_{d} = 1\).
Then a reserve is of order \(n\), and \(\Psi\) is bounded below.
Beyond the active depth cutoff, take \(q_{d} = 1\) as well; the
coefficient tail in the envelope pays for these depths.

Choose fixed \(B_{0}\), \(b_{0} > 0\), and \(D_{0}\) with
\(D_{0} \eta_{-} > 2 \sup \chi + 1\). Set

\[
 D(G)=\min\left\{1,(2+n)^{-D_0}+
       \sum_{d\ge0}(1+d)^{B_0}e^{-b_0d^\gamma}q_d(G)\right\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.22}
\]

Choose \(C_{\mathrm{cut}}\) large after \(D_{0}\) so the coefficient tail raised
to any allowed plateau power is \(O ( ( 2 + n )^{- D_{0} \eta} )\). Fractional
subadditivity and (21) then prove

\[
 (2+n)^{-D_0}\le D\le1,\qquad E D^\eta\le C\Psi.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.23}
\]

At depth zero the necessary original path bound gives \(q \le CD\) for
every complete type. Additional curved walls, named regularity and broad
banks only reduce \(q\). The uncolored envelope is fixed before any
target and before any complete type is read. If several blocks
share a history-depth charge, their finite number permits choosing
\(b_{0}\) below its allocated positive coefficient; the floor
exponent is unchanged.

\subsubsection{Result at actual complete count types}

The strong lower family and its named refinement give the lower
moment, while the necessary tests give the pointwise envelope and
its upper moment. Combining (18), the relative broad-bank retention,
and (23) yields

\[
 \boxed{\ q\le CD,\quad E q^\eta\ge c\Psi,\quad
                E D^\eta\le C\Psi,\quad
                (2+n)^{-D_0}\le D\le1\ }.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.24}
\]

The expectations are in the original uncolored clock at its fixed
actual total. The private probability is in the original uniform
mark/permutation law at the fixed final complete type. Each plateau uses its own power in its compact interval. All selected
spatial tests are imposed after the count adjustment, under the final
complete type; the lower family is constructed at that type rather
than transported from a previously accepted path.

Ordinary deterministic marks have their separate exact bridge
factor \(\min ( 1 , ( 1 + X ) ( 1 + Y ) / ( 1 + n ) )\). The same two-end preparation,
middle tube, asymmetric continuation and REG deletion establish
that factor. Its deterministic private marks are treated by the ordinary bridge
construction, with its own ballot factor.

\subsubsection{The full relative bad-event estimate}

We give the full calculation behind the relative deletion used above.
A bad prefix can improve later survival through a favorable ending
height, so we bin that height and pay it by the reserve comparison.
A late bad block instead factors from a necessary early survival
prefix. Both arguments include coupling auxiliaries in their
sigma-fields.

Take \(b \le n / 2\). Given the extended prefix environment, let \(p_{r}\) be
the private probability of \(D\) and positive prefix increment in
\([ r , r + 1 )\), using \(r = 0\) for all nonpositive increments as well.
Dropping prefix survival and using independence of the remaining
original channels gives

\[
 E q_{\rm survive,D}^{\eta}
   \le\sum_{r\ge0}E p_r^\eta\,F_{n-b}(h+r+1).
\]

Here \(F\) is the flat-wall experiment. Its preparation proof gives
the linear reserve comparison
\(F_{m} ( h + u ) \le C ( 1 + u ) F_{m} ( h )\). In detail, stop a zero-mean walk on leaving
the interval between a fixed positive lower reserve and a height
of order \(1 + u\). Optional stopping, bounded mean overshoot and a
fixed central tube give a preparation event of ordinary probability
at least \(c / ( 1 + u )\) which ends above \(h + u\) by time \(C ( 1 + u )^{2}\).
For \(u \le C_{0} \sqrt{m}\) the bounded scaled drift is paid by its
exponential likelihood on the central preparation totals. For
\(u > C_{0} \sqrt{m}\), the crude lower \(F_{m} ( h ) \ge c m^{- 1 / 2}\) and
\(F_{m} ( h + u ) \le 1\) prove the reserve comparison directly, with no
long preparation at nonzero drift. Attach an independent future of
length \(m\). The preparation may lengthen the full survival event,
which only strengthens its implication of survival for the first
\(m\) steps. Given its successful clock/mark preparation, use the
future conditional private mass from reserve \(h + u\). Averaging the
preparation before raising to \(\eta\) retains at least its ordinary
success probability, since \(p^{\eta} \ge p\). Independence then gives
\(F_{m} ( h ) \ge c ( 1 + u )^{- 1} F_{m} ( h + u )\).

This argument is also valid for a negative soft power wall
\(- g j^{\gamma}\): the flat preparation is stronger, and the attached
future wall \(- g j^{\gamma}\) is above the global wall
\(- g ( m + j )^{\gamma}\). It is not the proof for a positive wall
\(+ g j^{\gamma}\), whose shifted global wall is higher. For positive
strong walls only the flat bad-event majorant is used.
For a negative soft wall, dropping its first \(b\) steps changes the
remaining wall by at most \(g b^{\gamma}\), because
\(( b + j )^{\gamma} \le b^{\gamma} + j^{\gamma}\). Include that amount in the remaining
reserve; the factor is at most \(C ( 1 + r + b^{\gamma} )\) and is absorbed in
the quadratic \(b\) loss below. Doubling and time
monotonicity give \(F_{n - b} ( h ) \le CF_{n} ( h )\) since
\(n \le 2 ( n - b )\). Jensen then implies

\[
 E p_r^\eta\le\mathbb P(D,\text{bin }r)^\eta
       \le\mathbb P(D)^{\eta/2}
                      \mathbb P(H_b^+\ge r)^{\eta/2}
 \quad(r\ge1).
\]

Bounded scaled drift implies \(| \mathbb{E} H_{b} | \le C_{D} \sqrt{b}\); exponential
moments of the centered gap or Gaussian channel give
\(\mathbb{P}( H_{b}^{+} \ge r ) \le C_{D} \exp [ - c \min ( r^{2} / ( 1 + b ) , r ) ]\). The fixed drift
displacement is absorbed in the constant for \(r \le 2 C_{D} \sqrt{b}\)
and in a smaller tail exponent otherwise. For \(r = 0\), use
\(\mathbb{E} p_{0}^{\eta} \le \mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta}\). Summing the Gaussian part on
\(r \le 1 + b\) and the exponential part afterwards gives

\[
 \sum_{r\ge0}(2+r)E p_r^\eta
       \le C(1+b)\mathbb P(D)^{\eta/2}
       \le C(1+b)^2\mathbb P(D)^{\eta/4}.
\]

This proves (12) for the flat experiment and its negative-wall
variant. In the bounded-positive-jump orientation use
\(H_{b} \le lb\) directly to get the stronger
\(C ( 1 + b ) \mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta} F_{n} ( h )\). The tails used here are unconditional intersection and height tails
on a marginal of the product coupling. Coupling auxiliaries only enlarge the
prefix \(\sigma\) field; the unconditional intersection and tail bounds
above remain valid on either marginal of the coupling.

For a late \(D\), retain necessary survival on the first \(\lfloor n / 16 \rfloor\)
steps. Every coupling block read by \(D\), including all auxiliaries,
is disjoint from every whole coupling block used by that prefix;
these complete sigma-fields are independent on the product coupling
space. The bounded range in which the initial block prevents this
separation is treated by Jensen and the crude survival lower bound.
Conditional private masses factor for this relaxed
event. Thus

\[
 E q_{\rm survive,D}^{\eta}
   \le F_{\lfloor n/16\rfloor}(h)
           E\mathbb P_{\rm private}(D\mid E_{\rm future})^\eta
   \le CF_n(h)\mathbb P(D)^\eta,
\]

by Jensen and a fixed number of doublings. A negative soft wall has
the same necessary initial survival on its original prefix and the
same doubling argument. This supplies the two relative failure
cases needed for every dyadic block in (13). Positive strong-wall
failure deletion is performed only after flat comparability has
been established by the relative coupling argument above.

\subsubsection{Uniform exact-type asymmetric continuation}
\label{supp:exact-type-continuation}

The continuation is needed separately for every retained complete
prefix. We compare the first half with independent color Poisson
clocks, retain a central count window within its survival mass, and
use a reversed maximal estimate to pay for late failure.

For two exact color counts \(n_{i}\) on duration \(P\), write
\(\lambda_{i} = n_{i} / P\), let all marks be at most \(w_{+}\), and let
\(\tau = P / ( n + 1 ) \ge \tau_{-}\). The exact type/clock law is equivalent to
independent uniform positions for the two colors. Relative to their
independent Poisson clocks, the density on the first half is

\[
 \prod_{i=0}^1
  \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Pois}(n_i/2)=n_i-N_i(P/2)\}}
       {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Pois}(n_i)=n_i\}}.
\]

It is bounded above by \(C_{\mathrm{den}}\) everywhere and below by
\(c_{\mathrm{den}} ( K ) > 0\) on \(| N_{i} ( P / 2 ) - n_{i} / 2 | \le K \sqrt{n_{i}}\) once
\(n_{i} \ge N_{0} ( K )\). The same statements hold on the reversed half.
Set

\[
 C_{\exp}=w_+^2e^{w_+}/(2\tau_-),\quad
 \kappa=\min\{v_{\max}^{-1},(2C_{\exp})^{-1}\}.
\]

For positive signed drift \(v\) and either orientation, Taylor's
bound gives exponential compensator at parameter \(\theta \le 1\)
at most \(- v \theta + C_{\mathrm{exp}} \theta^{2}\). At \(\theta = \kappa v\),
\(\exp ( - \theta Z )\) is a nonnegative supermartingale. Starting from
\(x \ge a / v\), the Poisson first-half exit probability is at most
\(\exp ( - \kappa a )\), so survival has probability at least
\(p_{a} = 1 - \exp ( - \kappa a ) > 0\). Choose
\(K \ge \max ( 1 , \sqrt{2 / p_{a}} )\). Chebyshev on the two Poisson counts
has total failure at most \(K^{- 2} \le p_{a} / 2\). Consequently exact
first-half survival has probability at least

\[
 b_{\rm left}(a)=c_{\rm den}(K)p_a/2>0.
\]

At a time \(P - u\) on the late half the exact identity is
\(Z ( P - u ) = x + v ( P - u ) - \epsilon M_{\mathrm{rev}} ( u )\), where \(M_{\mathrm{rev}}\) is the centered
reversed color-weight sum. Failure forces
\(\sup_{u \le P / 2} \epsilon M_{\mathrm{rev}} ( u ) \ge vP / 2\). The Poisson exponential
maximal inequality, and then the exact half-density upper, give

\[
 P_{\rm exact}(\text{late-half failure})
                \le C_{\rm den}e^{-\kappa Pv^2/4}.
\]

Choose $R(a)$ so that
\begin{align*}
 R(a)&\ge(4/\kappa)\log\{2C_{\mathrm{den}}/b_{\mathrm{left}}(a)\},\\
 R(a)/v_{\mathrm{max}}^2&\ge\tau_+[N_0(K)/\epsilon+1],
\end{align*}
where both color fractions are at least $\epsilon$. Then $Pv^2\ge R(a)$ ensures
the central half-density thresholds and a late failure at most
\(b_{\mathrm{left}} ( a ) / 2\). The full exact bridge survives with probability
at least \(b_{\mathrm{left}} ( a ) / 2\), uniformly in its individual exact type.

In the asymmetric binary bridge's retained effective prefix,
\(m\) is comparable to \(\delta^{- 2}\), its height \(H\) is comparable
to \(\sqrt{m}\), and its remaining physical drift \(v '\) is comparable
to \(\delta\). Increasing the fixed asymmetry cutoff makes
\(H v ' \ge a_{0}\) and \(P ' ( v ' )^{2} \ge 4 R ( a_{0} / 4 )\) for every retained prefix.
Use the same actual remaining marks with speed
\(c_{\mathrm{half}} = ( c + M ' / P ' ) / 2\), entrance \(H / 2\), and drift \(v ' / 2\).
The preceding continuation then has constant probability and
implies the original path stays above \(( H + v ' s ) / 2\).
Because \(H\) and \(v '\) are comparable to \(\sqrt{m}\) and
\(1 / \sqrt{m}\), respectively,

\[
 (H+v's)/2\ge c\sqrt m(1+s/m),\qquad
 d_P(T_{\rm pre}+s)^\gamma\le C m^\gamma(1+s/m)^\gamma.
\]

One fixed effective-time threshold pays any prescribed global
sub-square-root curve for all remaining horizons. Empirical
remaining color rates differ from the full ones by
\(O ( \sqrt{m} / n ) \le O ( n^{- 1 / 2} )\); choose ordinary regularity intercept after
the above continuation lower constant. The central prefix density
(14) has a uniform lower for all retained complete prefix totals.
Thus, at each fixed outer clock, the full mass satisfies
\(0 \le U \le Cq_{\mathrm{pre}}\) and \(\mathbb{E}_{\mathrm{remaining}} U \ge c q_{\mathrm{pre}}\). Equation (15)
retains its fractional moment. The central density and continuation estimates apply to each retained
prefix, with the remaining total and type determined by that prefix.


\subsection{Coupling of the rank channels}
\label{supp:explicit-rank-coupling}
We now derive the two scalar rank couplings and their constants.
The exponential channel is obtained by integrating an empirical
process coupling; truncation near the singular endpoint produces
the additional logarithmic factor. Independent copies then give a
product coupling for the environmental and private channels.

The primary source is Castelle and Laurent-Bonvalot,
\emph{Strong approximations of bivariate uniform empirical processes},
Ann. IHP 34 (1998), 425--480, Theorem 2.2(ii), equation (2.4), printed
page 429, together with the construction in Section~3.2, pp.~438--439
\cite{CastelleLaurent1998}. The latter writes $K(m,u)=\sum_{i\le m}B_i(u)$
and proves the bound with this index. We follow that construction,
correcting the printed $K(n,u)$ in (2.4) to $K(m,u)$.
The theorem is available at
\href{https://www.numdam.org/item/AIHPB_1998__34_4_425_0/}{Numdam}.

In their convention \(\ell_{n} = \log ( n \vee e )\). For iid uniform \(U_{i}\) and
their centered counting process
\(R_{m} ( u ) = \sum_{i \le m} ( \mathbf{1}_{U_{i} \le u} - u )\), a Kiefer process can be coupled so
that

\[
 \mathbb P\left(\max_{1\le m\le n}\sup_{0\le u\le1}
 |R_m(u)-K(m,u)|>(x+60\ell_n)\ell_n\right)
       \le0.67e^{-x/30}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

The Kiefer covariance is
\(\min ( s , t ) [ \min ( u , v ) - uv ]\). This empirical-process estimate is the sole coupling input. The
Bernoulli specialization, exponential integral, interpolation error,
and dyadic accumulation are calculated below.

\subsubsection{Uniform Bernoulli marks}

Fix any \(p \in [ 0 , 1 ]\). Let \(B_{i} = \mathbf{1}_{U_{i} \le p}\) and
\(W_{p} ( m ) = K ( m , p )\). The increments of \(W_{p}\) are independent centered
Gaussians of variance \(p ( 1 - p )\). At \(x = 30 ( A + 2 ) \ell_{n}\), (1) gives

\[
 \max_{m\le n}\left|\sum_{i\le m}(B_i-p)-W_p(m)\right|
        \le30(A+4)\ell_n^2
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

with failure probability at most \(0.67 n^{- A - 2}\), for every
\(A \ge 1\), \(n \ge 2\). This holds uniformly in \(p\); positivity of the
variance is only needed later for a scalar persistence theorem.

\subsubsection{Centered exponential gaps}

Use an independent copy of (1), and set \(E_{i} = - \log ( 1 - U_{i} )\). These
are iid mean-one exponentials. Define the Gaussian process

\[
 W_E(m)=-\int_0^1\frac{K(m,u)}{1-u}\,du
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

as a mean-square integral. It is Brownian motion at integer times:
its Gaussian increments are independent, and its variance per
increment is

\[
 \int_0^1\int_0^1
       \frac{\min(u,v)-uv}{(1-u)(1-v)}\,du\,dv=1.
\]

The empirical identity is

\[
 \sum_{i\le m}(E_i-1)
       =-\int_0^1\frac{R_m(u)}{1-u}\,du.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

Choose \(\epsilon = \exp [ - ( A + 2 ) \ell_{n} ]\). On the event
\(\max_{i \le n} U_{i} \le 1 - \epsilon\), the omitted empirical integral over
\(( 1 - \epsilon , 1 )\) has absolute value exactly \(m \epsilon \le n \epsilon\).
The exceptional probability is at most
\(n \epsilon \le n^{- A - 1}\).

The omitted Gaussian integral is a Brownian motion in the first
time coordinate of variance per unit time

\[
 v_\epsilon=\int_0^\epsilon\int_0^\epsilon
          \frac{\min(a,b)-ab}{ab}\,da\,db
                     =2\epsilon-\epsilon^2\le2\epsilon.
\]

By reflection, for \(h > 0\),

\[
 \mathbb P\left(\max_{m\le n}|W_{E,\rm tail}(m)|>h\right)
        \le4\exp[-h^2/(4n\epsilon)].
\]

At \(h = 4 ( A + 2 ) \ell_{n}\) this is at most \(n^{- A - 2}\). Indeed
\(n \epsilon \le n^{- A - 1}\) and
\(4 ( A + 2 )^{2} \ell_{n}^{2} n^{A + 1} \ge ( A + 2 ) \log n + \log 4\) for \(n \ge 2\), \(A \ge 1\).
On the good event in (1), the retained integral error is at most

\[
 30(A+4)\ell_n^2\log(1/\epsilon)
             =30(A+4)(A+2)\ell_n^3.
\]

Adding the two tails gives the fully numerical estimate

\[
 \mathbb P\left(\max_{m\le n}
 \left|\sum_{i\le m}(E_i-1)-W_E(m)\right|
          >100(A+4)^2\ell_n^3\right)\le3n^{-A}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

The last constants include all preceding three
failure terms. A mean-\(\tau\) exponential channel is obtained simply
by multiplying (3)--(5) by \(\tau\).

\subsubsection{The marked risk and independent dyadic blocks}

Let \(M \ge 1\), let \(c , \tau , b\) be positive and bounded above by \(M\), and take the
centered rank risk

\[
 S_m=c\tau\sum_{i\le m}(E_i-1)
                       +b\sum_{i\le m}(B_i-p).
\]

Couple the exponential and Bernoulli channels by independent copies
of (1). The resulting two Brownian motions are independent, with
the exact environmental/private variances
\(( c \tau )^{2}\) and \(b^{2} p ( 1 - p )\). From (2), (5),

\[
 \mathbb P\left(\max_{m\le n}|S_m-W(m)|
             >200M^2(A+4)^2\ell_n^3\right)\le4n^{-A}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

The environmental coupling is outside the private conditional
probability, and the private coupling is inside. Survival is evaluated under the original channel laws on this product
space. Independent copies of the entire construction on successive
deterministic dyadic blocks supply the block independence used in the
relative bad-event proof.

For continuous Gaussian interpolation, reflection on each unit
interval and a union bound add at most
\(20 M^{2} ( A + 4 ) \ell_{n}\) to (6), with probability at most \(n^{- A}\).
Thus the enlarged constant \(1000 M^{2} ( A + 4 )^{2} \ell_{n}^{3}\) has total
failure at most \(5 n^{- A}\). 

On dyadic blocks of lengths \(2^{j} L_{0}\), up to physical rank \(s\),
the accumulated endpoint errors have deterministic good-event
bound

\[
 1000M^2(A+4)^2\sum_{j\le\log_2(s/L_0)+1}
                [\log(2^jL_0\vee e)]^3.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

This is a fixed polynomial of degree four in \(\log ( 2 + s )\) with
explicit coefficients depending on \(M , A , L_{0}\). After Lamperti
normalization it has bounded Cameron--Martin action. This accumulated wall therefore fits the scalar bridge comparison
after the explicit wall-action and minimum-reserve inequalities are
adjusted. The power-wall exponent and the parameter regimes remain
the same.

For \(n = 1\), a direct quantile coupling or the fixed initial-block
treatment handles the bounded experiment; no asymptotic statement
about that case is used in (2)--(7).


\subsubsection{Action of the accumulated coupling-error wall}
\label{threshold:coupling-action}

The good-event discrepancy becomes a polynomial times a decaying
exponential in OU time. To insert it as a wall, we must control its
derivatives as well as its amplitude. The next lemma bounds both the
action and the total variation of its Cameron--Martin functional,
uniformly in the horizon.

\begin{lemma}[A logarithmic coupling wall]
\label{couplingwall:lemma}
Fix an integer $1\le m\le4$, $a\ge4m$, and $c\ge0$. On any finite
OU time interval $[0,T]$, put
\[
 w(s)=c(a+s)^m e^{-s/2}.
\]
With the action and variation functionals
\[
 A(w)=w(0)^2+\int_0^T(w'+w/2)^2\,ds,
\]
\[
 V(w)=|w'(T)+w(T)/2|+|w(0)/2-w'(0)|
                  +\int_0^T|w/4-w''|\,ds,
\]
one has, uniformly in $T$,
\[
 A(w)\le3m^2c^2a^{2m},\qquad
 V(w)\le10m^2ca^m.
\]
The same bounds hold for the reversed wall $w(T-s)$. For a sum of
one wall at each end, the action is at most twice the sum of the
individual actions and the variation is at most their sum.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For every $0\le j\le2m-2$,
\[
 (a+s)^j\le a^j e^{js/a}\le a^j e^{s/2},
\]
and for $0\le j\le m-1$ the last exponential can be replaced by
$e^{s/4}$. Also
\[
 w'+w/2=cm(a+s)^{m-1}e^{-s/2},
\]
\[
 w/4-w''=ce^{-s/2}
     \{m(a+s)^{m-1}-m(m-1)(a+s)^{m-2}\},
\]
where the last term is absent for $m=1$. The corresponding integrals
are bounded using $\int_0^\infty e^{-s/2}ds=2$ and
$\int_0^\infty e^{-s/4}ds=4$. The endpoint term
$(a+T)^{m-1}e^{-T/2}$ is at most $a^{m-1}$ because
$a\ge2(m-1)$. Thus
\[
 A(w)\le c^2a^{2m}+2m^2c^2a^{2m-2}
             \le3m^2c^2a^{2m},
\]
\[
 V(w)\le c\{a^m+2ma^{m-1}\}
          +4cm\{a^{m-1}+(m-1)a^{m-2}\}
             \le10m^2ca^m.
\]
Reversal preserves the action: expanding the two squares makes their
difference an endpoint term that cancels the difference of the initial
squares. It also interchanges the two boundary variation terms and
preserves the interior one. Finally, the assertions for sums follow
from $(u+v)^2\le2u^2+2v^2$ and the triangle inequality.
\end{proof}

Take the numerical compact parameter set $M\ge10$, with the two centered
channel standard deviations at least $M^{-2}$, the coefficients and
mean gaps at most $M^2$, and $\rho\ge M^{-1}$. In the numerical rank
coupling choose the tail power $A=400M$. The continuous-interpolation
bound on a block of length $L$ is
\[
 1000M^4(A+4)^2\log^3(L\vee e)
       \le 2\cdot10^8M^6\log^3(L\vee e).
\]
A block crossing rank time $t$ has length at most $2t$. There are at
most $2+\log_2(t/L_0)$ blocks up to that time, and
$\log(2t)\le2(1+\log t)$. Summing these bounds gives
\[
 2\cdot10^8M^6\{2+\log_2(t/L_0)\}\log^3(2t)
      \le 10^{10}M^6(1+\log t)^4\qquad(t\ge L_0).
\]
The total Gaussian standard deviation is at least $M^{-2}$.
Dividing by it and then by $\sqrt\rho$ to place the wall in the
environmental channel is therefore covered by the larger coefficient
\[
 C=10^{10}M^{12}.
\]
In particular the separate gap factors $c$ and $\tau$ enter through
the product $c\tau$ already present in the rank coupling. The coefficient bound is uniform in the time horizon and reserve.

On the good event, the accumulated stepwise error, including every
jump and within-block interpolation, is pointwise dominated by this
smooth majorant. In Lamperti time $s=\log(t/L_0)$, its wall is
\[
 w(s)=\frac{C}{\sqrt{L_0}}
             (1+\log L_0+s)^4e^{-s/2}.
\]
Apply the lemma with $m=4$, $a=1+\log L_0$, and
$c=C/\sqrt{L_0}$. Both its action and the square of its variation are
bounded by $26000C^2a^8/L_0$, uniformly in the final horizon. For
\[
 L_0=\left\lceil\exp\{\exp(M^{400})\}\right\rceil,
\]
one has $a\le2\exp(M^{400})$. The logarithm of the last bound is at
most
\[
 70+24\log M+8M^{400}-\exp(M^{400})<-100\log M.
\]
For example, the last inequality follows from
$e^u\ge u^2/2$, $u=M^{400}>300$, and $\log M\le u$.
Thus $A(w)+V(w)^2<M^{-100}$. The two-end version follows from the
last assertion of the lemma. This calculation establishes the
claimed bounded action uniformly over all later lengths.

A physical power wall of exponent $\gamma=1/8$ has Lamperti decay
exponent $1/2-\gamma=3/8$, which belongs to the numerical wall construction's
interval $[1/3,1/2]$. Reserve terms have exponent $1/2$. Therefore
the logarithmic wall and all the reserve and power walls
used here have the stated finite action and variation bounds.


\subsection{Explicit exact-clock and exact-type middle continuation}
\label{supp:explicit-middle-continuation}

Here we quantify the middle tube used when both inner endpoint
heights are central and positive. We retain nearly central totals in
a fixed number of subblocks, then control fluctuations inside each
exact subblock. A final chord calculation converts the rank bounds
to the whole physical path, including both sides of every jump and
the terminal gap. A common added reserve does not affect this
calculation.

Let \(M \ge 2\), \(0 < a \le 1\). Consider \(n\) exact marks with a uniform
\(K\)-subset, \(p = K / n \in [ 1 / M , 1 - 1 / M ]\), and independent exact uniform
clock gaps: \(n + 1\) exponentials conditioned on their sum
\(P = ( n + 1 ) \tau\), \(\tau \in [ 1 / M , M ]\). Let a risk have coefficients
\(0 < c , b , w_{+} \le M\), jumps \(w_{+} , w_{+} - b\) positive, and endpoint
reserves \(x , y \ge a \sqrt{n + 1}\). Their legality means that for one
fixed sign \(\epsilon \in \{- 1 , 1\}\) they satisfy the exact identity

\[
 y-x=\epsilon(cP-nw_++bK).
\]

At time \(t\), with \(r ( t )\) the number of marks already read and
\(s ( t )\) their selected-subset count, the risk and its physical chord
are

\[
 R(t)=x+\epsilon\{ct-w_+r(t)+bs(t)\},\qquad
 C(t)=x+(y-x)t/P.
\]

The endpoint difference is fixed by the exact count and clock totals.
Adding a common reserve raises the chord without changing that
difference or the fluctuation law.

Set

\[
 J=\left\lceil(10^8M^4/a^2)^2\right\rceil,
 \qquad \delta=\frac a{100M^2J},\qquad
 N_0=\left\lceil10^8M^8J^4/a^4\right\rceil,
\]

\[
 c_{\rm mid}=\frac12e^{-100MJ}
                     \left(\frac\delta{100M}\right)^{2J}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

For \(n + 1 \ge N_{0}\), the actual exact bridge stays within
\(a \sqrt{n + 1} / 2\) of its positive chord with probability at least
\(c_{\mathrm{mid}}\). In particular it stays above \(a \sqrt{n + 1} / 2\).
The constants do not depend on \(n , K , P , x , y\). Every one of the
\(n + 1\) gaps, including the final unmarked gap, is retained.

\subsubsection{Subblock totals have explicit positive mass}

Divide the \(n\) mark slots into \(J\) consecutive groups of sizes as
equal as possible. Allocate their corresponding gaps to these same
groups and allocate the one final gap to the last group. If \(q_{j}\)
is a gap shape, then, at (1),
\(( n + 1 ) / ( 2 J ) \le q_{j} \le 2 ( n + 1 ) / J\). Mark group sizes satisfy the same
bounds with \(n\) in place of \(n + 1\).

For the first \(J - 1\) groups retain their gap sums within
\(\delta \sqrt{n + 1}\) of \(\tau q_{j}\), and their subset counts within
\(\delta \sqrt{n}\) of \(p m_{j}\). The last totals are fixed by the
two global exact totals and differ from their means by at most
\(J \delta \sqrt{n + 1}\) and \(J \delta \sqrt{n}\). All these totals are
feasible: (1) makes their displacements smaller than half the
smallest gap mean and half each of the two smallest mark means.
Each first mark interval contains at least \(\delta \sqrt{n}\) integers.

The joint density of the first gap sums is exactly

\[
 \frac{\prod_{j=1}^J f_{q_j,\tau}(t_j)}
              {f_{n+1,\tau}(P)},\qquad t_J=P-\sum_{j<J}t_j.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

Elementary Stirling bounds imply, for \(m \ge 2\), \(| u | \le m \tau / 2\),

\[
 f_{m,\tau}(m\tau+u)
       \ge\frac1{4\tau\sqrt m}
                     \exp[-2-2u^2/(m\tau^2)],
 \quad
 f_{N,\tau}(N\tau)\le\frac1{\tau\sqrt N}.
\]

In (2), summing squared standardized displacements gives at most
\(4 J^{3} \delta^{2} M^{2}\). Integrating the \(J - 1\) intervals yields a mass
at least

\[
 e^{-10J-8J^3\delta^2M^2}
             \left(\frac\delta{10M}\right)^{J-1}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

For marks the exact joint probability of a specified count vector is
\(\prod_{j} \mathbb{P}( \operatorname{Bin} ( m_{j} , p ) = k_{j} ) / \mathbb{P}( \operatorname{Bin} ( n , p ) = K )\). On these central
displacements, Stirling and the elementary relative-entropy upper
\(D ( p + u / m | | p ) \le 4 u^{2} / ( m^{2} p_{\mathrm{min}} )\) give

\[
 \mathbb P(\operatorname{Bin}(m,p)=mp+u)
       \ge(4\sqrt m)^{-1}
                    e^{-4M-4Mu^2/m}.
\]

The denominator at its mean is at most \(2 \sqrt{M / n}\). Summing the
\(J - 1\) integer intervals therefore gives a mass at least

\[
 e^{-10MJ-8MJ^3\delta^2}
                       \left(\frac\delta{10}\right)^{J-1}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

The numerical lower bound in (1) is smaller than one half the
product of (3)--(4); use \(J^{3} \delta^{2} M^{2} \le J / 10^{4}\) and \(M \ge 2\).
Gap and subset total vectors are independent before and after their
own respective exact conditioning.

\subsubsection{Conditional subblock fluctuations have constant success}

After these two complete total vectors are fixed, different subblocks
are independent. Inside a gap subblock the exact-total law is a
Dirichlet spacing law. On its first half its density relative to iid
exponentials of its exact mean is at most 100: divide a Gamma
maximum density by its exact-mean density and use Stirling. The
same statement holds on its reversed half.

For iid centered mean-\(\tau\) exponentials, the elementary exponential
martingale gives

\[
 \mathbb P\{\max_{r\le m}|\sum_{i\le r}(E_i-\tau)|>u\}
 \le2\exp[-\tfrac14\min\{u^2/(m\tau^2),u/\tau\}].
\]

Applying this on the two halves after the density comparison bounds
the exact subblock gap failure by
\(400 \exp [ - c \min ( u^{2} / ( m \tau^{2} ) , u / \tau ) ]\), with \(c = 1 / 16\) sufficient.

For an exact binary subset of size \(k\) in \(m\) positions, write
\(B_{r} = \sum_{i \le r} B_{i} - rk / m\). The process
\(B_{r} / ( m - r )\) is a martingale for \(r < m\). On the first half its
increments have absolute value at most \(4 / m\). The maximal Azuma
bound, then reversal for the second half, gives

\[
 \mathbb P\{\max_{r\le m}|B_r|>u\}
                         \le4e^{-u^2/(16m)}.
\]

Take \(u = a \sqrt{n + 1} / ( 100 M^{2} )\). The true conditional gap means stay
in \([ 1 / ( 2 M ) , 2 M ]\); at (1) both subblock failure exponents dominate
\(a^{2} J / ( 2\cdot10^{6} M^{6} )\). Consequently the total failure over all subblocks
and both channels is at most

\[
 800J\exp[-a^2J/(2\cdot10^6M^6)]<\frac12.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

The last strict inequality follows directly from the explicit choice
of \(J\): its exponent is at least \(5\cdot10^{9} M^{2} / a^{2}\), while
\(\log ( 1600 J ) \le 100 M^{2} / a^{2}\).

Here is the physical-chord calculation, including the final gap.
Put \(N = n + 1\), \(A = n w_{+} - bK\), and let \(T_{r}\) be the time of the
\(r\)th mark, \(S_{r}\) its cumulative number of selected marks. At all
physical times, including the final unmarked gap,

\[
 R(t)-C(t)=-\epsilon\left[
 w_+\{r(t)-nt/P\}-b\{s(t)-Kt/P\}\right].
\]

At time \(T_{r}\), the bracket is

\[
 r w_+-bS_r-(A/P)T_r.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

The coefficient \(A / P\) is in \([ 0 , M^{2} ]\), since all jumps are positive.
Writing \(T_{r} = r \tau + e_{r}\) and \(S_{r} = pr + v_{r}\), (6) becomes
\(r ( w_{+} - bp ) / N - bv_{r} - ( A / P ) e_{r}\); its first term is at most \(M\).
The retained total displacements and the within-block events give
\(| e_{r} | \le J \delta \sqrt{N} + u\) and
\(| v_{r} | \le J \delta \sqrt{n} + u\). Thus the absolute value in (6) is at
most \(M + 2 M^{2} ( J \delta \sqrt{N} + u )\). Immediately before a mark there
is one further jump of size at most \(M\). Between marks the chord
error is linear, so its maximum occurs at one of these endpoints.
On the final unmarked gap it is again linear and ends at zero.
Consequently the complete physical-path error is at most

\[
 2M+2M^2(J\delta\sqrt N+u)
       \le 2M+\frac{a\sqrt N}{25}
       <\frac{a\sqrt N}{2},
\]

where the last inequality follows from \(N \ge N_{0}\). Both risk signs
use this same absolute deviation. Combining (3)--(5) proves (1).

\subsubsection{Completing the conditional private mass}

This is a joint ordinary continuation for each retained prefix
word with compatible inner endpoint heights at least \(a \sqrt{n}\).
For a fixed prefix environment let its already accepted private
mass be \(q\), and let the completed private mass be \(U\) as a function
of the remaining environment. Then \(0 \le U \le q\) and
\(\mathbb{E} U \ge c_{\mathrm{mid}} q\); hence \(\mathbb{E} U^{\eta} \ge c_{\mathrm{mid}} q^{\eta}\) before averaging the
prefix. The prefix remains fixed in this inequality; its rare mass is
averaged only after the remaining-clock fractional moment has been
bounded.

If a physical strong curve has amplitude \(g\) and exponent
\(\gamma < 1 / 2\), additionally require

\[
 n+1\ge(4gM^\gamma/a)^{1/(1/2-\gamma)}.
\]

Then the retained tube dominates that curve. Named REG is completed
by its pointwise uniform conditional refinement bound; if ordinary
REG is imposed here, choose its explicit error smaller than
\(c_{\mathrm{mid}} / 4\) before subtracting it. That is a finite elementary tail
condition once the desired slopes/intercepts are specified.

This gives explicit middle-continuation constants. The next
subsection supplies the endpoint-box and wall constants for the OU
comparison.


\subsection{Numerical OU endpoint, wall and multiplicativity constants}
\label{supp:explicit-ou-construction}
Fix \(M \ge 2\) and

\[
 M^{-1}\le\eta\le1,\qquad M^{-1}\le\rho\le1-M^{-1}.
\]

Let \(E , W\) be independent stationary OU processes with covariance
\(\exp ( - | s - t | / 2 )\), and put

\[
 q_t(E)=\mathbb P_W\{\sqrt\rho E_s+\sqrt{1-\rho}W_s\ge0,
                         0\le s\le t\mid E\},\qquad
 F(t)=\mathbb E q_t(E)^\eta.
\]

At $\eta=1$, $F(t)=\pi^{-1}\arcsin(e^{-t/2})$; in this
case set $\chi(1,\rho)=1/2$.

The following constants cover the endpoint tails, multiplicativity,
and wall comparisons. We choose them with ample room for the later
relative-error estimates:

\[
 a_*=2^{-48}M^{-2},\qquad C_*=2^{10},\qquad
 B_*=2^{28}M^2,\qquad C_Q=2^{80}M^2.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

Every assertion below first holds on a finite time grid; monotone
refinement and continuity give the continuous assertion. No
constant in (1) depends on the time or on the grid cardinality.

\subsubsection{The conditional private endpoint}

As in Lemma~\ref{pr:filter}, fluctuations around the endpoint mode have
a Gaussian bound. The mode contracts over each fixed-length segment
and is driven by the negative part of the environmental wall. We make
both estimates numerical here.

For a fixed environment, the endpoint density of \(W\) conditioned on
survival is \(\phi ( z ) g ( z )\), where \(g\) is increasing and log-concave.
The monotonicity follows by running the OU bridge backwards from
its endpoint: its conditional mean at every earlier time is an
increasing multiple of \(z\). Log-concavity is the Gaussian
Pr\'ekopa's theorem applied to the convex set of path inequalities.
Consequently its log density has curvature at most \(- 1\), and its
mode \(m\) is nonnegative. The usual density-ratio proof gives

\[
 |W-m|\preceq_{\rm st}|N(0,1)|,
 \quad |\mathbb EW-m|\le1,
 \quad \mu\le_{\rm lr}m+|N(0,1)|.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

For the last comparison, the ratio of \(\mu ( m + u )\) to the half-normal
density is decreasing for \(u \ge 0\): differentiate and use the
curvature bound and the zero derivative at the mode. Below \(m\)
the half-normal density is zero. OU transition and killed
transition kernels are TP2, so this likelihood-ratio order
propagates through a future segment.

Consider a segment of length \(v \in [ 1 , 2 ]\), and let
\(B = \sup ( - \sqrt{\rho / ( 1 - \rho )} E )_{+}\) there. Raise its wall to \(B\)
and raise its incoming law to \(m + | N |\). Let \(r = \exp ( - v / 2 )\).
An OU noise segment is \(\exp ( - s / 2 ) B_{\exp ( s ) - 1}\), and
\(\exp ( 2 ) - 1 < 7\). The explicit Brownian tube bound

\[
 \mathbb P\{\sup_{u\le7}|B_u|\le1\}\ge e^{-100}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

is enough. For example, divide \([ 0 , 7 ]\) into 28 intervals of length
\(1 / 4\), retain each interval endpoint in \([ - 1 / 4 , 1 / 4 ]\), and require
its bridge fluctuation to have absolute value at most \(1 / 2\).
The Gaussian transition density on that endpoint interval is at
least \(e^{- 1 / 2} / \sqrt{2 \pi / 4}\) and the Brownian bridge reflection
bound gives bridge success at least \(1 - 2 e^{- 2}\). The product is
larger than \(e^{- 100}\).

If \(rm \ge B + 2\), (3) gives survival probability at least \(e^{- 100}\).
The unrestricted endpoint relative to \(rm\) is bounded by
\(r | N_{1} | + \sqrt{1 - r^{2}} N_{2}\); its positive tail is at most
\(4 \exp ( - u^{2} / 8 )\). Tail integration after dividing by \(e^{- 100}\)
gives conditional mean at most \(rm + 100\).

If \(rm < B + 2\), retain the starting half-normal in
\([ e ( B + 3 ) , e ( B + 3 ) + 1 ]\). Since \(0 \le m \le e ( B + 2 )\), this costs at most
\(\exp [ - 101 ( B + 1 )^{2} ]\) in the exponent. With (3) the survival
probability is at least \(\exp [ - 201 ( B + 1 )^{2} ]\). The same tail
integration with cutoff \(100 ( B + 1 )\) gives conditional mean at
most \(rm + 101 ( B + 1 )\). By (2), in either case the new mode satisfies

\[
 m_{\rm new}\le rm+1024(B+1).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

For an initial segment of duration at most one the same proof
starts at the unfiltered stationary normal and gives the same
\(1024 ( B + 1 )\) bound. Decompose backwards into intervals of lengths
in \([ 1 , 2 ]\), with at most one initial short interval. Since
\(\sqrt{\rho / ( 1 - \rho )} \le \sqrt{M} \le M\), (4) gives the pointwise bound

\[
 m_t(E)\le\mathcal M_t(E)
   :=8192M\left(1+\sum_{j\ge0}e^{-j/2}
                 \sup_{s\in I_j}(-E_s)_+\right).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

The functional on the right is decreasing in every environment
coordinate. For a stationary OU interval of length at most two,
its supremum \(Z\) in absolute value satisfies
\(\mathbb{P}( Z > u ) \le 6 \exp ( - u^{2} / 56 )\) by the representation above and reflection.
Thus \(\mathbb{E} \exp ( Z^{2} / 112 ) \le 7\). Put \(S = \sum \exp ( - j / 2 ) < 3\).
Weighted Cauchy--Schwarz and Jensen, without independence of the
intervals, give

\[
 \mathbb E\exp(2^{-40}M^{-2}\mathcal M_t^2)\le8.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

\subsubsection{Relative moments of the tilted environment}

The environment law tilted by \(q_{t}^{\eta}\) is MTP2 and lies in
stochastic order between its original law and the law tilted by
\(q_{t}\). This follows from monotonicity of \(q_{t}\), MTP2 of \(q_{t}\),
and association under each intermediate tilt. Applying these
orders separately to the positive and negative parts suffices;
the square moment is assembled from these two monotone functions.

Under the \(q_{t}\) tilt, rotate into the positive composite channel
\(Z = \sqrt{\rho} E + \sqrt{1 - \rho} W\) and its independent orthogonal OU
channel. At a time \(u \in [ 0 , t ]\) its conditional density is

\[
 \frac{\phi(z)p_u(z)p_{t-u}(z)}{F_1(t)},\quad z\ge0,
 \quad p_v(z)=2\Phi\left(\frac z{\sqrt{e^v-1}}\right)-1,
 \quad F_1(t)=\pi^{-1}\arcsin(e^{-t/2}).
\]

For \(v = 0\), take \(p_{0} = 1\). The inequalities
\(p_{v} ( z ) \le \min ( 1 , \sqrt{2 / \pi} z / \sqrt{e^{v} - 1} )\) and
\(F_{1} ( t ) \ge \pi^{- 1} \exp ( - t / 2 )\) show, by splitting according as both
durations exceed one, that this density is at most
\(10 ( 1 + z )^{2} \phi ( z )\). Therefore the environment at every time under
the \(q_{t}^{\eta}\) tilt satisfies

\[
 \mathbb E_{\rm tilt}e^{uE_s^2}\le2^8,
                       \qquad0\le u\le1/8.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

For the negative part use the original normal law; for the
positive part use the rotated density just displayed. Inequality
(6), under the tilt, follows from its decreasing functional and
stochastic order. Together with (2), Cauchy--Schwarz, and time
reversal, (6)--(7) give the two-end bound

\[
 \mathbb E_E\left[
   e^{a_*(E_0^2+E_t^2)}
   \left(\mathbb E_W[1_{\rm survive}
                     e^{a_*(W_0^2+W_t^2)}\mid E]\right)^\eta
                  \right]\le C_*F(t).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

All exponents left after the four Cauchy--Schwarz steps are
smaller than the exponents in (6) and (7); the numerical factors
are smaller than \(2^{10}\).

\subsubsection{Quasi-multiplicativity and endpoint boxes}

The mixed endpoint moment controls the Mehler density across a fixed
gap. It also lets us discard large endpoints relative to the surviving
mass and then translate the retained endpoints into positive boxes.
Both operations have costs independent of the horizon.

Separate two surviving segments by
\(g = 2 \log ( 1 / a_{*} ) + 4\). Their Mehler density relative to independent
endpoints is at most
\(( 1 - r^{2} )^{- 1 / 2} \exp ( r ( x^{2} + y^{2} ) / ( 2 ( 1 + r ) ) )\), \(r = \exp ( - g / 2 )\).
Use it first inside the private integral and then outside. Its
quadratic coefficient is at most \(a_{*}\), so (8) gives

\[
 F(s+g+t)\le2^{22}F(s)F(t).
\]

Association gives \(F ( s + g + t ) \ge F ( s + t ) F ( g )\), and
\(F ( g ) \ge F_{1} ( g ) \ge \exp ( - g / 2 ) / \pi\). Hence

\[
 F(s)F(t)\le F(s+t)\le C_QF(s)F(t),\qquad
 C_Q^{-1}e^{-\chi t}\le F(t)\le e^{-\chi t}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

The exponential rate exists by superadditivity, and
\(\eta / 2 \le \chi \le 1 / 2\), as in the fractional persistence theorem.

Remove every endpoint outside \([ - B_{*} , B_{*} ]\). The environmental
tail uses (8) directly. For a private tail, fractional
subadditivity and (8) give cost at most
\(C_{*} \exp ( - a_{*} \eta B_{*}^{2} ) F ( t )\). Since
\(a_{*} \eta B_{*}^{2} \ge 256 M\), the four deletions cost less than \(F ( t ) / 4\).
Translate both channels by

\[
 h(s)=4B_*\{e^{-s/2}+e^{-(t-s)/2}\}.
\]

This raises the whole path, and takes both endpoints into
\([ 3 B_{*} , 9 B_{*} ]\). For one channel its Cameron--Martin norm squared
is at most \(4 ( 4 B_{*} )^{2}\), while its linear functional on the retained
box has absolute value at most \(8 B_{*}^{2}\). The two translations
therefore cost at most \(\exp ( - 80 B_{*}^{2} )\), including the fractional
private density factor. Thus the moment with these four positive
endpoint restrictions is at least

\[
 \tfrac12e^{-80B_*^2}F(t).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

Wider compatible boxes only increase this lower bound.

\subsubsection{Explicit bounded-action walls}

An environmental translation imposes the desired composite wall.
After integration by parts, its likelihood uses a signed measure of
path values. The tilted pointwise Gaussian moment therefore controls
the likelihood through the total variation of that measure.

For a deterministic twice differentiable OU shift \(h\), write

\[
 A(h)=h(0)^2+\int_0^t(h'+h/2)^2ds,
\]

\[
 V(h)=|h'(t)+h(t)/2|+|h(0)/2-h'(0)|
             +\int_0^t|h/4-h''|ds.
\]

Integration by parts expresses its Cameron--Martin functional
as a signed path-value measure of total variation at most \(V ( h )\).
From (7), Jensen with its normalized variation measure, and
\(u | z | \le z^{2} / 8 + 2 u^{2}\), one obtains

\[
 \mathbb E_{\rm tilt}e^{\pm L_h}
                          \le2^8e^{2V(h)^2},
 \quad |\mathbb E_{\rm tilt}L_h|\le8V(h).
\]

Consequently the fractional moment for the shifted environmental
path satisfies the explicit comparison

\[
 e^{-8V(h)-A(h)/2}F(t)
 \le\mathbb E q_t(E+h)^\eta
 \le2^8e^{2V(h)^2}F(t).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

To impose a composite wall \(b ( s )\), take \(h = b / \sqrt{\rho}\) and the
appropriate sign. For a sum of \(d\) terms
\(C_{l} \exp ( - \alpha_{l} s )\) or \(C_{l} \exp ( - \alpha_{l} ( t - s ) )\), with
\(\alpha_{l} \in [ 1 / 3 , 1 / 2 ]\), let \(W = \sum | C_{l} |\). Direct integration gives

\[
 A(h)\le12MW^2,\qquad V(h)\le16\sqrt M W.
\]

Thus all Lamperti reserve, \(\gamma \le 1 / 6\) power-wall, and bounded
scaled-drift terms of total amplitude at most \(W\) have an upper
comparison constant \(2^{8} \exp ( 512 MW^{2} )\) and lower constant
\(\exp ( - 128 \sqrt{M} W - 6 MW^{2} )\). Their endpoint displacement is at most
\(\sqrt{M} W\); enlarge the four endpoint boxes by this fixed amount.
These bounds specify the widths of the Gaussian endpoint boxes and
the separation needed for the Mehler comparison. The dimension-dependent
values of \(M,W\), together with the hierarchy, regularity, count, and
grid bounds, are chosen in Section~\ref{supp:explicit-fixed-lift-rule}.


\subsection{Numerical flat preparation, relative failures and whole-block independence}
\label{supp:explicit-relative-bad-construction}

This subsection makes the relative coupling argument effective. First
we prepare a larger reserve at a deterministic time, so that a fresh
future is independent of the preparation. We then prove doubling,
sum the favorable-prefix-height bins, and verify that late failures
read blocks disjoint from the retained early prefix. These comparisons
are established for the flat walk before its persistence exponent is
used.

Let \(M \ge 10\). All positive coefficients, gap means, nonzero jump
sizes, and centered channel standard deviations are in
\([ M^{- 2} , M^{2} ]\); both binary fractions and their complements are
at least \(M^{- 2}\); \(M^{- 1} \le \eta \le 1\); the associated
Lamperti correlation satisfies \(M^{-1}\le\rho\le1-M^{-1}\); and
the signed mean drift obeys \(| \delta | \sqrt{n} \le M\). Choose
\(M\) large enough to satisfy all these bounds.
Let \(F_{n} ( h )\) be the conditional fractional survival moment for the
flat walk, with the continuous pre/post-jump convention retained.

One possible construction is

\[
 h\ge M^{100},\quad
 C_{\rm prep}=\exp\{\exp(M^{200})\},\quad
 C_{\rm double}=\exp(M^{5000}),\quad
 C_{\rm bad}=\exp\{\exp(M^{300})\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

For every \(n \ge 1\), every \(u \ge 0\), and every event \(D\) reading a
prefix of \(b \le n / 2\) original channels and their independent coupling
auxiliaries, the following inequalities hold after a fixed
initial finite convention with the same bounds:

\[
 F_n(h)\ge C_{\rm prep}^{-1}
                 \min\{1,(1+h)/\sqrt{1+n}\},
\]

\[
 F_n(h+u)\le C_{\rm prep}(1+u)F_n(h),\quad
 F_n(h)\le C_{\rm double}F_{2n}(h),
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

\[
 \mathbb E q_{{\rm survive},D}^{\eta}
 \le C_{\rm bad}(1+b)^2\mathbb P(D)^{\eta/4}F_n(h).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]
