For a bad event whose whole coupling-block sigma-field is independent
of every whole block used by the retained first
\(\lfloor n/16\rfloor\) slots, the right side can instead be
\(C_{\mathrm{bad}} \mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta} F_{n} ( h )\). At small \(n\), retain the actual event and use the constant in (1).
The finite convention is thus fixed by the original walk and the
displayed compact input, before the Gaussian exponent or the
conditional survival normalization enters.

\subsubsection{Numerical ordinary preparation at a deterministic time}

The stopped walk reaches an upper height with a controlled probability,
but its hitting time is random. The tube construction extends each
retained entrance to one deterministic terminal time while keeping
both channel totals central. This is the point at which the later
concatenation obtains independent future channels.

First center the walk by changing the exponential mean by its
signed mean drift. For \(n \ge M^{100}\), this changed mean remains
in \([ M^{- 3} , M^{3} ]\), since \(| \delta | \le M / \sqrt{n}\). For smaller \(n\),
the reserve \(h \ge M^{100}\) and the exponential tail give ordinary
survival of probability at least one half; all comparisons below
are then covered by (1). Continuous survival in the orientation
with negative clock motion costs at most one extra bounded jump:
start its discrete argument from reserve \(h - M^{2} \ge h / 2\).

For the centered walk stopped on leaving \([ - h / 2 , u ]\), put
\(l = u + h + 2 M^{3}\). Every exponential-side overshoot has conditional
mean at most \(2 M^{3}\) and second moment at most \(8 M^{6}\), by
memorylessness; the opposite overshoot is bounded by \(M^{2}\).
Optional stopping of the walk and of its square minus variance
times time gives

\[
 \mathbb P(\text{upper exit})\ge\frac{h}{4l},\qquad
 \mathbb E\tau_{\rm exit}\le M^{20}(h+1)l.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

For the upper inequality on the mean exit time, first bound the
upper-exit probability above by \(( h + 2 M^{3} ) / u\) when \(u \ge h\), then
its square contribution by \(M^{6} ( h + 1 ) l\). If \(u < h\), the crude
bound \(M^{6} l^{2} \le 4 M^{6} ( h + 1 ) l\) suffices. Divide by variance at
least \(M^{- 4}\). Truncation justifies the stopped identities.

Take \(R = \exp ( M^{40} )\). Markov's inequality on (4) removes less
than one tenth of the upper exits when the stopping time exceeds
\(Rl^{2} / 4\). The individual centered clock and mark martingales
have stopped second moments at most \(M^{30} ( h + 1 ) l\).
Their Doob bound removes less than another tenth if either
absolute value exceeds \(M^{30} l\) before the retained exit.

Extend each retained exit to the deterministic time
\(m = \lceil Rl^{2} \rceil\), staying positive and ending above the
desired enlarged reserve. For a fresh segment of length between
\(l^{2} / M^{30}\) and twice that length, retain binary counts in a
central interval of width \(\sqrt{\mathrm{length}} / M^{20}\) and
the Gamma total in an interval giving signed risk increment between
zero and \(\sqrt{\mathrm{length}} / M^{20}\). Central Stirling
bounds give this joint total event probability at least
\(\exp ( - M^{100} )\).

Conditional on the retained exact totals, apply the middle tube in
Section~\ref{supp:explicit-middle-continuation} with compact parameter
\(M ' = M^{10}\) and endpoint fraction \(a = M^{- 20}\). Its
explicit constants \(J , N_{0} , c_{\mathrm{mid}}\) satisfy

\[
 J\le M^{300},\qquad N_0\le M^{2000},\qquad
 c_{\rm mid}\ge e^{-M^{1000}}.
\]

For a segment of length below \(M^{2000}\), retain each increment
in a fixed favorable interval. Such an interval has probability
at least \(\exp ( - M^{20} )\) and positive increment at least
\(M^{- 10}\). In the exponential-positive orientation choose its
gap in a unit interval far enough above its mean and choose the
favorable binary mark; in the opposite orientation choose its
gap below half its mean and the favorable mark. Thus every short
segment has a tube probability at least \(\exp ( - M^{3000} )\).
If \(l < M^{2000}\), this same direct event handles the entire
fixed preparation time; it costs at most
\(\exp [ - M^{20} R M^{4002} ] \ge \exp [ - \exp ( M^{100} ) ]\).

For \(l \ge M^{2000}\), split the remaining time after the stopped
entrance into the displayed segment sizes, with a possibly
short last segment. There are at most \(2 RM^{30} + 1\) segments.
All starting and ending reserves are at least a fixed fraction
of \(l\), so the exact middle tube applies. Every segment has
nonnegative endpoint increment, and its within-segment error is
less than \(l / 100\). Its two individual channel totals remain in
central windows of width at most \(M^{30} l\) per segment. The
product lower bound is at least
\(\exp [ - \exp ( M^{100} ) ]\), uniformly in the retained stopping time.

Changing the exponential mean back to its original value on
these retained total windows costs at most
\(\exp [ - M^{100} R^{2} ]\); expand its exact Gamma likelihood and use
\(| \delta | l \le M\) when \(l \le \sqrt{n}\). This is again larger than
\(\exp [ - \exp ( M^{150} ) ]\). The final preparation has probability

\[
 \mathbb P(\text{fixed-time preparation})
      \ge C_{\rm prep}^{-1}\frac{h}{u+h+2M^3}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

The final time is deterministic, so its two fresh future
channels are independent of the preparation. If the private
preparation probability at a fixed environment is \(p\), then
\(\mathbb{E} p^{\eta} \ge \mathbb{E} p\). Concatenation therefore proves the reserve
inequality when \(l \le \sqrt{n}\), since the full concatenated event
implies the original first \(n\) steps. The preparation may be
longer than \(n\); its likelihood bound above only used
\(| \delta | l \le M\), so that causes no difficulty. Independently,
ordinary survival follows by preparation at height
\(\sqrt{n / ( 10 R )}\) in at most \(n / 2\) steps and its positive tube to
time \(n\). For this continuation use the actual smaller
height fraction \(a_{R} = ( 100 M^{10} \sqrt{R} )^{- 1}\) and compact parameter set
\(M ' = M^{10}\), rather than \(a = M^{- 20}\). Its explicit formulas give

\[
 J_R\le e^{M^{41}},\qquad N_R\le e^{M^{42}},\qquad
 c_R\ge\exp[-\exp(M^{43})].
\]

For example \(\log J_{R} \le 24 \log 10 + 120 \log M + 2 M^{40} \le M^{41}\);
the displayed \(N_{R}\) and \(c_{R}\) bounds follow by substitution.
Sum the unconditioned count and gap totals in compatible central
intervals of width \(a_{R} \sqrt{n} / ( 100 M^{10} )\) to obtain legal
endpoints both at least \(a_{R} \sqrt{n}\); their total mass is at
least \(\exp ( - M^{100} ) a_{R}^{2}\). Then apply the exact middle tube.
If \(n < N_{R}\), a fixed favorable increment event costs at most
\(\exp [ - M^{20} N_{R} ] \ge \exp [ - \exp ( M^{43} ) ]\). Thus a uniform ordinary
continuation constant \(\exp [ - \exp ( M^{50} ) ]\) suffices. It is much
larger than the inverse \(C_{\mathrm{prep}}\) used in (2). This gives the
first line of (2), including saturation when the original
reserve already exceeds that height. If
\(l > \sqrt{n}\), then either \(h \ge \sqrt{n} / 4\) and this ordinary lower
is a fixed constant, or \(u \ge \sqrt{n} / 4\) (the fixed \(2 M^{3}\)
allowance is harmless as \(h \ge M^{100}\)). In the latter case
\(( 1 + u ) F_{n} ( h )\) has a fixed lower bound. Use \(F_{n} ( h + u ) \le 1\).
All lost powers of \(R\) are smaller than \(C_{\mathrm{prep}}\).
This proves the crude lower and reserve comparison using only
stopped moments, central total probabilities, and the explicit
middle tube.

\subsubsection{Numerical doubling for flat survival}

Remove prefix environments whose unfavorable centered clock
sum exceeds \(100 M^{4} \sqrt{n}\). Its ordinary probability is at most
\(M^{- 4} / 100\); its mass under the survival tilt is at most the
same fraction, since survival and the unfavorable event have
opposite coordinate monotonicities. Product association bounds the weighted loss directly by the
unweighted unfavorable-clock probability.

At every remaining environment, force the \emph{one-sided favorable
binary-count tail} whose displacement is at least
\(M^{12} \sqrt{n}\). It is a lower count tail when fewer selected
marks are favorable, and an upper count tail in the opposite
orientation. This event is monotone in the same direction as
survival. For \(n \ge M^{100}\), obtain its probability lower bound
\(\exp ( - M^{50} )\) by a central subinterval contained in that tail.
The subinterval is used only to estimate the tail probability;
it is not the event used in association or in the continuation.
If feasibility fails, \(n\) is below a fixed power of \(M\) and
the favorable supported word has probability at least
\(\exp ( - M^{200} )\). Its intersection with private survival retains
at least this fraction by binary product association. We retain the whole favorable count tail, since continuation uses
only the lower bound \(M^{- 10} \sqrt{n}\) on the ending reserve.

An independent second half from this reserve has ordinary
survival probability at least \(\exp ( - M^{4000} )\). Use the same
central total windows and explicit exact middle tube as above;
when the sample size is below its displayed threshold, the
fixed favorable word/gap event costs at most \(\exp ( - M^{4000} )\).
If a prefix private mass is \(f\) and its completion at the future
environment has mass \(Z\), then \(0 \le Z \le f\) and \(\mathbb{E} Z \ge cf\).
Thus \(\mathbb{E} Z^{\eta} \ge c f^{\eta}\). Combining the two retentions proves
the numerical doubling constant in (1).

\subsubsection{Summing the relative bad-event costs}

Bin the positive prefix risk increment in intervals \([ r , r + 1 )\),
putting every nonpositive value in bin zero. If \(p_{r}\) is its
conditional private mass intersected with \(D\), independence of
the remaining original channels and the reserve comparison give

\[
 E q_{{\rm survive},D}^\eta
 \le C_{\rm prep}C_{\rm double}
              F_n(h)\sum_{r\ge0}(2+r)E p_r^\eta.
\]

The centered exponential and bounded binary Chernoff bounds give

\[
 \mathbb P(H_b^+\ge r)
 \le10\exp\left[-\frac1{1000M^{10}}
               \min\left(\frac{r^2}{1+b},r\right)\right]
\]

after shifting the mean by at most \(M \sqrt{b}\), which only enlarges
the constant to \(\exp ( M^{30} )\). Jensen and Cauchy--Schwarz give
\(\mathbb{E} p_{r}^{\eta} \le \mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta / 2} \mathbb{P}( H_{b}^{+} \ge r )^{\eta / 2}\) for \(r \ge 1\),
and \(\mathbb{E} p_{0}^{\eta} \le \mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta}\). Sum the Gaussian part through
\(r \le 1 + b\) and then the exponential part. The sum is at most
\(\exp ( M^{50} ) ( 1 + b ) \mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta / 2}\). The constants from (1), and
one doubling to compare \(n - b\) with \(n\), are smaller than
\(C_{\mathrm{bad}}\); weakening the power and the polynomial proves (3).

For a late bad event the separation is on the \emph{whole product
block-coupling space}, including every auxiliary. In the dyadic
construction, a block of length \(2^jL_0\) has left endpoint
\(a=(2^j-1)L_0\) and right endpoint \(b=(2^{j+1}-1)L_0=2a+L_0\).
Thus \(b>n/4\) and \(n\ge16L_0\) imply
\(a>3n/32>n/16\). Retain necessary survival only on
the first \(\lfloor n/16\rfloor\) original channels. Every whole
coupling block used by this prefix has a different block index from
every late block just identified. Consequently the complete
\(\sigma\) fields, including all auxiliaries, are independent.
Jensen bounds the other factor
by \(\mathbb{P}( D )^{\eta}\); a fixed number of doublings gives the displayed late
inequality. If \(n < 16 L_{0}\), handle the initial block by the
early estimate or the final reserve chosen larger than
\(100 M L_{0}^{2}\); the early estimate controls that overlapping-block range.
For a general event the late variant requires its entire
coupling blocks to be disjoint from the retained prefix.
Every early event can read auxiliaries because the intersection
estimate and the height tail are unconditional.

\subsubsection{An explicit coupling starting scale}

Apply Section~\ref{supp:explicit-rank-coupling} with \(A = 400 M\) on dyadic blocks.
The block error is at most
\(1000 M^{4} ( A + 4 )^{2} \log^{3} ( L \vee e )\) after a harmless coefficient
enlargement, and its failure is at most \(5 L^{- A}\). An explicit
starting scale is

\[
 L_0=\left\lceil\exp\{\exp(M^{400})\}\right\rceil.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

The relative bad-block series is bounded by
\(10 C_{\mathrm{bad}} L_{0}^{2 - A \eta / 4} < \exp ( - M^{100} )\).
Section~\ref{threshold:coupling-action} gives a smooth pointwise
majorant for the accumulated good errors, including jumps and
interpolation. Its action plus squared variation is less than
$M^{-100}$, uniformly in the final horizon.
The quantitative OU wall estimates absorb the accumulated good
errors, while the relative series pays the bad errors at the same
survival scale.

A negative soft power wall uses the same preparation because
its attached future wall is stronger than the shifted global
wall. Choose \(h \ge ( 100 g )^{1 / ( 1 - 2 \gamma )}\) first; its normalized
Lamperti amplitude is at most \(1 / 100\). A positive strong wall is
treated by flat bad-event domination and the Gaussian lower
comparison. For that wall the error is paid by the established flat relative
bound.

These probability estimates depend only on the stated physical compact input $M$. Sections~\ref{supp:finite-history-constants} and \ref{supp:explicit-fixed-lift-rule} explicitly bound the deterministic, count, and regularity constants in terms of $k$ and imply the choice of $\Lambda_k$.


\subsection{Numerical ordinary bridge estimates}
\label{supp:explicit-ordinary-construction}

The constant-mark bridge requires its own effective construction.
There is one gap channel and no private count variance. A stopped
quadratic potential gives the drifted upper bound; one-channel
Gaussian survival and relative coupling give the strong lower bound.
The exact bridge is then completed by a middle tube or an asymmetric
continuation. We keep the physical coefficient bound separate from
the larger probability constants, so that the final reserve does not
enter the definition of an earlier threshold.

\subsubsection{Parameters and explicit bounds}

Two constants must be kept separate. Let \(A \ge 10\) bound the physical
coefficients, and choose

\[
 M\ge \exp(A^{1000}).                                      \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

Assume \(w , c , \tau \in [ A^{- 1} , A ]\), \(P = ( n + 1 ) \tau\), \(n \ge 1\), and
\(\epsilon \in \{- 1 , 1\}\). The clock is the uniform clock of \(n\)
marks in \([ 0 , P ]\); equivalently all \(n\)+1 gaps are exponentials of
mean \(\tau\) conditioned on their total \(P\). Put

\[
 R(t)=x+\epsilon\{wN(t)-ct\},\quad
 y-x=\epsilon(nw-cP),\quad
 C(t)=x+(y-x)t/P.                                           \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

The exact chord identity is

\[
 R(t)-C(t)=\epsilon w\{N(t)-nt/P\}.                          \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

The exact signed increment links the two endpoints. Adding a common
reserve changes the chord but leaves the centered fluctuation and
the coefficient in (3) unchanged.

Fix \(\gamma = 1 / 8\), \(\zeta = 1 / 16\), \(0 \le g \le A\), a REG slope
\(\nu \ge M^{- 1}\), and a grid with at most \(A\) boundaries per physical
unit interval. Rates within \(A / \sqrt{1 + n}\) of \(n / P\) are permitted.
The following construction suffices:

\[
 L_0=\lceil e^{e^{M^{2300}}}\rceil,\quad
 h_{\rm pre}=\lceil e^{e^{M^{2400}}}\rceil,\quad
 N_{\rm core}=\lceil e^{e^{M^{2600}}}\rceil,
\]

\[
 \boxed{h_{\rm ord}=\lceil e^{e^{M^{3000}}}\rceil,
 \quad K_{\rm ord}=\lceil e^{e^{M^{3500}}}\rceil,
 \quad C_{\rm ord}=e^{e^{M^{4000}}}.}                         \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

For every legal \(x , y \ge h_{\mathrm{ord}}\), with regularity intercept at least \(K_{\mathrm{ord}}\),

\begin{equation}
\begin{gathered}
 C_{\rm ord}^{-1}\beta_n(x,y)
 \le \PP\{R(t)\ge g d_P(t)^{1/8}\ (0\le t\le P),
                         \ \operatorname{REG}\}
 \le C_{\rm ord}\beta_n(x,y),\\
 \beta_n(x,y)=\min\{1,(1+x)(1+y)/(1+n)\}.
\end{gathered}\tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\end{equation}

Here \(d_{P} ( t ) = \min ( t , P - t )\) and REG means

\[
 |N(t)-N(s)-\lambda_0(t-s)|
 \le\nu(t-s)+K[1+d_P(s)^{1/16}+d_P(t)^{1/16}]
                                                                  \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

for grid pairs, or all physical pairs after reducing the initial
slope by a factor 100 and enlarging \(K\) by a factor \(100 A^{4}\).
These fixed factors are smaller than (4). For a contracted chord
\(\theta C + ( R - C )\), \(0 < \theta \le 1\), use (5) at endpoints  \(\theta x\),
\(\theta y\) whenever both exceed \(h_{\mathrm{ord}}\). Its speed is

\[
 c_\theta=\theta c+(1-\theta)nw/P,                            \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

which lies in \([ 1 / ( 2 A ) , 2 A^{2} ]\); replacing A by \(2 A^{2}\) in (1)
is an explicit compact-input enlargement. The factor changes by
at most \(\theta^{- 2}\). The estimate (5) is an ordinary probability estimate for this
one-channel clock.

The powers in (4) are chosen to fit the existing bounds for the fixed length threshold:
physical and asymmetry constants can be bounded by \(A = M_{1}\),
probability constants by \(M = M_{2}\), after harmless enlargement of
A in (1). Every threshold in (4) is smaller than \(h_{W}\), and \(K_{\mathrm{ord}}\)
is smaller than \(K_{\mathrm{REG}}\). These choices precede the final geometry reserve \(h\).

\subsubsection{Elementary drifted one-end upper bound}

Let \(E_{j}\) be independent mean-one exponentials and consider the
rank walk

\[
 Z_j=h+\epsilon\sum_{l\le j}(w-c\tau E_l),\qquad
 \delta=\epsilon(w-c\tau).
\]

Its variance per step lies in \([ A^{- 4} , A^{4} ]\). Both exit overshoots
from any interval have conditional first moment at most \(A^{2}\)
and second moment at most \(2 A^{4}\): on the unbounded side this is
memorylessness, and the other side is bounded by \(w\). Put

\[
 q=10A^4,\quad
 u=\min\left\{\frac{\sqrt n}{100A^6},
                        \frac1{100A^6|\delta|}\right\},     \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

where the second entry is infinity when \(\delta\) is zero. For \(h < u\)
stop at the first exit from \(( 0 , u )\) and use
\(V ( z ) = ( z + q ) ( u + q - z )\). While inside,

\[
 E[V(Z_{j+1})-V(Z_j)\mid Z_j=z]
  =(u-2z)\delta-E(Z_{j+1}-Z_j)^2
  \le-A^{-4}/2.                                           \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

At exit the negative contribution to \(V\) has expectation at most
\(3 A^{2} ( u + 3 q )\). If \(u \ge 10 q\), truncation of (9), followed by the
overshoot bounds, gives

\[
 E\tau\le 20A^4(h+q)u,
 \qquad P(Z_\tau\ge u)\le3(h+q)/u.                         \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

For the probability bound use
\(\mathbb{E} Z_{\tau} = h + \delta \mathbb{E} \tau\) and lower overshoot mean at most \(A^{2}\);
\(20 A^{4} | \delta | u \le 1 / 5\) absorbs the drift term. If \(u < 10 q\),
the trivial probability bound already has the claimed form.
The event of survival to \(n\) is contained in upper exit or \(\tau > n\).
Markov's inequality and (8)--(10) prove

\[
 P(\min_{j\le n} Z_j\ge0)
 \le 1000A^{10}\min\{1,(h+q)(n^{-1/2}+|\delta|)\}.          \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

The same bound with a larger factor \(10 A^{2}\) handles the physical
pre/post-jump convention. In particular, when
\(| \delta | \sqrt{n} \le M\) it is bounded by
\(M^{100} \min ( 1 , ( 1 + h ) / \sqrt{1 + n} )\). The stopped-potential argument thus gives an explicit upper bound
directly from the overshoot moments.

For a Gaussian rank walk with increment mean $\delta$ and
standard deviation $\sigma$, the normal Mills-ratio inequality
bounds either exit overshoot by $|\delta|+\sigma$ in first moment
and $2\delta^2+2\sigma^2$ in second moment. Here
$|\delta|,\sigma\le A^2$, so the bounds are $2A^2$ and $4A^4$.
The same potential argument, with its intermediate constants
enlarged by a factor at most four, remains within the prefactor
$1000A^{10}$ in (11).

\subsubsection{Flat preparation and relative coupling failures, with one channel}

The following is the ordinary specialization of the proof of
the flat-preparation argument in Section~\ref{supp:explicit-relative-bad-construction}, rather than a specialization
of its binary statement. Delete the Bernoulli coordinate, its
central count constraint, and its favorable-count event. All
remaining events are in the exponential channel. Use the internal
compact parameter \(M ' = M^{10}\). Its variance, mean, speed and
bounded scaled drift cover \([ A^{- 1} , A ]\) and
\(| \delta | \sqrt{n} \le M\). The numerical exit, deterministic preparation,
Gamma-total and exact-total tube calculations in that section are
then unchanged, or improved by deleting a constraint. The middle-tube
proof in Section~\ref{supp:explicit-middle-continuation} needs only its
Gamma formulas (2)--(3), spacing formula (5), and physical identity (6); its binary factor can
be deleted. One may retain the original smaller \(c_{\mathrm{mid}}\).

For completeness, a short favorable gap event is explicit. For
positive jumps choose \(E \le w / ( 2 c \tau )\); it has probability at least
\(A^{- 3} / 4\) and positive increment at least \(w / 2\). For the opposite
orientation retain \(E\) in a unit interval starting beyond
\(2 w / ( c \tau ) + 1\); its probability is at least \(\exp ( - 10 A^{4} )\) and
its positive increment is at least \(A^{- 2}\). The fixed-time
preparation uses at most \(2 \exp ( ( M ' )^{40} ) ( M ' )^{30} + 1\) tubes,
exactly as in that proof. The actual smaller saturation-tube
fraction is \(( 100 ( M ' )^{10} \sqrt{\exp ( ( M ' )^{40} )} )^{- 1}\); its
\(J\), \(N_{0}\) and inverse probability logarithm are bounded there by
\(\exp ( ( M ' )^{41} )\), \(\exp ( ( M ' )^{42} )\), \(\exp ( ( M ' )^{43} )\).
All these costs are smaller than

\[
 C_{\rm flat}=e^{e^{M^{2100}}}.                              \tag{\papertagprefix.12}
\]

Combining this explicit preparation lower with (11), for
\(h \ge M^{1000}\) and both orientations, gives

\[
 C_{\rm flat}^{-1}\min(1,(1+h)/\sqrt{1+n})
 \le F_n(h)\le C_{\rm flat}\min(1,(1+h)/\sqrt{1+n}).         \tag{\papertagprefix.13}
\]

The preparation includes saturation for the reserve \(h\) and gives
the linear reserve comparison by the same deterministic concatenation.
All preparation events belong to the exponential channel, as required
for deterministic marks.

An even simpler bad-event calculation is now available. If \(D\)
reads a prefix of \(b\) original gaps, including its coupling auxiliaries,
drop prefix survival and apply (11) to the remaining independent
walk. Prefix positive increments have second moment at most
\(M^{100} ( 1 + b )^{2}\). Cauchy--Schwarz, (13) and one time comparison
therefore give

\[
 P(\text{flat survival},D)
 \le C_{\rm bad}(1+b)^2 P(D)^{1/2}F_n(h),
 \qquad C_{\rm bad}=e^{e^{M^{2200}}},\quad b\le n/2.          \tag{\papertagprefix.14}
\]

For an event whose entire coupling blocks start after \(n/4\), retain
only the necessary prefix of length \(\lfloor n / 16 \rfloor\). Its \emph{whole
product \(\sigma\) field}, auxiliaries included, is disjoint from \(D\).
Equations (11)--(13) give instead \(C_{\mathrm{bad}} \mathbb{P}( D ) F_{n} ( h )\).
For \(n < 16 L_{0}\) use the early estimate; the first finite block is
covered by \(h_{\mathrm{pre}} > 100 M^{2} L_{0}^{2}\). This is the same separation
adjustment already checked for the binary construction. The Gaussian walk
has the same proof, with its normal second moment and overshoot
bounds. The constants use the explicit flat brackets and the original
gap-tail estimates.

\subsubsection{The one-channel Gaussian estimates and strong one-end boxes}

For one stationary standard OU process of covariance
\(\exp ( - | s - t | / 2 )\), reflection gives exactly

\[
 F_1(t)=P(Z_s\ge0,0\le s\le t)
       =\pi^{-1}\arcsin(e^{-t/2}),
 \qquad \pi^{-1}e^{-t/2}\le F_1(t)\le\tfrac12e^{-t/2}.       \tag{\papertagprefix.15}
\]

At any time \(s\) under this survival tilt its density is

\[
 \frac{\phi(z)p_s(z)p_{t-s}(z)}{F_1(t)},\quad z\ge0,
 \qquad p_v(z)=2\Phi(z/\sqrt{e^v-1})-1,
\]

with \(p_{0} = 1\). Splitting according as both durations exceed one
and using \(p_{v} ( z ) \le \min ( 1 , \sqrt{2 / \pi} z / \sqrt{e^{v} - 1} )\) gives the
uniform majorant \(10 ( 1 + z )^{2} \phi ( z )\). Direct Gaussian integration
therefore gives

\[
 E_{\rm survive}e^{Z_s^2/8}\le256,
 \quad E_{\rm survive}e^{(Z_0^2+Z_t^2)/16}\le256.            \tag{\papertagprefix.16}
\]

Delete endpoints outside \([ 0 , B ]\), \(B = 2^{20}\). The deleted mass
is at most \(512 \exp ( - B^{2} / 16 ) F_{1} ( t ) < F_{1} ( t ) / 4\). Translate by
\(4 B ( e^{- s / 2} + e^{- ( t - s ) / 2} )\). This is a sum of covariance
representers; its norm squared is at most \(64 B^{2}\) and its linear
functional has magnitude at most \(8 B^{2}\) on the retained box.
Hence both endpoints can be confined to \([ 4 B , 9 B ]\) with mass at
least \(e^{- 100 B^{2}} F_{1} ( t ) / 2\).

For a twice differentiable wall shift \(h\) define A(\(h\)),\(V(h)\) exactly
as in the bounded-action wall argument in Section~\ref{supp:explicit-ou-construction}. Equation (16), normalized-variation
Jensen and \(u | z | \le z^{2} / 8 + 2 u^{2}\) yield, directly for this single law,

\[
 e^{-8V(h)-A(h)/2}F_1(t)
 \le P(Z+h\ge0)\le256e^{2V(h)^2}F_1(t).                   \tag{\papertagprefix.17}
\]

For \(d\) decaying exponentials with exponents in \([ 1 / 3 , 1 / 2 ]\) and
total absolute amplitude \(W\), \(A ( h ) \le 12 W^{2}\), \(V ( h ) \le 16 W\).
Reserve, bounded scaled drift and the \(\gamma = 1 / 8\) physical power
wall are just these terms under Brownian Lamperti time. This
proves the one-channel Brownian one-end factor
\(\min ( 1 , ( 1 + h ) / \sqrt{1 + n} )\), with compatible positive end boxes,
with comparison loss at most \(\exp ( M^{1000} )\). The initial
Brownian tube of duration of order \(h^{2}\) is the explicit fixed
increment/bridge tube from the scalar estimates; if \(h\) is already a
fixed fraction of \(\sqrt{n}\), use that same tube for saturation.
For compact variance and drift bounds, all normalized endpoint
boxes have endpoints below \(M^{100}\) and positive inner endpoint
at least \(M^{- 100}\). For an effective asymmetric prefix with
\(| \delta | \sqrt{m} \le 1\) and initial cap \(A^{20} \sqrt{m}\), these bounds
can instead be taken \([ A^{- 100} , A^{100} ]\); the strong wall's
normalized amplitude is below one once \(m\) exceeds \(h_{\mathrm{pre}}^{2}\).
The large \(M\) controls the coupling cutoff, not these latter
physical box coefficients.

The conversion to a physical curve is also literal. Use half the
initial reserve for the rank comparison and rank-wall amplitude
\(10 A^{4} ( 1 + j )^{1 / 8}\). In the positive-jump orientation flat survival
implies \(t \le ( h + Aj ) / c \le Ah + A^{2} j\) before the jth jump. Hence
\(g t^{1 / 8} \le g ( Ah )^{1 / 8} + g ( A^{2} j )^{1 / 8}\); its first term is
less than \(h/4\) and its second is paid by the rank wall. In the
opposite orientation the same argument applies when
\(t \le Ah + 2 A^{2} j\). Beyond that value \(ct - wj \ge ct / 2\), which pays
\(g t^{1 / 8}\) once \(t\) exceeds \(( 2 g / c )^{8 / 7}\); the half reserve
pays the remaining fixed interval. Pre-jump/post-jump differences
are at most \(w\), already included in \(h_{\mathrm{pre}}\). These two time ranges verify that the rank-wall event enforces the
stated physical curve in either orientation.

Use the exponential coupling (5) of Section~\ref{supp:explicit-rank-coupling},
without its Bernoulli part, independently on dyadic blocks. Take
coupling tail power 200. The accumulated good-event error is at
most \(10^{8} M^{2} \log ( 2 + s )^{4}\); include continuous interpolation.
Its Lamperti amplitude and action are below \(M^{100}\) after the
cutoff \(L_{0}\). Indeed \(\log ( 2 + s )^{4} / s^{3 / 8}\) is decreasing for
\(\log s \ge 100\), and substitution of (4) gives this bound at \(L_{0}\).
The good-event wall can be inserted in (17).

For early bad blocks, (14) bounds the loss by a constant times
\(C_{\mathrm{bad}} L_{0}^{- 90}\); for late blocks use whole-block separation.
The geometric series is less than \(\exp ( - \exp ( M^{2250} ) )\),
which is smaller than the Brownian strong-box retention and
all flat comparison costs above. The initial block's exponential
tail is even smaller, because \(h_{\mathrm{pre}}\) exceeds \(100 M^{2} L_{0}^{2}\).
Thus, for \(h \ge h_{\mathrm{pre}}\) and \(n \ge h_{\mathrm{pre}}^{2}\), the one-ended
exponential risk has the strong curve, a central total and the
compatible capped-reserve positive end box defined below,
with probability between

\[
 e^{-e^{M^{2500}}}\min(1,(1+h)/\sqrt{1+n})
 \quad\hbox{and}\quad
 e^{e^{M^{2500}}}\min(1,(1+h)/\sqrt{1+n}).                 \tag{\papertagprefix.18}
\]

The upper follows already from (11). REG is deleted relatively
by (14) and the Gamma Chernoff bound. After reducing its slope
by \(100 A^{10}\), this bound has coefficient at least \(M^{- 12}\).
The elementary grid-pair series of polynomial degree at most ten
is bounded by \(\exp ( - K / ( 10^{6} M^{20} ) )\) once
\(K > \exp ( M^{100} )\); use the change of variable \(u = t^{1 / 16}\)
in its two integrals. With \(K_{\mathrm{ord}}\) this is smaller than half the
retained lower in (18). Crossing long intervals are paid by
their length tail; late short intervals use the whole-block
separation. Inversion of rank-gap REG gives physical REG;
its factors \(100 A^{10}\) and the two unit boundary adjustments
are paid by (4).

\emph{Endpoint boxes with a large common reserve.} In (18), the
auxiliary box is imposed on a capped-height surrogate, whose centered
fluctuation is the original one. Retain the original
gap mean, drift and centered fluctuation \(S_{j}\), and replace only the
initial height by
\(h_{\mathrm{cap}} = \min ( h , M^{20} \sqrt{n} )\). The lower event reads
\(h_{\mathrm{cap}} + S_{j}\), with its ending height in
\([ M^{- 100} \sqrt{n} , M^{100} \sqrt{n} ]\). Its actual ending height is
\(h - h_{\mathrm{cap}} + H_{\mathrm{cap}}\); the actual risk is the capped risk plus the
same constant \(h - h_{\mathrm{cap}}\) at every physical time. The retained
Gamma-total window is central because
\(H_{\mathrm{cap}} - h_{\mathrm{cap}} - \delta n = O ( M^{100} \sqrt{n} )\), independent of that
large common reserve. Thus when \(h\) is large, the actual endpoint adds the uncapped common
reserve to this auxiliary box and can be arbitrarily larger than
\(\sqrt{n}\).
Since \(n \ge h_{\mathrm{pre}}^{2}\), \(h_{\mathrm{cap}}\) is still at least \(h_{\mathrm{pre}}\). Shorter
experiments are handled by the final reserve/whole-chord branches
of the exact central and asymmetric bridge constructions below and do not need this auxiliary box assertion.
For the asymmetric prefix use the physical cap \(A^{20} \sqrt{m}\)
and its physical box \([ A^{- 100} , A^{100} ] \sqrt{m}\).

\subsubsection{Exact central bridge: one joint density and one middle tube}

Put \(K_{\mathrm{asym}} = \exp ( A^{700} )\); it is smaller than \(M\) by (1).
First suppose \(x , y \le K_{\mathrm{asym}} \sqrt{n}\). The reference independent
exponential gap mean is \(\tau\), and its signed drift satisfies
\(| \delta | \sqrt{n} \le 2 A^{2} K_{\mathrm{asym}} < M\). If both endpoints exceed \(\sqrt{n}\),
replace the chord by the smaller constant chord \(\sqrt{n}\) and the
speed by \(nw / P\); its event implies the original event by (3).
Otherwise take disjoint outer rank segments with at most \(n/4\)
marks each. At the left and reversed right use (18), its strong
curve and positive endpoint box. Their ordinary probabilities
multiply, because their entire reference gap sets are disjoint.
The pre/post-mark bounded adjustments are paid by \(h_{\mathrm{pre}}\).

There is one exact-clock density for both outer segments:

\[
 \frac{f_{n+1-m_L-m_R,\tau}(P-T_L-T_R)}
      {f_{n+1,\tau}(P)}.                                  \tag{\papertagprefix.19}
\]

Stirling gives its all-support upper at most 100, and its lower
on the retained central outer totals at least \(\exp ( - M^{300} )\);
with wider boxes the exponent can be bounded by \(M^{1000}\).
The joint density retains the common residual total of both
exposed ends. If an outer box is saturated, truncate its initial reserve
to a fixed multiple of \(\sqrt{n}\) for the lower; the omitted common
height can only help the actual chord.

At each retained pair of outer paths, the unread middle has an
exact-total spacing law. Its legal endpoints are at least
\(M^{- 100} \sqrt{n}\). Delete the subset coordinate in the proved
Section~\ref{supp:explicit-middle-continuation} tube and apply its displayed
\(J , \delta , N_{0} , c_{\mathrm{mid}}\) with enlarged coefficient compact bound
\(M^{100}\) and fraction \(M^{- 100}\). The loss has logarithm
less than \(M^{2000}\), and its length threshold is below
\(N_{\mathrm{core}}\). Its chord identity is (3), so huge outer common reserves
do not change its fluctuation coefficient. Since the remaining
horizon is a fixed fraction of \(n\), the same tube pays the global
power curve for \(n \ge N_{\mathrm{core}}\); join its REG with the outer REG after
reserving a fixed fraction of the slope. The long crossing pairs
are deleted by their unconditional exact Binomial/Gamma tail,
whose exponent dominates the reciprocal polynomial ballot factor.
Thus (19) and the middle continuation give (5) in the central
range with loss much smaller than \(C_{\mathrm{ord}}\).

For the upper, use (11) on both reference ends and the all-support
upper in (19). Their product is at most a fixed multiple of \(\beta\).
This gives the central flat upper with an explicit constant from
the one-end potential estimate and the joint Gamma density.

\subsubsection{All reserves: explicit asymmetric constants}

Reverse the whole exact clock when necessary. Outside the central
box it suffices to handle \(x < \sqrt{n}\), \(y > K_{\mathrm{asym}} \sqrt{n}\).
The reference signed drift is positive and satisfies exactly

\[
 \delta=\frac{y-x+\epsilon c\tau}{n}.
\]

Take \(m = \lfloor A^{- 100} \delta^{- 2} \rfloor\),
\(x ' = \min ( x , A^{20} \sqrt{m} )\) and \(y ' = y - x + x '\). Increasing \(K_{\mathrm{asym}}\)
ensures \(m \le n / ( 16 A^{2} )\); the remaining reference clock mean
stays in \([ 1 / ( 2 A ) , 2 A ]\). Above the fixed threshold
\(m_{*} = h_{\mathrm{pre}}^{8} M^{1000}\), (18) gives a retained prefix of
probability at least \(\exp ( - \exp ( M^{2500} ) )\) times

\[
 \min(1,(1+x')/\sqrt m)\asymp_A\beta_n(x,y),
\]

with central total and capped ending height
\(H \in [ A^{- 100} \sqrt{m} , A^{100} \sqrt{m} ]\). The original
risk and endpoint have the additional common shift \(x-x\prime\). Its density in the full
exact clock is the ratio
\(f_{n + 1 - m , \tau} ( P - T_{m} ) / f_{n + 1 , \tau} ( P )\), with uniform central lower.
For each retained prefix the remaining physical drift \(v '\) obeys

\[
 \delta/(4A^2)\le v'\le4A^2\delta,
 \quad Hv'\ge A^{-200},
 \quad P'(v')^2\ge16\exp(A^{600}).                         \tag{\papertagprefix.20}
\]

These follow by inserting the retained \(O_{A} ( \sqrt{m} )\) endpoint and
duration errors: \(\sqrt{m} \delta \ge A^{- 51}\), whereas
\(n \delta^{2} \ge K_{\mathrm{asym}}^{2} / ( 4 A^{4} )\). Thus every error is at most
\(A^{200} / K_{\mathrm{asym}}^{2}\) of the main increment. The estimates hold separately for every retained prefix path and
its actual duration and endpoint.

Here are numerical constants for the residual exact continuation:

\[
 \kappa=A^{-20}e^{-A},\quad a=A^{-250},\quad
 K_c=4A^{200}e^A,\quad R_c=e^{A^{600}}.                    \tag{\papertagprefix.21}
\]

A rate-\(\lambda\) Poisson clock, \(\lambda = n ' / P ' \in [ 1 / ( 2 A ) , 2 A ]\),
with deterministic jump \(w\) has compensator at \(\theta \le 1/A\)
bounded above by \(- v \theta + 2 A^{4} e^{A} \theta^{2}\). At
\(\theta = \kappa v\) it is at most \(- v \theta / 2\). Optional stopping
from entrance \(a/v\) therefore gives first-half survival probability
\(p_{a} = 1 - \exp ( - \kappa a ) \ge \kappa a / 2\). Retain its count within
\(K_{c} \sqrt{n'}\) of its mean; Chebyshev removes at most \(p_{a}/2\).
The exact first-half density relative to that Poisson clock is
at most 25 everywhere and at least
\(( 1 / 16 ) \exp ( - 4 - 8 K_{c}^{2} )\) on this count event, whenever
\(n ' \ge 16 K_{c}^{2}\). The resulting first-half lower is

\[
 b_L\ge(p_a/32)e^{-4-8K_c^2}.
\]

On the reversed late half, failure of the positive drift path
requires a centered count fluctuation at least vP'/2. The same
exponential maximal inequality and density upper give
\(25 \exp ( - \kappa P ' v^{2} / 4 )\). Since

\[
 (4/\kappa)\log(50/b_L)
 \le 1000A^{420}e^{3A}<R_c,
\]

and \(R_{c} / ( 100 A^{6} ) > 16 K_{c}^{2}\), (21) guarantees continuation
probability at least \(b_{L}/2\). This is the one-channel Poisson comparison for the constant mark
law.
Apply it to the half-chord process
\(Q ( s ) = R_{\mathrm{rem}} ( s ) - ( H + v ' s ) / 2\), whose entrance is \(H/2\), drift is
\(v = v ' / 2\), and speed is \(( c + n ' w / P ' ) / 2\). Its reversed entrance
is \(( H + v ' P ' ) / 2\) and its reversed drift is \(- v ' / 2\). Consequently
late-half failure means

\[
 \epsilon M_{\rm rev}(u)>H/2+v'(P'-u)/2\ge v'P'/4,
       \qquad0\le u\le P'/2.
\]

The maximal bound is therefore
\(25 \exp ( - \kappa P ' ( v ' )^{2} / 16 )\), exactly the bound above with
\(v = v ' / 2\). Equation (20) has the extra factor 16, so no margin
is lost by this factor-four change. Moreover the entrance/drift
product is \(Hv ' / 4 \ge A^{- 200} / 4 \ge a\) in (21). Its event is the
half-chord bound

\[
 R_{\rm rem}(s)\ge(H+v's)/2
               \ge A^{-210}\sqrt m(1+s/m).                \tag{\papertagprefix.22}
\]

The global power curve is at most
\(A^{2} m^{1 / 8} ( 1 + s / m )^{1 / 8}\) because \(T_{m} \le 2 A m\).
Already \(m \ge m_{*}\) makes (22) dominate it. Unconditional ordinary
REG failure is less than \(b_{L}/4\) at \(K_{\mathrm{ord}}\). Rate discrepancies
at the junction are \(O_{A} ( m^{- 1 / 2} )\) and \(O_{A} ( \sqrt{m} / n )\), smaller
than the reserved slope above \(m_{*}\). Thus each retained prefix
has the required completion with this fixed lower, and integration
in its single exact-prefix density proves the asymmetric lower.
The logarithm of every continuation inverse loss above is below
\(\exp ( A^{700} ) < M\); it fits (4) with a large margin.

If \(m < m_{*}\), use the whole half-chord construction with the final
reserve \(h_{\mathrm{ord}}\). The positive physical drift is at least
\(v_{0} = 1 / ( 10 A^{102} \sqrt{m_{*} + 1} )\). This bound and \(m_{*}\) are fixed
before \(h_{\mathrm{ord}}\). The elementary maximum

\[
 \sup_{t\ge0}\{g t^{1/8}-v_0t/4\}
 \le 2A^2 v_0^{-1/7}
\]

is smaller than \(h_{\mathrm{ord}}/4\), and \(h_{\mathrm{ord}} v_{0} / 4 > 1\).
The first-half lower therefore follows from (21), even more
strongly with the larger entrance. If \(Pv_{0}^{2} < R_{c}\), the horizon
is at most \(R_{c} / v_{0}^{2} < N_{\mathrm{core}}\); on that bounded range the final
reserve is larger than \(100 A^{2} ( P + n + 1 )\) and the strong event is
automatic. \(K_{\mathrm{ord}}\) makes REG automatic there as well. This treatment
does not feed the larger output reserve back into \(m_{*}\).

The asymmetric upper uses only (11) and the all-support exact
prefix density upper. Since \(\delta \le 4 A^{2} y / n\) and \(y\ge\sqrt{n}\),
it is at most \(C_{A} \min ( 1 , ( 1 + x ) y / n ) \le C_{A} \beta\). This completes
all-reserve upper without an asymptotic ballot constant.

Finally, on \(n < N_{\mathrm{core}}\) with legal \(x , y \ge h_{\mathrm{ord}}\), the full path is
at least \(\min ( x , y ) - An\), whereas its curve is at most
\(A [ A ( n + 1 ) ]^{1 / 8}\). The chosen \(h_{\mathrm{ord}}\) makes this deterministic
strong inequality hold. Every count displacement is at most
\(2 n + A^{2} \sqrt{n}\), below \(K_{\mathrm{ord}}\), so REG is automatic. The whole bounded-horizon range is therefore covered deterministically
at these final reserve and intercept thresholds, within
\(C_{\mathrm{ord}}\).

\subsubsection{Application to the terminal suffix and fixed lift}

Equations (2)--(22) establish an effective ordinary strong/REG
bracket with its exact clock and signed endpoint identity. Uniform
fine-name refinement at a fixed complete type is then the same
pointwise hypergeometric calculation as in the history estimates: the path reads no fine
name, so the refinement retains a fixed fraction before averaging
this ordinary path. Broad banks are retained by their exponentially
small conditional failure relative to \(\beta \ge c / ( 1 + n )\). These add
at most \(\exp ( M^{2000} )\) to the inverse-loss logarithm and are
covered by \(C_{\mathrm{ord}}\). The ordinary source is linear in its one
reservoir count atom; this construction changes only its conditional path
bracket and does not introduce a second root atom.

Specifically, after the accepted terminal prefix is frozen, the arithmetic construction
reads the remaining suffix count and its conditional
uniform clock. On a weak ordinary original block the imposed local
event is \(\theta C_{\mathrm{actual}} ( t ) + E_{\mathrm{actual}} ( t ) \ge g d_{P} ( t )^{1 / 8}\), together
with uncolored regularity, original fine-name REG, and the broad-bank
conditions when designated. The actual endpoint pair is
\(\theta x_{\mathrm{actual}} , \theta y_{\mathrm{actual}}\), with its exact signed increment;
the suffix/root count is unchanged. Apply (5)--(7) to that pair.
The Gaussian and Gamma end boxes in (18)--(19) are auxiliary
proof events on the independent reference end segments. They are
not additional upper restrictions on the actual source suffix
endpoint or on its prescribed root count. If both legal endpoints
exceed \(\sqrt{n}\), the whole constant-chord surrogate in the exact central bridge construction has the
same centered fluctuation and lies below the actual chord. If an
asymmetric initial endpoint is capped, both legal endpoints are
shifted by its one common constant, leaving the increment and
clock law unchanged. At each retained prefix the actual middle
pair is still legal and positive; no already sampled terminal
label or accepted prefix path is changed. Complete-cell lower
events follow from this continuous event; the reverse comparison
adds only \(c \Delta_{*} + g \Delta_{*}^{1 / 8}\) to reserves as in
Section~\ref{supp:dyadic-lift-evaluator}, paid by \(h_{\mathrm{ord}}\).

For the specified fixed lift, take the already fixed physical
compact bound \(A = 2 M_{1}^{2}\) and \(M = M_{2}\). Requirement (1) follows
from \(( 2 M_{1}^{2} )^{1000} < M_{1}^{100000}\). Every threshold in (4), and the
continuation inequalities (20)--(22) are then dominated by the
existing \(K_{\mathrm{REG}} = e^{e^{M_{2}^{5000}}}\) and
\(h_{W} = e^{e^{M_{2}^{5500}}}\). The actual contracted endpoints
exceed \(h_{\mathrm{ord}}\) because \(\theta M_{0}^{- 20} h > h_{\mathrm{ord}}\) for the existing
\(\theta = M_{1}^{- M_{1}}\) and \(h = e^{e^{M_{2}^{6000}}}\).
Hence the ordinary case \(\rho = 1\) uses the same \(\Lambda_k\), scalar
compact parameter, or the \(h\)-independent weak selection.

The ordinary bridge estimate and its application to the actual
terminal suffix therefore fit the same fixed lift as the binary
construction.


\section{Count types and the selected measure}\label{appendix:counts}
This appendix constructs the bounded word weight used in the lower
bound and proves its first-mass estimate. Count admission and spatial
acceptance play different roles: counts may couple every block, whereas
at a fixed complete type the clocks and uniform multiset words remain
independent. We exploit this distinction before introducing the adaptive
targets by recoloring.

The construction has four stages. Partial-revelation and free-interval
estimates produce one uncolored dominating cost for each selected
block. A mixed-moment identity combines these costs over the whole
count source. An ordinary suffix supplies one root atom and its path
factor. Finally, a bounded-density transport realizes the targets,
and an exact likelihood calculation evaluates the nominal first mass.
The complete-cell construction and finite disintegration at the end
verify that these stages retain their stated conditioning.

\subsection{The joint lower measure and its transport}
\label{app:lower-details}

This appendix supplies the probability and measure constructions used in
Section~\ref{lower:chapter}.  We keep the original physical blocks
throughout.  Conditional on its uncolored total \(n_i\), a block has
\(n_i\) uniform points on its interval and all \(n_i+1\) spacings.
Its fine labels have their original categorical law.  Conditional on
a complete named count vector, they are a uniform multiset permutation.
Constants in this appendix depend on the fixed dimension and the fixed
compact scalar, count, and wall parameters.

\subsubsection{Revealing part of an original word}

A comparison class reveals some labels but leaves the rest under
their original law. The cost of retaining a central count band is
then a ratio of multinomial atoms. Summing this ratio over the whole
coupled count weight, rather than choosing one type, gives a bound
that charges only the blocks and strips actually revealed.

\begin{lemma}[Central counts after partial revelation]
\label{ld:reveal}
In block \(i\), let \(N_i\) labels be independent with alphabet size
\(a_i\le H\) and probabilities \(p_{i,c}\ge p_*>0\).  The blocks are
independent under their original law \(\pi\).  Let \(A(K)\ge0\) be
a finite weight on their complete count vectors, supported on
\[
 |K_{i,c}-N_ip_{i,c}|\le B\sqrt{1+N_i},
 \qquad W=\mathbb E_\pi A.
\]
Fix \(m_i\) slots in block \(i\).  For any positive-probability event
\(Q\) measurable in just these slots, including coupled or partial
signatures,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_\pi[A\mid Q]\le CW
 \prod_{i:m_i>0}
 \left(\frac{1+N_i}{1+N_i-m_i}\right)^{(a_i-1)/2}
 \le CW\prod_{i:m_i>0}(1+m_i)^{(a_i-1)/2}.
 \label{ld:reveal-bound}
\end{equation}
If \(m_i\le N_i/2\) in every affected block, the ratio is bounded
by a fixed constant.  A block with no revealed slots incurs no factor.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
For a fixed \(a\)-letter law in this compact simplex, its multinomial
mass \(P_{n,p}(k)\), with \(d=a-1\), satisfies
\begin{equation}
 \sup_kP_{n,p}(k)\le C(1+n)^{-d/2},\qquad
 P_{N,p}(k)\ge c(1+N)^{-d/2}
 \quad\text{on the stated central window}.
 \label{ld:multinomial-atoms}
\end{equation}
For the first bound, Fourier inversion, with the last coordinate set
to zero, bounds a coefficient by the integral of
\(\lvert p_a+\sum_{j\le d}p_je^{it_j}\rvert^n\).  The square of
this modulus is at most
\[
 1-2p_*^2\sum_{j\le d}(1-\cos t_j)
       \le1-c\sum_{j\le d}t_j^2,\qquad |t_j|\le\pi.
\]
Its integral is \(O((1+n)^{-d/2})\).  For the lower bound, Stirling's
inequalities give
\(P_{N,p}(k)\ge cN^{-d/2}\exp\{-ND(k/N\Vert p)\}\) when
\(N\) is large.  The entropy Hessian is bounded on the segment between
\(p\) and \(k/N\), so its exponent is \(O(B^2)\).  Bounded \(N\)
is covered by compactness and feasibility.  The case \(a=1\) is
deterministic.

Expose the specified labels exactly, and let \(b_i\) be their
count vector. Independence under the original law gives the remaining
type mass explicitly:
\[
 \pi(K=k\mid\text{revealed labels})
       =\prod_iP_{N_i-m_i,p_i}(k_i-b_i).
\]
When \(m_i=0\), the factor is exactly its original type mass and
cancels in the ratio. On each affected block,
\eqref{ld:multinomial-atoms} bounds the ratio by the corresponding
factor in \eqref{ld:reveal-bound}. Multiply by \(A(k)\) and sum
the entire coupled type vector. Conditioning on \(Q\) then averages
these uniform bounds over its exact revealed assignments.
The last inequality follows from
\((1+N)/(1+N-m)\le1+m\).  If \(W=0\), all the relevant feasible
type weights vanish, and the conclusion is immediate.
\end{proof}

For a fixed original history and anchor, a signature class is
an event \(Q\) of this kind: it reads only the slots with nontrivial
partitions.  This applies to that fixed class under the original law.
It does not change that law to a law conditioned on an adaptively chosen
history.  In particular, if a class fully exposes blocks in \(I\) and
reads \(m_j\) additional slots elsewhere, its count cost is at most
\[
 C\prod_{i\in I}(1+N_i)^{(a_i-1)/2}
       \prod_{j\notin I}(1+m_j)^{(a_j-1)/2}.
\]
Only counts in actually revealed blocks or strips appear.

\subsubsection{Two free intervals in the original class}

The local path upper bound uses two disjoint intervals just inside
the exposed endpoint strips. At a fixed complete type the remaining
binary labels form one uniform subset, so both intervals must first
be compared jointly with an independent Bernoulli law. Opposite
monotonicities of the forward and reverse walls then give one envelope
uniform over all retained types.

We next bound the path part after the complete type and exposed labels
have been fixed.  Consider one selected block of length \(P\), total
\(n\asymp P\), and binary risk
\[
 R(t)=ct-aN(t)+bN_B(t),\qquad c,b,a-b>0,
\]
with these parameters in fixed compact intervals.  Every accepted word
has an actual endpoint pair satisfying
\begin{equation}
 0\le x\le C_{\rm box}X,\quad 0\le y\le C_{\rm box}Y,
 \quad y-x=cP-an+bk,\quad x+R(t)\ge-h,
 \label{ld:bank-path}
\end{equation}
where \(X,Y\ge h_*>0\).  All additional walls and refinements can
remain in the acceptance.  Assume the uncolored endpoint bound
\begin{equation}
 N([0,t])+N([P-t,P])\le C_{\rm occ}(1+t),
       \qquad 0\le t\le P/2.
 \label{ld:endpoint-occupancy}
\end{equation}
The original class may read prescribed slots in endpoint strips of
width \(C_s(1+d)\), but is unrestricted between them.  This last
condition is a statement about its signatures.

Put
\begin{equation}
 \mathcal T=\frac{(1+X)(1+Y)}n,\qquad
 p_0=\frac{a-cP/n}{b},\qquad
 \rho_0=\frac{(cP/(n+1))^2}
 {(cP/(n+1))^2+b^2p_0(1-p_0)}.
 \label{ld:bank-parameters}
\end{equation}
On the rare branch \(\mathcal T<t_0\), the accepted interior type
and \eqref{ld:bank-path} imply that \(p_0\) belongs to a fixed compact
subinterval of \((0,1)\).  Define
\(\Psi=\mathcal T^{2\chi(\eta,\rho_0)}\) on this branch and
\(\Psi=1\) otherwise, where \(\eta\) lies in a fixed compact
subinterval of \((0,1)\).

Fix \(0<\gamma<1/2\) and
\[
 D_n=[C_{\rm cut}\log(2+n)]^{1/\gamma}.
\]
Set \(q_d=1\) if the branch is saturated, if \(n<n_0\), or if
\(d>D_n\).  Here \(n_0\) is chosen so that, in the remaining cases,
the endpoint strips contain at most a fixed small fraction of \(n\)
slots and the following two intervals fit in the free middle.  Choose
their starting and ending boundaries \(s_d,t_d\) just inside those
strips.  Write
\begin{equation}
 U_d=1+X+d,\quad V_d=1+Y+d,\quad M_d=\max(U_d,V_d),\quad
 L_d=\varepsilon_0\min\{P,(n/M_d)^2\}.
 \label{ld:bank-length}
\end{equation}
Take intervals \([s_d,s_d+L_d]\), \([t_d-L_d,t_d]\).
The constant \(\varepsilon_0\) is small enough that they are disjoint
and their combined occupancy is at most half the unread slots, by
\eqref{ld:endpoint-occupancy}.  Grid rounding changes only fixed
allowances.  If the resulting length is below a fixed scalar threshold,
again set \(q_d=1\).

In the remaining case set
\[
 p_\pm=p_0\pm C_1(X+Y+1+d)/n.
\]
Reduce \(t_0\) and increase \(n_0\) to keep these probabilities
uniformly interior.  Let \(q_L\) be the iid Bernoulli \(p_+\)
probability on the actual slots of the left interval that
\[
 cv-aN([s_d,s_d+v])+bN_B([s_d,s_d+v])\ge-C_2U_d,
       \qquad 0\le v\le L_d.
\]
Let \(q_R\) be the iid Bernoulli \(p_-\) probability on the right
interval, read backwards, that
\[
 -cv+aN([t_d-v,t_d])-bN_B([t_d-v,t_d])\ge-C_2V_d.
\]
Define \(q_d=\mathbf1_{\eqref{ld:endpoint-occupancy}}q_Lq_R\).
These iid probabilities are upper bounds for the original conditional
law, not the law of the accepted word.

To prove this, fix all revealed labels and a complete named type.
If \(m\) slots and \(e\) binary successes have been revealed, the
remaining binary word is a uniform \((k-e)\)-subset of \(N=n-m\)
slots.  Its fraction \(p'=(k-e)/(n-m)\) satisfies
\[
 |k-np_0|\le C(X+Y),\qquad
 |p'-p_0|\le C(X+Y+1+d)/n,
\]
so \(p_-\le p'\le p_+\).  Let \(M_J\le N/2\) be the combined
number of slots in both free intervals.  Relative to iid Bernoulli
\(p'\), their joint density under the exact subset law is
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(N-M_J,p')=Np'-j\}}
 {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(N,p')=Np'\}}\le C.
 \label{ld:joint-subset-density}
\end{equation}
The numerator is bounded by a maximum atom and the denominator is a
central atom.  This is one comparison for both intervals and holds
for every assignment on them.  The endpoint identity and occupancy
bound show that \eqref{ld:bank-path} requires both displayed tests,
with the stated allowances.  Under the iid law the intervals are
independent.  The left event increases and the right event decreases
with binary successes, so coordinatewise uniform coupling gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P\{\text{accepted path}\mid
              \text{complete type, revealed labels}\}\le Cq_d(G).
 \label{ld:type-bank-upper}
\end{equation}
Additional named restrictions within either binary list do not change
this uniform binary-subset marginal.

For several blocks the multiplication is made at a fixed whole type
and fixed exposed labels. Suppose
\(0\le F\le A(K)\) times the necessary path indicators, with
\(A\) supported on the original central windows and
\(W=\mathbb E_\pi A\). Multiply \eqref{ld:type-bank-upper} under
the independent residual block laws, sum the whole type, and then
apply Lemma~\ref{ld:reveal}. This gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_\pi[F\mid Q]\le CW R_{\rm strip}
 \prod_{j\in I}(1+n_j)^{(a_j-1)/2}
 \prod_{\substack{i\notin I\\i\ {\rm selected}}}q_{i,d_i}(G_i),
 \label{ld:class-banks}
\end{equation}
where \(I\) denotes fully exposed blocks and
\[
 R_{\rm strip}=
 \prod_{i\notin I:\,m_i>n_i/2}(1+m_i)^{(a_i-1)/2}.
\]
At active depths, \(m_i\le\varepsilon n_i\), so this extra factor
only concerns the discarded large-depth regime.  Conditioning on a
partial-signature event \(Q\) last averages the uniform bound over
its exact revealed assignments.  There is no factor \(1/\pi(Q)\),
and the type acceptance need not factor across blocks.

\subsubsection{Moments of the free-interval costs}

The preceding envelope is pointwise in the clock. Its fractional
moment is evaluated by a second joint comparison, now between the
exact-total clock and a Poisson clock on the two free intervals.
Summing the envelopes over depths with decaying coefficients produces
a positive uncolored cost that dominates every needed local test and
has the correct persistence moment.

For \(d\le D_n\), the functions just constructed satisfy
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{G\mid n}q_d(G)^\eta\le C(1+d)^C\Psi.
 \label{ld:bank-moment}
\end{equation}
Here and below \(A(K)\) and deterministic parameters must be fixed
before these unread clocks for a clock moment assertion.  The class
bound itself is pointwise after fixing the clocks.

The exact-total uniform clock restricted jointly to the two free
intervals has density, relative to a rate \(n/P\) Poisson clock,
\begin{equation}
 \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Pois}(n(1-\kappa))=n-N_J\}}
 {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Pois}(n)=n\}}\le C,
 \qquad \kappa=2L_d/P<1/2.
 \label{ld:joint-clock-density}
\end{equation}
Conditional point locations also agree.  Only after this single joint
comparison are the two reference restrictions independent.  Drop the
occupancy indicator for the upper bound.  The auxiliary risk drifts
have magnitude \(O((X+Y+1+d)/n)\), whose product with \(\sqrt{L_d}\)
is bounded.  Theorem~\ref{pr:physical-one}, for either sign,
therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E q_d^\eta\le C
 \min\left\{1,\left(\frac{U_d}{\sqrt{1+L_d}}\right)^{2\chi_+}\right\}
 \min\left\{1,\left(\frac{V_d}{\sqrt{1+L_d}}\right)^{2\chi_-}\right\}.
 \label{ld:two-one-ends}
\end{equation}
The one-end theorem is applied to the original positive mark pair in
both orientations, with compact drift changes; all original spacings
were retained before \eqref{ld:joint-clock-density}.

If \(M_d\le\sqrt n\), then \(1+L_d\asymp n\) and the product
of the reserve ratios is \(\asymp U_dV_d/n\).  If
\(M_d>\sqrt n\), then \(1+L_d\asymp(n/M_d)^2\); the larger
reserve factor is bounded by one and the smaller ratio is
\(\asymp U_dV_d/n\).  The exponent changes satisfy
\[
 |\chi_+-\chi(\eta,\rho_0)|+
 |\chi_--\chi(\eta,\rho_0)|
       \le C\{\mathcal T+(1+d)/n\}.
\]
Every nontrivial reserve ratio in \eqref{ld:two-one-ends} is at least
\(c\min(1,\mathcal T)\).  Multiplying its negative logarithm by
the last bound is uniformly bounded, because
\(\mathcal T|\log\mathcal T|\) is bounded and \(d\le D_n\).
Replace both exponents by \(\chi(\eta,\rho_0)\) and use
\(U_dV_d\le(1+d)^2(1+X)(1+Y)\) to prove
\eqref{ld:bank-moment}.  If the free interval was too short for the
one-end theorem, then \(M_d\gg n\), and \(d=o(\sqrt n)\)
forces one of \(X,Y\) to have order \(n\).  Thus \(\mathcal T\)
has a fixed positive lower bound and the convention \(q_d=1\) is
valid.  Bounded \(n<n_0\) is treated in the same upper estimate;
this does not enlarge the support convention of the source lower.

Fix \(b_0>0\) and an integer \(B_0\) large enough to sum the
later pivot multiplicities.  Choose \(D_0\) with
\(D_0\eta_->2\sup\chi+1\), and set
\begin{equation}
 D^{\rm raw}(G)=(2+n)^{-D_0}
       +\sum_{d\ge0}(1+d)^{B_0}e^{-b_0d^\gamma}q_d(G),
 \qquad D(G)=\min(1,D^{\rm raw}(G)).
 \label{ld:cost-envelope}
\end{equation}
Choose \(C_{\rm cut}\) after \(D_0\) so that the \(\eta\)-powers
of the numerical coefficient tail beyond \(D_n\) sum to at most
\(C(2+n)^{-D_0\eta}\), uniformly in \(\eta\).
Subadditivity and \eqref{ld:bank-moment} then give
\begin{equation}
 (2+n)^{-D_0}\le D\le1,\qquad
 \mathbb E D^\eta\le C\Psi.
 \label{ld:cost-moment}
\end{equation}
At depth zero \eqref{ld:type-bank-upper} gives \(q\le CD\) for
each supported complete type.  Clipping at one preserves this bound
because \(q\le1\).

Beyond the active cutoff the convention \(q_d=1\) provides no
small moment. The geometric depth charge pays this regime directly.
When it contains \(cd^\gamma\), enlarge \(C_{\rm cut}\) until
\begin{equation}
 e^{-cd^\gamma/2}(1+n)^{H/2}\le C(2+n)^{-D_0},
       \qquad d>D_n.
 \label{ld:large-depth}
\end{equation}
This pays both the selected bridge floor and any large-strip reveal
ratio in that block, leaving half the penalty to sum pivots.  An
unselected block with \(m>n/2\) instead has
\(n\le2m\le C(1+d)\), so its reveal ratio is a polynomial in
its actual depth.  For active depths use
\(q_d\le CD(1+d)^{-B_0}e^{b_0d^\gamma}\), choosing \(b_0\)
below the available geometric coefficient.  When several blocks
share a depth parameter, divide its fixed penalty among the
dimension-bounded number of factors before choosing these constants.

A related count extraction will sometimes be useful in a completely
free interior interval.  Conditional on every label outside it, a
band of at most \(C(1+R)\) possible counts there has probability at
most \(\min(1,C(1+R)/\sqrt{1+N_I})\), irrespective of its center.
This is the binomial maximum-atom bound in
\eqref{ld:multinomial-atoms}.  The whole band is summed before taking
a power.  If this interval and the two path intervals are disjoint
with total length less than half the original block, the single
density comparison \eqref{ld:joint-clock-density} applies to all
three at once.  The count factor has moment
\(O(\min(1,(1+R)/\sqrt{1+P})^\eta)\); atypically small occupancy
has exponentially small probability.  This explains the ordinary
count-window factor without replacing the original class by three
independently conditioned experiments.

\subsubsection{Named regularity on each retained word}

Binary acceptance leaves two actual lists to be refined into fine
names. Regularity must survive this refinement conditionally on each
retained parent word, however rare that word may be. A uniform
hypergeometric estimate gives this per-word statement before any
fractional moment is averaged.

\begin{lemma}[Uniform named refinement]
\label{ld:named regularity}
Let a fixed parent list of \(n\le C(1+L)\) points in an original
block satisfy, at the fixed grid boundaries,
\begin{equation}
 |N((a,b])-(n/L)(b-a)|\le
 \theta_{\rm in}(b-a)+K_{\rm in}
       \{1+d_L(a)^\zeta+d_L(b)^\zeta\},
 \label{ld:parent-REG}
\end{equation}
where \(0<\zeta<1/2\) and the grid has bounded boundary density.
For every feasible full refinement type \((k_c)\), its original
uniform multiset refinement satisfies, simultaneously in the finitely
many names,
\begin{equation}
 |N_c((a,b])-(k_c/L)(b-a)|\le
 \theta_{\rm out}(b-a)+K_{\rm out}
       \{1+d_L(a)^\zeta+d_L(b)^\zeta\}
 \label{ld:child-REG}
\end{equation}
with conditional probability at least \(1-\varepsilon\).
Here \(\theta_{\rm in}\) is sufficiently small in terms of the
prescribed \(\theta_{\rm out}>0\), and \(K_{\rm out}\) is sufficiently
large in terms of the fixed data and \(\varepsilon\).  The assertion
holds for every fixed parent word, however it was previously selected.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Condition on the parent positions. On an interval containing \(m\)
positions, the name-\(c\) count is hypergeometric with mean
\(\alpha m\), where \(\alpha=k_c/n\). Its exponential moments
are bounded by those of independent Bernoulli sampling: apply the
elementary-symmetric-mean inequality to the \(n\) values \(e^t\)
or \(1\), and use complementation for the lower tail.
Chernoff's argument therefore gives
\[
 \mathbb P\{|N_c-\alpha m|>u\}\le
       2\exp\{-cu^2/(m+u)\}.
\]
The displacement of the mean from \((k_c/L)(b-a)\) is bounded by
\eqref{ld:parent-REG}, and
\(m\le C(b-a)+K_{\rm in}(1+d_L(a)^\zeta+d_L(b)^\zeta)\).
After the stated choices, the probability of violating
\eqref{ld:child-REG} is at most
\[
 C\exp\{-c_1(b-a)-c_2K_{\rm out}
                 (1+d_L(a)^\zeta+d_L(b)^\zeta)\}.
\]
The sum over all grid endpoint pairs is uniformly finite.  Pairs
near an original endpoint are summed by the convergent series
\(\sum_{j\ge0}e^{-cj^\zeta}\); pairs in opposite halves also pay
\(e^{-c_1(b-a)}\).  Increasing \(K_{\rm out}\) makes the finite
union over names and blocks have probability at most
\(\varepsilon\).  Bounded blocks have bounded counts, absorbed
by the fixed intercept; empty lists have their unique empty refinement.
\end{proof}

Apply this lemma to both actual lists of a retained binary word,
conditioning on that word and its complete type.  It supplies named
REG with constant conditional success before any rare bridge is
averaged.  If natural rather than empirical rates are used, a central
type changes the rate by \(O(L^{-1/2})\), absorbed by a spare
linear slope above a fixed length threshold.  The lemma concerns
this per-word refinement only; any later function of the selected
spatial lists remains in its own conditional measure.

\subsubsection{Admission of the macroscopic recoloring intervals}

The later transport needs many occurrences of two specified names
in an interior interval. Its admission failure is exponentially small
in the interval length, whereas the bridge factor has a polynomial
lower bound. We use this separation inside the local fractional moment,
so bank admission retains a fixed proportion even of a rare bridge
mass.

Consider a prescribed original block with \(P,n\asymp T\), complete
central fine type \(|K_c-np_c|\le B\sqrt{1+n}\), and a fixed
interior interval \(I\) of length at least \(\rho P\), a fixed
positive distance from both endpoints.  For two specified actual
fine names \(s,t\), require
\begin{equation}
 m=N(I)\ge c_In,\qquad
 |K_{I,s}-p_sm|+|K_{I,t}-p_tm|
                  \le\frac{m}{\log(2+T)}.
 \label{ld:broad-bank}
\end{equation}
The same requirement may be imposed in finitely many prescribed
intervals.  Conditional on \(n\), the uncolored occupancy failure
has probability \(O(e^{-cn})\).  Conditional on the complete type
and a clock with \(m\ge c_In\), the named occupancy is
hypergeometric, with mean \(mK_c/n\).  Its distance from \(p_cm\)
is \(O(m/\sqrt n)\), which is less than
\(m/(8\log(2+T))\) above a fixed threshold.  The same Chernoff
bound as in Lemma~\ref{ld:named regularity} gives, at each full central type,
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P_{G,\pi}\{\eqref{ld:broad-bank}\text{ fails}\mid K\}
            \le C\exp\{-cT/\log^2(2+T)\}.
 \label{ld:broad-failure}
\end{equation}

Let \(q(K,G)\) already include the allocated curved path, binary REG,
and full named regularity, with
\begin{equation}
 q\le CD,\qquad \mathbb E q^\eta\ge c\Psi,\qquad
 \mathbb E D^\eta\le C\Psi,\qquad
 \Psi\ge c_0(2+n)^{-B_1}.
 \label{ld:local-inputs}
\end{equation}
The all-reserve and contracted-chord bridge theorems
\ref{bridge:all-reserves} and \ref{bridge:contracted}, followed by
Lemma~\ref{ld:named regularity}, supply the lower assertion.  The free-interval
construction supplies the other two assertions.  Let \(q_{\rm good}\)
also impose \eqref{ld:broad-bank}, and put
\(q_{\rm bad}=q-q_{\rm good}\).  Subadditivity, then Jensen, give
\begin{align}
 \mathbb E q_{\rm good}^\eta
 &\ge\mathbb E q^\eta-\mathbb E q_{\rm bad}^\eta\notag\\
 &\ge c\Psi-(\mathbb E q_{\rm bad})^\eta
 \ge c\Psi-C\exp\{-c\eta T/\log^2(2+T)\}
 \ge c'\Psi.
 \label{ld:local-bank-retention}
\end{align}
The final inequality follows after one fixed threshold enlargement,
uniformly in the compact range of \(\eta\), from the polynomial
lower bound.  All walls and REG restrictions were already inside
\(q\), and the dominating cost \(D\) does not change.  The same
argument applies to an unselected regular block with \(D=\Psi=1\).
This local fractional estimate is taken before any later scale or
root probability is integrated.
For large \(T\), \eqref{ld:broad-bank} also guarantees at least
\(cn\) occurrences of each of its two names, enough for every
prescribed \(O(\log T)\) recoloring.

\subsubsection{Mixed moments of the coupled count measure}

The count source is a single measure on complete types. For each
fixed type, H\"older turns the local fractional survival estimate into
a mixed first moment with the dominating cost. Only these mixed
integrands are multiplied across independent clocks; Tonelli then
integrates the coupled type measure. This order retains every plateau's
own exponent.

The count construction in Section~\ref{app:endpoint-details} precedes
the unread positions.  More precisely, the diagonal exit bands and
their endpoint count transports (\ref{paper:ep-diagonal},
\ref{paper:ep-count-box}, and \ref{paper:ep-count-transport}) use
only the nonterminal plateaux.  Projecting out terminal private names and
then filling their prefix lists under the original conditional law
gives the whole prefix count measure of
\ref{paper:ep-prefix-source}.  Conditional on every original prefix
total in its own central window, this is one positive measure \(\mu\)
on full fine types and count-only state, independent of newly unread
prefix positions, with
\begin{equation}
 W=\mu(1)\asymp\prod_{j<m}w_j.
 \label{ld:whole-count-mass}
\end{equation}
It retains the displaced good-name box.  The conditional terminal
completion in \ref{paper:ep-terminal-admission} has constant mass
for each retained prefix type and each suffix root vector in the
specified central construction.  Independence from suffix uncolored
counts follows from the preceding support of the nonterminal-plateau
construction.

For each fixed complete type, take the legal pair of
\ref{paper:ep-local-pair}, namely \eqref{lower:local-pair}.  All its
outside contexts have the same actual increment, so it is below
both actual intrinsic endpoint minima and belongs to their common
positive boxes.  Write its path as \(\ell_i^-+E_i\), with
\(\ell_i^-\) the joining chord.  Impose on that original clock
\begin{equation}
 \theta\ell_i^-(t)+E_i(t)\ge
         2g\min(t,L_i-t)^\gamma-h_W,
       \qquad 0<\zeta<\gamma<1/2,\quad0<\theta<1,
 \label{ld:source-wall}
\end{equation}
together with binary REG.  Conditional on this word, refine both
lists by Lemma~\ref{ld:named regularity}.  On unselected blocks require
only the appropriate ordinary and named regularity.  Each local mass
\(q_i(\omega,G_i)\) then satisfies \eqref{ld:local-inputs} at
\(\eta_i=\sigma_{\operatorname{plateau}(i)}\), with the factor
\(\Psi_i^I\) of \eqref{lower:conditional-factor}.
The necessary flat path follows from \eqref{ld:source-wall} because
its uncontracted chord is larger and nonnegative, so the depth-zero
bank bound applies at these intrinsic scales.  Bounded supported
experiments retain their fixed positive conditional mass and have
\(D_i=\Psi_i^I=1\); a scalar parameter is not assigned to a zero
count.  Applying \eqref{ld:local-bank-retention} incorporates all
prescribed macroscopic recoloring intervals without changing these
estimates.

The following measure identity retains the individual plateau powers.
\begin{lemma}[Whole-type mixed moment]\label{ld:mixed}
Let \(\mu\) be any finite positive measure on complete types,
independent of the original independent environments \(G_i\), and
suppose \eqref{ld:local-inputs} holds uniformly in its support, with
possibly different \(\eta_i\in[\eta_-,\eta_+]\subset(0,1)\).
Then, for
\(f(G)=\int\prod_iq_i(\omega,G_i)\,d\mu(\omega)\),
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\left[f(G)\prod_iD_i(G_i)^{\eta_i-1}\right]
          \asymp\mu(1)\prod_i\Psi_i.
 \label{ld:mixed-result}
\end{equation}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For each fixed \(\omega\) and \(i\), H\"older applied to
\[
 q_i^{\eta_i}
  =(q_iD_i^{\eta_i-1})^{\eta_i}
                (D_i^{\eta_i})^{1-\eta_i}
\]
gives
\[
 \mathbb E[q_iD_i^{\eta_i-1}]
 \ge\frac{(\mathbb E q_i^{\eta_i})^{1/\eta_i}}
            {(\mathbb E D_i^{\eta_i})^{(1-\eta_i)/\eta_i}}
 \gg\Psi_i.
\]
The pointwise domination \(q_i\le CD_i\) gives both the upper
estimate and finiteness. At each complete type, independence of the
original environments lets us multiply the local mixed integrands.
Their two-sided estimates are uniform in the type, so Tonelli
integrates the product over the full measure \(\mu\).
\end{proof}

For the present prefix,
\(f_{\rm pre}(G)=\int\prod_iq_i(\omega,G_i)\,d\mu(\omega)\).
The plateau costs in \eqref{lower:plateau-cost} give the deterministic
width multiplier \(\prod_{j<m}w_j^{\sigma_j-1}\).
Multiplying \eqref{ld:whole-count-mass} by this multiplier yields
exactly \(\prod_{j<m}w_j^{\sigma_j}\), while every local path
retains its own plateau power.

\subsubsection{The ordinary suffix and its one count atom}

The suffix estimate must hold pointwise in the complete retained
prefix and uniformly over its later uncolored root target. We first
identify the ordinary weak block's two small endpoint scales, then
select the actual reservoir count and impose the path event at that
same count. This gives one suffix kernel containing both the ordinary
factor and the root atom. Suppose first
that the suffix contains the designated near-threshold group in the
convention of \eqref{profile:ordinary}. We call this its ordinary weak
block; throughout this construction that term refers to the fixed
profile neighborhood, with no additional drift cutoff. It is the
first suffix block. Let \(M_0\) be its length, \(P\) the entire
preceding original length, and \(B\) the following positive-drift
length. All later suffix drifts have a fixed positive lower bound,
by the separation of the finitely many thresholds.
The clipped-reference and KKT surplus estimates give
\begin{equation}
 A_{\rm mean}=\sum_{g<i}L_gg_g(r_g)\asymp P,\quad
 B_{\rm mean}=-\sum_{g>i}L_gg_g(r_g)\asymp B,\quad
 A_{\rm mean}+M_0g_i(r_i)=B_{\rm mean}.
 \label{ld:ordinary-balance}
\end{equation}
Thus \(D=A_{\rm mean}\asymp P\),
\(P\le C(M_0+B)\), and \(B\le C(P+M_0)\), including zero-side
cases.  This sums all original earlier groups and does not assign a
common drift sign to each of them.

At the weak block's left endpoint, reference clipping gives cost
at least \(c\min(P,M_0+B)\gg P\).  The full-prefix context has
cost exactly \(A_{\rm mean}\) and no proper good-group term.
At the right endpoint the same argument gives a lower bound
\(c\min(P+M_0,B)\gg B\), attained up to constants by the
full-prefix context of cost \(B_{\rm mean}\).  Therefore the
intrinsic endpoint minima are
\begin{equation}
 X_0^I\asymp1+P,\qquad Y_0^I\asymp1+B.
 \label{ld:ordinary-small-boxes}
\end{equation}
In both comparisons the common terminal target is initially zero;
there is no incoming-exit reserve in the small endpoint.
The constant-mark theorem \ref{bridge:ordinary-strong}, applied
to the legal representative with actual increment
\(r_iM_0-n\log(r_i+1)\), gives the local scale
\begin{equation}
 \beta_{min}\asymp
     \min\{1,(1+P)(1+B)/(1+M_0)\}.
 \label{ld:weak-beta}
\end{equation}
This uses the deterministic-mark theorem directly.

If the weak block is a largest suffix block, this is the bracket in
\eqref{lower:ordinary-factor}, by \eqref{ld:ordinary-balance}.
If a later positive block is largest, then \(B\ge M_0\), so
\eqref{ld:weak-beta} is bounded below. Write \(M\) for that
largest length and \(A_*,B_*\) for the preceding and following
lengths within the suffix; these are the lengths \(A,B\) in
\eqref{lower:ordinary-factor}. There are fixed \(g_H,C_H>0\)
such that each later drift is at least \(g_H\) and the absolute
first-block drift is at most \(C_H\). Thus
\[
 D\ge0,\qquad D\ge g_HM-C_HM_0,\qquad A_*\ge M_0.
\]
If \(M\ge2C_HM_0/g_H\), then \(D\ge g_HM/2\);
otherwise \(A_*\ge g_HM/(2C_H)\). In either case
\(D+A_*\ge c_HM\), so the bracket in
\eqref{lower:ordinary-factor} is also bounded below by a fixed
positive constant. If no designated near-threshold group is
present, all suffix drifts are uniformly positive, giving
\(D\gg U\) and the same conclusion. These comparisons preserve
the suffix convention and its fixed threshold neighborhoods.

Condition on a complete retained prefix.  Its uncolored discrepancy
\(\Delta_{\rm pre}\) satisfies
\(|\Delta_{\rm pre}|\le C\sqrt{1+V_{\rm pre}}\), and the Euler
identity gives the suffix target
\begin{equation}
 E_x=D+(x-\Delta_{\rm pre})/r_m,\qquad
 |E_x-D|\le C_A\sqrt{1+D}
 \label{ld:root-target}
\end{equation}
for every prefix-uncolored
\(0\le x\le A\log(2+V_{\rm pre})\), using
\(D\gg V_{\rm pre}\).  Fix the nonreservoir suffix counts in
their own central windows.  In a predetermined largest block use
the actual new count
\begin{equation}
 n_*^x=\left\lfloor
 \frac{\sum_{\rm suffix}c_iL_i+E_x-
                \sum_{i\ne *}w_in_i}{w_*}\right\rfloor,
 \qquad w_i=\log(r_i+1),\quad c_i=r_i.
 \label{ld:new-root}
\end{equation}
The support threshold and central root construction of
Theorem~\ref{bridge:ordinary-root} make it nonnegative and central,
with Poisson mass \(\asymp(1+U)^{-1/2}\).  All its original
\(n_*^x+1\) gaps are then sampled.  In the unconditional Poisson
experiment this means retaining the event that the sampled total
equals \eqref{ld:new-root}; it does not alter a previously fixed
tuple.  The bounded floor error is \(-C\le\epsilon\le0\).

The count \(n_*^0\) with \(x=0\) is a numerical device for
verifying the prefix boxes by
\ref{paper:ep-terminal-admission}; the experiment samples a clock
only at its actual selected count. As \(x\) increases, early
terminal lower bounds gain the common entrance, while late intrinsic
lower bounds are independent of both that entrance and the incoming
carry. The prefix paths, costs, and local pairs can therefore be
fixed before evaluating \(x\).

If the weak block is not the reservoir, its local count is unchanged.
If it is, put \(k=n_*^x-n_*^0\ge0\).  Then \(k\le C(1+x)\),
and the max formula for the legal pair gives
\begin{equation}
 \Delta_x=\Delta_0-w_*k,\quad
 x_0^-\le x_x^-\le x_0^-+w_*k,\quad
 a_*Y_0^I\le y_x^-\le y_0^-.
 \label{ld:root-pair-change}
\end{equation}
Equation \eqref{ld:ordinary-small-boxes} absorbs
\(w_*k\le C_A\log(2+P)\) in the left box, while the right
endpoint keeps its positive lower box.  Its scale is still
\eqref{ld:weak-beta}; an incoming exit or \(x\) has not been
added to its small right endpoint.

Keep every terminal fine label already sampled in the accepted prefix
fixed. Refine only the newly unread suffix labels under their conditional categorical law. The zero-target prefix completion supplies
the deterministic guards \eqref{paper:ep-own-central},
\eqref{paper:ep-box-strong} and the clipped-prefix lower bound; the
actual positive-root completion retains these guards by the exact
intrinsic cancellation. Section~\ref{supp:joint-count-source}
gives the complete finite disintegration, and
Section~\ref{supp:explicit-ordinary-construction} supplies the actual ordinary
strong-wall event with capped auxiliary end boxes. Impose that event
and uncolored regularity on the actual $n_*^x+1$-gap clock. No accepted prefix
label is resampled and no clock at the virtual zero-root count is reused.  The other suffix blocks have separated drift.
Reading a positive slope from the left, or a negative slope from
the right, their REG implies the allocated inward wall: absorb
\(K(1+t^\zeta)+gt^\gamma\) into a fixed intercept and a fraction
of the linear drift.  Long central blocks preserve the drift gap;
bounded supported blocks use their fixed finite convention.  The
same argument pays the strong and reference-paid local comparisons.
After counts are fixed, the original suffix clocks are independent;
there is at most one weak ordinary probability.  Fill named regularity
on each retained clock by Lemma~\ref{ld:named regularity}.  This constructs
a joint completion of order
\(\mathcal B_I=(1+U)^{-1/2}\beta_0\) on the same word.

For the matching upper and the support needed later, retain the
lawful full-stop context for every suffix \(q=0\) comparison:
all eligible names remain until its moving cut, then disappear.
Its intrinsic cost is the original reverse suffix risk, with no
incoming reserve.  At a fixed count its centered fluctuation agrees
with that of the minimum representative; the latter's positive
chord, including its \(\theta\)-contraction, lies below the
full-stop chord.  Thus the imposed weak and paid strong walls
imply on their actual joint support
\begin{equation}
 h_{\rm base}+R_{\rm tail}(v)\ge0\qquad(0\le v\le U)
 \label{ld:global-ordinary-wall}
\end{equation}
for one fixed reserve, large enough for floor and fixed intercept
errors.  Drop other filters and apply the all-count upper in
Theorem~\ref{bridge:ordinary-root} at this reserve and target
\eqref{ld:root-target}.  It gives \(O(\mathcal B_I)\), with the
reservoir denominator retained before its Poisson supremum.
Consequently, for every retained complete prefix word and every
permitted \(x\), its actual suffix completion kernel is comparable
to \(\mathcal B_I\).  Integrating the private prefix gives the
pointwise relation
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_{\rm suffix}f_0^x(G_{\rm pre},G_{\rm suffix})
        \asymp\mathcal B_I f_{\rm pre}(G_{\rm pre}).
 \label{ld:suffix-kernel}
\end{equation}
This expectation includes the one root atom, all suffix positions,
and the original named refinements.  It may be multiplied by any
nonnegative prefix-uncolored cost, but it does not scalarize a
future private-list weight.

Apply \eqref{ld:suffix-kernel} first, then Lemma~\ref{ld:mixed}
at each full type, and finally \eqref{ld:whole-count-mass}.  This
proves the source mixed moment
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E\left[f_0^x\prod_j(D_j^{\rm own})^{\sigma_j-1}\right]
 \asymp\mathcal B_I\prod_{j<m}w_j^{\sigma_j}
                  \prod_{i\in\mathcal I}\Psi_i^I(\sigma_{\rm plateau(i)}).
 \label{ld:source-mixed}
\end{equation}
The ordinary factor is linear and occurs once.

\subsubsection{Targets fixed by the costs and a fine-word density}

The cost floors bound the entire logarithmic target range in advance.
Within that range, one triangular cascade chooses the required numbers
of recolorings. The exact preimage count of the uniform subset kernel
