Put $A_j=\log S_j(\text{first})$, $b_j^{\rm flip}=u_jA_{j+1}$.
The construction gives
\begin{equation}
 b_j^{\rm flip}e_j-A_je_{j-1}=y_j+\delta_j,\quad e_0=0,\quad
 0\le\delta_j<b_j^{\rm flip},\quad e_j\ll\log(2+T_j),
 \label{history:cascade}
\end{equation}
and the original fine prior ratio is
$\log[p(c_j)/p(d_j)]=b_j^{\rm flip}-A_{j+1}$.
Thus the full residual changes by
$\Delta R=\sum_{j<m}e_j(b_j^{\rm flip}-A_{j+1})$.
At a regular endpoint bank the possible signatures and per-flip
increments of the fine cost are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{plateau full}&0\\
 \text{plateau zero, child full}&b_j^{\rm flip}\\
 \text{plateau zero, child zero}&b_j^{\rm flip}-A_{j+1}.
 \end{array}
\]
Here ``full'' means the entire relevant eligible cell, with no mixed
state at those two levels. The missing signature, plateau full with a
split child, is mixed. The increments follow directly by subtracting
$\Delta I$ from the stated $\Delta R$; for instance in the middle
case $\Delta I=-A_{j+1}$. This keeps the prior change.

Any discrepancy from the ideal coefficient
$b_j^{\rm flip}s_j-A_{j+1}s_{j+1}$ is paid by
$J(h)\gg\sqrt{T_j}-C$. The exhaustive cases are: a proper parent
or child state contributes an early/bad length or good-group square
root in its local or earlier group; a mixed state contributes the
whole group; an early full plateau or child has an early prefix reaching
that group; a late zero plateau has a zero tail containing it; a late
zero child has a tail containing its entire local length, which is
$\gg T_j$ by the hierarchy. Every per-flip coefficient is bounded.
Since $\log(2+T_j)\le\epsilon'\sqrt{T_j}+C_{\epsilon'}$, these
exceptional banks consume an arbitrarily small fixed part of $J$.
Regular banks keep their exact increments.

The main coefficients telescope without any monotonicity of the flags:
\[
 \sum_{j<m}e_j(b_j^{\rm flip}s_j-A_{j+1}s_{j+1})
 =\sum_{j<m}s_j(y_j+\delta_j)-s_mA_me_{m-1}.
\]
Since $r_jb_j^{\rm flip}=r_{j+1}A_{j+1}$, the actual root gives
\begin{equation}
 a_m-A_me_{m-1}
 =y_m-\sum_{j<m}(r_j/r_m)\delta_j=y_m+O_H(1).
 \label{history:terminal-cancellation}
\end{equation}
Thus every fine endpoint star on the target satisfies
\begin{equation}
 C_y(h)\ge\sum_{j:s_j=1}y_j+cH(h)-C.
 \label{history:target-endpoint}
\end{equation}
This bound retains coefficient one on every early target, including
the terminal target. The telescope applies to every pattern of early
and late plateaux.

For later use, if a late plateau's endpoint template is not full on an
original local block $g$, its charge is at least $c\sqrt{L_g}-C$.
Indeed a zero parent pays its zero tail; a proper parent pays its bad
length or good square root; a full parent with a nonfull fine class
is mixed on the entire group. For the terminal plateau the
atomic and fine alphabets agree. These charges add over the finite
set of affected groups after reducing the common coefficient.

\subsubsection{Intrinsic chords within a global fine history}

A local atomic wall remains useful inside a global history only if
its chord is dominated by the global endpoint budget. We prove this
for a proper coordinate even when its child is partly split, using
either the intrinsic chord or a linear charge on the current block.
Terminal coordinates use a root-separated budget and their actual
same-count source representatives.

Fix a local canonical full-current-input to deepest-suffix edge in
plateau $j$ and physical block $i=[l_i,b_i]$. First consider a global
endpoint context in which the whole immediate child remains intact
on the open block. Its varying bundle is exactly the indicated plateau
exteriors, with deadlines at least $b_i$; all other cuts are fixed
lawful endpoints. The global endpoint difference and centered bridge
are precisely the atomic ones:
\[
 C_0(h^+)-C_0(h^-)=K_j(v_j^+)-K_j(v_j^-)=\Delta_i,
 \qquad
 \Delta_i=(r_i-q)L_i-\log S_i\,n_i+\log(q+z)K_{i,B}.
\]
Let $\ell_i^{\rm intr}$ be the adjusted chord from the two actual all-context intrinsic minima,
shifted by their fixed reserve $h_{\rm intr}$.
If the child is early, $t_{j+1}\ge b_i\ge L_i$, so both global
endpoints have a charge $cL_i+h_*$ after one fixed shift. If the
child is late, the intrinsic score upper is
\[
 K_j(v_j)+h_{\rm intr}\le C(h_{\rm intr}+s_ja_j+J_j).
\]
For an early nonterminal plateau followed by a late child,
\eqref{history:enhanced-endpoint} retains exactly $a_j=\eta_j$;
for a late plateau $J_j$ suffices. At the terminal plateau it retains
$s_ma_m$. Hence in these cases both global endpoints dominate a
fixed positive multiple of the intrinsic endpoints. Interpolation
gives the same chord domination.

Choose a global budget share $\theta_{\rm glob}>0$. The linearly
paid case plus \eqref{history:bridge-REG} pays a strong inward wall.
In the chord case choose in advance
$0<\theta_{\rm intr}\le c_*\theta_{\rm glob}$.
The source's actual contracted wall
$\theta_{\rm intr}\ell_i^{\rm intr}+\mathcal R_i\ge gd_i^\gamma-h_W$
then implies the global allocated wall. This is why the contractions
are fixed before the source probability construction.

Terminal coordinates require the root to remain outside this allocation.
The source supplies same-root representatives with actual local
increment and
$x_i^-\le C_AX_i^0$, $y_i^-\le C_AY_i^0$, where the deterministic
scores $X_i^0,Y_i^0$ are computed at zero terminal target.
For a terminal prefix these follow by a virtual zero-root count
completion of its actual type; for the ordinary reservoir the actual
root count stays fixed and the extra left reserve is
$O_A(\log(2+V_{\rm pre}))\ll X_i^0$, while the right stays in its
fixed box. No virtual clock is used. After subtracting $a_ms_m$ from
a completed terminal endpoint, \eqref{history:enhanced-endpoint}
dominates its zero-target score. Consequently its root-separated
endpoint chord dominates a fixed multiple of the actual source
representative chord, even if the separated endpoint difference itself
is no longer $\Delta_i$.

Now allow an arbitrary fine star. Synchronize by plateau within each
original physical block: $\alpha=(j,i)$ has mean time $\tau_\alpha$,
spread $D_\alpha$, and endpoint depth $d_\alpha$.
Atomic curvature pays the within-block spread, also when the terminal
child has weight $z=1$. Thus
\[
 \sum_jK_j(h_j)\ge\sum_jK_j(h_j^{\rm sync})
       +c_s\sum_\alpha D_\alpha
       -C[1+\sum_\alpha d_\alpha^\zeta].
\]
For a fine star its mixed time has the exact formula
$S_{{\rm mix},j}=(t_j-\theta_j)_+$, where $t_j$ is the plateau's
largest exterior cut and $\theta_j$ is the smallest cut of any
nonanchor fine name in its entire child. All child names are eligible
until $V_j\ge t_j$. Maxima, minima and positive parts are Lipschitz,
so synchronization changes total mixed time by at most
$C_H\sum D_\alpha$. The actual mixed contrast is at least
$c_M\sum S_{{\rm mix},j}$ minus
$C[1+\sum(d_\alpha^\zeta+D_\alpha^\zeta)]$: every nontrivial
error endpoint is an original cut, within its spread of its mean.
Choose a small fixed $\epsilon_{\rm mix}>0$ relative to $c_M,c_s$.
The fine cost therefore dominates
\[
 F(\tau)=\sum_jK_j(h_j^{\rm sync})
                  +\epsilon_{\rm mix}\sum_jS_{{\rm mix},j}(h^{\rm sync})
\]
plus a positive spread charge and the stated depth error.

In each physical block order all its synchronized plateau-group times.
On this ordered chamber the mixed term is affine. Use ordered-simplex
endpoint weights within that block, and products only across distinct
blocks. If $F_v$ is the endpoint value and $a=a_m$, then exactly
\begin{equation}
 F(\tau)=a\mathcal S+\widehat L+\sum_\alpha\mathcal R_\alpha,
 \quad\mathcal S=\sum_v\omega_vs_m(v),\quad
 \widehat L=\sum_v\omega_v(F_v-as_m(v)).
 \label{history:root-separated-interpolation}
\end{equation}
The enhanced endpoint argument applies with
$\epsilon_{\rm mix}S_{\rm mix}$ and yields
\[
 F_v-as_m(v)\ge
 \sum_{j:s_j=1,s_{j+1}=0}\eta_j+cJ(v)-C,
 \quad \widehat L+C\ge c\sum_v\omega_vJ(v)\ge0.
\]
The coordinate marginal remains
$\mathbb P(v_\alpha=b_i)=(\tau_\alpha-l_i)/L_i$.
We keep the root term $a\mathcal S$ separate from $\widehat L$
throughout the wall allocation.

A proper local weak coordinate can have a partially split child;
its $\mathcal R_\alpha$ is still the atomic projection bridge.
Fix only interpolation choices in other physical blocks. Let
$t_{\rm out}$ be the largest cut of the immediate child plateau there, including fixed
boundary cuts. It is at most $l_i$ or at least $b_i$.
If $t_{\rm out}\ge b_i$, the child's flag is fixed. An early child
pays $cL_i$ at every current vertex; a late child leaves either the
positive plateau exit for an early plateau or its $J_j$ for a late one,
so the intrinsic chord comparison applies.
If $t_{\rm out}\le l_i$ and there are child cuts in this block,
a right child cut is entirely old and its reference cost is at least
$c b_i\ge cL_i$. If all child cuts are left but the parent bundle
is right, the whole block is mixed. Thus every parent-right vertex
has charge $cL_i$, and the coordinate marginal pays
$c(\tau_\alpha-l_i)$. With no child cut in this block, its flag is
fixed: an early child gives the same mixed payment and a late one
allows the intrinsic comparison. Averaging the outside choices gives
\begin{equation}
 \widehat L+C\ge c\min\{\tau_\alpha-l_i,
                         \ell_\alpha^{\rm intr}(\tau_\alpha)\}.
 \label{history:partial-child}
\end{equation}
The first branch plus regularity pays the inward curve; the second
plus the same actual $\mathcal R_\alpha$ is supplied by the contracted
source wall. The identity $\min(A,B)+E=\min(A+E,B+E)$ completes
this case.

Strong coordinates have a fixed reference drift gap and are paid
from their cheaper endpoint. Old weak and local proper-input or
wrong-name weak coordinates have two-ended reference charge $cL_i$.
These statements apply vertex by vertex using the actual marginals.
Remaining terminal coordinates use the zero-target representative
comparison above, including the actual ordinary root count. Choose
$\theta_{\rm glob}\le1/(4H^2)$ and all source contractions small
enough in advance. For every coordinate,
\[
 \theta_{\rm glob}(\widehat L+C)+\mathcal R_\alpha
                         \ge g_0d_\alpha^\gamma-C_0.
\]
There are at most $H^2$ shares. Their sum leaves at least three quarters
of $\widehat L+C$. After absorbing the earlier $d^\zeta$ errors,
\begin{equation}
 C_0(h)\ge a\mathcal S+c\sum_v\omega_vJ(v)
                      +c\sum_\alpha(d_\alpha^\gamma+D_\alpha)-C.
 \label{history:star-interpolated}
\end{equation}
Every empirical bridge has been paid once.

\subsubsection{Selecting an endpoint without losing the root}

Endpoint interpolation gives an average of costs, while history
summability needs one representative. A maximum-weight lawful vertex
has uniformly positive weight and controlled distance from every
cut. We transfer the terminal early flag to this vertex with a small
part of the retained reference and depth budgets, preserving the
root coefficient.

Choose in each physical block an ordered-simplex vertex of maximum
weight, with a fixed tie rule. Their product $v^\#$ is lawful and
has weight at least $(H+1)^{-H}$. A chosen endpoint side has marginal
probability at least $1/(H+1)$. If it is the nearer side, its movement
is $d_\alpha$; if farther, that marginal is $d_\alpha/L_i$, so
its movement is at most $(H+1)d_\alpha$. Original unsynchronized
cuts add their spread. In particular
\begin{equation}
 \sum_v\omega_vJ(v)\ge(H+1)^{-H}J(v^\#),\qquad
 |t_c-v_c^\#|\le C_H(d_\alpha+D_\alpha).
 \label{history:positive-vertex}
\end{equation}
The maximum-weight rule supplies the uniform marginal lower bound
needed to control movement. Coordinatewise nearest choices need not
have such a bound.

Suppose $0\le a\le A\log(2+T)$, where $T=V_m$. Then for every
$\epsilon>0$,
\begin{equation}
 a|\mathcal S-s_m(v^\#)|
 \le\epsilon\sum_v\omega_v\overline C_m(v)
                      +\epsilon\sum_\alpha d_\alpha^\gamma+C_\epsilon.
 \label{history:flag-payment}
\end{equation}
Only the unique physical block $[l,b]$ crossing $T/2$ can vary the
flag, unless another fixed-late cut forces all flags to zero. The
coordinate marginals and controlled movement give
$|\mathcal S-s_m(v^\#)|\le C_H\sum d_\alpha/L$ in this block,
as follows: for an early representative use the union bound
for a right choice; for a late one use one chosen-right coordinate to
bound the all-left event. If $L\ge T/4$, then
$A\log(2+T)d/L\le A\log(2+4L)L^{-\gamma}d^\gamma$,
whose coefficient is arbitrarily small at large $L$; bounded $L$
costs a constant. If $L<T/4$, both endpoints lie inside
$(T/4,3T/4)$, and every contributing endpoint has last terminal cut
there. The clipped-prefix reference lower
$\overline C_m(v)\ge c_H\min(t_v,T-t_v)$ therefore pays $c_HT$.
It absorbs $A\log(2+T)$ with an arbitrarily small share and a constant.
This proves \eqref{history:flag-payment} and keeps the full root
coefficient. Applying it to \eqref{history:star-interpolated} gives
\[
 C_0(h)\ge as_m(v^\#)+cJ(v^\#)
                     +c\sum_\alpha(d_\alpha^\gamma+D_\alpha)-C.
\]

We need a slightly stronger weighted form. Put
\[
 F_\epsilon^0(h^*)=\sum_jK_j^0(h_j^*)+
                   \epsilon\sum_{j<m}S_{{\rm mix},j}(h^*),
 \quad B(h^*)=\sum_j\overline C_j(h_j^*),
 \quad\Pi(h^*)=\sum_\alpha(D_\alpha+d_\alpha^\gamma).
\]
For fixed sufficiently small $\epsilon>0$, the same proof yields
\begin{equation}
 F_\epsilon^0(h^*)\ge as_m(v^\#)
           +c[J(v^\#)+B(h^*)+\Pi(h^*)]-C.
 \label{history:weighted-star-source}
\end{equation}
Indeed mixed-time Lipschitz and atomic synchronization apply directly
to this deterministic mixed-length term. At endpoints any fixed
positive mixed coefficient pays adverse flag changes. Reserve positive
shares of reference and spread, in addition to all bridge allocations:
\[
 0\le B(h^*)-B(h^{\rm sync})\le C_H\sum_\alpha D_\alpha.
\]
The lower is concavity; the upper follows because the rank profiles
differ only between each group's first and last cut, with uniformly
bounded integrands. These shares retain $B(h^*)$, while further shares
pay $J$, curves, spread and the flag interpolation. All allocations
are fixed before constructing the source.

\subsubsection{From a general fine history to its source and target costs}

We can now assemble the geometric reductions. Projection and
branching supply delay, lifetime, and mixed-time gains. Synchronization
and endpoint selection supply reference and depth gains. Their
positive shares absorb all named-regularity errors and still leave
a summable charge on every original history. Recoloring transfers the
same structure to the target word.

\begin{proposition}[Original-history source geometry]
\label{history:source}
On the source support just constructed, every lawful original fine
history $h$ has a lawful comparison star $h^*$ and endpoint
representative $v=v^\#$ such that
\begin{equation}
 C_0(h)\ge as_m(v)+c\Lambda(h)-C,
 \quad
 \Lambda=J(v)+B(h^*)+\Pi(h^*)+D_{\rm gap}+D_*+
                                   S_{\rm pure}+S_{\rm off}\ge0.
 \label{history:source-geometry}
\end{equation}
For every fixed $\delta>0$, the associated geometric envelope has a
uniformly bounded sum over all original histories and original pivot
representatives. All constants are independent of length ratios and
strict product gaps.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Recursively apply the lawful projection \eqref{history:projection},
keeping original time labels and selected lists. The exact identity is
\[
 C_0(h)=\sum_jK_j^0(h_j)+D_{\rm gap}+M_{\rm orig},
\]
with $M_{\rm orig}\ge c_MS_{\rm orig}
-C[1+\sum_{\text{original cuts }t}d_E(t)^\zeta]$ from
\eqref{history:mixed-actual}. Apply
\eqref{history:proper-branching} to nonterminal plateaux and
\eqref{history:floating}, \eqref{history:anchor-comparison} to the
terminal one. Their signed output normalizations cancel in each
same-word difference. They retain positive proper pure lifetimes,
terminal off-spine lifetimes and true clipping delay $D_*$.
The remaining terminal loss is
\[
 C_H\vartheta T_{\rm float}+
 C_K[1+T_{\rm float}^\zeta+\sum_{\rm births}d_E(\beta)^\zeta],
 \qquad B(h^*)\ge a_HT_{\rm float}.
\]
If there is no terminal nonsingleton interval, choose its comparison
cuts zero, $D_*=$ the sum of its original times, and
$S_{\rm off}=T_{\rm float}=0$; this case is exact.
By \eqref{history:mixed-domination}, a sufficiently small
$\epsilon<\min(c_M/2,c_p/4)$ retains
$\epsilon S_{\rm mix}(h^*)$ while leaving positive shares of
original mixed and pure time. The weighted quantity in
\eqref{history:weighted-star-source} is therefore available.

We pay the depth errors by tracking their original events. An erased
projection event is paired to a physical deadline, with distance charged
to $D_{\rm gap}$. A terminal event is retained, clipped to its deadline,
or clipped to $\tau$. In the last case,
$d_E(e)\le d_E(\tau)+(e-\tau)$, and $e-\tau$ belongs to $D_*$;
$\tau$ is a retained terminal cut when it is not a physical endpoint.
The same alternatives treat expired-first births. Retained cuts lie
within their group spread of its synchronized time. Thus all errors
are bounded by
\begin{equation}
 C[1+D_{\rm gap}^\zeta+D_*^\zeta+
                    \sum_\alpha(d_\alpha^\zeta+D_\alpha^\zeta)].
 \label{history:all-depth-errors}
\end{equation}
First choose the regularity slope so that a reserved part of
$B(h^*)\ge a_HT_{\rm float}$ pays the linear floating error.
Young's inequality pays the sublinear floating error from another
part. Delay and spread pay their $\zeta$-powers; the inward curves
with $\gamma>\zeta$ pay $d_\alpha^\zeta$. Each allocation leaves
a fixed positive share of its budget, proving
\eqref{history:source-geometry}.

The projection fibers sum by \eqref{history:erased-fiber}. Terminal
fibers at a physical endpoint sum by the same bound; at interior
$\tau$ they incur the finite polynomial in
\eqref{history:terminal-fiber}, paid by the retained inward and
spread budgets. Remaining cuts lie in the endpoint strips
\eqref{history:positive-vertex}; their polynomial multiplicity is
summed by exponential spread and stretched-exponential depth weights.
Finite assignment chambers, names, tie resolutions and permutations
only change the constant. Generated repeated deadline representatives
remain in the enlarged positive row. This proves summability without
replacing an original class by a comparison class.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Original-history target geometry]
\label{history:target}
For the transported bounded density $F_y$ on the same actual
root tuple, every word of positive weight and every original fine
history satisfy, with the constructions above,
\begin{equation}
 C_y(h):=R_y-I_h(\omega_y)
       \ge\sum_{j:s_j(v)=1}y_j+c\Lambda(h)-C.
 \label{history:target-geometry}
\end{equation}
Its geometric envelope has the same original-pivot summability.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Fix any retained source preimage of the target word. Such a preimage
exists for every positive value of the transported density.
For a comparison fine star define
$F_\epsilon^q=\sum_jK_j^q+\epsilon S_{\rm mix}$ for $q=0,y$.
Mixed time depends only on names and cuts, so exactly
\[
 \Delta F_\epsilon(h^*)=\Delta R-\sum_j\Delta I_j(h_j^*).
\]
Each atomic information is a sum over original slots, zero when a
slot does not route to that plateau; the formula remains exact when
recoloring changes child membership. Compare this change with the
change at the endpoint representative $v$ on the same source/image
pair. The residual $\Delta R$ cancels. The bounded atomic mark
vector changes only if a flipped slot meets a movement strip.
Bank $j$ has depth $\gg T_j$ in its original block; such an
intersection forces $\Pi(h^*)\ge c_HT_j^\gamma-C_H$.
Since it contains $O(\log(2+T_j))$ flips, for every fixed $\alpha>0$
\begin{equation}
 |\Delta F_\epsilon(h^*)-\Delta F_\epsilon(v)|
                      \le\alpha\Pi(h^*)+C_\alpha.
 \label{history:strip-transfer}
\end{equation}

At a regular endpoint bank, the three per-flip increments computed
above apply to $\sum_jK_j$ itself: the relevant mixed contrasts vanish
identically, ancestor exteriors have expired, and deeper plateaux read
neither changed shallow name. Exceptional signatures have
$J(v)\gg\sqrt{T_j}-C$, by the exhaustive endpoint cases already
proved. Their logarithmic number consumes any small fixed fraction
of $J(v)$. Hence
\[
 \Delta F_\epsilon(v)\ge
 \sum_{j<m}e_j(b_j^{\rm flip}s_j-A_{j+1}s_{j+1})
                                  -\alpha J(v)-C_\alpha.
\]
Apply \eqref{history:weighted-star-source},
\eqref{history:strip-transfer}, and the exact telescope
\eqref{history:terminal-cancellation}; nonnegative $\delta_j$ only
help. For small $\alpha$,
\begin{equation}
 F_\epsilon^y(h^*)\ge\sum_{j:s_j(v)=1}y_j+
                          c[J(v)+B(h^*)+\Pi(h^*)]-C.
 \label{history:weighted-star-target}
\end{equation}
The telescope retains coefficient one on the terminal root of the
fixed source-image pair. It uses the exact output changes and endpoint
charges, keeping the same root tuple throughout.

The target retains the original named regularity with prescribed spare
margins. An interval meeting a flipped interior bank either has length
$\gg T_j$ or an endpoint of depth $\gg T_j$; otherwise it cannot
reach that bank. A spare linear slope in the first case, or a spare
$\zeta$-depth coefficient in the second, pays
$O(\log(2+T_j))$ flips after fixing a sufficiently large plateau
threshold. Routed atomic counts are sums of finitely many fine counts.
Thus choose target regularity constants first and construct the source
inside them; no clock or reference intensity changes.

Project the original history on this target word. Its exact identity
is $C_y(h)=\sum_jK_j^y(h_j)+D_{\rm gap}+M_y$.
Use the proper and terminal same-word comparisons and mixed-time
domination exactly as in the preceding proof. The available weighted
budget is now \eqref{history:weighted-star-target}. The floating
reference cost pays the linear and sublinear floating errors;
\eqref{history:all-depth-errors} is paid by the same true delays,
spread and inward curves. Positive shares remain, proving
\eqref{history:target-geometry}. Fiber counting is unchanged and
keeps every original representative. This argument holds simultaneously
for all histories on the chosen source/image pair; it does not compare
class posteriors.
\end{proof}

\subsubsection{The actual comparison class and the complete row}

The geometric representative estimates cost, but the conditional
probability is taken in the original complete-cell class. Endpoint
strips identify which labels this class reveals. On a late block,
nonfull signatures are geometrically paid; the remaining blocks have
genuinely free intervals. We then sum complete types and diagonal
count bands under the original target law before taking a fractional
power.

Throughout this geometric row calculation, $Q_h$ is the
complete-cell class $\bar Q_h$ of Section~\ref{lower:row}; its
$I_h,C_y(h)$ and relative posterior are computed with that same
class and the unchanged original multiplier. The original slot
history remains its index.

Set, for the predeclared environmental costs and count widths,
\[
 \begin{gathered}
 D_j^{\rm own}=w_j\prod_{i:\operatorname{plateau}(i)=j}D_i\quad(j<m),
 \qquad D_m^{\rm own}=\prod_{i:\operatorname{plateau}(i)=m}D_i,\\
 y_j=-\log D_j^{\rm own},\qquad
 D_{\rm all}=\prod_jD_j^{\rm own}.
 \end{gathered}
\]
These targets are fixed before reading the private word. Fix its actual
class $Q_h(\omega)$ and the bounded transported acceptance $F=F_y$.
It has the actual root, named count support, strict exits, reconstructed
source tests, and bounded full relative likelihood established in the
transport construction.

In a physical block $g=[l_g,b_g]$, choose an integer endpoint-strip
radius $r_g\ge1$ dominating, by a dimension factor, the depths of
all original cuts and all movement strips from $h^*$ to $v$; cap it
at $L_g/2$ when necessary. From the exact depth bookkeeping,
\begin{equation}
 \sum_gr_g^\gamma\le C_H(1+\Lambda).
 \label{history:strip-budget}
\end{equation}
If $r_g<L_g/4$, the original partition is constant on the middle
interval and $h^*$ there agrees with $v$. These are partition facts,
independent of label probabilities. Proper projection and star
comparison preserve eligible unresolved rank. The only possible
increase for $h^*$ is from expired terminal off-spine first names,
whose number is at most the original terminal off-spine internal-cell
count. Thus, pointwise,
\[
 0\le r(h^*)-r(h)\le m_{\rm off}.
\]
If $v$ is full but the original middle is not, this rank difference
is at least one over an interval of length $L_g/2$, so
$S_{\rm off}\ge L_g/2$. If $v$ is nonfull on a late plateau's local
block, its endpoint charge is $J(v)\ge c\sqrt{L_g}-C$, as proved
above. If the strips occupy a quarter block, their own
$L_g^\gamma$ charge pays. Every late block is therefore geometrically
paid or the original class is full outside its endpoint strips.
Any missing polynomial floor on a paid block is absorbed by an
arbitrarily small fixed fraction of $\Lambda$ at its own length scale.

For a proper late plateau's count bank, either those strips reach its
interior or the original class is full on the bank. In the first case
$\Lambda$ has a positive power of $T_j$ and pays the width floor
$w_j\gg(2+T_j)^{-1/2}$. Let $J_{\rm free}$ be the remaining free banks. The original
class reads no label in them. Condition first on complete types and
exactly read strip labels. Unread permutations in different blocks
are independent uniform residual multisets, and the type-uniform path
envelopes give
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P(\text{necessary path tests}\mid
       \text{complete types, read strips})
       \le C\prod_{i\in I_{\rm free}}q_{i,r_i}(G_i).
 \label{history:free-path-banks}
\end{equation}
Sum the coupled type law inside this bound before taking any
fractional power. To estimate its exit probability, next reveal the
pair-coarsened bank labels and the labels outside those pairs. The
diagonal identities $\eta_j=h_j+b_j^{\rm flip}K_j$ leave every
$h_j$ independent of the unread splits. Maximum split atoms bound a
band by $C(1+R_j)/\sqrt{1+M_j}$ at the actual pair total $M_j$.
Averaging all original pair totals, including zero, gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb P(\text{exit restrictions}\mid Q_h(\omega))
       \le C\prod_{j\in J_{\rm free}}
                   \min\{1,R_j/\sqrt{1+T_j}\}.
 \label{history:free-count-banks}
\end{equation}
Indeed $M_j$ is binomial under the fully free bank's original law;
Chernoff gives $\mathbb E(1+M_j)^{-1/2}\le C(1+T_j)^{-1/2}$.
The original bank total is supplied by named regularity; if it fails,
the accepting density is zero. This proof does not infer an exit-only
bound from empty accepting support on a small-pair fiber.
Combining the two finite disintegrations proves
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E_\pi[F\mid Q_h(\omega)]
 \le C\prod_{j\in J_{\rm free}}w_j
           \prod_{i\in I_{\rm free}}q_{i,r_i}(G_i).
 \label{history:actual-class}
\end{equation}
The fully stated lemma, its elementary proof, the actual diagonal
cancellation and the joint free-bank density construction appear in
Section~\ref{supp:posterior-tensorization}. The class in that proof is
the target class with its changed old lists.

The same environmental envelopes can be chosen for any sufficiently
small fixed $b_0>0$ so that
$q_{i,r}\le CD_i e^{b_0r^\gamma}$. Their stretched-exponential
coefficient sum is finite, so clipping and normalization into $[0,1]$
changes only a fixed constant. Their prescribed polynomial floors and
source moments persist. Choose $b_0$ small relative to the coefficient
in \eqref{history:target-geometry} and
\eqref{history:strip-budget}. Pay all missing late widths and path
floors with the local payments above. Then
\[
 \mathbb E_\pi[F\mid Q_h(\omega)]
 \le C e^{(c/2)\Lambda}\prod_{j:s_j(v)=0}D_j^{\rm own}.
\]
The floor fixes the logarithmic target
range independently of $b_0$; that range fixes the finite geometry;
then choose $b_0$, and only afterwards construct envelopes and source.
Combining with \eqref{history:target-geometry} gives
\[
 e^{-C_y(h)}\mathbb E_\pi[F\mid Q_h(\omega)]
                      \le CD_{\rm all}e^{-c'\Lambda}.
\]
For retained compatible competitors the full likelihood ratio is
$e^{E_y(\omega)-E_y(\omega')}$, whose amplitude is bounded by the
strict-exit weighted likelihood identity. Therefore the true relative
posterior
\[
 q_h^{\rm rel}=\mathbb E_\pi
       [F(\omega')\pi(\omega)/\pi(\omega')\mid Q_h(\omega)]
\]
satisfies the same bound with a fixed extra factor. Raising to a fixed
$\delta>0$ and using original-pivot summability proves
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{h\ {\rm original}}e^{-\delta C_y(h)}(q_h^{\rm rel})^\delta
                              \le C_\delta D_{\rm all}^{\delta}.
 \label{history:full-row}
\end{equation}

\subsubsection{Bounded family weights and the arithmetic first mass}

The relative row becomes an unnormalized counting row through an
exact finite class identity. Combined with the prime-cell kernel,
it bounds a higher moment of the weighted box count by its first
mass. H\"older then retains that first mass to the first power in the
volume lower bound. The final linear projection removes auxiliary
nominal data without moving any fractional power through it.

For the arithmetic quantities in this paragraph, write
$Q_h^{\rm arith}$ for the class
\eqref{eq:cc-slot-partition}, and $Q_h^{\rm cell}$ for its
complete-cell enlargement. The row just obtained for
$Q_h^{\rm cell}$ bounds the row by
$\sum_{Q_h^{\rm arith}}F\le\sum_{Q_h^{\rm cell}}F$,
with the same $\Phi_g(h)$ and the same original index set.

Fix an original cell occupancy $g$, its finite legal label space
$\Omega$, and $0<\delta\le1$. An acceptance $F:\Omega\to[0,1]$
may couple all slots, but is independent of actual prime values and
invariant under within-cell slot permutations. Set
\[
 Z_F=\sum_YF(Y),\qquad
 M_h(F;Y)=\sum_{Z\in Q_h^{\rm arith}(Y)}F(Z),\qquad
 R_F(Y)=\sum_h\Phi_g(h)^\delta M_h(F;Y)^\delta.
\]
The finite weighted class identity is exactly
\begin{equation}
 \sum_h\Phi_g(h)^\delta\Psi_{h,1+\delta}(F)
                =\sum_YF(Y)R_F(Y).
 \label{history:weighted-class-identity}
\end{equation}
It is simply the expansion of the class power sum, so a pointwise
bound $R_F\le C$ on $F>0$ gives a total at most $CZ_F$. For any
positive product law $\pi$,
\[
 M_h(F;Y)=\frac{\pi(Q_h^{\rm arith}(Y))}{\pi(Y)}
                         q_{h,\rm arith}^{\rm rel}(F;Y),
\]
where the relative posterior on the right is conditioned on
$Q_h^{\rm arith}(Y)$ itself.
This follows by inserting $\pi(Z)/\pi(Z)$ in the finite class sum;
bounded $F$ alone does not remove its relative likelihood. A pointwise
row for a support indicator also holds for every smaller bounded
weight, by positivity; a merely averaged row does not imply this.

Suppose the correlated prime-cell kernel applies and the retained
occupancy has squarefree supply $cW_g\le S_g\le W_g$, with all tuples
inside the required size cutoff. On harmonic tuple measure times
Lebesgue space define
$f(\mathbf a,t)=\sum_YF(Y)\mathbf1_{B_Y(\mathbf a)}(t)$,
where the original boxes have side $b=\log2$. Then
$\int f=b^kS_gZ_F\gg W_gZ_F$.
At a point of $B_Y$, every other containing box overlaps $B_Y$, so
its divisor log vector is within $b$ in each coordinate. The correlated
kernel and \eqref{history:weighted-class-identity} consequently give
$\int f^{1+\delta}\ll W_gZ_F$. H\"older on this same unnormalized
measure yields
\[
 \operatorname{meas}\{f>0\}
 \ge\frac{(\int f)^{(1+\delta)/\delta}}
          {(\int f^{1+\delta})^{1/\delta}}
 \gg W_gZ_F.
\]
Its support is in the original divisor union. Occupancies partition
the tuple space and can be summed, retaining the linear dependence
on the bounded acceptance.

Finally, extra nominal data may be removed in a linear first-mass
identity when their support is already cell-measurable. Suppose that,
conditional on $g$, the joint law of $(Y,\Xi)$ and an acceptance
$a(Y,\Xi)\in[0,1]$ are equivariant under within-cell permutations,
and accepted realizations have an invariant cell-label support $S(Y)$.
Let $\pi_0(Y)=\mathbb P_{\rm joint}(Y\mid g)$ be the actual marginal,
and set $F(Y)=\mathbb E_{\rm joint}[a(Y,\Xi)\mid Y,g]$ where
$\pi_0(Y)>0$, with $F(Y)=0$ otherwise. Then $F$ is invariant and
$0\le F\le\mathbf1_S$. For every nonnegative $Y$-measurable weight $w$,
\[
 \sum_Y\pi_0(Y)w(Y)F(Y)
       =\mathbb E_{\rm joint}[w(Y)a(Y,\Xi)\mid g].
\]
For a desired nonnegative counting weight $v$, take $w=v/\pi_0$
where $\pi_0>0$ and $w=0$ otherwise; the left side is then
$\sum_Yv(Y)F(Y)$. Use Tonelli for an outer occupancy integral.
The conditional law of $\Xi$ may depend
on $Y$. This preserves linear likelihood factors; it does not commute
conditional expectation with a fractional power. Uniform deletion of
specified-color slot subsets and count-dependent target laws are
permutation equivariant, so the transport has this property whenever
its source and boundary support do. The complete-cell construction in
the main proof retains its nested fractional quantities before this
linear arithmetic projection.


\subsection{Endpoint forests and summability of original pivots}
\label{supp:history-geometry}

The reductions above change names and sometimes replace a cut by a
deadline. A cut-token construction tracks these changes monotonically
and identifies their total backward motion with the delay budget.
It then bounds every original pivot depth by final depths, spreads,
and delay. A single stretched-exponential estimate sums all original
histories and their within-cell multiplicities.
\subsubsection{Original data and notation}

Fix a dimension bound \(H \ge 2\). There are \(B \le H\) original physical blocks
\([ a_{g} , b_{g} ]\), with \(L_{g} = b_{g} - a_{g} > 0\), and at most \(n \le H - 1\) original cuts.
The physical endpoint set is

\[
 E=\{a_g,b_g:1\le g\le B\},\qquad
 d_E(t)=\min_{e\in E}|t-e|.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

Within a block this is its ordinary endpoint depth. The original pivot
grid includes its original representatives with their slot
multiplicities. Its uncolored regularity implies, for fixed constants
\(C_{\mathrm{occ}} , \kappa\),

\[
 \#\{\text{original representatives }t:
               d_E(t)\in[q,q+1)\}
       \le B C_{\rm occ}(1+q)^\kappa,
 \qquad q=0,1,\ldots .
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

The zero pivot contributes one extra representative. Original
permutations, zero pivots and ties remain included.

For example, the named regularity inequality at Section~\ref{app:history-details}, gives (2) by summing
over the at most \(H\) names and applying the resulting uncolored upper
bound to a unit interval at depth \(q\) near either end. Its linear
reference intensity is bounded in terms of \(H\). Its endpoint error is
at most \(C ( 1 + ( q + 1 )^{\zeta} )\). A bounded complete-cell mesh only enlarges
that interval by a fixed amount and therefore changes the constant.
Thus one may take \(\kappa = \zeta\); any larger fixed power also suffices.
This argument includes every original representative in an occupied
cell, rather than assuming bounded interior occupancy.
In particular, when several distinct original slot pivots round to
the same cell boundary, each is counted separately in (2). The
summability theorem below is therefore a sum indexed by the
original histories, with the rounded geometric times and their
full original multiplicities.

The original history is a refinement tree of an anchored permutation,
with activation times legal for each original boundary's deadline.
Owners form the nested chain of exterior alphabets and a
compound child. Their proper child weights satisfy \(z \ge z_{-} > 1\); the
terminal alphabet has equal weights. Throughout,

\[
 0<\zeta<\gamma<1/2.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

After lawful plateau projections, proper star comparisons, terminal
floating-chain comparison and reanchoring, let \(h^{*}\) be the resulting
fine comparison star. Its cuts in a given plateau/physical-block group
\(\alpha\) are synchronized at their mean \(\tau_{\alpha}\). Write

\[
 D_\alpha=\max_{r\in\alpha}t_r^*
                         -\min_{r\in\alpha}t_r^*,\qquad
 d_\alpha=d_E(\tau_\alpha),\qquad
 \Pi(h^*)=\sum_\alpha(D_\alpha+d_\alpha^\gamma).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

There are at most \(H - 1\) nonempty groups. Let \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\) be the accumulated
projection delay, \(D_{*}\) the terminal clipping delay, and
\(D = D_{\mathrm{gap}} + D_{*}\). All are nonnegative. Let \(S_{\mathrm{pure}}\) and \(S_{\mathrm{off}}\) be the
proper pure-cell and terminal off-spine lifetimes. These are the same
quantities defined above.

\subsubsection{The forest-token lemma}

Each internal refinement event carries one token. Projection may
rename the token or move it to a deadline, but does not create an
untracked event. The cumulative rank comparison matches erased times
to earlier added deadlines. The terminal spine uses the same tokens,
so all backward displacements add to the two delay quantities.

\begin{lemma}[Monotone cut tracking]\label{forest:tracking}
The canonical constructions can be
implemented by retaining \(n\) cut tokens. Their original times are
\(t_{1} , \ldots , t_{n}\); their final comparison-star times, with multiplicity, are
\(t_{1}^{*} , \ldots , t_{n}^{*}\). Token names can change, but

\[
 t_r^*\le t_r\quad(1\le r\le n),\qquad
 \sum_r(t_r-t_r^*)=D_{\rm gap}+D_*.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

Physical endpoint cuts added in projections are included as the new
positions of old tokens, not as extra untracked cuts.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
At one exterior/child projection, the formal parent events
and child events partition the original event multiset. A child
boundary is the minimum-time event in its intervening original
segment; distinct child boundaries use disjoint segments. The other
events belong to the formal parent. This retains all the times before
augmentation.

The augmented parent isolates an expired exterior name at its physical
deadline when necessary. Here is a rank proof that its activated-event
count is at least the formal parent's at every time. Let \(F\) separate
the exterior deadlines from all child deadlines. Before \(F\) the child
has no expired first name, so its unactivated rank equals its eligible
unresolved rank. The augmented parent also has zero expired-first
delay. Eligible unresolved ranks add under projection. Thus, before
\(F\), original unactivated rank minus the two projected unactivated
ranks is exactly the nonnegative original expired-first delay density.
After \(F\) the parent rank is zero. Every unactivated child boundary
uses an entire disjoint intervening segment of unactivated original
boundaries, so original unactivated rank is at least the child's.
Since the formal-parent and child event multisets partition the
original one, this proves, on both sides of \(F\), that formal-parent
unactivated rank is at least augmented-parent unactivated rank. Their
activated-event counts have the reverse inequality. Cancel the common event times with
multiplicity. If \(e_{1} \le \ldots \le e_{j}\) are the remaining formal-parent times
and \(a_{1} \le \ldots \le a_{j}\) the remaining added deadlines, the cumulative count
inequality gives \(a_{l} \le e_{l}\) for every \(l\). Move token \(l\) from \(e_{l}\) to
\(a_{l}\). The loss of total activation time is
\(\sum_{l} ( e_{l} - a_{l} ) = D_{\mathrm{gap}}\) for this projection: integrating the difference
of unactivated-boundary ranks gives exactly the same quantity. This is
the explicit rank identity. Repeat recursively.
Each stage moves existing tokens backwards; all displacements add.

A proper same-cut star changes the tree and its name order but retains
the event-time multiset. In the terminal plateau, choose the surviving
spine representative in the last nonsingleton interval as above. At each binary refinement retain the spine
representative on its ancestral branch and retain the left-child
representative on every off-spine subtree. The discarded
representative receives that event's original time. There is exactly
one discarded representative per internal tree vertex, so before
clipping the times are the original multiset. Clip a discarded name's
time to its own physical deadline if necessary and then to the final
nonsingleton time \(\tau\). Both operations move times backwards.

For \(t < \tau\), the retained set consists of the eligible names in the
spine cell and the nonfirst names of off-spine internal cells.
Consequently its unresolved rank is the original unactivated rank
minus the indicator of an expired spine first name. After \(\tau\) its
rank is zero. Integrating the rank difference gives precisely

\[
 D_*=\int_0^\tau\delta_{\rm sp}(t)\,dt
                  +\int_\tau^T d_{\rm orig}(t)\,dt
       =\sum_r(t_r^{\rm before}-t_r^{\rm after}).
\]

Reanchoring the floating chain at the permanent original anchor only
exchanges the spine and anchor names; its removal-time multiset is
unchanged. If no nonsingleton interval exists, all terminal cut tokens
are moved to zero and the displacement is their original time sum,
as specified above. This proves (5).
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Original pivot depths]\label{forest:depths}
The tracked construction
satisfies the dimension-only bound

\[
 \sum_{r=1}^n d_E(t_r)^\gamma
     \le H^2\bigl(1+D_{\rm gap}+D_*+\Pi(h^*)\bigr).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Distance to a fixed set is 1-Lipschitz. If token \(r\)
belongs to final group \(\alpha\), then

\[
 d_E(t_r)\le (t_r-t_r^*)+D_\alpha+d_\alpha.
\]

Because \(0 < \gamma < 1\), the \(\gamma\) power of a sum is at most the sum
of its \(\gamma\) powers. H\"older's inequality and concavity give
\(\sum_{r} ( t_{r} - t_{r}^{*} )^{\gamma} \le n^{1 - \gamma} D^{\gamma}\). There are at most \(n\)
tokens in a group, and \(v^{\gamma} \le 1 + v\). Hence

\[
 \sum_r d_E(t_r)^\gamma
 \le n^{1-\gamma}(1+D)+n\sum_\alpha(D_\alpha^\gamma+d_\alpha^\gamma)
 \le n^{1-\gamma}(1+D)+n^2+n\Pi.
\]

For \(n \le H - 1\), the last expression is at most the right side of (6).
The case \(n = 0\) is immediate.
\end{proof}

The depth bound also gives \eqref{history:strip-budget}. Up to a dimension
factor, the largest original depth or movement in a block bounds its
required strip radius. The sum above, together with the corresponding
final spread and mean-depth charges, therefore bounds the \(\gamma\)th
power of that radius.

\subsubsection{Summability of all original pivots}

The token depth bound converts the geometric penalty into a product
of penalties in the original pivot depths. Since original regularity
bounds the number of representatives at each depth by a polynomial,
these one-dimensional sums converge uniformly. Relaxing order,
deadline, and distinctness restrictions enlarges the sum and makes
its factorization immediate.

\begin{theorem}[Summability of original pivots]\label{forest:summability}
Suppose the geometry assigns

\[
 \Lambda(h)\ge D_{\rm gap}+D_*+\Pi(h^*)
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

and uses the tracked constructions of Lemma~\ref{forest:tracking}. Then, for every fixed
\(\delta > 0\),

\[
 \sum_{h\ {\rm original}} e^{-\delta\Lambda(h)}
 \le e^\delta H!\left[
 1+BC_{\rm occ}\sum_{q=0}^\infty(1+q)^\kappa
                    e^{-\delta q^\gamma/H^2}
                 \right]^{H-1}<\infty.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

The bound is independent of block lengths, length ratios, strict
product gaps, original grid size and the number of representatives.
If the row convention duplicates a history by finitely many named tie
resolutions, multiply the right side by that fixed dimension-only
number.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Equations (6), (7) imply

\[
 e^{-\delta\Lambda(h)}
 \le e^\delta\prod_{r=1}^n
             e^{-\delta d_E(t_r)^\gamma/H^2}.
\]

Sum this product over every original time tuple, ignoring deadline
constraints, ordering constraints and distinctness constraints. All
terms are nonnegative, so this only enlarges the sum. There are at
most \(H !\) original name permutations. Bound each one-dimensional pivot
sum using (2) and the zero pivot. This proves (8). The numerical series
converges because a stretched exponential with any positive exponent
dominates every fixed polynomial.
\end{proof}

In particular, the full original-pivot summability assertion in \ref{history:source}, follows from its
specified nonnegative \(\Lambda\), once its cost estimate is established.
No separate bounds on individual projection fibers are needed.

\subsubsection{The arbitrary-history cost reduction}

To use the token summability theorem, we need a cost estimate retaining
all of its positive charges. The following deterministic reduction
separates pure-cell, off-spine, and mixed-time gains from their named
regularity errors. Section~\ref{supp:chord-comparison} supplies the
weighted source-star inequality that pays those errors.
Let \(q = 0\) or \(q = y\) denote one source or target word. Define

\[
 F_\epsilon^q(h^*)=\sum_jK_j^q(h_j^*)+
                      \epsilon\sum_{j<m}S_{{\rm mix},j}(h^*),
 \qquad B(h^*)=\sum_j\overline C_j(h_j^*).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

Assume the actual fine names obey the original named regularity, with fixed
depth-intercept coefficient \(K\) and a sufficiently small linear slope
\(\vartheta\). There exist positive constants \(c_{p} , c_{o}\) and finite
\(C_{H} , C_{K}\) such that the canonical reduction gives

\[
 \begin{split}
 C_q(h)\ge{}&F_\epsilon^q(h^*)+D_{\rm gap}+D_*
                   +c_pS_{\rm pure}+c_oS_{\rm off}\\
 &-C_H\vartheta T_{\rm float}
   -C_K\left[1+T_{\rm float}^{\zeta}
                   +\sum_{r=1}^n d_E(t_r)^\zeta\right],
 \end{split}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

for sufficiently small fixed \(\epsilon > 0\). Here \(T_{\mathrm{float}}\) is the
terminal interval away from the permanent anchor, and

\[
 B(h^*)\ge a_HT_{\rm float},\qquad a_H>0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

These facts are deterministic same-word comparisons. Their proofs are
as follows; they do not use the posterior row being proved.

The lawful projection has the exact cost decomposition into atomic
costs, nonnegative projection delay and per-slot mixed contrasts. On a
nonterminal plateau a current pure original internal cell has \(k + 1\) original
names and either \(k + 1\) or \(k\) eligible names. Moving its \(k\) nonfirst
names into the star increases reference residual entropy by at least

\[
 \gamma_z=(z_--1)\log(1+1/z_+)>0
\]

per unit reference coefficient when its first name remains alive;
expiration increases this gain. Sum over pure-cell lifetimes. Named
regularity on the fixed, bounded number of constant-partition intervals converts
this reference gain to \(c_{p} S_{\mathrm{pure}}\), with a small linear error and
errors at the original birth/split depths. The output normalization
cancels in the same-word difference. This proves the claimed comparison.

In the terminal floating chain, the spine cell has at least two
eligible names. Absorbing an off-spine internal cell into its mass
gains at least \(\log ( 1 + 1 / H )\) per reference coefficient, giving
\(c_{o} S_{\mathrm{off}}\). The loss of activation time is exactly \(D_{*}\). Reanchoring
exchanges the two equal-probability fine names only on the floating
interval, so its remaining actual-word error is bounded by
\(C_H\vartheta T_{\mathrm{float}}+C_K[1+T_{\mathrm{float}}^\zeta+\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal D_{\mathrm{orig}}}d_\alpha^\zeta]\). Here \(\mathcal D_{\mathrm{orig}}\) indexes the original birth and split depths in this reanchoring, and \(d_\alpha\) denotes the corresponding depth.
These are the required floating-chain error bounds, with every original depth error retained.

For (11), while the chain floats its rank \(d\) lies between 1 and
eligible capacity minus one. Retaining the permanent anchor on the
whole floating interval increases that rank by one; discarding the
other last-cell survivor at the interval's left end decreases it by
one. Both comparison histories are lawful. They share the original
entrance normalization and have nonnegative complete reference costs.
For \(g_{g} ( d ) = d - \kappa_{g} ( d + 1 ) \log ( d + 1 )\),

\[
 2g_g(d)-g_g(d-1)-g_g(d+1)\ge\kappa_*/H.
\]

Integrate over the floating interval and use the two nonnegative
comparison costs. Its reference cost is at least
\(a_{H} T_{\mathrm{float}}\) with \(a_{H} = \kappa_{*} / ( 2 H )\); reanchoring preserves that
reference cost. Other atomic reference costs are nonnegative. This
proves (11), using the complete-reference nonnegativity theorem proved in Section~\ref{paper:ep-reference}.

Finally, a comparison child has unresolved rank at least that of the
original child, so it has no more eligible cells. If a comparison mixed
indicator is one and its proper original parent has no pure internal
cell, that parent already agrees with its same-cut star and the
original child has at least two eligible cells. The original indicator
is therefore one. If the parent has a pure internal cell, charge its
lifetime. Thus, pointwise and then integrated,

\[
 \sum_jS_{{\rm mix},j}(h^*)
       \le\sum_jS_{{\rm mix},j}(h)+S_{\rm pure}.
\]

The original mixed contrast has positive reference gap on every mixed
interval; REG supplies its linear gain minus the same depth errors.
Choose \(\epsilon\) smaller than half this mixed gain and half the proper
pure gain. This retains the mixed term in (9) and positive shares of
both original gains, proving (10).



\subsection{Partial-child, root-separated and weighted source-star comparisons}
\label{supp:chord-comparison}

This subsection proves the two chord comparisons needed by the global
wall allocation. A partially split proper child is paid either by
a linear old-prefix charge or by the parent's intrinsic chord.
A terminal coordinate is paid by its source chord after the root
has been separated. We then combine these comparisons with curvature
and a maximum-weight endpoint to retain the full reference, spread,
and inward-depth budgets.
\subsubsection{Actual source quantities}

Use the fixed ordered KKT profile and the source constructed in Section~\ref{lower:chapter}. Owners have products
\(\sigma_{1} > \ldots > \sigma_{m}\),

\[
 u_j=\sigma_{j+1}/\sigma_j,\quad d_j=u_j^{-1}-1,
 \quad r_j=\sigma_j/\sigma_1.
\]

All these products are in a dimension-only compact subinterval of
\(( 1 / 2 , 1 )\). Write \(T_{j}\) for local plateau length and \(V_{j}\) for its
total old plus local length. The independently derived plateau
balance gives

\[
 V_{j-1}\le C_{\rm hier}T_j,
 \qquad C_{\rm hier}=2H^3(1+\log H)^3.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

This is Section~\ref{paper:geometry}. It is a bounded-ratio
inequality for a complete maximal plateau, not a claim that every
local block is longer than its predecessors.

The actual source word has proper targets zero, root
\(X_{1} = x + \epsilon\), \(- C \le \epsilon \le 0\), and strict exits satisfying

\[
 \eta_j\ge0,\quad \eta_j\le C\sqrt{1+T_j},\quad
 \sum_{j<m}d_j\eta_j\le C.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

Set

\[
 a_j=\eta_j,\ b_j=\eta_{j-1}/u_{j-1}\quad(j<m),\qquad
 a_m=x/r_m,\ b_m=\eta_{m-1}/u_{m-1}-\epsilon/r_m.
\]

The atomic outputs are \(Z_{j} = a_{j} - b_{j}\); an absent incoming term is
zero. The actual intrinsic endpoint cost is
\(K_{j} ( v_{j} ) = Z_{j} - I_{j} ( v_{j} )\). For an endpoint fine star put

\[
 s_j(v)=\mathbf1_{\{t_j(v)\le V_j/2\}},\quad
 J_j(v)=\overline C_j(v_j)+S_{{\rm good},j}(v_j),
 \quad J(v)=\sum_jJ_j(v)+\sum_{j<m}S_{{\rm mix},j}(v).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

Here \(t_{j}\) is the last positive cut of plateau \(j\) itself. Cuts in
deeper plateaux do not enter this maximum.

For fixed sufficiently small \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{mix}} > 0\), define the endpoint
value

\[
 F(v)=\sum_jK_j(v_j)+\epsilon_{\rm mix}
                                   \sum_{j<m}S_{{\rm mix},j}(v).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

All these terms use the same source word; histories change cuts and
partitions, not the word's labels or its old lists.

\subsubsection{Two endpoint estimates}

The displaced count box gives a lower cost with coefficient one on
the early signed output and an upper cost in terms of the intrinsic
score. Both follow from exact prefix and tail expressions. Keeping
these formulas separate prevents a full-group square-root error from
entering the late endpoint scale.

The displaced own-scale source count box gives, simultaneously on its
actual support,

\[
 K_j(v_j)\ge s_j(v)Z_j+c_0J_j(v)-C_0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

For a named endpoint context containing a local cut, one also has

\[
 K_j(v_j)+h_{\rm intr}
       \le C_0'\bigl(h_{\rm intr}+s_j(v)a_j+J_j(v)\bigr).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

Here all constants are dimension-only once the fixed count-box and
reserve constants are chosen. These are not assertions about a
conditioned mean. They follow from the exact prefix/tail formulas for
the actual named counts, as follows.

The box row is
\(C_{v} \ge b_{j} + Z_{\mathrm{tail}} + ( 3 / 4 ) \overline{C}_{v} + G_{v} - C_{\mathrm{box}}\), with
\(G_{v} \ge c S_{\mathrm{good}} - C\). Subtract \(b_{j}\). At an early endpoint the exact
prefix formula replaces \(Z_{\mathrm{tail}}\) by \(Z_{j}\) minus centered prefix
discrepancies of size \(O ( \sqrt{1 + t_{j}} )\). Its positive reference prefix
charge pays this square root, retaining a fixed part of \(\overline{C}_{v}\) and
the good-group gain. At a late endpoint use the exact tail expression;
only the zero-rank tail has a centered square-root error. Reference
cost controls its length and the bad-group lengths, so it pays those
errors while retaining the good-group gain. This proves (5).

For the upper bound at an early local-containing endpoint,
\(K_{j} \le a_{j} - b_{j} + \overline{C}_{v} + O ( \sqrt{1 + t_{j}} )\).
The local cut ensures \(t_{j} \ge V_{\mathrm{old}}\). Reference cost controls \(t_{j}\)
when the endpoint is early, and \(b_{j} \ge 0\) can be discarded, giving (6).
At a late endpoint the exact intrinsic tail formula cancels the
incoming \(b_{j}\); zero-tail and bad-group square roots are paid by
reference cost, and good-group square roots are \(S_{\mathrm{good}}\). This again
gives (6), without any incoming-exit reserve in the late score.
These exact formulas and cancellations are proved in Section~\ref{paper:ep-intrinsic-section}.

\textbf{Endpoint root removal.} There are constants \(c_{E} > 0 , C_{E}\) such that

\[
 E(v):=F(v)-a_ms_m(v)+C_E
 \ge c_E\left[J(v)+
       \sum_{j<m:\ s_j(v)=1,\ s_{j+1}(v)=0}\eta_j\right]\ge0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

\textbf{Proof.} Sum (5), retaining a fixed positive coefficient of the
mixed lengths in (4). The output identity is exactly

\[
 \sum_js_jZ_j
 =s_ma_m+s_m\epsilon/r_m
       +\sum_{j<m}\eta_j(s_j-s_{j+1}/u_j).
\]

Equal-one terms sum to \(- \sum d_{j} \eta_{j}\), bounded by (2). Keep every
positive \(\eta_{j}\) at a \(1 \to 0\) transition. A \(0 \to 1\) loss is at most
\(C \sqrt{1 + V_{j}}\). It has a charge at its own scale: if
\(t_{j + 1} \ge t_{j} / 2\), the child's early prefix has length at least \(V_{j} / 4\);
otherwise on \(( t_{j + 1} , t_{j} )\) an eligible parent exterior is retained
in the fine anchor cell and an immediate-child exterior is already a
singleton. This is a mixed interval of length at least
\(V_{j} / 4\). In either case \(J ( v ) \ge c V_{j} - C\) for that transition. Spend
at most a \(1 / ( 2 H )\) fraction of the retained \(J\) budget for each such
loss, using \(C \sqrt{V} \le \epsilon V + C_{\epsilon}\). There are at most \(H - 1\)
losses. A positive coefficient of \(J\) and every positive \(1 \to 0\) exit
remain; bounded floor errors enter \(C_{E}\). This proves (7). \qed

\subsubsection{A child cut in this block pays its own old prefix}

A cut in a parent's local block is an old cut for its child. If that
child reaches the right endpoint, its complete reference prefix cost
pays the current block even when its own local lengths are uneven.
We recover the clipped-prefix estimate on the original coefficient
chain and use the plateau hierarchy to compare the child's remaining
length with this old interval.

We need the reference fact that a plateau endpoint with last positive
cut \(t\) has

\[
 \overline C(v)\ge c_{\rm ref}\min(t,V-t),\qquad c_{\rm ref}>0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

This is the clipped-positive-prefix statement in Section~\ref{paper:ep-prefix-guards}. Its proof can be checked entirely
on the original reference profile. Reverse compression makes any
positive endpoint rank profile dominate a clipped rank profile
\(\min ( r_{g} , R )\), \(R \ge 1\). The compression update \(A \to D\) is legal because
the normalized secant
\(\log ( ( f ( z + D ) - f ( z + A ) ) / ( D - A ) ) / \log ( z + D )\), \(f ( v ) = v \log v\), decreases in
its upper endpoint; hence an update lowering the current benchmark
also lowers every already processed local benchmark. For earlier groups,
already processed coefficients are larger, giving the same assertion
directly. This is the original secant/compression proof, not a
stationarity assertion for a truncated vector.

For each fixed \(R\), write its coefficient as

\[
 f_g=g_g(\min(r_g,R))
       =\min(r_g,R)(1-S_g^{t_g}).
\]

The original transported coefficients and decreasing integer
capacities make consecutive \(t_{g}\) increase by at least

\[
 d_0=\min\left\{\frac{d_*}{\log H},\frac1{24H^2},
           \frac{\log(2\log2)}{H\log^2H}\right\}>0,
\]

where the old coefficient gap has the explicit lower bound

\[
 d_* =\min\left\{\frac{\varepsilon_H}{H^2},
 H^{-H-1}\left[1-(1-H^{-1})^{\varepsilon_H}\right]\right\},
 \quad \varepsilon_H=\frac{2\log2-1}{2H(\log H)^2}.
\]

Put \(c_{\mathrm{ref}} = 1 - 2^{- d_{0} / 3}\). If any prefix coefficient is at most
\(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\), its \(t_{g} \ge - d_{0} / 3\) and every later coefficient is at most
\(- c_{\mathrm{ref}}\). Otherwise every prefix coefficient exceeds \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\).
The first alternative gives prefix cost at least \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\) times tail
length, because the complete clipped reference cost is nonnegative;
the second gives at least \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\) times prefix length. Minimizing
over \(R\) proves (8). This uses the complete reference comparison,
not a lower bound on the lengths of intervening groups.

Now take a parent plateau \(j\) and one of its local physical blocks
\([ a , b ]\), \(L = b - a\). All cuts of the immediate child plateau \(j + 1\) in this
block are old cuts. If a child endpoint has last positive cut \(b\),
then (1) and (8) give

\[
 J_{j+1}(v)\ge\overline C_{j+1}(v)
 \ge\frac{c_{\rm ref}}{\max(1,C_{\rm hier})}\,b
 \ge\frac{c_{\rm ref}}{\max(1,C_{\rm hier})}\,L.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

Indeed \(b \le V_{j}\), and the child's length after \(b\) is at least its
local total \(T_{j + 1} \ge V_{j} / C_{\mathrm{hier}} \ge b / C_{\mathrm{hier}}\). This is precisely the
old-interval payment needed in the partial-child argument.

\subsubsection{Partial-child comparison on the endpoint forest}

Ordered-simplex interpolation couples parent and child endpoint
choices within the same physical block. We therefore fix only the
choices in other blocks. According to the last child cut outside
the current block, every parent-right vertex is paid either by an
old-prefix or mixed-time charge, or by the parent's intrinsic
endpoint. Its exact coordinate marginal then gives the required
chord bound.

Fix a proper local canonical weak coordinate \(\alpha\) of plateau \(j\)
in \([ a , b ]\). Its synchronized cut is \(\tau\), and
\(u = ( \tau - a ) / L\). Its atomic projection is full current input to the true
deepest suffix. All contexts below are original lawful named contexts.

Let \(x_{\mathrm{intr}} , y_{\mathrm{intr}}\) be the actual intrinsic minima over paired outside
contexts, shifted by the fixed reserve. Their difference is the
actual local increment \(\Delta\), because moving only the current
atomic bundle across this original block changes no outside term.
Write

\[
 \ell_{\rm intr}(\tau)=(1-u)x_{\rm intr}+u y_{\rm intr}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

If the source uses the adjusted sufficient pair instead, its two
endpoints are no larger than these minima: both actual minima lie
above the lower common box, their difference is \(\Delta\), and the
adjustment is \(\max ( a_{*} X , a_{*} Y - \Delta )\). Thus proving the inequality with
(10) also proves it for the actual sufficient source chord.

Synchronize every plateau in the current block and use its lawful
ordered-simplex vertices. Take products of their interpolation
weights only across different physical blocks. Fix an outside-block
vertex choice. Define \(t_{\mathrm{out}}\) to be the largest cut of plateau \(j + 1\)
in those outside blocks, including its fixed boundary cuts. Therefore
\(t_{\mathrm{out}} \le a\) or \(t_{\mathrm{out}} \ge b\). The child may have deeper plateaux; their
cuts remain present but do not enter this definition of \(t_{\mathrm{out}}\).

There are two possible bounds for the conditional current-block
average of \(E ( v )\):

\[
 \mathbb E_{\rm current}E(v)\ge c(\tau-a)
 \quad\hbox{or}\quad
 \mathbb E_{\rm current}E(v)\ge c\ell_{\rm intr}(\tau),
 \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

with the same dimension-only positive \(c\). Here and below these
expectations are finite geometric interpolation averages, not
probabilities of random words.

If \(t_{\mathrm{out}} \ge b\), the immediate child's plateau flag is fixed. If it is
early, its prefix has length at least \(b\), so (7) pays \(cL\) at every
current vertex and yields the first bound in (11). If it is late,
(7) retains \(\eta_{j}\) when the parent is early, while \(J_{j}\) pays when
the parent is late. Equation (6) therefore gives, at every current
vertex,

\[
 E(v)+C\ge c\bigl(K_j(v_j)+h_{\rm intr}\bigr).
\]

When the parent coordinate is left, its right-hand side is at least
\(c x_{\mathrm{intr}}\); when it is right, at least \(c y_{\mathrm{intr}}\). Atomic parent
endpoints do not depend on how the fine child is partitioned: the
parent projection merges all child-touching cells into its compound
child. The actual incoming word and local counts remain the same. The
parent's right marginal is exactly \(u\), even with dependent ordered
choices for every child coordinate in this block. Interpolation
gives the second bound in (11).

If \(t_{\mathrm{out}} \le a\) and plateau \(j + 1\) has cuts in this block, consider every
vertex at which the parent bundle is right. A child bundle at the
right endpoint has last child cut \(b\), and (9), (7) pay \(cL\). If all
child bundles are left, an immediate-child exterior is already a
singleton throughout the block; a parent exterior in the varying
bundle remains in the fine anchor cell until \(b\). Both are eligible
on the entire block. Thus the block is mixed and (7)
again pays \(cL\). Other current vertices have \(E(v) \ge 0\) by (7).
The parent-right marginal \(u\) yields \(cLu = c ( \tau - a )\).

If plateau \(j + 1\) has no cut in this block, its flag is fixed. A late
child gives the intrinsic bound as above. An early child has all its
exterior cuts at or before \(a\), so a parent-right vertex is again
mixed throughout the block and gives the linear bound. These cases
exhaust every lawful current vertex, regardless of cuts of deeper
plateaux in the same block.

In the intrinsic cases a fixed additive constant was displayed;
increase \(C_{E}\) once by that dimension-only amount. Each outside
choice therefore gives at least the smaller of the two quantities
in (11). Average the outside choices. Since
\(\sum_{v} \omega_{v} E ( v ) = \widehat{L} + C_{E}\), the result is exactly

\[
 \boxed{\ \widehat L+C\ge c\min\{\tau-a,
                                  \ell_{\rm intr}(\tau)\}\ }.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.12}
\]

This proves \eqref{history:partial-child} for the actual partially
split fine child. No independence within one physical block, no
replacement of an actual class, and no assumed comparison of global
and local endpoint differences has been used.

\subsubsection{Terminal root removal preserves the actual source chord}

Subtracting the terminal root flag changes the global endpoint
budget, but leaves a positive budget for the zero-target intrinsic
score. We compare that score with the actual source representative:
a terminal prefix keeps its original type, and an ordinary reservoir
uses the newly selected count. Endpoint domination then transfers
the source wall without requiring equality of global and local
endpoint differences.

For a terminal local coordinate, let \(X_{0} , Y_{0}\) be the minima of the
zero-common-target intrinsic scores on its original lawful left and
right contexts. The zero-target endpoint score is

\[
 S_0(v_m)=\begin{cases}
 h+\overline C_m(v_m),&s_m=1,\\
 h+\overline C_m(v_m)+S_{{\rm good},m}(v_m),&s_m=0.
 \end{cases}
\]

Thus \(S_{0} ( v_{m} ) \le h + J_{m} ( v )\) at every endpoint, including endpoints
whose actual source root is positive. Equation (7), with its fixed
shift increased once, gives

\[
 E(v)\ge c S_0(v_m).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.13}
\]

The actual source representative endpoints satisfy

\[
 x^-\le C_P X_{0},\qquad y^-\le C_P Y_{0}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.14}
\]

with a uniform dimension-only \(C_{P}\). Here is why (14) holds for the
actual source construction, rather than being a new assumption.

For a selected terminal binary prefix edge, the source pair and its
local full type are fixed before the prefix-uncolored root target is
read. The reservoir lies in the unread ordinary suffix. At a numerical
zero-root count completion, the same prefix type has actual endpoint
minima in the common \(X_{0} , Y_{0}\) boxes, with the same local increment
\(\Delta\). The source's max-formula pair is no larger than these minima.
Evaluating the later root target changes no point, label or local
increment in this prefix block. This proves (14) for prefix edges.
The completion only verifies a finite count identity; no clock at a
virtual count is sampled or reused. These are exactly the admission
and sampling rules in Section~\ref{app:lower-details}.

For an ordinary suffix edge, \(X_{0}\) is comparable to \(1 + P\), where \(P\)
is the entire preceding physical length, and \(Y_{0}\) to \(1 + B\), where
\(B\) is the following positive-drift length. Let its positive reference
prefix and negative reference tail be \(A_{\mathrm{mean}} , B_{\mathrm{mean}}\), respectively.
They satisfy

\[
 cP\le A_{\rm mean}\le CP,\qquad
 cB\le B_{\rm mean}\le CB.
\]

The exact actual terminal output and own-scale central side counts give
for the weak block's actual increment

\[
 \Delta=B_{\rm mean}-A_{\rm mean}-x/r_m
                      +O(\sqrt{1+P}+\sqrt{1+B}).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.15}
\]

The incoming strict exit is included in the \(O ( \sqrt{1 + P} )\) term.
The actual root has \(x \le A \log ( 2 + V_{\mathrm{pre}} ) \le A \log ( 2 + P )\). Take the fixed
max-formula constant \(a_{*}\) sufficiently small compared with the
positive constants in these two reference comparisons. Then

\[
 x^-=\max\{a_*X_{0},a_*Y_{0}-\Delta\}\le C(1+P),\qquad
 y^-=\max\{a_*Y_{0},a_*X_{0}+\Delta\}\le C(1+B).
\]

Indeed the negative linear \(- cB\) pays the \(\sqrt{B}\) error in the first
maximum, and the negative linear \(- cP\) pays the \(\sqrt{P}\) error in the
second. The remaining \(\log ( 2 + P )\) term is at most a fixed multiple of
\(1 + P\); its sign in the second maximum is favorable. This proves
(14) directly at the actual root count, without changing that count.

Equivalently, if the weak block is the reservoir, its actual count
increase \(k = n_{*}^{x} - n_{*}^{0}\) is nonnegative and \(O ( 1 + x )\). The max formula
gives exactly \(x_{0}^{-} \le x_{x}^{-} \le x_{0}^{-} + w_{*} k\) and
\(a_{*} Y_{0} \le y_{x}^{-} \le y_{0}^{-}\). Since \(X_{0}\) is comparable to \(1 + P\), the
logarithmic root increase is absorbed in its left box. The direct
argument (15) also covers the case where the reservoir is another
suffix block. No incoming-exit or root reserve is added to \(Y_{0}\).

At a current endpoint with the terminal coordinate left,
\(S_{0} ( v_{m} ) \ge X_{0}\); at a right endpoint, \(S_{0} ( v_{m} ) \ge Y_{0}\). Combine
(13), (14), then use the exact coordinate marginal \(u\). The
root-separated global chord therefore satisfies

\[
 \boxed{\ \widehat L+C\ge
       (c/C_P)\bigl[(1-u)x^-+u y^-\bigr]\ }.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.16}
\]

This is the actual source representative chord, including the true
ordinary reservoir count. Its endpoint difference need not equal the
root-separated global endpoint difference. That equality is not
needed: (16) follows from endpoint domination and the same atomic
centered remainder. This proves the claimed comparison.

\subsubsection{Closing the weighted source-star estimate}

We assemble the local comparisons while reserving positive shares
for later use. Curvature pays synchronization spread; the allocated
source walls pay inward depth; endpoint interpolation retains
reference and good-count costs. A maximum-weight representative
converts the average to a single endpoint, and the terminal flag
transfer keeps the root coefficient one.

Let \(h^{*}\) be any of the actual fine comparison stars in
Section~\ref{supp:history-geometry}. Synchronize plateau cuts inside each
original physical block, retaining all names. Let \(D_{\alpha} , d_{\alpha}\)
be its spreads and mean depths, and
\(\Pi = \sum_{\alpha} ( D_{\alpha} + d_{\alpha}^{\gamma} )\).

Atomic reference curvature is uniform:
\(g_{g} '' ( d ) = - \kappa_{g} / ( d + z ) \le - \kappa_{*} / H\). Between the first and last
of a bundle's original cuts, its integer intermediate rank lies
strictly between its before and after ranks. The curvature excess
over the synchronous chord is therefore at least
\(\kappa_{*} D_{\alpha} / ( 2 H )\). The actual same-word excess differs from that
reference excess only on this spread interval. Named REG gives error
at most

\[
 C_H\vartheta D_\alpha+
 C_K[1+d_\alpha^\zeta+D_\alpha^\zeta].
\]

Choose the regularity slope below a fixed fraction of the curvature
constant and pay each \(D_{\alpha}^{\zeta}\) by another fraction of
\(D_{\alpha}\), plus a constant. Mixed length is Lipschitz under
synchronization, with loss at most \(C_{H} \sum D_{\alpha}\); choose
\(\epsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}\) below the remaining curvature fraction. This proves

\[
 F(h^*)\ge F(h^{\rm sync})+c_D\sum_\alpha D_\alpha
                        -C_K[1+\sum_\alpha d_\alpha^\zeta].
 \tag{\papertagprefix.17}
\]

There is no reference error on a whole unaltered group. All constants
are fixed before source construction.

In each physical block use the ordered-simplex endpoint weights.
The deterministic mixed term is affine in that chamber, while each
atomic same-word cost has its exact centered bridge. Consequently

\[
 F(h^{\rm sync})=a_m\mathcal S+\widehat L+
                                      \sum_\alpha\mathcal R_\alpha,
 \qquad \mathcal S=\sum_v\omega_vs_m(v).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.18}
\]

Equation (7) gives, with \(\widehat{E} = \widehat{L} + C_{E}\),

\[
 \widehat E\ge c_E\sum_v\omega_vJ(v)\ge0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.19}
\]

Choose \(\theta_{\mathrm{glob}} \le 1 / ( 4 H^{2} )\). For every weak proper coordinate,
(12) and its actual contracted source wall give
\(\theta_{\mathrm{glob}} \widehat{E} + R_{\alpha} \ge g_{0} d_{\alpha}^{\gamma} - C\).
On the linear branch of (12), REG pays the same inequality; its
distance \(\tau - a\) is at least \(d_{\alpha}\). Terminal weak coordinates
use (16). Strong coordinates have a fixed reference slope gap:
the expensive endpoint has reference charge at least \(cL\), so (19)
pays its distance from the cheaper endpoint, which is again at least
\(d_{\alpha}\). Reference-paid weak coordinates have charge at least
\(cL\) at both endpoints and are paid in the same way. In all linear
cases, first choose \(\vartheta\) small, then absorb
\(d_{\alpha}^{\zeta}\) and the desired \(\gamma\) curve into a fixed fraction
of the linear charge plus a constant. Thus simultaneously,

\[
 \theta_{\rm glob}\widehat E+\mathcal R_\alpha
                         \ge g_0d_\alpha^\gamma-C_0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.20}
\]

For proper and terminal weak coordinates choose the intrinsic source
contraction no larger than their proved chord-domination constant
times \(\theta_{\mathrm{glob}}\). These choices are made before sampling the source.
There are at most \(H^{2}\) coordinates, so summing (20) in (18) leaves
at least three quarters of \(\widehat{E}\). Combine with (17), and pay its
\(\zeta\) powers by a small fraction of the retained \(\gamma\) powers:

\[
 F(h^*)\ge a_m\mathcal S+c_J\sum_v\omega_vJ(v)
                  +c_D'\sum_\alpha D_\alpha
                  +c_\gamma\sum_\alpha d_\alpha^\gamma-C.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.21}
\]

The reference cost \(B ( h^{*} )\) may be retained as well. Concavity and
the rank-integral identity for synchronization give

\[
 0\le B(h^*)-B(h^{\rm sync})\le C_B\sum_\alpha D_\alpha,
 \qquad B(h^{\rm sync})=\sum_v\omega_vB(v)
                                    \le\sum_v\omega_vJ(v).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.22}
\]

Both inequalities are pointwise: rank profiles change only on their
spread intervals, and all reference integrands are dimensionally
bounded. Splitting the positive budgets in (21) therefore retains
\(cB ( h^{*} )\) together with positive \(J\), spread and inward-depth charges.

Choose the maximum-weight vertex in each physical block. Its product
\(v^{\#}\) is lawful and has weight at least
\(\omega_{0} = ( H + 1 )^{- H}\). Hence
\(\sum_{v} \omega_{v} J ( v ) \ge \omega_{0} J ( v^{\#} )\).
It remains to move the root coefficient from \(S\) to \(s_{m} ( v^{\#} )\).
This costs arbitrarily small fixed fractions of the two existing
budgets, plus a constant:

\[
 a_m|\mathcal S-s_m(v^\#)|
 \le\epsilon\sum_v\omega_v\overline C_m(v_m)
                 +\epsilon\sum_\alpha d_\alpha^\gamma+C_\epsilon.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.23}
\]

Here is a direct proof. Only the physical block crossing \(V_{m} / 2\)
can vary the terminal flag, unless an outside later terminal cut fixes
every flag at zero. In that crossing block \([ a , b ]\), put \(L = b - a\).
The selected endpoint marginal is at least \(1 / ( H + 1 )\), because the
whole block vertex has at least that weight. If it selects the farther
endpoint, its distance is at most \(H\) times the nearer distance.
Thus
\(| S - s_{m} ( v^{\#} ) | \le H d_{\alpha} / L\). If \(L \ge V_{m} / 4\), use
\(a_{m} \le A \log ( 2 + V_{m} )\) and
\(d_{\alpha} / L \le L^{- \gamma} d_{\alpha}^{\gamma}\); the coefficient
\(AH \log ( 2 + 4 L ) L^{- \gamma}\) tends to zero. Bounded \(L\) costs a
constant. If \(L < V_{m} / 4\), both endpoints of the crossing block lie in
\(( V_{m} / 4 , 3 V_{m} / 4 )\). Every contributing terminal endpoint has last cut
there, so (8) pays at least \(c_{\mathrm{ref}} V_{m} / 4\) in each reference endpoint
cost. This absorbs \(A \log ( 2 + V_{m} )\) with any fixed positive fraction
and a constant. These two cases prove (23).

Apply (23) to (21), with \(\epsilon\) below the retained positive
coefficients. Use (22) and the maximum-vertex weight. The conclusion is

\[
 \boxed{\ F_{\epsilon_{\rm mix}}^0(h^*)\ge a_ms_m(v^\#)
       +c_*[J(v^\#)+B(h^*)+\Pi(h^*)]-C_*\ }.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.24}
\]

All coefficients remain dimension-only positive constants. The root
has coefficient one. Equation (24) is \eqref{history:weighted-star-source}, proved from the actual endpoint
count support and the actual source walls, with the partial-child
and terminal comparisons supplied by (12), (16).

Together with the endpoint-forest and original-pivot proof, this establishes the source cost used by the target recoloring and posterior sections.


\subsection{Recoloring and weighted history costs}
\label{supp:target-history}

The source geometry must hold for every positive target word produced
by recoloring. We compare one accepted source with one of its images
on the same uncolored environment and root count. Exact atomic
increments telescope at regular endpoint banks; exceptional signatures
and movement strips pay their logarithmic discrepancies from already
retained geometric charges. Spare regularity margins then extend
the estimate to arbitrary target histories.
\subsubsection{Actual source/image pair and deterministic geometry}

Fix one full uncolored environment \(G\), the physical ordered KKT
profile, and the predetermined environmental targets \(y_{j} \ge 0\).
There are at most \(H - 1\) nonterminal plateaux. Retain one actual accepted
source word \(\omega_{0}\); its actual root count is the source construction's
count at

\[
 x=\sum_jr_jy_j,\quad r_j=\sigma_j/\sigma_1,
 \quad a_m=x/r_m.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

Let \(\omega_{y}\) be any permitted image of this word under the actual
uniform-subset recoloring kernel. Each nonterminal plateau \(j\) has one
macroscopic original local bank in a block of length \(P_{j}\) with

\[
 P_j\ge T_j/H,\qquad
 \min_{t\ {\rm in\ bank}}d_E(t)\ge\rho P_j
                              \ge\rho T_j/H,
 \quad\rho>0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

Every bank is a union of complete cells. A fixed cell mesh changes the
right side by only a dimension-only additive constant, absorbed by the
fixed plateau threshold. Banks for distinct plateaux belong to distinct
original physical blocks. In bank \(j\), recolor \(e_{j}\) copies of the
immediate child's first shallow fine name \(c_{j}\) to the current
block's eligible shallow exterior name \(t_{j}\). Set

\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 A_j&=\log S_j({\rm first}),\qquad b_j=u_jA_{j+1},\qquad e_0=0,\\
 b_je_j-A_je_{j-1}&=y_j+\delta_j,\qquad0\le\delta_j<b_j,\\
 e_j&\le A_e\log(2+T_j).
\end{aligned}
\tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\end{equation}

These are the actual integer transfers; the root and every uncolored
position remain fixed. All effective alphabets have size at most \(H\),
so \(A_{j} , b_{j} \le \log H\).

Fix any original history \(h\). Its lawful projections, star comparisons,
terminal spine and clipping, synchronization, and maximum-weight
endpoint representative depend on names, cuts and deadlines only.
They therefore produce the same \(h^{*}\), \(v\), \(D_{\mathrm{gap}}\), \(D_{*}\), \(\Pi\),
reference \(B\), and geometric \(J ( v )\) on this source/image pair. The
labels used to evaluate their information costs do change. This
distinction is essential.

Write

\[
 F_\epsilon^q(h^*)=\sum_lK_l^q(h_l^*)+
                     \epsilon\sum_lS_{{\rm mix},l}(h^*),
 \quad q=0,y.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

The mixed lengths in (4) are geometric and do not change with the
word. The weighted source-star inequality proved in
Section~\ref{supp:chord-comparison}, equation (24), is

\[
 F_\epsilon^0(h^*)\ge a_ms_m(v)+
                        c_*[J(v)+B(h^*)+\Pi(h^*)]-C_*.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

\subsubsection{Exact atomic changes, including the old target lists}

A transfer changes only the current plateau and its immediate child.
The child's incoming list loses the recolored original slot, so its
information is evaluated with the changed membership indicator.
Subtracting these exact information increments from the output
increments gives the three regular endpoint coefficients used in
the target telescope.

Changing one \(c_{j}\) to \(t_{j}\) changes the atomic outputs exactly by

\[
 \Delta Z_j=b_j,\qquad \Delta Z_{j+1}=-A_{j+1},
 \qquad \Delta Z_l=0\quad(l\ne j,j+1).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

At an ancestor plateau all its exterior names have expired on this
local bank; both changed labels belong to its only eligible compound
child. Its atomic information increment is zero. At a deeper plateau
\(l > j + 1\), both labels are outside its incoming fine alphabet, so neither
contributes to its atomic information. The immediate child's \emph{old
list loses this actual original slot}. It is not identified with its
source old list. Every atomic information is evaluated as a sum over
