original slots with its fine-membership indicator; the indicator is
zero when that slot does not route to that plateau. Thus (6) is valid
on the changed lists.

For the fixed endpoint history \(v\), atomic state \(\mathrm{full}\) means all
eligible exterior names remain in the compound-child cell; \(\mathrm{zero}\)
means none remains; other states are \(\mathrm{proper}\). All states are
constant on the original bank block. Directly subtracting
\(\Delta I_{l}\) from (6) gives the following per-flip increments in
\(\sum_{l} K_{l}\):

\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{parent full, immediate child full}&0\\
 \text{parent zero, immediate child full}&b_j\\
 \text{parent zero, immediate child zero}&b_j-A_{j+1}.
 \end{array}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

For example, in a full parent cell replacing its compound-child mark
by its exterior mark increases residual information by \(\log z = b_{j}\),
canceling \(\Delta Z_{j}\). In a full immediate-child cell, removing its
first shallow name decreases information by \(A_{j + 1}\), canceling
\(\Delta Z_{j + 1}\). In a zero cell its information is identically zero.
This proves every entry in (7). Deeper fine splits do not invalidate
these atomic calculations; the changed shallow name lies outside
every deeper plateau. The deterministic mixed term in (4) has zero
increment.

Every atomic residual-information coefficient is between zero and
\(\log H\). Only plateaux \(j , j + 1\) can change at this bank. Consequently
any endpoint per-flip increment is bounded in absolute value by
\(4 \log H\), and its discrepancy from the ideal
\(b_{j} s_{j} - A_{j + 1} s_{j + 1}\) by \(6 \log H\).

\subsubsection{Geometric charges for exceptional endpoint intervals}

The ideal transfer coefficient is determined by the two early flags.
When an endpoint bank's signatures disagree with that coefficient,
a proper, mixed, early-full, or late-zero charge pays at least its
square-root length scale. Since only logarithmically many slots are
recolored, a small fixed share of that charge pays the entire
exceptional bank.

Here \(s_{j}\) is the plateau's actual early/late endpoint flag, exactly as
in Section~\ref{supp:chord-comparison}. No monotonicity of the sequence of
flags is imposed. Unless the states and flags match one of

\[
 \begin{array}{c|c}
 \text{parent full, child full}&s_j=s_{j+1}=0\\
 \text{parent zero, child full}&s_j=1,\ s_{j+1}=0\\
 \text{parent zero, child zero}&s_j=s_{j+1}=1,
 \end{array}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

the endpoint has

\[
 J(v)\ge c_{\rm ex}\sqrt{T_j}-C_{\rm ex},
 \quad c_{\rm ex}>0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

For completeness, these are all the cases.

\begin{itemize}
\item If either relevant atomic state is proper, it is either bad
(retaining its eligible shallow name) or good (omitting it).
A bad row has reference cost at least \(\kappa_{*} P_{j} / ( 2 H^{2} )\) by
exchanging the shallow retained name and a deeper missing name.
The two comparison histories are lawful; their discrete second
difference is at least \(\kappa_{*} P_{j} / H\), and reference nonnegativity
pays half that amount. A good row contributes \(\sqrt{P_{j}}\) to
\(S_{\mathrm{good}}\). This includes the immediate child's earlier group;
its eligible shallow name is precisely \(c_{j}\).
\item A full parent with a nonfull immediate child is mixed on the
entire original bank block: a retained parent exterior lies in
the fine anchor cell while an immediate-child exterior is a
singleton. The length charge is \(P_{j}\).
\item If a full parent is early, its last cut reaches the bank block;
its early prefix has length at least \(P_{j}\). The clipped-prefix
reference lower bound pays that length. The same argument applies
to an early full immediate child, whose last cut also reaches this
old bank block.
\item If a zero parent is late, every later eligible parent name is
already cut. Its zero tail contains the original bank block and
pays \(P_{j}\).
\item If a zero immediate child is late, all its exterior names have
been cut by this old bank block. Its zero tail contains its entire
local total \(T_{j + 1}\). The plateau hierarchy gives
\(T_{j + 1} \ge V_{j} / C_{\mathrm{hier}} \ge T_{j} / C_{\mathrm{hier}}\), so this tail also pays at
the current bank's scale.
\end{itemize}

The clipped-prefix constant \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\) and hierarchy constant are
explicit in Section~\ref{supp:chord-comparison}. For large supported banks
one may, for example, take a smaller constant than

\[
 \min\{\kappa_* /(2H^3),\ H^{-1/2},\ H^{-1},
                  c_{\rm ref}/H,\ c_{\rm ref}/C_{\rm hier}\}
\]

in (9); bounded supported conventions only change \(C_{\mathrm{ex}}\). This
establishes (9) on original source reference geometry, independently
of which recoloring subset was chosen.

On banks satisfying (8), (7) is exactly the ideal coefficient. On
all other banks, use the uniform coefficient bound and (9). Because
there are at most \(H - 1\) banks and
\(\log ( 2 + T ) \le \epsilon \sqrt{T} + C_{\epsilon}\), for every fixed \(\alpha > 0\),

\[
 \Delta F_\epsilon(v)\ge
       \sum_{j<m}e_j(b_js_j-A_{j+1}s_{j+1})
                          -\alpha J(v)-C_\alpha.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

Sharing the single \(J\) budget among the finite exceptional banks
only changes the choice of \(\epsilon\); it creates no length-ratio or
product-gap condition.

\subsubsection{Moving from the endpoint to the actual comparison star}

The change in residual output is common to the comparison star and
its endpoint, so it cancels in their difference. Only flipped slots
inside a movement strip contribute. Reaching an interior bank forces
a macroscopic movement or depth, whose positive-power penalty absorbs
the logarithmic number of flips.

The residual output increment cancels when comparing the changes at
\(h^{*}\) and at its representative \(v\):

\[
 \Delta F_\epsilon(h^*)-\Delta F_\epsilon(v)
       =-\sum_l\bigl[\Delta I_l(h_l^*)-\Delta I_l(v_l)\bigr].
 \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

A flipped slot contributes to the right side only if it belongs to a
movement strip between an original comparison-star cut and its chosen
endpoint. Outside those strips the two relevant eligible partitions
are identical, so their mark coefficients agree exactly. Every
per-flip contribution to (11) has absolute value at most \(4 \log H\).

For a synchronized group \(\alpha\), maximum-weight endpoint selection
gives

\[
 |t_r^*-v_r|\le D_\alpha+(H+1)d_\alpha.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.12}
\]

Indeed its chosen side has marginal at least \(1 / ( H + 1 )\); when it is
the farther side its distance is at most \(H\) times the nearer one.
If a movement strip meets bank \(j\), (2), (12) force either
\(D_{\alpha} \ge cT_{j}\) or \(d_{\alpha} \ge cT_{j}\) for one of the bounded number of
groups in that physical block. Therefore

\[
 \Pi(h^*)\ge c' T_j^\gamma-C'.
\]

The corresponding \(O ( \log ( 2 + T_{j} ) )\) flips can be paid by any fixed
positive fraction of this charge, plus a constant. Sum over the
finite banks, as in the previous section. For every \(\alpha > 0\),

\[
 |\Delta F_\epsilon(h^*)-\Delta F_\epsilon(v)|
                                  \le\alpha\Pi(h^*)+C_\alpha.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.13}
\]

This proves \eqref{history:strip-transfer} using the original source
and image's atomic membership indicators. It remains valid
when a flip removes an original slot from a later old list. Nothing
asserts equality or monotonicity of those old lists.

\subsubsection{Exact cascade and the weighted target-star inequality}

After the exceptional-bank and movement-strip errors have been paid,
the regular transfer coefficients telescope. The terminal contribution
combines with the already selected root to produce the terminal
target. Thus every early target remains with coefficient one while
positive shares of all geometric budgets survive.

The finite coefficients telescope exactly:

\[
 \sum_{j<m}e_j(b_js_j-A_{j+1}s_{j+1})
       =\sum_{j<m}s_j(y_j+\delta_j)-s_mA_me_{m-1}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.14}
\]

Since \(r_{j} b_{j} = r_{j + 1} A_{j + 1}\), multiplying (3) by \(r_{j}\) and
summing gives

\[
 A_me_{m-1}=\sum_{j<m}(r_j/r_m)(y_j+\delta_j),
 \quad a_m-A_me_{m-1}
       =y_m-\sum_{j<m}(r_j/r_m)\delta_j.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.15}
\]

The last sum is bounded by a dimension-only constant: products lie
in \(( 1 / 2 , 1 )\), so \(r_{j} / r_{m} \le 2\), and \(\delta_{j} < \log H\). No gap or
length enters this bound. Combine (5), (10), (13), (14), and (15).
The proper terms \(s_{j} \delta_{j}\) are nonnegative. Choose
\(\alpha < c_{*} / 4\) for each of the two error allocations. A fixed part
of every geometric budget remains, and

\[
 \boxed{\ F_\epsilon^y(h^*)\ge
       \sum_{j:s_j(v)=1}y_j+
                  c_y[J(v)+B(h^*)+\Pi(h^*)]-C_y\ },
 \quad c_y>0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.16}
\]

This is the target weighted-star estimate on the actual source/image
pair. Each target has coefficient one. The terminal root is the
actual fixed root of that pair; (15) does not compare different root
tuples or different local minima.

\subsubsection{Image regularity and spare margins}

The information estimates for the image require named regularity
about the same original reference intensities. Interior recoloring
changes an interval count by at most a logarithmic amount. Every
affected interval has either macroscopic length or a deep endpoint,
so fixed spare slope and depth margins pay this change uniformly.
The order of constants below makes this choice independent of the
sampled word.

Let an original bank block have length \(P\) and its bank have depth
at least \(\rho P\). Every interval \([ s , t ]\) in that block which meets
the bank either has length at least \(\rho P / 2\), or an endpoint with
depth at least \(\rho P / 2\). Otherwise an interval shorter than
\(\rho P / 2\) with both endpoints within \(\rho P / 2\) of physical
endpoints cannot meet that interior bank.

For each individual fine name the count change on such an interval
is at most \(e \le A_{e} \log ( 2 + T )\). Choose fixed target REG parameters
\(\vartheta_{t} , K_{t}\) with spare margins over source parameters
\(\vartheta_{s} , K_{s}\). Because \(P \ge T / H\), one fixed length threshold
ensures

\[
 A_e\log(2+T)\le
 (\vartheta_t-\vartheta_s)\rho P/2,
 \qquad
 A_e\log(2+T)\le(K_t-K_s)(\rho P/2)^\zeta.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.17}
\]

Use the first inequality in the long-interval case, the second in
the deep-endpoint case. Intervals missing the bank have no change.
Thus the image retains the target named regularity about the \emph{same
unconditional original fine intensities}, with fixed margins.
If REG is centered at an empirical type, its rate changes by at most
\(e / P\); the resulting interval error is also at most \(e\) and is paid
by doubling the fixed allowance in (17).

Every routed atomic named count, including a count on a changed old
list, is a sum of at most \(H\) original fine-name indicators. Summing
their REG inequalities supplies atomic REG about the corresponding
original routed reference intensities. The same calculation applies
to each original physical group; it does not regard the new old list
as a clock sampled from the old source conditional law.

These constants can be fixed without a circular dependence. First
fix the compact profile, source count-box parameters, width floors
and the envelope floor exponent. The floors determine the entire
logarithmic target/transfer cap \(A_{e}\). Fix the positive reference,
mixed and curvature coefficients, global wall allocation and small
source contractions. Choose the target linear REG slope below the
geometric mean-gain thresholds and the source slope smaller again.
Choose source wall and refinement constants, including a finite
\(K_{s}\); then choose \(K_{t}\) larger by a fixed margin, allowing the
factor \(H\) for routed names. The larger depth-intercept constant
only enlarges additive constants in the geometric absorption
inequalities: it does not change their positive linear or inward
coefficients. Finally enlarge the fixed plateau-length threshold to
satisfy (17) and all count/bridge thresholds. The envelope's small
depth coefficient is chosen below the already fixed positive
history charge; its floor stays fixed. Construct the source
and the image only after all these constants have been fixed.

Hence requiring image REG does not ask the source to meet a smaller
intercept after it has been sampled, and does not change any physical
clock, fine prior, local point or root count.

\subsubsection{Arbitrary original target histories and classes}

The weighted target-star estimate now enters the canonical reduction
for every original history. Image regularity supplies the same
branching and mixed gains as on the source. Token summability handles
all original pivots. Since every positive image density has a retained
preimage, the estimate holds throughout the transported support;
the probability of its changed class is evaluated separately.

Apply the deterministic canonical reduction in
Section~\ref{supp:history-geometry} to the target word. The same original
history gives the same projection/spine geometry. Its actual cost is
the exact sum of target atomic costs plus projection delay and target
per-slot mixed contrasts. Image REG, proved above, supplies the
proper pure-cell gain, terminal off-spine gain and mixed gain about
the original reference profile. The same terminal floating reference
budget pays its anchor-comparison error.

Insert (16) in that reduction and pay the \(\zeta\)-depth errors by
positive \(\gamma\) inward charges and true delays. One obtains

\[
 \boxed{\ C_y(h)=R_y-I_h(\omega_y)
       \ge\sum_{j:s_j(v)=1}y_j+c\Lambda(h)-C\ },
\]

\[
 \Lambda=J(v)+B(h^*)+\Pi(h^*)+D_{\rm gap}+D_*
                                      +S_{\rm pure}+S_{\rm off}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.18}
\]

Theorem~\ref{forest:summability} gives
\(\sum_{h} \exp ( - \delta \Lambda ( h ) ) \le C_{\delta}\) for every fixed \(\delta > 0\).
This proves \eqref{history:target-geometry}, including original-pivot
summability, on every retained source/image pair.

The target density is the scaled push-forward of the
accepted source measure. Positive target density therefore has at
least one retained source preimage. The preceding argument works
for each such preimage and every original history simultaneously;
all geometry and targets are fixed by \(G\) and the history. Thus it
holds for every target word of positive density.

The target class \(Q_{h} ( \omega_{y} )\) uses the original eligible
per-slot signatures containing the target label. Recoloring can
change those signatures, so its conditional mass is evaluated anew
under the original label law. Section~\ref{supp:posterior-tensorization}
provides that disintegration; equation (18) supplies its arithmetic
cost input.



\subsection{Conditional label laws and comparison sums}
\label{supp:posterior-tensorization}

We finish with the finite probability argument used by the geometric
row. Complete-type conditioning controls the path events under uniform
residual multisets. A second disintegration coarsens the free count
banks and uses the diagonal binomial exit variables. These are
successive estimates under one original law, so a count bank and a
path block may belong to the same physical block.
\subsubsection{Finite statement}

The hypotheses distinguish three kinds of data: the fixed uncolored
environment, the labels revealed by the comparison class, and the
unread labels in free banks. Path envelopes are uniform after full
types and exact revealed assignments have been fixed. Exit bounds
instead use independent pair splits after coarsening; their centers
may depend on all the coarsened data.

Fix an uncolored environment \(G\): it specifies the original physical
blocks, every slot's position and eligible alphabet, and all deterministic
targets. In original block \(i\), let its \(n_{i}\) labels be independent
categorical variables with probabilities \(p_{i , c} \ge p_{*} > 0\); labels in
different blocks are independent. Write \(\pi_{G}\) for this finite product
law and \(K_{i}\) for the complete named count vector of block \(i\).

A comparison class \(Q\) is a positive-probability product of
per-slot signature restrictions. In each free path block \(i\), these
restrictions read only an endpoint-strip slot set \(R_{i}\); every other
slot in that block has the full eligible alphabet. Paid blocks may be
restricted arbitrarily.

There are finitely many disjoint count banks \(B_{j}\), belonging to
different original blocks, such that \(Q\) imposes no restriction on any
slot of \(B_{j}\). Each has two designated fine names \(s_{j} , t_{j}\), whose
original probabilities are bounded below by \(p_{*}\). Its uncolored number
of slots \(n_{B_{j}}\) satisfies

\[
 n_{B_j}\ge c_*T_j,\qquad T_j\ge T_*>0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

Let \(\eta_{j}\) be a function of the complete named count vectors only.
Condition on every label outside all designated pairs in their banks,
and on the pair-coarsened labels inside those banks. If \(M_{j}\) is the
number of slots coarsened to \(\{s_{j} , t_{j}\}\) and \(L_{j}\) the number of their
\(t_{j}\) labels, suppose the exact identity is

\[
 \eta_j=h_j+\beta_j L_j,\qquad
 0<\beta_-\le\beta_j\le\beta_+,
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

where every \(h_{j}\) is measurable in the coarsened \(\sigma\)-field and depends
on none of the unread split variables \(L_{l}\). Allowed exit bands are
\(\eta_{j} \in I_{j}\), where every \(I_{j}\) has length at most \(C_{R} R_{j}\),
\(R_{j} \ge 1\). Its location may depend arbitrarily on \(G\) and the coarsened
data, provided its defining restriction is measurable in the complete
type \(K\) and the fixed environment. These intervals
are the actual fixed-target carry bands, so this last condition holds.

An arbitrary additional type-only admission set \(T_{0}\) may be imposed;
in particular it may contain the original central fine-count windows.
In each free path block \(i\), let \(E_{i}\) be a local necessary path event.
Its deterministic parameters may depend on the whole complete type
\(K\) and all exactly revealed strip labels. Suppose that for every
feasible such type and strip assignment in \(T_{0}\) and the exit bands,

\[
 \mathbb P_{\pi_G}(E_i\mid K,\text{all exactly revealed labels})
       \le q_i(G),
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

where \(q_{i} ( G )\) is the same nonnegative envelope for every type and
revealed assignment. Local path events concern only the remaining
labels of their own block after these data are fixed. No factorization
of any accepting density is assumed.

\textbf{Theorem.} For any acceptance \(0 \le F \le 1\) supported on \(T_{0}\), all the
exit bands and all the necessary events \(E_{i}\),

\[
 \mathbb E_{\pi_G}[F\mid Q]
   \le C\prod_j\min\left(1,\frac{R_j}{\sqrt{1+T_j}}\right)
              \prod_iq_i(G).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

The constant depends only on the fixed number of banks and blocks,
\(p_{*} , c_{*} , \beta_{-} , \beta_{+} , C_{R}\). Free count banks and free path blocks may
belong to the same original block. The proof does not assume that their
accepted events are independent.

\subsubsection{Proof}

First bound the path probability at each complete type and sum that
type law inside the original class. This leaves the conditional
probability of the count admission. Then reveal the data outside the
free pairs, use maximum binomial atoms for the exit bands, and average
all pair totals. Neither stage factors the accepting density.

First condition on all exact labels in the strip sets read by \(Q\) and
on all exact labels in paid blocks. Denote this revealed data by \(A\).
The class restriction \(Q\) becomes fixed. Next fix the whole type
\(K = ( K_{i} )_{i}\). By the original product categorical law, the unrevealed
labels in each block are a uniform permutation of the residual multiset
of that block's type, and these residual permutations are independent
across blocks. This follows directly by writing the joint probability of
an assignment: its product probability is constant over permutations of
a fixed type; the type and revealed constraints factor over blocks once
their values are fixed.

The type-only event \(C\) comprising the exit bands and \(T_{0}\) is fixed
by \(K\) and \(G\). Thus (3), dropping
all extra accepting restrictions, gives

\[
 \mathbb E_{\pi_G}[F\mid K,A]
       \le\mathbf1_C(K)\prod_iq_i(G).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

Summing the original conditional type law and then the revealed
assignments compatible with \(Q\) gives exactly

\[
 \mathbb E_{\pi_G}[F\mid Q]
      \le\prod_iq_i(G)\,\mathbb P_{\pi_G}(C\mid Q).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

This finite disintegration uses independence only after the complete
type and exact revealed labels have been fixed. Summing them afterwards
retains the original coupled posterior law.

For the remaining count probability, drop \(T_{0}\), reveal the
labels outside the count banks, and coarsen each designated pair.
Let \(S\) be this \(\sigma\)-field. Since \(Q\) reads no bank
slot, it is \(S\)-measurable. Conditional on \(S\), the unread
splits have independent laws

\[
 L_j\mid S\sim\operatorname{Bin}(M_j,\theta_j),\qquad
 \theta_j=\frac{p_{j,t_j}}{p_{j,s_j}+p_{j,t_j}}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

Both \(\theta_{j}\) and its complement are bounded below. By (2), each exit
band admits at most \(C ( 1 + R_{j} )\) integer split counts, uniformly in every
band center and every other coarsened datum. The elementary maximum-atom
bound for a binomial with compact probability parameter gives

\[
 \mathbb P(C\mid S)
    \le\prod_j\min\left(1,
          \frac{C(1+R_j)}{\sqrt{1+M_j}}\right).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

Conditional on \(Q\), the labels in the fully free banks still have their
original product laws, independently for different banks. Consequently
the variables \(M_{j}\) remain independent binomials with parameters

\[
 (n_{B_j},\ p_{j,s_j}+p_{j,t_j}).
\]

The maximum-atom bound (8) is uniform in the centers \(h_{j}\)
from (2), so their dependence on outside labels no longer enters.
A Chernoff bound below half the pair-total mean gives

\[
 \mathbb E(1+M_j)^{-1/2}
   \le\frac1{\sqrt{1+\mathbb EM_j/2}}
        +\mathbb P(M_j<\mathbb EM_j/2)
   \le\frac C{\sqrt{1+n_{B_j}}}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

Since \(R_{j} \ge 1\), (1), (8), (9), and independence of the pair totals
imply

\[
 \mathbb P(C\mid Q)
    \le C\prod_j\min\left(1,
                  \frac{R_j}{\sqrt{1+T_j}}\right).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

Combining (6) and (10) proves (4). The maximum-atom bound itself can
be proved without a local limit theorem: Fourier inversion bounds its
mass by
\(( 2 \pi )^{- 1} \int_{- \pi}^{\pi} | 1 - \theta + \theta \exp ( iu ) |^{m} \,\mathrm{d}u\),
whose integrand is at most \(\exp ( - c m u^{2} )\) for compact \(\theta\);
the integral is \(O ( ( 1 + m )^{- 1 / 2} )\). \qed

\subsubsection{Diagonal exit variables}

The finite theorem requires a simultaneous diagonal identity, not
just a recursive description of the carries. The atomic transfer
coefficients provide it: a flip changes its own carry, while its
two neighboring output contributions cancel in every later carry.
Disjoint original banks then leave all split variables unread.

For the plateau products \(\sigma_{1} > \ldots > \sigma_{m}\), let
\(u_{j} = \sigma_{j + 1} / \sigma_{j}\),

\[
 \eta_l=\sum_{a\le l}\frac{\sigma_a}{\sigma_l}(Z_a-y_a).
\]

In the bank of plateau \(j\), changing its immediate child's first shallow
fine label \(c_{j}\) into its current shallow exterior label \(t_{j}\) changes
the grouped outputs by

\[
 \Delta Z_j=b_j=u_jA_{j+1},\qquad
 \Delta Z_{j+1}=-A_{j+1},\qquad
 \Delta Z_a=0\quad(a\ne j,j+1).
\]

For \(l < j\), this changes no term of \(\eta_{l}\). For \(l = j\), it changes
\(\eta_{j}\) by \(b_{j}\). For \(l > j\), the change is exactly

\[
 \frac{\sigma_j}{\sigma_l}b_j
      -\frac{\sigma_{j+1}}{\sigma_l}A_{j+1}=0.
\]

Hence every unread bank split changes exactly its own exit. Because
the original banks are disjoint, repeated single-slot changes prove
(2) simultaneously, with all \(h_{j}\) independent of every unread split.
This is the actual cancellation at Section~\ref{paper:ep-prefix-guards}, proved by the exact identity.
It is not merely triangular independence or a change to a selected-word
law.

\subsubsection{Direct construction of the path envelope}

The envelope must bound every feasible remaining type after the
class has exposed its endpoint strips. One joint exact-subset density
comparison handles both free intervals. Forward and reverse wall
monotonicities allow opposite Bernoulli parameters, chosen to cover
all types and permitted inverse transfers before the target is read.

The uniformity required in (3) follows from the
two-free-interval argument (Section~\ref{app:lower-details}), as follows.

Fix the complete type and exact revealed strip labels in one binary
projection. With \(n\) total labels, \(k\) binary successes, \(m\) revealed
labels and \(e\) revealed successes, the unread word is a uniform
\(k - e\) subset of \(N = n - m\) slots. Its success proportion is

\[
 p'=(k-e)/(n-m).
\]

The actual endpoint identity \(y - x = cP - an + bk\), with the allowed endpoint
box and strip occupancy bound, gives a deterministic interval
\(p_{-} \le p ' \le p_{+}\) whose endpoints depend only on the uncolored environment,
the allowed endpoint-box scales and strip width. If \(M \le N / 2\) slots
are retained jointly in two disjoint free end intervals, the exact
subset law has the following density relative to iid Bernoulli \(p '\)
on those slots:

\[
 \frac{\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(N-M,p')=Np'-j\}}
      {\mathbb P\{\operatorname{Bin}(N,p')=Np'\}}\le C.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

The denominator is the atom at the integer mean of a compact binomial
law and is bounded below by \(c ( 1 + N )^{- 1 / 2}\) by central Stirling; the
numerator is at most \(C ( 1 + N - M )^{- 1 / 2}\). This is one joint density for
the two intervals, including every allowed type and revealed assignment.

The necessary left signed wall is increasing in binary successes, and
the necessary reversed right wall is decreasing in them. Under the iid
reference the two interval restrictions are independent. Increasing
the first success parameter to \(p_{+}\) and decreasing the second to
\(p_{-}\) therefore bounds the joint event by the product of the two
corresponding iid wall probabilities. The density constant in (11) then proves (3) with one envelope valid
for every type in the subsequent sum. Dropping further refinements,
source regularity, and accepting restrictions only enlarges this
necessary-event probability.

For transported source words, the permitted inverse recolorings are
bounded by the predeclared uncolored range \(E_{\mathrm{max}} = O ( \log ( 2 + T ) )\).
Enlarge \(p_{+} - p_{-}\) and the signed speed to cover that entire fixed range
before defining the envelopes. Thus they remain uniform in the inverse
type and do not need to be independent of the final accepting density.
This proves the finite conditional inequality; the separate moment
evaluation of these envelopes still uses scalar persistence estimates.

\subsubsection{The uncolored bank-size condition}
The maximum-atom factors above are averaged over all original pair
totals, including zero. The bank-size condition concerns the uncolored
bank alone and is supplied by named regularity.

The required uncolored bank-size bound (1) follows on any nonempty
accepting support from its named regularity inequality: summing over the
finite alphabet gives an uncolored lower count on a fixed interior
interval of length comparable to \(T_{j}\). Choose the REG linear slope
smaller than one quarter of the compact lower uncolored intensity.
The endpoint-depth error is \(O ( 1 + T_{j}^{\zeta} )\) with \(\zeta < 1\); a fixed
sufficiently large length threshold absorbs it into half that interval's
linear expected count. If this deterministic uncolored condition fails,
the accepting density vanishes on that environment, so its posterior
row is vacuous.

\subsubsection{Normalization of the relative comparison sum}

The endpoint cost pays early plateaux, and the conditional class
estimate pays late plateaux. Multiplying the two inequalities includes
every uncolored plateau cost once. A bounded retained-word likelihood
then gives the relative row; the exact carry identity supplies the
last normalization needed for the arithmetic counting row.

In the geometric application of the finite lemma below, the classes
$Q_h$ are the complete-cell enlargements of
Section~\ref{lower:row}. Every information $I_h$, cost $C_y(h)$,
class probability and relative posterior uses that same class;
the original arithmetic multiplier and original index $h$ are
retained. After (16), the arithmetic row follows from
nonnegative class inclusion. No separate comparison of the two
information costs or the two conditional posteriors is required.

The source and target geometric estimates and the finite label
bound now combine by multiplication. The following finite lemma
records the resulting row estimate for Section~\ref{app:history-details}.

Fix an accepted anchor \(\omega\) in the same finite environment. For each
original history \(h\), let its geometric representative assign early/late
flags \(s_{j} ( h )\) and a nonnegative charge \(\Lambda ( h )\). Set
\(D_{j} = \exp ( - y_{j} )\), \(y_{j} \ge 0\), and \(D_{\mathrm{all}} = \prod_{j} D_{j}\). Suppose, with constants
independent of the histories,

\[
 C_y(h)\ge\sum_{j:s_j(h)=1}y_j+c\Lambda(h)-C_0,
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_\pi[F\mid Q_h(\omega)]
 \le C_1e^{c\Lambda(h)/2}\prod_{j:s_j(h)=0}D_j,
 \tag{\papertagprefix.12}
\]

and suppose the likelihood ratio between any two accepted words in
this environment is at most \(C_{R}\). Then the relative posterior

\[
 q_h^{\rm rel}
 =\mathbb E_\pi\left[
 F(\omega')\frac{\pi(\omega)}{\pi(\omega')}
 \mathrel{\Big|}Q_h(\omega)\right]
 \tag{\papertagprefix.13}
\]

satisfies, pointwise in the anchor and every original history,

\[
 e^{-C_y(h)}q_h^{\rm rel}
 \le e^{C_0}C_1C_R D_{\rm all}e^{-c\Lambda(h)/2}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.14}
\]

Indeed, the likelihood ratio is only needed where \(F ( \omega ' ) > 0\), so
\(q_{h}^{\mathrm{rel}} \le C_{R} \mathbb{E} [ F | Q_{h} ]\). Multiplying the two inequalities in (12)
then includes each plateau cost exactly once, since its flag is either
zero or one. This proves (14). For any fixed \(\delta > 0\), if the original
history sum satisfies

\[
 \sum_{h\ {\rm original}}e^{-\delta c\Lambda(h)/2}\le A_\delta,
 \tag{\papertagprefix.15}
\]

raising (14) to the power \(\delta\) and summing gives the asserted full
relative row, with constant
\(A_{\delta} ( \exp ( C_{0} ) C_{1} C_{R} )^{\delta}\). All type summations have already
been performed in the proof of (4); no fractional power is moved
through a conditional expectation here.

For completeness, the subsequent passage to the unnormalized finite
counting row has one additional exact factor that should be kept visible.
With the actual arithmetic history multiplier \(\Phi_{h}\) and its information

\[
 I_h=\log\Phi_h+
             \log\frac{\pi(Q_h(\omega))}{\pi(\omega)},
 \qquad C_y(h)=R_y-I_h,
\]

the finite class identity gives

\[
 \Phi_h M_h(F;\omega)=e^{I_h}q_h^{\rm rel}
                    =e^{R_y}e^{-C_y(h)}q_h^{\rm rel}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.16}
\]

Consequently the counting row is bounded by a constant times
\(( \exp ( R_{y} ) D_{\mathrm{all}} )^{\delta}\), rather than directly by \(D_{\mathrm{all}}^{\delta}\).
The exact carry identity is

\[
 R_y=\sum_j y_j+\epsilon/r_m
          -\sum_{j<m}(u_j^{-1}-1)\eta_j^y,
 \qquad -C\le\epsilon\le0,\quad \eta_j^y\ge0.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.17}
\]

Thus \(\exp ( R_{y} ) D_{\mathrm{all}} \le 1\); the extra factor in (16) is harmless.
The same identity bounds the full likelihood ratio: its only
word-dependent contribution in a fixed environment is the exit sum,
which lies in a fixed compact interval by strict exit support. This
gives the constant \(C_R\) in (13). The inputs (12) and (15) follow from
the source/target comparisons in Section~\ref{supp:history-geometry}
and the original-pivot sum in Theorem~\ref{forest:summability}.
For the arithmetic classes, replace $M_h$ on the left of
(16) by the smaller sum over $Q_h^{\rm arith}(\omega)$.
The same unnormalized row bound follows, with every original
positive pivot, zero pivot and within-cell multiplicity intact.


\section{Prime grids and harmonic mass}\label{appendix:arithmetic}
The probabilistic lower construction produces weighted label words
on complete cells. To convert their mass into divisor-box volume, we
need two arithmetic facts: enough squarefree prime selections at
every accepted occupancy, and a bound for the overlap of their boxes.
The first is a cellwise distinct-draw estimate. The second reduces
collisions to a finite family of triangular pivot constraints and
keeps the correlations of the label weight intact.

We prove these estimates and then carry the accepted family to the
prime grid at the fixed physical optimizer. The later subsections
assemble the transfer in the notation of the original harmonic sum
and give numerical choices for the grid constants.

\subsection{Prime supply, collisions, and the arithmetic grid}
\label{app:arithmetic-details}

Actual prime values are assigned only after the accepting density is
defined on complete cell words. This order lets us first prove an
arithmetic collision bound for any admissible weight. We then verify
squarefree supply on its supported occupancies and use H\"older's
inequality to recover one first power of the selected mass. The
remaining work is to compare the grid construction with the physical
profile, including its count bands and ordinary root.

\subsubsection{A fractional collision kernel for correlated label weights}
\label{sec:correlated-collision-kernel}
Two divisor boxes can meet only if their coordinate logarithms are
close. For a fixed pair of labels, successive maximal pivots turn these
closeness conditions into a triangular system in at most one prime
per coordinate. Integrating those primes produces a history factor.
The remaining label contribution is a power sum over history classes.

The accepting weight may couple different slots, so this class power
sum must be evaluated for the whole weight. The triangularization is
related to the unweighted argument of \cite[Section~7.1]{Kouk}; the
finite history construction below gives the weighted form needed here.

\paragraph{Cells, slots, and the arithmetic moment}
We separate the choice of prime cells from the label weight. Named
slots record the occupancy of each cell; permutation invariance will
later recover the exact factorial multiplicity of an arithmetic tuple.

Fix $k\ge1$, put $b=\log2$, and set
\[
 \eta_i=\frac{\log(k-i+2)}{k-i+1},\qquad \rho_i=e^{\eta_i},
 \qquad y_0=3\le y_1\le\cdots\le y_k.
\]
Use pairwise disjoint prime cells
$D_{i,t}=(\lambda_{i,t-1},\lambda_{i,t}]\cap\mathbb P$
for $1\le t\le v_i$, satisfying
\begin{align}
 &\lambda_{i,t-1}\ge3,\qquad
   \sum_{p\in D_{i,t}}p^{-1}\le\eta_i,\notag\\
 &\log\lambda_{i,t-1}\ge c_*\log y_{i-1}\rho_i^t,\qquad
 \left|\log\frac{\log y_i}{\log y_{i-1}}-\eta_iv_i\right|
       \le A_* .                                      \label{eq:cc-cell}
\end{align}
The constants $c_*>0,A_*<\infty$ are fixed. The elementary greedy
cells described below have $c_*^{-1},A_*\ll_k1$. Empty blocks with
$v_i=0$ are allowed; the last inequality still applies to them.

Fix integers $g_{i,t}\ge0$, and define
\[
 r_i=\sum_tg_{i,t},\quad R_i=\sum_{h\le i}r_h,\quad R_0=0,
 \quad G_g=\prod_{i,t}g_{i,t}!,\quad M_g=\prod_i\eta_i^{r_i}.
\]
The slots in block $i$ are $\mathcal B_i=(R_{i-1},R_i]\cap\mathbb Z$.
Assign its first $g_{i,1}$ slots to cell $1$, its next $g_{i,2}$
to cell $2$, and so on. Write $E_g(q)$ for the assigned cell of a
positive slot $q$, and set $E_g(0)=0$. No ordering of prime values
inside one cell is imposed.

A label is a map $Y$ assigning to a slot $q\in\mathcal B_i$ one
color in $C_q=\{0,i,i+1,\ldots,k\}$. Equivalently,
\[
 \mathcal P_{\mathbf r}=
 \{(Y_1,\ldots,Y_k):Y_j\subseteq\{1,\ldots,R_j\},\quad
                  Y_j\cap Y_h=\varnothing\ (j\ne h)\},
\]
where unused slots have color zero. Let
$F:\mathcal P_{\mathbf r}\to[0,\infty)$ be finite, independent
of all prime values, and invariant under every permutation of slots
within each assigned cell. No product structure is assumed for $F$.
It may depend on the entire occupancy vector $g$.

Let $\mathcal A(g)$ consist of squarefree tuples
$\mathbf a=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)$ having $g_{i,t}$ prime factors from
each $D_{i,t}$, with all prime factors coming from these cells.
Choose any named-slot representation $\mathbf p$ of such a tuple.
For labels $Y,Z$, put
\[
 Y\sim_{\mathbf p}Z
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \left|\sum_{q\in Y_j}\log p_q-\sum_{q\in Z_j}\log p_q\right|<b
                     \quad(1\le j\le k).
\]
For $1<P\le2$, define the arithmetic moment and its harmonic sum by
\begin{align}
 W_F^P(\mathbf a)
   &=\sum_{Y\in\mathcal P_{\mathbf r}}F(Y)
           \left(\sum_{Z:\,Y\sim_{\mathbf p}Z}F(Z)\right)^{P-1},
       \notag\\
 \mathcal W_F^P(g)
   &=\sum_{\mathbf a\in\mathcal A(g)}
                  \frac{W_F^P(\mathbf a)}{a_1\cdots a_k}.
                                                  \label{eq:cc-moment}
\end{align}
Within-cell invariance makes these definitions independent of the
chosen representation. Distinct labels correspond to distinct divisor
tuples because all the primes are distinct.

\begin{lemma}[Elementary cell supply]\label{lem:cc-cell-supply}
For every ordered cutoff vector above there are cells containing
exactly the primes $\max\{k,y_{i-1}\}<p\le y_i$ and satisfying
\eqref{eq:cc-cell} with constants depending only on $k$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
For one block put $u=\max\{k,y_{i-1}\}$ and $\eta=\eta_i$.
First greedily partition all primes above $u$ into successive maximal
finite cells whose reciprocal mass is at most $\eta$. This is
possible because every such prime satisfies $p^{-1}<\eta$ and the
prime reciprocal sum diverges. Let $\lambda_t$ be the last prime
in complete cell $t$, with $\lambda_0=u$, and let $q_{t+1}$ be the
first prime in the next cell. The mass $H_t$ of complete cell $t$
satisfies
\[
       \eta-q_{t+1}^{-1}<H_t\le\eta.
\]
Apart from at most $Q_k=\lceil2/\min_i\eta_i\rceil$ initial cells,
we have $q_{t+1}>Q_k$ and hence $H_t\ge\eta/2$.
The uniform Mertens estimate for $3\le u\le v$ gives
\[
 \sum_{u<p\le v}\frac1p
       =\log\frac{\log v}{\log u}+O(1).
\]
It follows that
$\log\lambda_t\ge c_k\log u\,e^{\eta t/2}$.
Consequently
\[
 \sum_{t\ge1}q_{t+1}^{-1}
 \le\sum_{t\ge1}\exp(-c_k\log3\,e^{\eta t/2})\ll_k1.
\]
Summing the deficits in $H_t$ now gives
$\sum_{s\le t}H_s=t\eta+O_k(1)$, whence
\[
           \log\lambda_t=\log u\,e^{t\eta+O_k(1)}.
\]
Now truncate at $y_i$: keep the nonempty cells intersecting
$(u,y_i]$ and give the last retained cell endpoint $y_i$.
Only the last cell can be incomplete, and its extra deficit is at
most $\eta$. The cumulative mass comparison therefore yields
$\log(\log y_i/\log u)=\eta v_i+O_k(1)$ for $y_i>u$,
also when there are no retained primes.
If $y_i\le u$, use no cells and note that
$\log y_i/\log y_{i-1}$ is bounded above and below in terms of $k$.
Finally $\log u/\log y_{i-1}\asymp_k1$; the estimates at preceding
endpoints, including $t=1$, give \eqref{eq:cc-cell}.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{All histories and their explicit partitions}
A history records the coordinate removal order and its pivot slots.
It also specifies which competitors can remain after each removal.
Writing this as a partition of each slot's alphabet makes the
compatibility relation explicit, including zero pivots and empty
blocks.

A history $h=(\sigma,\mathbf I)$ consists of a permutation
$\sigma=(\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_k)$ of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ and
integers satisfying
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-history-support}
       0\le I_j\le R_{\sigma_j},\qquad
       \text{all positive }I_j\text{ are distinct}.
\end{equation}
Assign a positive pivot $I_j$ to its slot block and every zero pivot
to block $1$. Define
\[
 \mathcal J_i(h)=\{j:I_j\text{ is assigned to block }i\},\quad
 n_i(h)=|\mathcal J_i(h)|,\quad J_i(h)=\sum_{s\le i}n_s(h).
\]
Let $\mathfrak H_{\mathbf r}$ be the histories in
\eqref{eq:cc-history-support} with $J_i(h)\ge i$ for every $i$.
Necessarily $J_k(h)=k$. No monotonicity of $I_1,\ldots,I_k$ is
imposed. Zero pivots can precede positive pivots.

Put $A_j(h)=\{\sigma_j,\ldots,\sigma_k\}$. For a slot $q$,
partition its color set $C_q$ by the following explicit equivalence:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-slot-partition}
 c\equiv_{h,q}c'\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 1_{c\in A_j(h)}=1_{c'\in A_j(h)}
       \ \text{for every }j\text{ with }I_j<q.
\end{equation}
Color $0$ belongs to none of the $A_j(h)$. Write $\Pi_{h,q}$ for
the nonempty equivalence cells. Declare $Z$ compatible with $Y$,
written $Z\equiv_hY$, if their colors lie in the same cell of
$\Pi_{h,q}$ for every slot $q$. Equivalently,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-union-compatibility}
 \bigcup_{s=j}^k\bigl(Z_{\sigma_s}\cap(I_j,R_k]\bigr)
 =\bigcup_{s=j}^k\bigl(Y_{\sigma_s}\cap(I_j,R_k]\bigr)
                         \quad(1\le j\le k).
\end{equation}
This equivalence follows simply by checking the membership of each
individual slot in the two unions. It includes repeated zero pivots,
empty blocks, and arbitrary ties among cell indices.

Define
\begin{align}
 \Phi_g(h)&=\prod_{i=1}^k
  \rho_i^{-(k-J_i(h))v_i-\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_i(h)}E_g(I_j)},
                                                     \label{eq:cc-phi}\\
 M_F(Y;h)&=\sum_{Z:\,Z\equiv_hY}F(Z),\qquad
 \Psi_{h,P}(F)=\sum_YF(Y)M_F(Y;h)^{P-1}.
                                                     \label{eq:cc-psi}
\end{align}
These are finite quantities determined by the occupancy and the label
weight. We sum over the stated history set, including any history
that is not generated by a pair; its nonnegative contribution only
enlarges the majorant.

\begin{theorem}[Correlated fractional collision majorant]
\label{thm:correlated-collision-kernel}
Under \eqref{eq:cc-cell}, uniformly for $1<P\le2$ and every weight
$F$ specified above,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-kernel}
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \mathcal W_F^P(g)
 \le C(k,c_*,A_*)\,
       \frac{\prod_i\eta_i^{r_i}}{\prod_{i,t}g_{i,t}!}
       \sum_{h\in\mathfrak H_{\mathbf r}}
                 \Phi_g(h)^{P-1}\Psi_{h,P}(F).}
\end{equation}
For the cells of Lemma~\ref{lem:cc-cell-supply} the constant is
$C_k$ only. It is independent of $P,\mathbf y,\mathbf r,g,F$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The proof has three steps. We express the moment on the original
named-prime measure, derive a linear collision bound for each pair
by triangular pivots, and interpolate on the whole measure before
summing the history classes. This order keeps both the original
factorials and the correlations of the weight.

\emph{The named-prime measure.} Every arithmetic tuple in $\mathcal A(g)$ has exactly $G_g$ named
representations by distinct primes in the prescribed cells. Hence,
writing $d\mu(\mathbf p)=(\prod_qp_q)^{-1}$ for this finite
named-prime measure and $\delta=P-1\in(0,1]$, we have the exact
identity
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-factorial-identity}
 \mathcal W_F^P(g)=\frac1{G_g}
   \sum_Y F(Y)\sum_{\mathbf p\text{ distinct}}d\mu(\mathbf p)
       \left(\sum_ZF(Z)1_{Y\sim_{\mathbf p}Z}\right)^\delta.
\end{equation}
The factorial therefore belongs to the original measure throughout
the argument. Its total mass is at most $M_g$ by
\eqref{eq:cc-cell}. For any nonnegative function $f$, finite-measure
H\"older (or concavity) gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-prime-interpolation}
        \sum d\mu\,f^\delta
        \le M_g^{1-\delta}\left(\sum d\mu\,f\right)^\delta.
\end{equation}
This includes $\delta=1$; if the measure has zero mass the desired
theorem is immediate.

\emph{Canonical pivots and prime integration.}
Fix a pair $Y,Z$. Its canonical history depends on the labels alone,
before the prime values are chosen.
Starting with all coordinate colors remaining, at step $j$ let
$U_j$ be the set of slots belonging to exactly one of
$Y_c\triangle Z_c$, as $c$ runs through the remaining coordinates.
If $U_j\ne\varnothing$, choose $I_j=\max U_j$, let $\sigma_j$
be the unique remaining coordinate containing that slot in its
symmetric difference, and remove $\sigma_j$. If
$U_j=\varnothing$, choose $I_j=0$, let $\sigma_j$ be the largest
remaining coordinate, and remove it. Continue for exactly $k$ steps.

A positive pivot belongs to
$Y_{\sigma_j}\triangle Z_{\sigma_j}$, giving $I_j\le R_{\sigma_j}$.
After that coordinate is removed, the pivot is in no remaining
difference and cannot be chosen again. Removing a coordinate at a
zero step can create exclusive slots, so later pivots may still be
positive. Every removed coordinate $c\le i$ has its pivot in the
first $i$ blocks, with a zero counted in block $1$. Hence $J_i\ge i$
and the resulting history is in $\mathfrak H_{\mathbf r}$.

The exclusive slots are exactly the symmetric difference of the
unions of remaining coordinate sets. To check this, use the fact
that each slot has at most one color in either label. If both of
its different colors remain, it occurs in two coordinate differences;
if exactly one color remains, it occurs in one. Maximality of $I_j$
therefore gives \eqref{eq:cc-union-compatibility}, also at $I_j=0$.

Fix the nonpivot primes, and keep the collision row at every positive
pivot step. Order both rows and pivot columns by those steps. A pivot
already removed has coefficient zero in each later row, while a
pivot's own coefficient is $1$ or $-1$. Thus the coefficient matrix
is upper triangular, with entries in $\{0,1,-1\}$ and dimension at
most $k$. Back substitution, or the finite unit-triangular inverse
expansion, bounds its inverse row sums by $2^k$. Discarding the
zero-step rows enlarges the feasible set. The remaining constraints
place every positive pivot logarithm in a product of intervals of
length at most $B_k=2^{k+1}b$, whose centers depend only on the
nonpivot primes and labels. We can therefore integrate over this containing rectangle; the
collision constraints themselves may still be correlated.

Chebyshev's prime-counting upper bound implies, for a fixed positive
$B_k$, that
\begin{align}
 \sum_{p\in D_{i,t}\cap[X,e^{B_k}X]}\frac1p
 &\le\frac{C_k}{\log\max\{3,\lambda_{i,t-1},X\}}
 \le\frac{C_kc_*^{-1}\rho_i^{-t}}{\log y_{i-1}}.
                                                     \label{eq:cc-pivot-mass}
\end{align}
For the first inequality, if the intersection is nonempty take
$L=\max\{\lambda_{i,t-1},X\}\ge3$ and contain it in
$[L,e^{B_k}L]$; then bound its number of primes by
$\pi(e^{B_k}L)$ and each reciprocal by $L^{-1}$.
Integrate first over this rectangle. We may then drop distinctness
and use $\eta_i$ as the mass of each nonpivot slot. Removing the
pivot masses from the nominal product loses at most $k$ factors
$\eta_i^{-1}$, a constant depending only on $k$. For the canonical
history $h(Y,Z)$, this gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-physical-kernel}
 \sum_{\mathbf p\text{ distinct}}d\mu(\mathbf p)
               1_{Y\sim_{\mathbf p}Z}
 \le C(k,c_*)M_g
     \prod_i(\log y_{i-1})^{-n_i(h)}
     \rho_i^{-\sum_{j\in\mathcal J_i(h)}E_g(I_j)}.
\end{equation}
Here a zero pivot deletes no prime. We inserted a factor
$(\log y_0)^{-1}$ for each such pivot; their number is at most
$k$, so this only changes the displayed constant.

The physical cutoff factors equal the factors in
\eqref{eq:cc-phi} up to the stated constant. More explicitly,
summation by parts gives
\begin{align*}
 \sum_i n_i(h)\log\log y_{i-1}
 &=k\log\log3+
   \sum_{i<k}(k-J_i(h))\log\frac{\log y_i}{\log y_{i-1}}\\
 &=\sum_i(k-J_i(h))\eta_iv_i+O(k+k^2A_*).
\end{align*}
Therefore the left side of \eqref{eq:cc-physical-kernel} is at
most $C(k,c_*,A_*)M_g\Phi_g(h(Y,Z))$.

\emph{Interpolation and the history sum.}
For fixed $Y$, partition the competitors $Z$ by their canonical
histories, and enlarge each generating class to all $Z\equiv_hY$.
Weights are nonnegative, so
\[
 \sum_ZF(Z)\sum_{\mathbf p\text{ distinct}}d\mu(\mathbf p)
                         1_{Y\sim_{\mathbf p}Z}
 \le C(k,c_*,A_*)M_g
            \sum_{h\in\mathfrak H_{\mathbf r}}\Phi_g(h)M_F(Y;h).
\]
Use \eqref{eq:cc-prime-interpolation} in the named-measure identity
\eqref{eq:cc-factorial-identity}, followed by
$(\sum_h a_h)^\delta\le\sum_h a_h^\delta$ for $a_h\ge0$.
The total nominal factor is exactly $M_g$, because the two powers
of $M_g$ add to one. Taking the fixed constant at least one makes its
$\delta$ power bounded by itself, uniformly for $0<\delta\le1$.
Summing over anchors with weight $F(Y)$ now proves
\eqref{eq:cc-kernel}.
Pivot choices are already recorded in the history sum. Removing the
corresponding primes consequently introduces no factor $g_{i,t}$ or
falling factorial, and $G_g$ remains the original multiplicity.
\end{proof}

\paragraph{The correlated partition term}
The theorem's label term has a useful exact interpretation: it is the
sum of powers of the total weights of the history classes. This is
also the form to which the relative-class estimates will be applied.

Let $\mathcal Q_h$ be the partition of the whole label space into
the equivalence classes of $\equiv_h$. This is the Cartesian
partition induced by the slot partitions \eqref{eq:cc-slot-partition},
but the weights of its classes need not factor. For every
nonnegative label weight, the exact identity is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cc-global-power-sum}
 \Psi_{h,P}(F)
       =\sum_{Q\in\mathcal Q_h}\left(\sum_{Y\in Q}F(Y)\right)^P.
\end{equation}
Indeed $M_F(Y;h)$ is constant on $Q$, with value
$\sum_{Z\in Q}F(Z)$, so the anchors in $Q$ supply the remaining
first power. If $F(Y)=\prod_qw_{q,Y(q)}$, and only in that
additional case for this factorization, the right side becomes
\[
        \prod_q\sum_{B\in\Pi_{h,q}}
                          \left(\sum_{c\in B}w_{q,c}\right)^P.
\]
For a Gibbs weight depending on aggregate counts from several slots,
we use \eqref{eq:cc-global-power-sum} with those correlations intact.
The product formula applies when the weight has the stated
product structure.

The theorem is pointwise in $g$. Thus one may multiply both sides
by any nonnegative occupancy test $T(g)$ and sum over $g$, allowing
$F=F_g$ separately at every occupancy. This preserves exactly the
nominal harmonic factorial mass $M_g/G_g$ and the same constant.
To obtain the lower bound for $K_k$, we next establish actual prime
supply at each accepted occupancy and bound the weighted history sum
on the right of \eqref{eq:cc-kernel}, with its required polynomial
factors. The occupancy measure in that sum remains the nominal
harmonic measure.

\subsubsection{Squarefree mass at every supported occupancy}
\label{arithdetail:supply}
The collision theorem is an upper estimate on a nominal cell measure.
The lower construction also needs actual squarefree mass. Because
acceptance can be rare, we compare the two masses at each supported
occupancy. A two-sided occupancy tube bounds the loss from repeated
prime draws, while the rapid growth of the cells makes the total loss
summable.

For a nonempty finite prime cell $D$, put
\[
 H_D=\sum_{p\in D}p^{-1},\quad p_D=\min D,\quad
 e_g(D)=\sum_{\substack{p_1<\cdots<p_g\\p_j\in D}}(p_1\cdots p_g)^{-1},
 \qquad e_0(D)=1.
\]
Drawing $g$ independent primes with probabilities $1/(pH_D)$ gives
the exact identity
\[
 g!e_g(D)=H_D^g\mathbb P\{\text{all draws distinct}\}.
\]
Conditional on $s$ distinct previous draws, their total probability
mass is at most $s/(H_Dp_D)$. If $(g-1)/(H_Dp_D)\leq1/2$, then
\[
 \mathbb P\{\text{all distinct}\}
 \geq\prod_{s=0}^{g-1}\left(1-\frac{s}{H_Dp_D}\right)
 \geq\exp\left(-\frac{g(g-1)}{H_Dp_D}\right).
\]
For a complete greedy cell with target mass $\eta$,
$0\leq\eta-H_D<1/p_{\rm next}\leq1/p_D$.
If $p_D\geq2/\eta$ and $(g-1)/(H_Dp_D)\leq1/2$, then
$H_D\geq\eta/2$ and
\begin{equation}
 1\geq\frac{g!e_g(D)}{\eta^g}
 \geq\exp\left(-\frac{2g^2}{\eta p_D}\right).
 \label{arithdetail:single-supply}
\end{equation}
This includes $g=0$.

Use only complete retained cells $D_{i,j}$, omitting the final
incomplete cell, and set $p_{i,j}=\min D_{i,j}$,
$\eta_*=\min_i\eta_i$, and
\[
 W_g=\prod_{i,j}\frac{\eta_i^{g_{i,j}}}{g_{i,j}!},\qquad
 S_g^{\rm all}=\prod_{i,j}e_{g_{i,j}}(D_{i,j}).
\]
The second expression is exactly the squarefree harmonic tuple mass,
since the cells are disjoint. Provided the single-cell capacity
conditions above hold, multiplication of
\eqref{arithdetail:single-supply} gives
\begin{equation}
 1\geq S_g^{\rm all}/W_g
 \geq\exp\left(-\frac2{\eta_*}\sum_{i,j}\frac{g_{i,j}^2}{p_{i,j}}\right).
 \label{arithdetail:product-supply}
\end{equation}

\emph{Occupancy bounds on the accepting support.}
We verify the cell capacity conditions uniformly on the accepting support.
Let $L_i=\eta_iv_i$, suppose the total count obeys $r_i/L_i\leq D_0$,
and each of its $h_i$ fine colors satisfies at cell boundaries
\[
 \left|N_{i,c}(t)-\frac{t}{L_i}q_{i,c}\right|
 \leq H_0+\theta\min(t,L_i-t).
\]
An empty block has count zero. Summing over colors gives, for the
uncolored cumulative count $G_i(j)=\sum_{s\leq j}g_{i,s}$,
\[
 \left|G_i(j)-\frac j{v_i}r_i\right|
 \leq h_iH_0+h_i\theta\eta_i\min(j,v_i-j).
\]
The left tube bounds $g_{i,j}\leq G_i(j)$, and the right tube
bounds $g_{i,j}\leq r_i-G_i(j-1)$. With
$A_0=(k+1)H_0$, $A_1=(\max_i\eta_i)(D_0+(k+1)\theta)$,
these two bounds give
\begin{equation}
 g_{i,j}\leq A_0+A_1\min(j,v_i-j+1).
 \label{arithdetail:two-sided-tube}
\end{equation}
An accepted labeling supplies the tube for its uncolored occupancy.
That occupancy is shared by all labelings and is preserved by recoloring. The named regularity bounds in the construction imply the displayed
linear tubes since $t^\zeta\leq1+t$ for $0<\zeta<1$.

\emph{A uniform distinctness ratio.}
Choose all retained primes greater than a fixed $Q\geq2/\eta_*$.
Each complete cell has mass at least $\eta_i/2$. The previous $j-1$
retained cells and the reciprocal-integer bound imply
\[
 p_{i,j}\geq\frac Q2e^{(j-1)\eta_i/2}.
\]
Let $q=e^{-\eta_*/2}$ and define
\begin{align*}
 B_1&=\frac{A_0}{1-q}+\frac{A_1}{(1-q)^2},\\
 B_2&=\frac{A_0^2}{1-q}
   +\frac{2A_0A_1}{(1-q)^2}
   +\frac{A_1^2(1+q)}{(1-q)^3}.
\end{align*}
These are the sums of $(A_0+A_1j)q^{j-1}$ and its squared-polynomial
counterpart. Thus
\[
 \frac{g_{i,j}}{H_{i,j}p_{i,j}}\leq\frac{4B_1}{\eta_*Q},
 \qquad
 \sum_{i,j}\frac{g_{i,j}^2}{p_{i,j}}\leq\frac{2kB_2}{Q}.
\]
Taking $Q\geq\max(3,2/\eta_*,8B_1/\eta_*)$ makes every capacity
condition valid, and yields pointwise
\begin{equation}
 1\geq S_g^{\rm all}/W_g
 \geq\exp(-4kB_2/(\eta_*Q))>0.
 \label{arithdetail:uniform-supply}
\end{equation}
Thus actual squarefree mass retains a fixed fraction of nominal mass
at every supported occupancy, including occupancies supporting a rare
accepting event.

\emph{The arithmetic size constraint.}
The right-hand tube also gives a fixed size bound. Write
$P_{i,j}=\max D_{i,j}$.
The $v_i-j$ later cells and the uniform Mertens difference estimate give
\[
 \log P_{i,j}\leq e^{C_{\rm M}}\log y_i\,
                         e^{-\eta_i(v_i-j)/2}.
\]
The right-hand tube in \eqref{arithdetail:two-sided-tube} therefore implies
\[
 \log a_i\leq\sum_jg_{i,j}\log P_{i,j}
 \leq e^{C_{\rm M}}B_1\log y_i.
\]
Choose the allowed size exponent at least
$A_{\rm tube}=\max(1,e^{C_{\rm M}}B_1)$.
Then the restricted actual mass equals $S_g^{\rm all}$ on every
supported occupancy, proving \eqref{lower:actual-supply}. The support
constants are fixed before this roughness and grid choice.

\subsubsection{Cancellation and one arithmetic first mass}
\label{arithdetail:first-mass}
We now combine the collision theorem with the relative-class bound.
The likelihood normalization cancels the selected costs, leaving a
uniform collision row for every accepted anchor. Squarefree supply
then bounds the first integral of the weighted box multiplicity, and
the row bounds its fractional higher integral. H\"older's inequality
converts these two integrals into the desired volume lower bound.

Apply the relative-class estimate of Section~\ref{app:history-details}
to the complete-cell enlargement $\bar Q_h$ of each original
arithmetic history. The multiplier $\Phi_g(h)$ and all original
pivot multiplicities are retained. Class inclusion and the exact
identity in Section~\ref{lower:row} then give
\[
 \sum_h e^{-\delta C_y(h)}(q_h^{\rm rel})^\delta
 \leq C\Big(\prod_jD_j^{\rm own}\Big)^\delta.
\]
The exact outputs give
$R_y=\sum_jy_j+\epsilon/r_m-E_y$, with
$E_y=\sum_{j<m}d_j\eta_j^y\geq0$ and $-C\leq\epsilon\leq0$.
Since $\prod_jD_j^{\rm own}=e^{-\sum_jy_j}$,
$e^{R_y}\prod_jD_j^{\rm own}\leq1$.
Also, with the actual class $Q_h(Y)$,
\[
 \Phi_g(h)\sum_{Z\in Q_h(Y)}F(Z)=e^{I_h}q_h^{\rm rel},
 \qquad C_y(h)=R_y-I_h.
\]
Multiplication proves the unnormalized row bound
\[
 \sum_h\Phi_g(h)^\delta
       \Big(\sum_{Z\in Q_h(Y)}F(Z)\Big)^\delta\leq C
 \qquad(F(Y)>0).
\]
Every original pivot is retained. A bounded clock discrepancy changes
the constant once per original cut.

With the collision row established, work on harmonic tuple measure
times Lebesgue measure and let
$f(\mathbf a,t)=\sum_YF(Y)1_{B_Y(\mathbf a)}(t)$ and
$Z_F=\sum_YF(Y)$. The weight is bounded, invariant under permutations
inside each cell and independent of the actual prime values there.
By \eqref{arithdetail:uniform-supply},
$\int f=(\log2)^kS_gZ_F\geq cW_gZ_F$.
If $t\in B_Y$, any other box through $t$ has its center within
$\log2$ of that of $B_Y$ in every coordinate. Thus, pointwise,
\[
 f^{1+\delta}
 \leq\sum_YF(Y)1_{B_Y}
       \Big(\sum_{Z:Y\sim_{\mathbf p}Z}F(Z)\Big)^\delta.
\]
Integrate and apply Theorem~\ref{thm:correlated-collision-kernel} and
the row bound to obtain $\int f^{1+\delta}\leq CW_gZ_F$.
H\"older on its support gives
\[
 \operatorname{meas}\{f>0\}
 \geq\frac{(\int f)^{(1+\delta)/\delta}}
             {(\int f^{1+\delta})^{1/\delta}}
 \geq cW_gZ_F.
\]
Its support is contained in the original divisor union. Summing over
the disjoint occupancies retains exactly the first power of the
selected nominal mass.

\subsubsection{Bounded perturbations with the physical optimizer fixed}
\label{arithdetail:frozen-grid}
The preceding arithmetic estimates concern complete cells. We compare
that construction with the physical profile in four stages: bound the
reference defects, handle the two exceptional endpoints exactly,
compare the finite endpoint scores, and compare their scalar exponents.
Count selection and root completion are addressed in the next
subsubsection.

Fix the geometric, scalar, count, regularity and occupancy constants, then
choose the roughness and cell grids. The initial roughness deletion
has bounded harmonic mass, and omitting the final incomplete cell
loses less than one fixed cell mass in each group. The coarse prime
sum comparison  therefore bounds the total resulting
length loss by a constant $R=O_k(1)$. Choose the lift above all source thresholds and above
$C_H(1+R)^2$. At the lifted physical vector $L$ optimize once and keep
its products, plateau partition, fine probabilities, selected edges and
ordinary suffix fixed. The complete-cell lengths $L'$ satisfy
$\sum_i|L_i'-L_i|\leq R$. Every original group remains present.

\emph{Reference defects.} Map each grid block affinely onto its physical block. This preserves
the order of activations, deadlines and eligible partitions of every
lawful history. All reference integrands are bounded on the compact
parameter ranges. Thus, uniformly over the full history space,
\begin{align}
 |\overline C_{L',s}(h')-\overline C_{L,s}(h)|&\leq C_HR,
 &\overline C_{L',s}(h')&\geq-C_HR,\notag\\
 |\partial_{s_i}J(L',s)-\partial_{s_i}J(L,s)|&\leq C_HR,
 &|J(L',s)-J(L,s)|&\leq C_HR.
 \label{arithdetail:bounded-defects}
\end{align}
Every fixed-coefficient reference charge inherits this additive
defect, including those for wrong names, old weak directions, mixed
times, pure lifetimes and terminal rank curvature. For instance,
the same two lawful competitors give
$\overline C_{\rm float}\geq c_HT_{\rm float}-C_HR$.
The old-mixture node equation has residual $O_H(R)$. Dividing it
by the old length gives the entropy error; multiplying by that
length in the old-group charge leaves an additive $O_H(R)$ error.
After the lift, a nonempty old collection is large, so
$V_{\rm old}\leq C_HT_{\rm plateau}+C_HR$ still has fixed-factor
strength. Compression and interpolation use $L'$ itself, with the
intercept only in their KKT lower bounds. The exact likelihood,
projection and carry identities do not use stationarity.

\emph{Exceptional endpoint rows.} For one plateau let
$m_{\rm ref}=\sum_g(\mathbb EH_g-r_gL_g')=O_H(R)$ and
$\zeta_g=H_g-\mathbb EH_g$. Its accepted exact output is
$Y=a_0-b_0=m_{\rm ref}+\sum_g\zeta_g$, so
\begin{align}
 C_v&=a_0-\sum_{g\leq l}\zeta_g+\overline C_v'
                         +\sum_{\rm proper}\nu_{v,g},\notag\\
 &=b_0+m_{\rm ref}+\sum_{g>l}\zeta_g+\overline C_v'
                         +\sum_{\rm proper}\nu_{v,g}.
 \label{arithdetail:exact-grid-endpoints}
\end{align}
For the all-zero template $C_v=a_0$ exactly. For the complete-deadline
template $\nu=0$ and $\overline C_v'=-m_{\rm ref}$, so $C_v=b_0$
exactly and its intrinsic cost is zero. Neither small endpoint is
enlarged by $R$.
For every other endpoint, an intrinsic charge absorbs the defect.
If its last positive time is strictly internal, clipped charging
contributes at least $c_H\min_gL_g$. If it reaches the end without
being everywhere full, a proper group contributes either a linear
bad-group charge or a displaced good-group square-root charge. Hence
\begin{equation}
 \overline C_v+S_{\rm good}(v)
 \geq c_H\sqrt{\min_gL_g}-C_H.
 \label{arithdetail:nonexceptional-charge}
\end{equation}
The chosen lift absorbs all bounded defects within the already
reserved fractions of these charges. The displaced named box is
retained; central uncolored counts alone would not imply this step.

\emph{Finite score comparison.} The finite context sets at $L,L'$ have identical indexing. Formal
perturbed scores may use $\max(0,\overline C_v')$, with the two
exceptional templates given their exact scores. Reference errors
are $O_H(R)$ and
$|\sqrt{L_g'}-\sqrt{L_g}|\leq\sqrt{|L_g'-L_g|}$.
Local exit scales are comparable. A change of early/late flag can occur only when
$|t_v-V_b/2|\leq C_HR$, where $V_b$ is the total earlier-plus-local
clock. The reference charge is then $\geq c_HV_b-C_HR$.
For large $V_b$, the plateau hierarchy makes this dominate either
addition to the score; for bounded $V_b$, use the positive score
floor. Thus the paired scores, and their separate minima, remain
within fixed factors.
The actual grid pair still uses
$\Delta_i'=c_iL_i'-a_in_i+b_ik_i$ in the max construction.

\emph{Scalar and ordinary factors.} At natural mean $\mu_i'=Z_iL_i'$, the centered parameter
$p_i^0=(a_i-c_i/Z_i)/b_i$ is unchanged; the gap-clock parameter
$L_i'/(\mu_i'+1)$ changes by $O_H(R)/(1+L_i)^2$.
The local Lipschitz estimate for $\chi$ and
$|\log T_i|\leq C_H\log(2+L_i)$ on the rare branch therefore
give a bounded exponent-times-log error. Score comparability gives
comparability of all binary factors, including threshold crossings.
Similarly $w_j'=R_j'/\sqrt{T_j'}\asymp w_j$.
The frozen ordinary suffix lengths change by $O_H(R)$; its numerical
factor is stable with $1+\max(D',0)$ in this comparison. If two
largest blocks are comparable, choosing either places the other on
a side and gives a fixed positive ballot factor. The numerical factor comparison covers this choice of largest block.
When the grid mean is negative by a bounded amount, the exact root
argument below supplies the legal endpoint pair required by the
probability theorem.

\subsubsection{Count bands and the exact root on the final grid}
\label{arithdetail:grid-counts}
The grid comparison must use counts that are realizable under the
original coupled count law. We translate the proper split bands and
multinomial boxes stage by stage, comparing their factorial weights
before sampling paths. We then solve the root equation at the grid
budget and check the ordinary endpoint pair separately according to
whether its prefix is empty.

For the same complete integer type, all grouped outputs and all
recursive exit coordinates change by deterministic $O_H(R)$ because
the count coefficients are fixed. Condition on the common pair-coarsened
field in the strict-exit construction. Each proper macro split remains
an independent $\operatorname{Bin}(m_j,p_j)$, with $m_j\asymp T_j$,
compact $p_j$, and the same coefficient in its exit; its effect on every
deeper exit cancels exactly. Band centers move by $O_H(R)$ without
reading any remaining split.

Begin in a fixed interior subband and translate each split by a
deterministic integer of size $O_H(R)$. The width floor exceeds
the finite lattice steps, so rounding leaves a fixed fractional
margin; that margin also absorbs the small width change. On the
central range, factorial ratios give logarithmic binomial weight
change $O_H(R/\sqrt{m_j}+R^2/m_j)$. The windows retain spare
width because $\sqrt{m_j}\gg R$. The same factorial comparison
applies to a finite multinomial thick box: its conditional center
and incoming count move by $O_H(R)$, and its fixed
$\sqrt{L_g}$ width stays unchanged. Make these comparisons
stage by stage, before sampling any path.

The natural uncolored means also change by $O_H(R)$.
For $|n-\mu|\leq C\sqrt\mu$, the logarithm of their Poisson ratio is
$n\log(\mu'/\mu)-(\mu'-\mu)=O_H(1)$.
Hence integration of the complete count measure retains its true
weights and mass $W'\asymp\prod_{j<m}w_j$.
Equations \eqref{arithdetail:exact-grid-endpoints} and
\eqref{arithdetail:nonexceptional-charge} supply the same strong-box
fractions and legal physical-score endpoint boxes. Terminal completion
is checked by the same thick-box calculation at every admitted root
count, retaining the original root clock.

\emph{The grid root.} The actual root count is the floor solving the exact grid equation.
At the same other counts it changes by at most $C_H(1+R)$ from the
physical-budget floor. Since $V_{\rm pre}\leq C_HU$ and
$U\gg(1+R)^2$, the Euler identity with its bounded residual gives
$|n_*'-\mu_*'|\leq C_H\sqrt U$. Its Poisson atom is comparable to
$U^{-1/2}$, uniformly over retained prefix environments and the
allowed logarithmic targets. All $n_*'+1$ gaps are then sampled at
this count.

\emph{The ordinary endpoint pair.} Let $P$ be the entire original length before the ordinary weak block
and $B$ its later positive-drift length. If $P>0$, the lift makes it
large; the physical relation $D\asymp P$ gives
$D_{\rm grid}\geq c_HP-O_H(R)>0$. The actual ordinary pair remains
in the boxes $X\asymp1+P$, $Y\asymp1+B$, so the ordinary exact-type
theorem applies. When $P=0$, there are no earlier plateaux and no terminal binary
head. The common targets vanish and $x=0$. The root equation
still fixes total risk to its bounded floor error, while the natural
grid mean may have either sign $O_H(R)$. For $B>0$, central counts
in the later blocks give surplus at least
$c_HB-C_H\sqrt B-O_H(R)\geq c_H'B$. Those counts and the root
floor determine the weak first-block increment exactly. One legal
endpoint is fixed and the other is comparable to $1+B$. For $B=0$,
the increment is just the bounded root floor, and both reserves are
fixed.

These legal pairs satisfy the all-reserve ordinary exact-type
strong-wall and REG theorem: their endpoint relation is exact, their
reserves are positive, and their marks, speed and gap parameter stay
compact. The theorem requires these conditions even when the natural
mean is negative. At central counts the other suffix blocks keep
their separated signed drifts. Conditional
on all counts, the original clocks and their constant-retention named
refinements give one joint kernel
\[
 \asymp U^{-1/2}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{(1+P)(1+B)}{1+M_{\rm weak}}\right\}
\]
when a weak block exists, and the saturated path factor otherwise.
The physical positive-tail identities identify this with the frozen
ordinary factor. Both sides use the same central root atom and the
same full-gap ordinary bridge; a later largest positive block makes
the path factor saturated.

\emph{Completion of the transfer.} All binary blocks now have supported central types, their actual grid
increments and positive common boxes. The curved-wall, regularity and
all-transfer estimates apply at the fixed physical products. Integrate
the mixed moments at a fixed full type and then sum the complete type
measure. The exact plateau powers and tilt identity give
\[
 K_k(\log3+L)\geq
 c_He^{-J(L';s)}\mathcal P_{\rm fixed}(L';s)
 \geq c_He^{-J(L;s)}\mathcal P_I(L).
\]
The first inequality is the first-mass transfer already proved; the
second uses \eqref{arithdetail:bounded-defects} and the factor
comparisons above. Products have remained fixed at the physical
optimizer throughout. All regularity and occupancy constants remain those
used to choose the grid; only the final length threshold and additive
geometric constants depend on its loss bound. Finally
Theorem~\ref{thm:ell-stability} compares the original vector with its
one fixed lift, as used in Theorem~\ref{lower:lifted}.


\subsection{Rectangles, root counts, and arithmetic multiplicities}
\label{supp:dyadic-arithmetic}
For later reference, we assemble the preceding estimates in the
notation of the original divisor-box sum. The upper transfer starts
with projected rectangles, makes the positive prime expansion, and
integrates one ordinary root. The lower transfer uses the correlated
collision row and pointwise squarefree supply to recover one first
mass. The formulas below keep their arithmetic normalizations and
counting ranges explicit.

\subsubsection{The arithmetic quantity and its exact counting range}

Let \(k \ge 1\), \(H = k + 1\), \(3 \le y_{1} \le \ldots \le y_{k}\), \(y_{0} = 3\),

\[
 L_i=\log\frac{\log y_i}{\log y_{i-1}},\qquad
 h_i=k-i+2,\qquad B_{\rm geo}=\sum_i(h_i-1)L_i.
\]

The first prime block is all primes at most \(y_{1}\), including 2
and 3; later blocks are \(( y_{i - 1} , y_{i} ]\). A tuple has squarefree,
pairwise coprime components supported on those blocks. Put

\[
 K_k=e^{-\sum_i h_iL_i}
       \sum_{\boldsymbol a}\frac{V(\boldsymbol a)}{a_1\cdots a_k},
 \quad
 V(\boldsymbol a)=\operatorname{vol}\bigcup_{d_1\cdots d_j\mid
 a_1\cdots a_j}\prod_{j=1}^k[\log(d_j/2),\log d_j).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

Koukoulopoulos \cite[Theorem~1.7]{Kouk} proves

\[
 \frac{H^{(k+1)}(x,\boldsymbol y,2\boldsymbol y)}x\asymp_k K_k,
 \qquad x\ge 2^k\Big(\prod_i y_i\Big)y_k.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

The convention $y_0=3$ agrees with the published logarithmic
normalization. Formula (2) applies throughout its displayed range.
It compares the full integer count with the squarefree harmonic
representation, so prime powers in \(n\), repeated factors in a
possible divisor, and the integer-count tail are all included in (2).

The positive size truncation in Section~\ref{paper:arithmetic-setup} applies to the full volume-weighted sum before any
probabilistic argument. Lemma~\ref{artrunc:lemma} shows that
for one fixed \(\tau_{k}\), this sum is at most twice its restriction to
\(a_{i} \le y_{i}^{\tau_{k}}\). The inserted-prime inequality is used on the
original volume, and the weighted logarithmic first moment is bounded
by \(C_{k} \log y_{i}\). Markov's inequality and a union over the \(k\) groups
give the factor two. The resulting actual prefix size bound
\(\log ( a_{1} \ldots a_{i} ) \le k \tau_{k} \log y_{i}\) supplies the full rectangles below.
The truncation thus supplies the rectangles before the profile is estimated.

\subsubsection{Actual projected rectangles}

With the normalized volume defined in
\eqref{upper:capacity-normalization}, the full divisor-box union has volume

\[
 I_0(\boldsymbol a)=e^{-B_{\rm geo}}V(\boldsymbol a).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

The cylinder estimates below use this same normalization and the
absolute probabilities of the original label classes, as in
Section~\ref{app:upper-details}.

Fix a size-truncated actual squarefree tuple and its uncolored prime
positions. For an active exterior set \(\mathcal C\), let \(E_c\) be the
original deadline and choose \(0\le\tau_c\le E_c\) for each
\(c\in\mathcal C\).
Reveal that name at prime positions right of \(\tau_{c}\), leaving the
actual descendant names compounded. Let \(Q_{\tau}\) be a cylinder under
the original fine categorical law, and let its probability be
\(\pi_{G} ( Q_{\tau} )\). Write

\[
 \Xi_\tau=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}(\tau_c-E_c)-\log\pi_G(Q_\tau),\qquad
 Z(t)=1+\sum_{x\le t}e^{x-t}.
\]

Each unresolved log-divisor displacement is at most
\(C_{H} e^{\tau_{c}} Z ( \tau_{c} )\). Earlier full coordinates use their original
size rectangles; compounded children use their original full-size
rectangles, without shots at their future deadlines. Their geometric
budgets cancel in the normalization. Lemma~\ref{updetail:cylinder-lemma}
therefore gives the cylinder
cap

\[
 \operatorname{Vol}_{\rm norm}(Q_\tau)
 \le C_H\pi_G(Q_\tau)e^{\Xi_\tau}
                         \prod_{c\in\mathcal C} Z(\tau_c).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

The original class probability in (4) cancels with \(- \log \pi\)
in \(\Xi\), expressing the deterministic rectangle width as a
likelihood-weighted capacity. Fixing a true ancestor route
multiplies by its probability and its fixed projected sizes;
the same absolute cap remains valid.

A fixed mesh of bounded density changes each shot by at most
\(e^{\Delta_{\mathrm{max}}}\). On a first mesh failure of a wall lowered by
\(A \log ( 1 + \mathrm{depth} )\), (4) gives \(e^{- h}\) times a summable depth weight and
fixed shot powers. The first-failure cylinders form an antichain in
the real reveal filtration: their original categorical probabilities
sum to at most one. Therefore their union has normalized volume at
most \(C_{H} S ( G ) e^{- h}\). This is the cover in Section~\ref{app:upper-details}, and is the basis of both
dual left walls and of the right first-hit cover. Its shots are then
integrated by finite occurrence partitions/Mecke, before summing
locations, as proved in Section~\ref{supp:causal-tower}.

\subsubsection{The exact positive prime expansion retains every tail}

Let \(H_{i} = \sum_{p \in \text{block } i} 1 / p\). Freeze a physical optimizer and its
rates \(Z_{i}\), products \(s_{i}\), and top product \(s\). Set

\[
 J=\sum_iL_i+\sum_i s_iV_i-\sum_iZ_iL_i,
 \qquad
 X=\frac{\sum_iN_i\log Z_i-\sum_i s_iV_i}{s}.
\]

Under \(P_{Z}\), prime \(p\) in block \(i\) has an independent count
\(\operatorname{Pois} ( Z_{i} / p )\). For every nonnegative symmetric function \(A\) of the
named lists, expansion of these finitely many Poisson atoms gives
the identity

\[
 e^{-\sum_iL_i}\sum_{\boldsymbol n\ge0}
  \prod_i\frac1{n_i!}
  \sum_{\text{ordered prime lists}} A\prod_qp_q^{-1}
 =e^{-J+\sum_iZ_i(H_i-L_i)}\,
                         \mathbb E_Z[e^{-sX}A].
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

Section~\ref{app:upper-details} proves the same identity. On distinct lists the factorials count each squarefree tuple
exactly. Extend (3) by zero off the actual squarefree size-truncated
support; (5) and the positive truncation give

\[
 K_k\le 2e^{-J+\sum_iZ_i(H_i-L_i)}
                         \mathbb E_Z[e^{-sX}I_0].
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

The geometric caps hold on the support of \(I_{0}\). Their
nonnegative numerical minimum majorizes the zero-extended integrand,
and can therefore be summed over unrestricted lists. The resulting
Poisson expectation includes repeated occurrences at a prime and
every count, while still bounding the original squarefree contribution.
Mertens' uniform difference gives \(| H_{i} - L_{i} | \le C_{H}\); hence the extra
factor in (6) is bounded above and below by constants depending only
on \(H\). Finitely many initial primes can alternatively be deleted
at the explicit fixed Euler-factor cost
\(\prod_{p \le Q_{H}} ( 1 + H / p )\) (Section~\ref{positive:section}).

For a deterministic actual prime bank, its cumulative harmonic
quantile map obeys \(| T ( u ) - u | \le C_{H}\). Push forward a homogeneous
Poisson process through this map, retaining its iid Gibbs marks.
This produces exactly the repeated atomic prime process. For a
positive jump test use pre-jump values; for a negative jump test use
post-jump values. A partial sum within a collapsed atom is then on
the favorable side. Only a bounded clock error changes the reserve;
there is no bound on multiplicity or total count. Section~\ref{positive:section} also keeps count-middle atoms
and shot insertion powers at their original plateau powers.

The unread root suffix uses completed equal-mass cells. Greedy cells
of target \(\eta = \log h / ( h - 1 )\) have mass at least \(3 \eta / 4\), and

\[
 p_{j+1}\ge e^{\eta/2}p_j,\qquad
 \sum_j(\eta-H_j)\le[Q_H(e^{\eta/2}-1)]^{-1}.
\]

Final/initial partial cells add at most two target masses per original
group. For all cells together the added tilted Poisson mean is
bounded. If \(\mu_{c} \le \mu_{c}^{*}\) and \(\Delta = \sum ( \mu_{c}^{*} - \mu_{c} )\), the exact
whole-law ratio is \(e^{\Delta} \prod ( \mu_{c} / \mu_{c}^{*} )^{n_{c}} \le e^{\Delta}\).
It bounds one entire nonnegative integrand, including its minimum,
root tilt and private powers. It needs no monotonicity under inserted
points. The original root is retained exactly by

\[
 X=\kappa+r\sum_i(w_iN_i-c_iL_i)
   =\kappa'+r\sum_i(w_iN_i-c_iU_i'),\quad
 \kappa'=\kappa+r\sum_i c_i(U_i'-L_i).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

Here \(U_{i} ' = L_{i} + O_{H} ( 1 )\). Section~\ref{positive:section}
gives this comparison for the complete Poisson law, including count zero.

\subsubsection{The ordinary root atom and ballot denominator are joint}

The ordinary factor comes from the root atom and the ordered-sum
ballot denominator at the same reservoir count.
Section~\ref{app:upper-details} proves the needed upper estimate for
all counts. On an unread suffix put

\[
 Z=\sum_i(w_iN_i-c_iL_i),\quad X=\kappa+rZ,
 \quad r=t/s,\quad 0<t\le s<1.
\]

Let \(M\) be a largest original block, \(U\) the total suffix length,
and \(A , B\) its earlier/later lengths. Condition on the outside counts.
Three actual rectangle caps and the prefix cap give

\[
 I\le C_H\min\{1,e^Z,e^{B_{\rm act}}W_{*,N_*},De^X\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

The capped ordered-sum rectangle \(W_{* , n}\) has the all-\(n\) tail

\[
 \mathbb P(W_{*,n}>e^{-\ell}\mid n)
 \le\min\left\{1,
 \frac{C_H(1+\ell)(C_1+Z_*+\ell)_+}{1+n}\right\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

Section~\ref{ordsumadjustment:section} derives (9) from the
\(A = 0\) part of \cite[Lemma~5.5]{Kouk}, with exact integer rounding and with
\(n = 0\) handled directly. The proof only needs the published flat and
crowding order-statistics estimates stated in Section~\ref{ordsumadjustment:section}. There
is no central-count assumption in (9).

At the same reservoir count, Stirling and the lower Poisson tail
give \(\sup p_{\mu} ( n ) \le C ( 1 + \mu )^{- 1 / 2}\) and
\(\sup p_{\mu} ( n ) / ( 1 + n ) \le C ( 1 + \mu )^{- 3 / 2}\). Outside a fixed-width root strip
there are at most \(1 + W / \log 2\) reservoir integers. The actual two
reserves in (9) become
\(1 + \ell + B_{\mathrm{act}}\) and \(C_{1} + Z + \ell + A_{\mathrm{act}}\). Their positive parts may be
enlarged to independent outside positive parts. Since
\(\mathbb{E}(B_{\mathrm{act}} )_{+} \le C B\) and \(\mathbb{E}(A_{\mathrm{act}} )_{+} \le C A\), averaging the two mode
bounds separately gives their minimum, with the ballot denominator
still present in the second bound.

Set \(H_{0} = ( - \log D - \kappa ) / r\), \(w = Z - H_{0}\). Layer cake in (8) gives
the exact integration weight \(D^{s} \exp [ - ( 1 - s ) \ell ]\). At fixed outside
