counts \(a = w + \ell / r\) is a translated lattice of spacing at least
\(\log 2\); \(a > 0\) and the endpoint cap imply \(a \ge - H_{0} - C\). Thus

\[
 \sum e^{-ta}\le C e^{-t(H_0)_-},\quad
 \sum e^{-ta}(C+H_0+a+b)_+
       \le C e^{-t(H_0)_-}[1+(H_0)_++b].
\]

Integration yields

\[
 \mathbb E[e^{-sX}I]
 \le C_HD^se^{-t(H_0)_-}(1+U)^{-1/2}
   \min\left\{1,
   \frac{(1+B)[1+(H_0)_++A]}{1+M}\right\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

There is no polynomial in a negative root deficit. A fixed polynomial
outgoing cap \(\min ( 1 , C e^{v} ( 1 + ( - v )_{+} )^{\beta} )\) changes the layer threshold
only to \(\ell + 2 \beta \log ( 2 + \ell ) + C\); its layer integral is finite uniformly
since \(1 - s\) has a fixed positive lower bound. Formula (10), then the
causal tower in Section~\ref{supp:causal-tower}, proves the root
portion of the upper cover. Completing the suffix changes (10) only
by the bounded translate in (7).

\subsubsection{Canonical rare banks and the unread suffix}

The bank selection is determined by the endpoint geometry.
Complete-reference nonnegativity in
Proposition~\ref{paper:ep-reference-positive} and the normalized
secants in Lemma~\ref{paper:ep-secants} give the weakness and
disjointness assertions of Section~\ref{app:upper-details}.

Output ordering is supplied by the numerical comparison in
Lemma~\ref{paper:ep-weak-order} of Section~\ref{paper:ep-reference}. If two weak full-input
edges have \(r_{1} > r_{2}\) but \(q_{1} \le q_{2}\), monotonicity in the lower secant
endpoint and the strict derivative bound give
\(\beta ( q_{2} , r_{2} ) - \beta ( q_{1} , r_{1} ) \ge 1 / ( 24 H^{2} )\), while weakness gives at most
\(1 / ( 48 H^{2} )\). Hence \(q_{1} > q_{2}\). This applies also to proper zero output,
because the secant lemma's hypothesis is \(b \ge 1\), not \(b \ge 2\).

If the rank intervals overlap, the lawful completion changes in
Section~\ref{app:upper-details} gives

\[
 X_2\ge1+\delta_H L_1,\qquad
 Y_1\ge1+c_H\min(L_1,L_2).
\]

Their persistence ratios are consequently bounded below on at least
one edge: if \(L_{2} \ge L_{1}\), the first edge ratio is bounded below; if
\(L_{2} < L_{1}\), the product of the displayed ratio bounds is bounded below.
Choose the fixed rarity cutoff below that bound. The intervals
\(( q_{i} , r_{i} ]\) of the retained rare edges are then disjoint. In particular
there is at most one retained edge per block, and a proper zero-output
edge is last. All discarded canonical factors have a fixed positive
lower bound; there are only \(O_{H} ( 1 )\) of them.

The deterministic one-end bank in Section~\ref{app:upper-details} has length
\(\ell = c_{\mathrm{bank}} L^{2} / ( 1 + X )^{2}\), belongs to the original current block, and
has \(\ell \le L / 16\). The endpoint geometry gives
\(1 + X \ge c \sqrt{1 + L}\), \(1 + Y \le C \tau \sqrt{1 + L}\) and intermediate local
length at most \(C Y\). Its exact projected rectangle yields a
necessary bank test with reserve \(h + C N_{\mathrm{intermediate}}\). Integrate the
intermediate word with its original mass; only its uncolored count
remains in the test. Its moments are at most \(C_{p} ( 1 + Y )^{p}\). The scalar
one-end upper then gives precisely the retained edge factor at the
original plateau power. In a proper zero-output edge the same statement
requires the explicit large-left-score hypothesis; the remaining
case is the hard two-wall cover proved in Section~\ref{supp:causal-tower}.

The current-plus-intermediate sets are disjoint by rank separation.
Shared count middles are separated by the proved covariance inequality
for a decreasing count weight and an increasing reserve, conditioning
on the other groups. No independent future acceptance law is used.

Terminal binary rare edges belong to the negative ordinary-drift
head. If a test reads counts in the selected suffix, trim its initial
intermediate groups and start at the first capacity at most its output.
The removed length is at most \(C_{H} \tau \sqrt{1 + L}\); the current negative
head pays the resulting mean change. With \(\tau\) fixed sufficiently
small, the largest original suffix block is retained,
\(U ' \asymp U\), and \(1 + D ' + A ' \asymp 1 + D + A\). Thus every mask is prefix
measurable for the final unread suffix. Section~\ref{app:upper-details}
contains this check; its terminal geometry inputs are part of the
independent deterministic estimate.

\subsubsection{A weighted collision theorem with exact original factorials}

The collision theorem of Section~\ref{app:arithmetic-details} applies
to any finite nonnegative label weight \(F\), invariant under permutations inside each assigned
prime cell and independent of prime values. It may couple all slots.

For occupancy \(g\), denote the original multiplicity by
\(G_{g} = \prod_{i , j} g_{i , j} !\) and nominal harmonic mass by
\(M_{g} = \prod_{i} \eta_{i}^{r_{i}}\). The exact named-prime identity is

\[
 \mathcal W_F^{1+\delta}(g)=G_g^{-1}
 \sum_Y F(Y)\sum_{\boldsymbol p\ {\rm distinct}}
 (\prod_qp_q^{-1})
       \left(\sum_ZF(Z)1_{Y\sim_{\boldsymbol p}Z}\right)^\delta,
 \quad0<\delta\le1.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

For each fixed \(Y , Z\), choose a canonical original history by repeatedly
taking the largest slot belonging to exactly one remaining coordinate
difference, or a zero pivot when none exists. Positive pivot rows and
columns in their removal order have an upper triangular matrix with
diagonal \(+ / - 1\). Its inverse row sums are at most \(2^{k}\). Conditional
on all nonpivot primes, the positive pivot logarithms therefore lie
in a product of intervals of length at most \(2^{k + 1} \log 2\). Chebyshev
gives each pivot harmonic mass at most
\(C_{k} / [ \log y_{i - 1} \rho_{i}^{\operatorname{cell} ( \mathrm{pivot} )} ]\). Only after this rectangle
containment are distinctness conditions discarded for an upper bound.
Zero pivots delete no prime and only insert a bounded first-block
normalizing factor.

Summation by parts identifies these factors with the construction's
history factor \(\Phi_{g} ( h )\), with error bounded by \(O_{H} ( 1 )\) since each
block has a fixed cell-budget defect. Finite-measure concavity on
the whole original prime measure in (11), followed by fractional
subadditivity over histories, proves

\[
 \mathcal W_F^{1+\delta}(g)
 \le C_H\frac{M_g}{G_g}
   \sum_h\Phi_g(h)^\delta
      \sum_YF(Y)\left(\sum_{Z\equiv_hY}F(Z)\right)^\delta.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.12}
\]

The original history sum already records each pivot choice, so
integration of a pivot introduces no falling factorial or extra
\(g_{i , j}\) factor. Uniformity as \(\delta\) decreases to zero follows
because the fixed majorant constant to power \(\delta\) is bounded by
that same constant.

\subsubsection{Pointwise squarefree supply and one linear first mass}

We use the squarefree supply estimate from Section~\ref{app:arithmetic-details}. In a complete cell \(D\), let \(H_{D} = \sum 1 / p\),
\(p_{D} = \min D\). Then

\[
 g!e_g(D)=H_D^g\mathbb P(\hbox{all }g\hbox{ iid weighted draws distinct}).
\]

If \(p_{D} \ge 2 / \eta\) and \(( g - 1 ) / ( H_{D} p_{D} ) \le 1 / 2\), successively excluding
the at most \(s / ( H_{D} p_{D} )\) mass of previous draws gives

\[
 1\ge\frac{g!e_g(D)}{\eta^g}
       \ge\exp[-2g^2/(\eta p_D)].
 \tag{\papertagprefix.13}
\]

Accepted named regularity and a fixed central total bound imply
\(g_{i , j} \le A_{0} + A_{1} \min ( j , v_{i} - j + 1 )\), with \(A_{0} , A_{1}\) fixed before
the roughness cutoff. Define \(q = \exp ( - \eta_{*} / 2 )\) and

\[
 B_1=\frac{A_0}{1-q}+\frac{A_1}{(1-q)^2},\qquad
 B_2=\frac{A_0^2}{1-q}+\frac{2A_0A_1}{(1-q)^2}
                          +\frac{A_1^2(1+q)}{(1-q)^3}.
\]

For retained primes greater than
\(Q \ge \max ( 3 , 2 / \eta_{*} , 8 B_{1} / \eta_{*} )\), greedy-cell growth gives
\(p_{i , j} \ge ( Q / 2 ) \exp [ ( j - 1 ) \eta_{i} / 2 ]\). Hence all capacity conditions
in (13) hold and, at every supported occupancy,

\[
 1\ge\frac{S_g^{\rm all}}{W_g}
       \ge\exp[-4kB_2/(\eta_*Q)]>0,
 \quad W_g=\prod_{i,j}\frac{\eta_i^{g_{i,j}}}{g_{i,j}!}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.14}
\]

The right-end tube and Mertens give the actual size bound
\(\log a_{i} \le e^{C_{M}} B_{1} \log y_{i}\). One fixed allowed size exponent covers
it. Thus (14) remains true in the actual size-restricted mass. The squarefree comparison is therefore multiplicative on the entire
accepting support.

The source and target history estimates first give the complete-cell
row. Enlarge each arithmetic class by rounding its positive
pivots to the right boundaries of their cells as in
Section~\ref{lower:row}. The multiplier and original summation
index are unchanged. Nonnegative class inclusion therefore proves,
on every accepted target word, the following row for the
classes $Q_h^{\rm arith}$:

\[
 \sum_h\Phi_g(h)^\delta
             \left(\sum_{Z\in Q_h^{\rm arith}(Y)}F(Z)\right)^\delta\le C_H.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.15}
\]

Its exact cancellation is retained: if
\(R_{y} = \sum y_{j} + \epsilon / r_{m} - E_{y}\), \(E_{y} \ge 0\), \(\epsilon \le 0\), and
\(\prod D_{j}^{\mathrm{own}} = \exp ( - \sum y_{j} )\), then
\(\exp ( R_{y} ) \prod D_{j}^{\mathrm{own}} \le 1\). The complete-cell class probabilities
and relative likelihoods are all computed under the original
conditional word law, as proved in Section~\ref{supp:posterior-tensorization}
and Section~\ref{supp:target-history}; the original-pivot sum is finite
uniformly by Section~\ref{supp:history-geometry} and Section~\ref{supp:chord-comparison}.

On harmonic tuple measure times Lebesgue measure define
\(f ( a , t ) = \sum_{Y} F ( Y ) \mathbf{1}_{B_{Y} ( a )} ( t )\). Because each box has volume
\(( \log 2 )^{k}\), (14) gives \(\int f \ge c_{H} W_{g} \sum_{Y} F ( Y )\).
If two boxes meet, their centers are within \(\log 2\) in every
coordinate. Consequently (12) and (15) give
\(\int f^{1 + \delta} \le C_{H} W_{g} \sum_{Y} F ( Y )\). H\"older's inequality on the support
then proves

\[
 \operatorname{meas}\{f>0\}
 \ge\frac{(\int f)^{(1+\delta)/\delta}}
           {(\int f^{1+\delta})^{1/\delta}}
 \ge c_H W_g\sum_YF(Y).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.16}
\]

This is one first power of the selected nominal mass. Its support
is contained in the original divisor union. Summation over disjoint
occupancies proves the lower arithmetic transfer; it does not raise
the entire rare probability to one terminal power. The chosen \(\delta\)
is a fixed dimension constant for this last step.

\subsubsection{Completion of the ordinary suffix}

Section~\ref{sec:bridges} supplies the ordinary suffix and root kernel.
Its count atom and path factor are constructed on one complete type. Conditional on all nonreservoir
central counts, the floor solving the actual root picks a
nonnegative central reservoir count. Its atom is of order
\(( 1 + U )^{- 1 / 2}\); all its original \(n + 1\) gaps are then sampled. There is
at most one nearly centered alphabet because the finite thresholds
\(\alpha_{h}\) strictly increase. Strong side blocks have outward path
probability bounded below. At the nearly centered block the actual
reserves are comparable to \(1 + h + B\) and \(1 + h + D + A\), by its exact
junction values and the central count errors. The ordinary ballot
lower gives precisely the bracket in (10). If another block is largest,
the separated drift makes both brackets saturated. The all-count
upper uses the same reservoir count atom and ballot denominator,
before its Poisson supremum.

For the lower source, the required stronger suffix kernel is Section~\ref{app:lower-details}. Its weak block is first;
complete balance gives \(D \asymp P\), where \(P\) is the full original
prefix before it. Its common endpoint scales are \(1 + P , 1 + B\), from
the actual complete reference. The logarithmic target changes only
the reservoir count by \(O ( 1 + x )\); if it is the weak block, the max
formula raises the left reserve by at most this amount and lowers
the right reserve while keeping its positive lower floor. Since
\(x \le A \log ( 2 + P )\), its scale is absorbed by \(1 + P\). The ordinary exact
strong-wall/REG theorem of Section~\ref{supp:single-block-source}, applied
to these legal actual endpoint pairs, gives the same path bracket.
All suffix clocks are independent after this complete count vector
is fixed. Genuine named refinement retains a fixed fraction on
every retained clock; it does not resample an accepted prefix.

The terminal completion of
Section~\ref{supp:profile-terminal-completion} retains the accepted
prefix terminal word and fills \emph{only the previously unread
suffix names} at the actual positive-root count. A zero-root count is
solely a numerical endpoint-box comparison. No clock at that
virtual count is sampled, and no positive-root early upper box
at zero-root scale is asserted. The early actual lower gains the
root entrance; the late intrinsic lower cancels it. The root atom
then appears once, linearly, before all prefix mixed moments.



\subsection{Complete cells, frozen physical optimizer and actual root counts}
\label{supp:dyadic-lift-evaluator}
The grid transfer can be read as a comparison of four objects: the
accepted cell-word density, reference costs, coupled count boxes, and
the ordinary root pair. We summarize each comparison here. Their
common feature is that the physical optimizer and the original
conditional word laws stay fixed.

\subsubsection{The complete-cell construction}

The construction in Section~\ref{app:lower-details} defines walls,
REG conditions, banks and costs directly on cell occupancies and
labeled slots. This is the appropriate discretization for fractional
moments: conditional averaging of an already accepted continuous
private mass would not preserve those moments. We instead compare
cell events with continuous events on every lift of the same word.

Cells have fixed maximum width \(\Delta_{*}\) and bounded boundary density.
For a positive-jump risk on a cell \([ l , r ]\),
\(Z ( t ) \ge Z ( l ) - c \Delta_{*}\); for the negative-jump risk,
\(Z ( t ) \ge Z ( r ) - c \Delta_{*}\). These inequalities hold for every lift
of the cell word to positions, regardless of cell occupancy. A strong
\(g d ( t )^{\gamma}\) wall changes by at most \(g \Delta_{*}^{\gamma}\), and its
contracted chord has a fixed compact positive speed. Boundary walls
therefore imply continuous walls with one fixed reserve allowance.
The continuous strong event is contained in the corresponding boundary
event. Boundary REG likewise implies continuous REG: expand or shrink
to adjacent boundaries, losing at most two meshes in length and a
fixed intercept. This uses no bound on interior-cell occupancy.

Free-bank envelopes are rebuilt as cell functions with endpoints
rounded to original boundaries. Exact subset and clock densities push
forward with the same upper bound; apply the preceding every-lift
wall implication. Their fractional moments have the same bounds as
the continuous envelopes. Fine named filling is uniform at each
fixed complete binary word on each lift; averaging a mixture of lifts
retains the pointwise fixed success bound. It does not average a
rare path probability before taking its power.

Conditional on total \(n_{i}\), the exact cell law is

\[
 \mathbb P(g_i\mid n_i)
    =n_i!\prod_c\frac{(|c|/L_i)^{g_{i,c}}}{g_{i,c}!}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

All cell costs and conditional private source masses are constant on
that fiber, so integration preserves \(q\), \(q^{\eta}\) and
\(q D^{\eta - 1}\) as identities. The original complete-type laws and
independent original block clocks are retained. Macroscopic banks
are unions of complete cells and retain their binomial/hypergeometric
estimates. The actual root floor is sampled once under (1), and its
ordinary suffix kernel is proved both ways by continuous comparison.

The uniform recoloring subset choice commutes with every within-cell
permutation. Its exact fine-word density calculation is unaffected.
Thus the final density \(F_{y}^{\operatorname{cell}}\) is bounded, cell invariant and
independent of the actual prime values assigned later. It is precisely
the weight allowed in the correlated arithmetic collision theorem.
The entire original-history proof applies on these boundary events:
the slot/output identities are count identities, and every boundary
wall and named regularity extends to every lift with only the fixed allowance.

\subsubsection{The physical optimizer is frozen through the grid change}

Section~\ref{app:arithmetic-details} chooses the
roughness/grid after fixing the geometric, count, regularity and occupancy
constants. It then chooses one sufficiently large lift. Optimize the
physical vector \(L\) once; retain its products, plateaux, probabilities,
selected edges and ordinary suffix on the grid vector \(L '\). Omitting
rough initial primes and incomplete final cells produces

\[
 \sum_i|L_i'-L_i|\le R=O_H(1).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

Map each grid block affinely onto its physical block. This preserves
the original activation/deadline order and every lawful named context.
Each reference integrand is bounded uniformly in the compact products
and alphabet. At a fixed mapped history, its integral changes by at
most \(C_{H} R\). The same bound applies to \(J\) and to each stationarity
derivative, because those expressions are linear in the block lengths
at the frozen products. Hence

\[
 |\overline C'(h')-\overline C(h)|\le C_HR,
 \quad \overline C'(h')\ge-C_HR,
 \quad |J(L';s)-J(L;s)|\le C_HR.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

All deterministic source/history comparisons acquire an additive
defect only. For an old entropy identity, divide its node residual by
the old length to compute the entropy error, and multiply back by
that same length in the charge; the total error is \(O_{H} ( R )\). Every
nonempty original group is large after the lift, so hierarchy and
the positive charge fractions remain fixed-factor inequalities.
Exact categorical likelihood, slot, output and carry identities do
not invoke stationarity and acquire no defect.

\subsubsection{The zero and full-deadline endpoints}

The two exceptional templates can have small endpoint costs, so they
are compared by exact identities rather than by an undifferentiated
\(O ( R )\) reference allowance. If \(m_{\mathrm{ref}} = \sum_{g} ( \mathbb{E} H_{g} - r_{g} L_{g} ' )\), the exact endpoint rows are

\[
 C_v=a_0-\sum_{g\le l}\zeta_g+\overline C_v'
                   +\sum_{\rm proper}\nu_{v,g}
   =b_0+m_{\rm ref}+\sum_{g>l}\zeta_g+\overline C_v'
                   +\sum_{\rm proper}\nu_{v,g}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

For the all-zero template, \(C_{v} = a_{0}\) exactly. For the complete-deadline
template, \(\nu = 0\) and \(\overline{C}_{v} ' = - m_{\mathrm{ref}}\), so \(C_{v} = b_{0}\) exactly and its
intrinsic cost is zero. No grid defect is added to either small
endpoint.

Every other endpoint has its own charge. If its last positive time
is an internal deadline, reference clipping gives at least
\(c_{H} \min_{i} L_{i}\). If it reaches the end but is not everywhere full,
an original group is proper: a bad group gives a linear charge,
and a displaced good group gives a square-root charge. Thus

\[
 \overline C_v+S_{\rm good}(v)
    \ge c_H\sqrt{\min_iL_i}-C_H.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

Choose the final lift so that the unused fraction of (5) pays
\(C_{H} R\) from (3). The displaced named count box is retained. It is this named displacement, in addition to central uncolored
totals, that supplies the square-root charge in (5).

The finite context sets on \(L\) and \(L '\) have identical indexing.
Square-root terms change by at most \(\sqrt{| L_{g} ' - L_{g} |}\). If an
early/late flag changes, its last positive time is within \(C_{H} R\)
of $V_b/2$, the midpoint of the total earlier-plus-local clock. The
clipped reference is then at least $c_HV_b-C_HR$ and, by the plateau
hierarchy, dominates both possible additions to the score.
The exceptional templates do not change flags. Therefore every
paired score, and its separate minimum, is comparable to the
physical one. The actual grid pair still uses its exact increment
\(\Delta_{i} ' = c_{i} L_{i} ' - a_{i} n_{i} + b_{i} k_{i}\) in the max construction.

\subsubsection{The grid count boxes and the root are actual counts}

Condition on the common pair-coarsened field. The original proper
macro splits remain independent \(\operatorname{Bin} ( m_{j} , p_{j} )\) with \(m_{j} \asymp T_{j}\)
and compact \(p_{j}\); their effect on every deeper exit cancels by the
same count identity. Grid band centers shift by \(O_{H} ( R )\) without
reading any unread split. Translate a central interior subband by
the nearest deterministic integer. The fixed width floor only needs
to exceed the finite lattice step, not the magnitude of the translate.
The factorial ratio on a central range is

\[
 \log\frac{p_{m,p}(n+u)}{p_{m,p}(n)}
       =O_H(R/\sqrt m+R^2/m),\qquad |u|=O_H(R).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

After the lift \(\sqrt{m}\gg R\), so these are feasible central bands with
unchanged fixed margins and comparable mass. The same elementary
factorial calculation treats every finite multinomial thick box,
before any path is sampled. Means change by \(O_{H} ( R )\), and the
central Poisson ratio \(n \log ( \mu ' / \mu ) - ( \mu ' - \mu )\) is bounded. Thus the
whole coupled count measure retains mass comparable to
\(\prod_{j} w_{j}\), and the earlier complete-type path proofs apply at
the frozen physical products.

The reservoir floor solves the exact grid root equation. Relative
to the physical floor it changes by at most \(C_{H} ( 1 + R )\). Its distance
from its own natural mean is at most \(C_{H} \sqrt{U}\), using the Euler
identity with bounded residual and \(V_{\mathrm{pre}} \le C_{H} U\). Choosing
\(U\gg (1+R)^2\) makes it nonnegative and central; its true Poisson atom
is comparable to \(U^{- 1 / 2}\). All its original gaps are sampled at
this actual count.

For the ordinary weak block let \(P\) be the whole preceding length
and \(B\) its later positive-drift length. If \(P > 0\), it is large after
the lift and \(D_{\mathrm{grid}} \ge c_{H} P - C_{H} R > 0\). Its actual legal pair still has
scales \(1 + P , 1 + B\). If \(P = 0\), there is no prefix and the common target
is exactly zero. The root sets total risk to its bounded floor
error, even when the nominal grid drift is negative by \(O_{H} ( R )\).
If \(B > 0\), its separated positive drift is at least
\(c_{H} B - C_{H} \sqrt{B} - C_{H} R \ge c_{H} ' B\). The weak block's actual endpoint
increment is determined by these actual counts and the root floor:
one endpoint is fixed and the other is comparable to \(1 + B\). If
\(B = 0\), both endpoints are fixed. The exact-type strong ordinary
bridge theorem applies directly to these pairs; it needs positive
legal endpoints and compact speed/gap parameters, not a
nonnegative nominal mean.

Consequently the grid source kernel is
\(U^{- 1 / 2} \min ( 1 , ( 1 + P ) ( 1 + B ) / ( 1 + M_{\mathrm{weak}} ) )\) when a weak block exists,
and the bracket is saturated otherwise. A later largest positive
block also saturates it. This is the frozen physical ordinary
factor. Combined with the per-type mixed moments and the
linear first-mass transfer of Section~\ref{supp:dyadic-arithmetic}, it gives
the fixed-lift lower at the physical profile, with constants depending
on \(H\) only. The rounded cell vector uses the original physical optimizer.

\subsubsection{Stability of the original harmonic sum, including zero axes}

The stability argument of Section~\ref{paper:assembly} compares the
original harmonic sums directly by removing primes whose block
membership changes and then reinserting them.
For two vectors \(\ell , \ell '\), put

\[
 \delta_i=\ell_i'-\ell_i,\quad
 D=\sum_{i=1}^k\left|\sum_{h\le i}\delta_h\right|,
 \quad
 A=\sum_i h_i|\delta_i|+H(D+2kC_M).
\]

Every prime whose block membership changes is in the union of the
\(k\) intervals between the old and new cutoffs. Its harmonic mass
is at most \(D + 2 k C_{M}\). Remove these primes in both configurations
and keep the common unnormalized volume sum \(S_{*}\). It is positive
because the empty tuple contributes \(( \log 2 )^{k}\). Inserting a prime
in block \(i\) makes at most \(h_{i}\) translates of the old union,
one unchanged. Therefore, for each of the two full sums,

\[
 S_*\le S_j\le S_*\prod_{p\in\mathcal B}(1+H/p)
                 \le S_*e^{H(D+2kC_M)}.
\]

The ratio \(S ' / S\) lies between the last exponential and its reciprocal;
its exponent is not doubled. Multiplying by the exact normalizing
ratio gives

\[
 e^{-A}K_k(\ell)\le K_k(\ell')\le e^AK_k(\ell).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

This proof allows coincident cutoffs and zero lengths. It changes no
integer-count \(x\) range, since it compares only the arithmetic \(K\).

For \(L_{i}^{\lambda} = \max ( L_{i} , \lambda )\), (7) has exponent at most
\(B_{k} \lambda + C_{0} ( k )\), where
\(B_{k} = k ( k^{2} + 3 k + 4 ) / 2\) and \(C_{0} = 2 kHC_{M}\). Fix the single numerical constant $\Lambda_k$ specified in the
full quantitative estimates, put $L_i^*=\max(L_i,\Lambda_k)$ and
$\ell_i^*=L_i^*+\log3$. The positive-core upper and the explicit
fixed-lift lower, both proved at this same vector, give

\[
 c_k\Psi_k(\mathbf L^*)\le K_k(\boldsymbol\ell^*)
 \le C_k\Psi_k(\mathbf L^*).
\]

Combining these bounds with (7) gives

\[
 c_ke^{-B_k\Lambda_k-C_0(k)}\Psi_k(\mathbf L^*)
 \le K_k(\boldsymbol\ell)
 \le C_ke^{B_k\Lambda_k+C_0(k)}\Psi_k(\mathbf L^*).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

Both displayed exponential factors depend only on $k$. The final
rule therefore evaluates the raw profile at this one fixed lift,
including vectors on equality faces. The complete scalar-inverse evaluator
is proved in Appendix~\ref{supp:ordered-saddle-scalar-elimination}.


\subsection{Numerical harmonic estimates, complete cells and squarefree supply}
\label{supp:explicit-arithmetic-grid}
We finish with numerical versions of the harmonic and squarefree
estimates. The elementary Mertens difference controls the clock
defect; geometric cell growth makes that defect and the distinctness
loss summable. Once the occupancy tube constants are fixed, the
roughness cutoff below determines every grid constant used in the
quantitative lift.

Put \(H = k + 1\),

\[
 \eta_i=\frac{\log(k-i+2)}{k-i+1},\quad
 \eta_* =\min_i\eta_i,\quad q=e^{-\eta_*/2}.
\]

For \(H \ge 2\), \(1 / ( 2 H ) \le \eta_{*} \le \eta_{i} < 1\).

\subsubsection{An elementary numerical Mertens difference}

For every real \(x \ge 3\),

\[
 -1\le\sum_{p\le x}p^{-1}-\log\log x\le17.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

Thus \(C_{M} = 40\) is safe in every two-end Mertens difference used in
the harmonic estimate. Here is a proof that requires no numerical asymptotic
prime theorem. If \(N \ge 2\) is an integer, the primes in
\(( \lceil N / 2 \rceil , N ]\) divide \(\binom{N}{\lfloor N / 2 \rfloor} \le 2^{N}\).
Iteration gives \(\theta ( N ) \le 3 N \log 2 < 4 N\), hence \(\theta ( x ) \le 4 x\).
Partial summation implies

\[
 \sum_{p\le x}\frac{\log p}{p}\le4+4\log x,
 \qquad
 \sum_{p\le x}\frac{\log p}{p-1}\le8+8\log x.
\]

For \(s = 1 + 1 / \log x\), integrate the Euler-factor logarithmic
derivative from 1 to \(s\). Its difference is at most 16, so

\[
 \prod_{p\le x}(1-p^{-1})^{-1}
 \le e^{16}\zeta(s)\le e^{16}(1+\log x)
 \le e^{17}\log x.
\]

This proves the upper side of (1), since the product logarithm
dominates the prime reciprocal sum. Conversely this product
contains the whole harmonic sum up to \(\lfloor x \rfloor\), which is at
least \(\log x\). The terms of order at least two in its logarithm
have sum at most
\(\sum_{m \ge 2} 1 / [ m ( m - 1 ) ] = 1\). This proves the lower side.
In particular prime reciprocal sums diverge, so the greedy
complete cells used below always exist. The weighted-prime
constant in Section~\ref{paper:arithmetic-setup} can also be set to
\(C_{W} = 8\), since \(4 + 4 \log x \le 8 \log x\) for \(x \ge 3\).

\subsubsection{Explicit cells and their clock defect}

Given the two occupancy constants \(A_{0} , A_{1} \ge 0\), define

\[
 B_1=\frac{A_0}{1-q}+\frac{A_1}{(1-q)^2},\qquad
 B_2=\frac{A_0^2}{1-q}+
       \frac{2A_0A_1}{(1-q)^2}+
       \frac{A_1^2(1+q)}{(1-q)^3},
\]

\[
 Q=\left\lceil\max\left(3,16H,\frac2{\eta_*},
              \frac{8B_1}{\eta_*},
              \frac{8kB_2}{\eta_*}\right)\right\rceil.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

Delete primes up to \(Q\). In every original prime block start at
\(u = \max ( Q , y_{i - 1} )\), greedily take the maximal successive prime
cell of reciprocal mass at most \(\eta_{i}\), and omit the final
incomplete cell at \(y_{i}\). Each complete cell has mass between
\(\eta_{i} - 1 / p_{\mathrm{next}}\) and \(\eta_{i}\); (2) makes it at least \(\eta_{i} / 2\).

The reciprocal-integer bound gives for the first prime in the
\(j\)th retained cell

\[
 p_{i,j}\ge(Q/2)e^{(j-1)\eta_i/2}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

Indeed the preceding cells have total mass at least
\(( j - 1 ) \eta_{i} / 2\), whereas the harmonic mass of all integers in
\(( Q , p )\) is at most \(\log ( 2 p / Q )\). Therefore the sum of the greedy
mass deficits is at most

\[
 \sum_{j\ge1}p_{{\rm next},j}^{-1}
 \le\frac2Q\frac1{1-e^{-\eta_i/2}}
 \le\frac{16H}Q\le1.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

Here \(1 - e^{- \eta_{i} / 2} \ge \eta_{i} / 4 \ge 1 / ( 8 H )\) was used. Combined
with (1), (4), and the omitted incomplete cell, the ideal complete
clock length \(L_{i} ' = \eta_{i} v_{i}\) differs from
\(\log ( \log y_{i} / \log u )\) by at most 82. If the entire block lies
below \(Q\), its lost physical length is at most \(\log \log Q\).
Hence a numerical total defect bound is

\[
 \sum_i|L_i'-L_i|\le R_k(Q):=
                         k(\log\log Q+100).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

The cell clocks have mesh at most one and boundary rate at
most \(2 H\); an inclusive interval of length one contains at most
\(2 H + 1 \le 3 H\) boundaries. If an affine endpoint map is used, its constant defect
in the quantitative fixed-lift construction can consequently be
taken from (5); no unspecified Mertens or cell-supply constant is
needed.

For completeness, the collision-cell geometric constants can be
set to \(c_{*} = \exp ( - 600 H^{2} )\) and \(A_{*} = 600 H^{2} + \log \log Q + 100\).
To see this before any roughness deletion, at most \(5 H\) greedy
cells have the next prime below \(\lceil 2 / \eta_{*} \rceil\); all later cells
have mass at least \(\eta_{i} / 2\). Applying (1) yields
\(\log \lambda_{t} \ge \log u \exp ( - 100 H ) \exp ( \eta_{i} t / 2 )\).
For the numerical series detail, put
\(a = \exp ( - 100 H ) \log 3\), \(b = \eta_{i} / 2 \ge 1 / ( 4 H )\). Monotonicity gives

\[
 \sum_{t\ge1}e^{-ae^{bt}}
 \le\frac1b\int_a^\infty e^{-v}\frac{dv}{v}
 \le4H\{\log(1/a)+e^{-1}\}
 <401H^2<500H^2.
\]

The first inequality is the decreasing integral test. In the
second, bound the integral on \([ a , 1 ]\) by \(\log ( 1 / a )\) and on
\([ 1 , \infty )\) by \(e^{- 1}\). Summing the deficits once more yields
\(\log \lambda_{t} \ge \log u \exp ( \eta_{i} t - 600 H^{2} )\).
The upper cumulative comparison and final incomplete cell give
the displayed \(A_{*}\). After deletion, (4) improves the deficit
bound, so these choices remain safe.

\subsubsection{Pointwise squarefree supply}

On the actual accepted support suppose

\[
 g_{i,j}\le A_0+A_1\min(j,v_i-j+1).
\]

The exact elementary-symmetric-sum calculation in
the pointwise squarefree supply argument in Section~\ref{supp:dyadic-arithmetic},
with (E.4.2)--(E.4.3), gives

\[
 1\ge\frac{S_g^{\rm all}}{W_g}
 \ge\exp\left(-\frac{4kB_2}{\eta_*Q}\right)
 \ge e^{-1/2}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

at every supported occupancy. The capacity condition follows
from \(4 B_{1} / ( \eta_{*} Q ) \le 1 / 2\); complete cell means are at least
\(\eta_{i} / 2\). This gives a fixed relative squarefree supply bound even for a rare
accepting mass. Formula (2) is a fixed roughness rule
once \(A_{0} , A_{1}\) are fixed, even for a huge number of cells.

The size exponent used for the lower harmonic source is allowed
to be at least \(\exp ( 80 ) B_{1}\); its lower sum is a subset of the
unrestricted \(K_{k}\) sum. It need not equal the upper-truncation
exponent \(2 kH C_{W} + 1\). Consequently this source does not require
deleting an additional number of last cells merely to match that
upper-truncation exponent.

Section~\ref{supp:finite-history-constants} bounds the deterministic
coefficient and both occupancy constants used in these grid inequalities.


\section{Covers and conditional upper estimates}\label{appendix:upper}
The upper bound rests on a geometric capacity estimate and two kinds
of conditional integration. A cylinder of partial label information
lies in a projected rectangle; its width can be written as its
original class probability times a risk exponent and a deterministic
shot sum. Necessary local tests control those exponents. Finally the
ordinary suffix is integrated with the root atom and its ballot
denominator at the same count.

We prove these ingredients and explain how their conditional bounds
compose in the original routing filtration. Keeping the geometric
capacities separate from the private masses makes the reveal order
and the dependence of each estimate explicit.

\subsection{Geometric covers and conditional estimates for the upper bound}
\label{app:upper-details}

We begin with the projected rectangles and positive prime expansion.
The rank-separation argument then selects disjoint rare banks, whose
one-end and whole-band estimates give the local assertions of
Proposition~\ref{upper:established-inputs}. After checking that the
terminal masks leave a suffix unread, we prove the ordinary root
estimate of Proposition~\ref{upper:root-contract}. Clocks and
eligibility sets retain their original block labels throughout.

\subsubsection{Rectangles and deterministic sums at stopping locations}
\label{updetail:rectangles}
A cut fixes the large-prime part of a divisor coordinate and leaves
its smaller-prime part free. The free displacement is bounded by an
exponential sum at that cut. The following lemma packages the product
of these width bounds as a capacity under the original fine-label law.

\begin{lemma}[Cylinder rectangles]\label{updetail:cylinder-lemma}
Fix a size-truncated squarefree tuple as in Lemma~\ref{artrunc:lemma}
and its uncolored prime positions. Let $\mathcal C$ be a set of
exterior coordinate names. For $c\in\mathcal C$, let $E_c$ be its
original logarithmic deadline and choose $0\le\tau_c\le E_c$.
A cylinder $Q_\tau$ specifies the assignments to these names at
positions to the right of their cuts; all remaining eligible names
stay compounded. Endpoint batches are placed on a fixed prescribed
side. Under the original fine categorical law $\pi$, put
\[
 B_{\mathcal C}=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}E_c,\qquad
 \Xi_\tau=\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}\tau_c-B_{\mathcal C}
                         -\log\pi(Q_\tau),\qquad
 Z(t)=1+\sum_{x\le t}e^{x-t}.
\]
Then
\begin{equation}
 \operatorname{Vol}_{\rm norm}(Q_\tau)
 \le C_H\pi(Q_\tau)e^{\Xi_\tau}
                  \prod_{c\in\mathcal C}Z(\tau_c).
 \label{updetail:rectangle}
\end{equation}
Coordinates outside $\mathcal C$ retain their deterministic full-size
rectangles; they contribute no shot at a future deadline.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The revealed factors determine translations, so only unresolved
widths need to be bounded. The sum in $Z$ uses every original
occurrence and therefore bounds the contribution of any selected
descendant list. The unresolved displacement in coordinate $c$ is at
most
\[
 \log2+(\log3)\sum_{x\le\tau_c}e^x
                         \le C_H e^{\tau_c}Z(\tau_c).
\]
For $c\notin\mathcal C$, the size truncation gives an interval of
width at most $C_H e^{E_c}$. Multiplying these widths and dividing
by the full geometric normalization gives
$C_H\exp(\sum_{c\in\mathcal C}(\tau_c-E_c))
\prod_{c\in\mathcal C}Z(\tau_c)$. Multiplication and division by
the absolute original probability $\pi(Q_\tau)$ proves the formula.
For a fixed ancestor atom $\alpha$, use its resolved coordinate
translations and inherited geometric multiplier. Temporary
conditioning replaces the joint mass by $\pi(Q_\tau\mid\alpha)$;
summing against $\pi(\alpha)$ restores the absolute joint mass.
\end{proof}

To use this capacity at first failures, we sum over a deterministic
mesh. This allows the moment estimates to be made at fixed locations
before the occurrence process is drawn. Partition a physical interval
$[a,b]$ into cells of length at most $\Delta$, with a bounded number of
endpoints per unit interval. If $v$ is the right
endpoint of a cell and $t$ belongs to that cell, positivity gives
\begin{equation}
 Z(t)\leq e^\Delta Z(v).
 \label{updetail:mesh-shot}
\end{equation}
Every term present at $t$ remains present at $v$, and its kernel
changes by $e^{v-t}$. At successive mesh points the reveal partitions
refine. The cylinders stopped at a first failure are disjoint because
each word has one first failure; their original probabilities hence
sum to at most one. We use this argument for each cover separately.
On an ancestor fiber, we then sum against the original ancestor mass. Suppose each
first-failure cylinder has capacity at most
\[
 C\pi(q)e^{-h}\omega(t)Z(t)^d\prod_c Z(\tau_c),
 \qquad d\leq H,
\]
where $\omega(t)=(1+\operatorname{dist}(t,\{a,b\}))^{-A}$, or its
one-ended version, and the outside cuts $\tau_c$ are deterministic.
Within one mesh cell $\omega(t)\leq C_{\Delta,A}\omega(v)$ and the
sum of the atom probabilities is at most one. Thus the total failure
capacity is bounded by $Ce^{-h}S$, with
\[
 S=\sum_v\omega(v)Z(v)^d\prod_c Z(\tau_c).
\]
The stopped atom probabilities have already been summed in this
expression.

The moment bound follows from the exponential decay in each shot.
For a Poisson process with bounded intensity per unit interval,
$Z(v)$ has all fixed moments uniformly in deterministic $v$: split
into unit intervals and sum their exponentially decreasing
coefficients, or use the Laplace functional. Taking fixed $A$ large
enough, Minkowski's inequality and $\sum_v\omega(v)<\infty$ then give
$\mathbb E S^p\leq C_{H,p}$ for every required fixed $p$. Finite sums over the endpoint contexts have
the same property. A cut within bounded distance of an endpoint is
covered by finitely many extra mesh cells. An incoming selected-list
sum is bounded pointwise by the original-list sum at the same
deterministic threshold.

The probability tests themselves may be made on the complete
deterministic mesh, including empty cells. The risk has one-sided
jumps and bounded linear speed; survival on that mesh implies the
corresponding continuous necessary wall after a fixed reserve
increase, using the appropriate side for the jump convention. The
rising wall has bounded derivative on the fixed interval, so the
same conclusion holds for its first-hit strip. Consequently the
fixed-time bank estimates below are only applied at deterministic
mesh locations.

Under insertion of $q$ fixed original occurrences, every deterministic
$Z(v)$ increases by at most $q$. Keeping the mesh and contexts fixed
therefore gives
\begin{equation}
 S(G+\text{insertions})\leq C_{H,q}S(G).
 \label{updetail:shot-insertions}
\end{equation}
The categorical log-likelihood changes at each fixed test by at most
$C_Hq$, which is paid by the reserve. A Poisson--Mecke expansion of a
fixed shot monomial uses finitely many partitions of its occurrences;
apply this insertion bound in each term before summing the deterministic
locations. This proves the fixed-moment and insertion assertions for the stopping
covers. The stopped locations have already been summed on the
deterministic mesh, so these assertions concern fixed-location shots.

\subsubsection{Positive prime expansion with the original root}
\label{updetail:prime-expansion}
We next express the harmonic sum under a tilted occurrence law.
The identity is exact on the original prime ranges. Geometric caps
are proved first on actual squarefree tuples and then extended by
positivity to all occurrence lists. This order allows the analytic
expectation to retain repeated occurrences and every count.

Let $\mathcal P_i$ be the original prime ranges, including $2,3$ in
$\mathcal P_1$, and put
\[
 H_i=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_i}\frac1p,\quad
 B_{\rm geo}=\sum_iV_i=\sum_i(h_i-1)L_i.
\]
Take fixed positive $Z_i,s_i$, put $s=s_1>0$, and define
\[
 J=\sum_iL_i+\sum_i s_iV_i-\sum_iZ_iL_i,
 \qquad
 X(G)=\frac{\sum_iN_i(G)\log Z_i-\sum_i s_iV_i}{s}.
\]
Let $\mathbb P_Z$ give independent occurrence counts
$\operatorname{Pois}(Z_i/p)$ at each $p\in\mathcal P_i$.
For every nonnegative symmetric functional $A$ on occurrence lists,
Tonelli and the Poisson exponential formula give the exact identity
\begin{align}
 &e^{-\sum_iL_i}
 \sum_{\mathbf n\geq0}\prod_i\frac1{n_i!}
 \sum_{p_{i,a}\in\mathcal P_i}
 A(G)\prod_{i,a}\frac1{p_{i,a}}
 \notag\\[-2pt]
 &\hspace{25mm}=
 e^{-J+\sum_iZ_i(H_i-L_i)}
       \mathbb E_Z[e^{-sX(G)}A(G)].
 \label{updetail:exact-expansion}
\end{align}
To verify the exponent, the unnormalized list sum equals
$e^{\sum_iZ_iH_i}\mathbb E_Z[A\prod_i Z_i^{-N_i}]$, and
$\prod_i Z_i^{-N_i}=e^{-sX-\sum_i s_iV_i}$.

For the saddle, $\log Z_i=G_i$ and $X$ is exactly the uncolored
routing root. The routing root agrees with the prime tilt by telescoping. At node
$j$, minus the local log-probability, multiplied by $s_j$, is $G_j$
for an exit and $G_j-G_{j+1}$ for a child route. Summing along the
route leaves $G_i$ at the occurrence's original block. Subtracting
the physical budgets proves the identity at the fixed coefficients;
stationarity is not needed and every child list is the original one.

Define $I_0(G)=e^{-B_{\rm geo}}L^{(k+1)}(\mathbf a(G))$ on the
squarefree size-truncated support, and $I_0=0$ elsewhere. Each squarefree
selection occurs $n_i!$ times among ordered lists, so
Lemma~\ref{artrunc:lemma} and \eqref{updetail:exact-expansion} imply
\begin{equation}
 K_k(\ell)\leq
 2e^{-J+\sum_iZ_i(H_i-L_i)}
       \mathbb E_Z[e^{-sX}I_0(G)].
 \label{updetail:arithmetic-upper}
\end{equation}
The geometric caps hold first on that actual support. If they give
$I_0\leq C C_l(G)$ there, with each $C_l$ nonnegative on every list,
then $I_0\leq C\min_l C_l$ on all lists, because of the zero
extension. Their numerical cap minimum is therefore evaluated on
unrestricted repeated lists under the same atomic Poisson law and root.

The uniform prime harmonic estimate gives $|H_i-L_i|\leq C_H$;
the discrepancy in \eqref{updetail:arithmetic-upper} is bounded since
$Z_i\leq H$. Deleting a fixed initial prime set pays its finite Euler
product and changes each $H_i$ by only a fixed amount. For later cell
completion, if $\mu_c^*\geq\mu_c$ and
$\sum_c(\mu_c^*-\mu_c)\leq C_H$, the product Poisson density ratio is
at most $e^{C_H}$. It is applied once to the whole nonnegative
integrand, retaining its minimum, powers and root. A change of the
physical cell budget is compensated in the external root translate.

\subsubsection{Separation of the rank intervals of rare comparisons}
\label{updetail:rank-separation}
We arrange disjoint inputs before multiplying the local probability
estimates. We prove that two sufficiently rare comparisons
in one plateau have disjoint rank intervals. Weakness places their
secants near the same level. If their intervals overlap, lawful
completion changes force a large endpoint score for at least one
comparison, contradicting rarity.

In one maximal plateau, write $\varepsilon=1-\sigma>0$ and
\[
 \kappa_r=(r+z)^{-\varepsilon},\qquad
 g_r(a)=a-\kappa_rE_a(z).
\]
The transported incoming coefficients are retained individually. They are
no larger than the natural coefficient at the first local capacity.
Every lawful complete reference history has nonnegative cost by the
KKT and reference-compression results of
Section~\ref{app:endpoint-details}.

Choose a fixed sufficiently small $\epsilon_0(H)>0$. An edge $r\to q$
is weak when $|g_r(r)-g_r(q)|\leq\epsilon_0$. If $m_-,m_+$ are the
two minimum reference costs, their common increment is
$m_+-m_-=L_i\nu_i$. Both are nonnegative and the endpoint scores
dominate $1+m_-$ and $1+m_+$. Hence
\[
 |\nu_i|L_i\leq m_-+m_+\leq X_i+Y_i.
\]
Since the natural mean is comparable to $L_i$, sufficiently small
$(1+X_i)(1+Y_i)/(1+\mu_i)$ implies this fixed weakness condition.

We need three strict comparisons: a weak edge viewed from a larger
capacity, a rank below its output, and a capacity between its output
and input. These supply the charges in the overlap argument. The normalized
secant estimate of Section~\ref{app:endpoint-details} is
\[
 \beta_b(y)=\frac{\log((y\log y-b\log b)/(y-b))}{\log y},
 \qquad \beta_b'(y)\leq-\frac1{24H^2}.
\]
For a weak edge $r\to q$ and an earlier capacity $h>r$, put
$T_a=(a+z)^{-\varepsilon}(E_a-E_q)/(a-q)$. Weakness gives
$|T_r-1|\leq\epsilon_0/(r-q)$, whence
$\beta_{q+z}(r+z)-\varepsilon\leq2\epsilon_0/\log2$.
If $\epsilon_0\leq\log2/(192H^2)$, then
$\log T_h\leq-\log2/(48H^2)$. At the other endpoint,
\[
 g_h(r)-g_h(q)
 =(r-q)\{1-(\kappa_h/\kappa_r)T_r\},
 \quad \kappa_h/\kappa_r\leq e^{-\varepsilon_{\min}/H}.
\]
Taking also
$\epsilon_0\leq(e^{\varepsilon_{\min}/H}-1)/2$ gives a positive
lower bound at both $r$ and $h$. Concavity then proves
\begin{equation}
 g_h(a)-g_h(q)\geq\delta_H>0\qquad(r\leq a\leq h).
 \label{updetail:earlier-rank}
\end{equation}
Reducing the coefficient increases this difference, so it also holds
in the relevant earlier groups. If $q\geq1$ and $0\leq a<q$, strict
concavity $-g_r''\geq H^{-2}$ gives
\[
 g_r(r)-g_r(a)\geq-H\epsilon_0+
                \frac{(q-a)(r-a)}{2H^2}
 \geq\frac3{4H^2}
\]
after $\epsilon_0\leq1/(4H^3)$. Finally the forward secant comparison
gives, for $q<h<r$,
\begin{equation}
 g_h(q)-g_h(h)\geq\gamma_H>0.
 \label{updetail:intervening-rank}
\end{equation}
All thresholds are chosen before any lengths.

Suppose the rank intervals of two weak edges overlap, with
$r_1>r_2$ but $q_1<r_2$. Output ordering gives $q_2<q_1$, hence
$q_1\geq1$. Consider an arbitrary left completion for the second edge. Its
earlier retained ranks are at least $r_2$; lowering all of them to
$q_2$ and keeping the later history gives a legal complete history.
The changed history has nonnegative cost. By
\eqref{updetail:earlier-rank}, the original completion therefore pays
$X_2\geq1+\delta_HL_1$.

For the right score of the first edge, keep fixed the prefix through
its block and the suffix after the second block. All capacities
between their right endpoints $b_1,b_2$ exceed $q_1$, so the
remaining names have no deadline there. The reference cost, as a function of
their ordered cut times, is a constant plus
\[
 \sum_{a=k_{\rm end}+1}^{q_1}
 \int_{b_1}^{\tau_a}\{g_t(a)-g_t(a-1)\}\,dt.
\]
Since $\kappa(t)$ is nondecreasing, each summand is concave. A
minimum on the ordered simplex is attained at a vertex, where every
cut is at $b_1$ or $b_2$. We may consequently replace the ranks on
that interval by one constant rank $a\leq q_1$ without increasing
cost. There are two cases. If $a<q_1$, lower the first-block rank to
$a$; strict concavity gives an original cost of at least $c_HL_1$.
If $a=q_1$, fill the intervening groups to their eligible capacities;
\eqref{updetail:intervening-rank} gives an original cost of at least
$c_HL_2$. In both cases the complete outside history is preserved.
Consequently
\[
 Y_1\geq1+c_H\min(L_1,L_2),\quad
 \overline T_1\geq c_1\frac{1+\min(L_1,L_2)}{1+L_1},\quad
 \overline T_2\geq c_2\frac{1+L_1}{1+L_2}.
\]
If $L_2\geq L_1$ the first ratio is bounded below; otherwise their
product is. Hence two sufficiently rare edges must have $q_1\geq r_2$.
Applying this to every pair proves disjointness of the rank intervals
$(q_i,r_i]$. The argument also applies to terminal nonzero edges:
$z=1$, but their secant bases are at least two and their marks remain
nondegenerate. The terminal zero-output edge remains ordinary.

\subsubsection{The two scales of a proper zero-output comparison}
\label{updetail:zero-scales}
A rare full-to-zero comparison has two different reserves. One
contains the old and earlier local lengths together with the exit
width; the other contains only the later local length. The following
endpoint calculation identifies these scales and shows that the
selected block dominates the other lengths. This is the geometry
needed for the hard-plateau two-wall estimate.

Consider a proper zero-output edge with sufficiently small persistence ratio $\overline T$. Let $M$ be the selected local block, $A,B$ the preceding and following
local lengths, and $V_{\rm old}$ the complete old length. Put
\[
 P=V_{\rm old}+A,\qquad T=P+M+B,\qquad
 R_{\rm exit}=\max\{R_0,\min(\sqrt{1+A+M+B},d^{-1})\}.
\]
Full input and zero output force the two completion times to be
$P$ and $P+M$ in every outside context. The clipped-prefix estimate
from Section~\ref{app:endpoint-details} gives
$\overline C_v\geq c_H\min(t_v,T-t_v)$.
If the block fails to cross $T/2$ strictly, one of its endpoint costs
is at least $c_HM$ and the persistence ratio is bounded below.
Thus sufficiently small ratio forces $P<T/2<P+M$.

For the converse score bounds, use the two explicit contexts that
retain each earlier name to its deadline and remove the current
names at the selected endpoint. Neither context has a good group. Complete plateau balance gives
\[
 \overline C^-_{\rm full}
 =\sum_{\rm old}L_gg_g(r_{\rm top})+
   \sum_{\rm local\ before}L_gg_g(r_g),\qquad
 \overline C^+_{\rm full}
 =-\sum_{\rm local\ after}L_gg_g(r_g).
\]
Their costs are nonnegative and at most $C_HP$ and $C_HB$,
respectively. Together with the clipped lower bound and the early/late
score definition, this proves
\begin{equation}
 X\asymp_H1+V_{\rm old}+A+R_{\rm exit},\qquad
 Y\asymp_H1+B.
 \label{updetail:intrinsic-zero-pair}
\end{equation}
In particular rarity implies $V_{\rm old}+A+B\leq C_H\tau M$;
for a small fixed $\tau$, $M$ dominates the entire old and local
length. Uniformly even as $d\downarrow0$,
\[
 R_{\rm exit}\asymp_H
 \varrho:=\max\left\{\varrho_0,
 \frac{c_0\sqrt{1+M}}{1+d\sqrt{1+M}}\right\}.
\]
Conversely a sufficiently small
$(1+B)(1+V_{\rm old}+A+\varrho)/(1+M)$ forces that dominance and
midpoint crossing, so the scales characterize the same rare region.
For the original mark
$W=\log(r+z)-\log z\,1_{\rm child}$, complete balance also gives
\[
 eM=\sum_{\rm old}L_gg_g(r_{\rm top})+
     \sum_{\rm local\ne i}L_gg_g(r_g),
 \qquad e=(r+z)^\sigma\mathbb EW-r,
\]
and therefore $|e|M\leq C_H(V_{\rm old}+A+B)$.
The two reserves in \eqref{updetail:intrinsic-zero-pair} remain
separate when applying a one-end or two-end probability estimate.

\subsubsection{Necessary one-end tests on original local intervals}
\label{updetail:one-end-banks}
For a nonzero output, the left endpoint score is at least diffusive.
A short deterministic bank near the other end then sees the smaller
reserve at the correct scale. Its necessary test may read counts in
intermediate local groups, but those groups are disjoint from the
bank and have length controlled by the smaller score. We first prove
this geometry, then derive the test from a projected rectangle, and
finally average its conditional mass.

Consider a weak edge $r\to q$ with $q\geq1$ on $[a,b]$, of length
$L$, in the rare region $\overline T<\tau$, where $\tau>0$ is
sufficiently small in terms of $H$. Write $S=r+z$, $B=q+z$, $\nu=g_r(r)-g_r(q)$, and let
$\mathcal J$ consist of the later local groups with $q<h<r$.
Their total length is $M_{\mathcal J}$.
We first prove
\begin{equation}
 1+X\geq c_H\sqrt{1+L},\quad
 1+Y\leq C_H\tau\sqrt{1+L},\quad M_{\mathcal J}\leq C_HY.
 \label{updetail:one-end-scales}
\end{equation}
A left completion retains a proper deepest subset in the current
block. For a late completion, that block is good and contributes
$\sqrt L$. For an early completion, the last positive time is at
least $b$, so clipped-prefix charging contributes at least $c_HL$.
These alternatives prove the first inequality; rarity then gives the
second.
For any right completion, compress the cuts between $b$ and the end
of $\mathcal J$ to the two endpoints, by the same concavity argument
as in Section~\ref{updetail:rank-separation}. The compressed rank is
some $a'\leq q$. If $a'<q$, lowering the current block costs at least
$\delta_HL$; if $a'=q$, filling the intermediate groups costs at least
$\gamma_HM_{\mathcal J}$. Complete reference nonnegativity thus gives
$Y\geq\min(\delta_HL,\gamma_HM_{\mathcal J})$. For sufficiently small
$\tau$, rarity excludes the first alternative, proving the last claim.
These arguments also hold for $z=1$ and positive $q$.

\emph{Selecting the bank.} The endpoint reference minima differ by $\nu L$, so
$|\nu|L\leq X+Y$. Choose the deterministic interval length
\begin{equation}
 \ell=c_{\rm bank}\frac{L^2}{(1+X)^2}.
 \label{updetail:effective-length}
\end{equation}
By choosing $c_{\rm bank}$ sufficiently small and then $\tau$
sufficiently small, \eqref{updetail:one-end-scales} and rarity imply
\[
 \ell_{\rm scalar}\leq\ell\leq L/16,
 \qquad |\nu|\sqrt\ell\leq C_H,
 \qquad
 \frac{1+Y}{\sqrt\ell}\asymp_H
 \overline T:=\frac{(1+X)(1+Y)}{1+S^\sigma L}.
\]
Indeed rarity gives $1+X\leq C_H\tau L/(1+Y)$ and hence
$\ell\geq c_H\tau^{-2}$. Neither $\ell$ nor its location is selected
from the sampled word.

\emph{The necessary test from the rectangle.}
Group the deepest $q$ names and the true compound child into the
category $B$, keeping the other names separate. Reveal the complete
coarse word in $\mathcal J$, and put
\[
 H_{\mathcal J}=\sum_{q<h<r}
 \{N_h\log(h+z)-K_{B,h}\log B-(h-q)L_h\}.
\]
Read the current interval backwards and set
\[
 W=\log S-\log B\,1_B,\qquad
 C(t)=H_{\mathcal J}+\sum_{x<t}W_x-(r-q)t.
\]
The original rate is $S^\sigma$ and its mean drift is $-\nu$.
Use full original sizes for the earlier exterior coordinates, the
shorter deadlines for the intermediate coordinates, and the original
full rectangle for the $B$ coordinates. The unresolved exterior
budget is the full budget less $(r-q)t+\sum_{\mathcal J}(h-q)L_h$.
The observed negative log-probability is the mark sum in the
risk expression. Formula
\eqref{updetail:rectangle} therefore gives the actual partial capacity
$C_H\pi_t e^{C(t)}\operatorname{Shot}_t$.
Stop at the first mesh failure of
$C(t)\geq-h-A\log(1+t)$, including $t=0$.
Section~\ref{updetail:rectangles} bounds the union of failures by
$CS e^{-h}$ with all required moments.

Because $H_{\mathcal J}\leq(\log H)N_{\mathcal J}$ pointwise,
every survivor satisfies the necessary test
\begin{equation}
 \sum_{x<t}W_x-(r-q)t
 \geq-h-C_HN_{\mathcal J}-A\log(1+t),\qquad 0\leq t\leq\ell.
 \label{updetail:necessary-one-end}
\end{equation}
First make this implication with the entire intermediate word fixed,
then integrate that word with its original mass. The right side now
reads only $N_{\mathcal J}$; any future private test remains in the
joint surviving-word operator.

\emph{The fractional moment.} Let $Q_h$ be the conditional private probability of
\eqref{updetail:necessary-one-end}. The signed logarithmic-wall
one-end estimate, on the original clock with bounded scaled drift,
gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{G_i}Q_h^\sigma
 \leq C_H\min\left\{1,
 \left(\frac{1+h+C_HN_{\mathcal J}}{\sqrt\ell}\right)^{2\chi(\sigma,\rho)}
 \right\},\qquad
 \rho=\frac{(\mathbb EW)^2}{\mathbb E W^2}.
\]
The intermediate count is independent of this original local clock,
with mean at most $C_HM_{\mathcal J}\leq C_HY$. Its fixed moments
are at most $C_p(1+Y)^p$. Integrating over all its counts proves
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E Q_h^\sigma\leq C_H(1+h)^K\overline T^{2\chi(\sigma,\rho)}.
 \label{updetail:one-end-moment}
\end{equation}
\emph{Matching the profile parameter.} To compare with the exact-type
parameter, write $a_0=\log S$,
$b_0=\log B$, $c=r-q$, $\lambda=S^\sigma$, $\mu=\lambda L$,
and $p=B/S$. Its centered type parameter and correlation are
\[
 \bar p=(a_0-c/\lambda)/b_0,
 \qquad
 \bar\rho=\frac{(cL/(\mu+1))^2}
 {(cL/(\mu+1))^2+b_0^2\bar p(1-\bar p)}.
\]
The identity $\bar p-p=-\nu/(b_0\lambda)$ gives
$|\bar\rho-\rho|\leq C_H(|\nu|+1/L)$.
As $\overline T\geq c_H/\sqrt\ell$,
$|\log\overline T|\leq C_H+\tfrac12\log\ell$.
The scaled-drift bound and $\ell\leq L/16$ bound the product of
this logarithm and the correlation error. Compact local Lipschitz
continuity of $\chi$ therefore permits either parameter in
\eqref{updetail:one-end-moment} at fixed comparison cost.
This includes every count and all $n+1$ conditional spacings.
Fixed insertions change the reserve by at most a constant per point;
the Mecke argument of Section~\ref{updetail:rectangles} attaches
the required shot powers at the same exponent $\sigma$.

\emph{Zero output with a large left score.}
For a proper $r\to0$ edge, assume explicitly
$1+X\geq c_X\sqrt{1+L}$. The child weight satisfies
$z\geq2^{u_{\min}}>1$, so the two marks remain nondegenerate.
Here $\mathcal J$ consists of all later local groups. At a right
completion, postpone the current cuts to their individual deadlines.
The complete earlier history is unchanged, and the difference of
reference costs is
$\sum_{0<h<r}[-g_h(h)]L_h\geq\gamma_HM_{\mathcal J}$.
Thus $M_{\mathcal J}\leq C_HY$ directly. The preceding proof applies
with $B=z$, $c=r$, and the child category in place of the deepest
suffix. In particular it supplies precisely the same moment
\eqref{updetail:one-end-moment}. The left-score hypothesis is needed:
there is no current proper-good group when the output is zero.

\emph{Disjoint inputs and the shared count.}
Rank separation makes the current-plus-intermediate group sets
disjoint for distinct rare edges of a plateau; they are also disjoint
across plateaux. Their label intervals
have length at most $L/16$ and avoid a count middle in the same
block. If the count middle lies in an intermediate group, its weight
is decreasing in that count and the necessary reserve is increasing.
For independent copies $N,N'$,
\[
 2\operatorname{Cov}(f(N),g(N))
 =\mathbb E[(f(N)-f(N'))(g(N)-g(N'))]\leq0
\]
when $f$ is decreasing and $g$ increasing. Applying this with all
other groups fixed supplies the required separation without an
independence assertion for the shared count.

\subsubsection{Leaving a terminal suffix unread}
\label{updetail:terminal-trimming}
The final root integral requires a suffix independent of all prefix
mask inputs. Some terminal binary tests initially read counts just
inside the chosen suffix. We remove those whole intermediate groups
from its beginning. Their short total length leaves the largest
block and the intrinsic ordinary factor comparable.

All terminal binary weak blocks lie in the negative ordinary-drift
head. The ordinary-suffix geometry gives, before trimming,
\[
 D_0\geq b_HV_{\rm old}+g_0L_{\rm head},\qquad
 U\geq c_HT_{\rm total},\qquad M_*\geq c_HT_{\rm total}/H.
\]
A terminal necessary test may read intermediate counts within this
suffix. If so, start the suffix at the first capacity at most its
output $q$. This is an original group boundary, so the removed
segment consists of whole original blocks. Its length satisfies
\[
 \delta\leq M_{\mathcal J}\leq C_HY
 \leq C_H\tau\sqrt{1+L}\leq C_H'\tau L.
\]
For several tests use the latest one; rank separation puts all earlier
read sets before it. The old head contains its current length $L$.
Choosing the fixed $\tau$ small enough, bounded ordinary drifts give
$E_H\delta\leq D_0/4$, $\delta\leq D_0/4$ and $\delta<M_*/2$.
Since a whole block of length $M_*$ cannot lie in a segment of
length less than $M_*/2$, the largest block and the earliest choice
in a tie are retained. Thus
\[
 U'=U-\delta\asymp U,\quad M_*'=M_*,\quad
 A_*'=A_*-\delta,\quad B_*'=B_*,\quad
 D'=D_0-\sum_{\rm removed}e_hL_h\asymp D_0.
\]
The new suffix still has $D'\geq c_HV_{\rm pre}'$ and
$U'\geq c_HT_{\rm total}$. Moreover $1+D'+A_*'$ is comparable to
$1+D_0+A_*$, so its ordinary factor is unchanged up to constants.
Every clock read by the necessary masks now belongs to the actual
prefix of this suffix. When no terminal binary rare edge is present,
no trimming is needed.

\subsubsection{Whole-band estimates with two variable reserves}
\label{updetail:whole-band}
The hard-plateau kernels need a count band together with two signed
end tests. The band is summed before its fractional power is taken.
A middle maximum atom supplies its width factor; end banks supply
the persistence factor. When one reserve is larger than diffusive,
only the opposite, smaller-reserve bank is needed.

Fix a compact nondegenerate positive binary law $W$, a compact positive
rate $\nu$ and speed $c$, and a power $\sigma$ in a compact subinterval
of $(0,1)$. Suppose $M,L,R\geq1$ and the band width $r$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
 1\leq r\leq C\sqrt M,\qquad r\leq CR,\qquad
 |\nu\mathbb EW-c|M\leq C(L+R).
 \label{updetail:band-assumptions}
\end{equation}
All interval locations are deterministic. Use a middle interval of
length comparable to $M$, disjoint from the retained end intervals.
An additional later-side count $N_B$ is independent, with Poisson mean
at most $CL$. Let the positive left test have reserve at most
$C(1+h+N_B)$ and the reflected negative right test have reserve at most
$C(1+h+R+(1+|j|)r)$. Both allow a fixed logarithmically lowered wall.
After fixing the entire outside private word, assume the whole band
permits at most $Cr$ values of the middle binary count.

Put $T=LR/M$ and
$\rho_{\rm nat}=(\mathbb EW)^2/\mathbb EW^2$.
There is a numerical majorant $B_{h,j}(G)$ for the conditional
probability of the band and its retained tests such that
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E B_{h,j}^{\sigma}
 \leq C(1+h)^K(1+|j|)^K
       (r/\sqrt M)^\sigma
       \min\{1,T^{2\chi(\sigma,\rho_{\rm nat})}\}.
 \label{updetail:whole-band-moment}
\end{equation}
Here the entire permitted count band is summed before the power.
\emph{The band and end-bank estimate.}
If $\max(L,R)\leq C_0\sqrt M$, retain end intervals
of length $M/16$. Otherwise retain only the smaller-reserve end,
of length $\ell=\min(M/16,c_*M^2/\max(L,R)^2)$.
Conditioning on all outside labels, the middle count is binomial,
so its maximum atom gives the pointwise majorant
\[
 B_{h,j}=\min\{1,Cr/\sqrt{1+N_{\rm mid}}\}\,q_{\rm left}q_{\rm right},
\]
with an omitted end factor equal to one. The bound is uniform in the
outside-dependent center. Integrate those outside labels afterwards.
The Poisson negative moment supplies $C(r/\sqrt M)^\sigma$, including
small middle counts. On every retained end the scaled drift is bounded
by \eqref{updetail:band-assumptions}. Thus the signed one-end estimate gives
\[
 \mathbb E q_H^\sigma\leq C
 \min\{1,[(1+H)/\sqrt{1+\ell}]^{2\chi_c}\},\quad
 \chi_c=\chi\left(\sigma,
 \frac{(c/\nu)^2}{(c/\nu)^2+\operatorname{Var}W}\right).
\]
When both ends are retained, their independence and the moments of
$N_B$ give $\min(1,(LR/M)^{2\chi_c})$ with the displayed reserve
polynomials. The inequality $r\leq CR$ controls every translated
right-band reserve. When one end is retained, divide its reserve by
$\sqrt\ell$; the result is bounded by the same polynomials times
$LR/M$, so the same path factor follows.
If $\ell$ is bounded, $\max(L,R)\geq cM$ and $T\geq c$; discard
the path test at fixed cost while retaining the middle atom.
On $T<1$ the drift hypothesis implies
$|\chi_c-\chi(\sigma,\rho_{\rm nat})|\leq C(L+R)/M\leq2CT$.
The replacement costs at most $e^{C|T\log T|}$. This proves
\eqref{updetail:whole-band-moment}; for $T\geq1$ both numerical path
factors equal one.

\emph{Atomic prime clocks.} The same bounds hold on actual prime clocks
by a pointwise quantile comparison. On a deterministic physical interval of length
$\ell$, its harmonic cumulative mass is $t+O_H(1)$ for every initial
length $t$, with the same statement for half-open intervals and their
reflections. The harmonic-to-physical quantile map therefore satisfies
$|T(s)-s|\leq C_H$. Its image of a homogeneous Poisson process is
the required atomic prime process, with repeated occurrences allowed.
A positive-jump wall is tested at its pre-jump minimum; a negative
wall at its post-jump minimum. During the collapse of any atom the
homogeneous partial sums dominate these minima up to the bounded
clock error. An actual necessary wall is consequently contained in
the homogeneous wall with a fixed reserve enlargement, for every mark
word and every atom multiplicity. Logarithmic allowances change by
only a fixed amount.

The homogeneous estimate applies to the full count law, as follows
from Theorem~\ref{pr:one}. Let $m=\lfloor\nu\ell/2\rfloor$.
The probability of fewer than $m$ arrivals by $\ell$ is exponentially
small. Otherwise survival implies a rank wall through the first $m$
independent exponential gaps. For the positive sign, survival at the
$j$th arrival implies
$cT_j\leq w_+j+h+A\log(1+T_j)$ and hence
$T_j\leq C(j+h+1)$. For the negative sign, when this latter bound
fails the signed risk is already nonnegative; in the complementary
case the same logarithmic comparison applies. In either direction
the rank-wall reserve is $C(1+h)$ with a fixed logarithmic allowance.
Theorem~\ref{pr:one} gives
$C(1+h)^{2\chi}(1+\ell)^{-\chi}$, and the exponentially small
exception is absorbed. This proof includes all original counts.

\emph{Fixed-width bands and insertions.}
At a first hit we use the following fixed-width version. Split
a deterministic interval $[0,z)$ into its left quarter, middle half,
and right quarter. Given both end words, a fixed terminal band admits
at most a fixed number of middle low counts. Hence, uniformly over
every band center $b$,
\[
 \sup_b q_b(G)\leq C(1+N_M)^{-1/2}\ell_h(G_L)r_{r_0}(G_R),
\]
and independence of these three deterministic restrictions gives
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E(\sup_bq_b)^\sigma
 \leq C(1+h)^{2\chi}(1+r_0)^{2\chi}
                   (1+z)^{-\sigma/2-2\chi}.
 \label{updetail:fixed-band}
\end{equation}
The terminal band contributes just its middle atom, without an
additional height factor. The bound is uniform for $z$ in a prescribed
comparable range. In a stopping cover we sum over those deterministic
$z$ locations with their original weights.

Insertion of $q$ fixed occurrences decreases the middle negative
count factor, relaxes the positive left reserve by at most $qw_+$,
and makes the negative right wall stronger. The same middle-binomial
argument can leave the original middle marks free after conditioning
on the inserted marks. Thus both displayed bounds remain valid with
that left reserve shift. To attach shots, for
$\beta=4/\sigma_{\min}$ form
\[
 C_z(G)=\sum_{h,r_0\geq0}
 (1+h)^{-\beta}(1+r_0)^{-\beta}
 (1+N_M)^{-1/2}\ell_h(G_L)r_{r_0}(G_R).
\]
Fractional subadditivity and \eqref{updetail:fixed-band} show
$\mathbb EC_z^\sigma\leq C(1+z)^{-\sigma/2-2\chi}$, since each
reserve exponent is at most $-3$. Reindexing after insertion gives
$C_z(G+q\text{ points})\leq C_q C_z(G)$.
Expanding an integrably weighted fixed-degree shot polynomial into
Poisson occurrence partitions and applying Mecke now preserves this
power of $1+z$. The expansion is valid for atomic intensities as well.

For the proper zero-output application, take the separate scales
$L=1+B$ and $R=1+V_{\rm old}+A+\varrho$ from
\eqref{updetail:intrinsic-zero-pair} and band width $\varrho$.
They satisfy all of \eqref{updetail:band-assumptions}, including
$\varrho\leq CR$. If $d\sqrt M<1$, then
$\varrho\asymp\sqrt M$ and $R\geq c\sqrt M$; the left-only
calculation gives the same bound with a width factor comparable to
one, uniformly as $d\downarrow0$.

\subsubsection{Joint count weights and the conditional routing tower}
\label{updetail:count-tower}
We now combine the simple-bank estimates with the proper count
weights. There are two distinct operations. Averaging over the
uncolored clocks gives the product of the local profile factors;
backward conditioning on private routes converts those costs into
geometric capacities. The latter operation uses bounds uniform in
every preceding atom, so future child masks are integrated before a
current count middle is varied.

For each nonterminal plateau choose a fixed middle in a largest local block,
write $n_j$ for its count, and set
$M_j=(1+d_j\sqrt{1+n_j})^{-1}$.
For each simple edge let $Q_i(h)$ be its necessary-test probability.
The only possible overlap between a count middle and these tests is
when the middle lies in an intermediate set $\mathcal J_i$.
With all other clocks fixed, $M_j^{\sigma_j}$ decreases in $n_j$
and $Q_i^{\sigma_{o(i)}}$ increases. The covariance inequality proved
above extracts $\mathbb EM_j^{\sigma_j}$. Each middle lies in at
most one such set by rank separation. The remaining test inputs are
disjoint original groups, so
\[
 \mathbb E\left[\prod_{j<m}M_j^{\sigma_j}
                    \prod_iQ_i(h)^{\sigma_{o(i)}}\right]
 \leq\prod_{j<m}\mathbb EM_j^{\sigma_j}
       \prod_i\mathbb EQ_i(h)^{\sigma_{o(i)}}.
\]
Splitting a Poisson count below and above half its mean gives
\[
 \mathbb EM_j^{\sigma_j}
 \leq C_H(1+d_j\sqrt{1+\mu_{C_j}})^{-\sigma_j},
\]
uniformly even as $d_j\downarrow0$. Together with
\eqref{updetail:one-end-moment} this gives all proper count and simple
local factors at their respective plateau powers. Fixed insertions
only decrease $M_j$ and shift each reserve by a fixed amount; the
same Mecke argument attaches the permitted shots. One unweighted
count insertion pays its original mean.

We next turn these environmental costs into a conditional capacity
bound. Fix the complete original uncolored word $G$ and let
$\mathcal Q_j$ reveal its first $j$ coarse plateau routes. In a local
block of plateau $j$, every earlier plateau has already expired; its
earlier routes are deterministically child. Thus on every $\mathcal Q_{j-1}$ atom its current labels still have probabilities
$1/(r+z_j)$ for each exterior name and $z_j/(r+z_j)$ for the child,
independently over original slots. Let $E_j$ avoid the count middle
and satisfy
$\pi_G(E_j\mid\mathcal Q_{j-1})\leq p_j(G)$ uniformly on those
atoms; for the terminal plateau assume the corresponding conditional
bound on $E_m$. Local-only masks have this property.

For any uncolored-measurable thresholds $\xi_j$, put
$\zeta_j=\eta_j-\xi_j$. Condition on the entire current coarse route
outside its middle. Then $E_j$ is fixed and
\[
 \zeta_j=H_0-\log z_j\,K_j,\qquad
 K_j\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n_j,z_j/(r+z_j)),
\]
where $H_0$ may depend arbitrarily on the actual incoming list.
The binomial maximum atom and the two exponential half-lattice sums
give, uniformly in $H_0$ and also for $n_j=0$,
\begin{align*}
 \mathbb E[e^{\zeta_j}1_{\{\zeta_j\leq0\}}1_{E_j}
                  \mid\mathcal Q_{j-1}]&\leq C M_jp_j,\\
 \mathbb E[e^{-d_j\zeta_j}1_{\{\zeta_j>0\}}1_{E_j}
                  \mid\mathcal Q_{j-1}]&\leq C M_jp_j.
\end{align*}
For the negative side use the geometric sum with ratio $e^{-\log z_j}$;
for the positive side use $e^{-d_j\log z_j}$ and cap the bound by one.
At $d_j=0$ the probability bound suffices. The bound is uniform in the arbitrary center, so the outside route
can now be integrated. Future child words remain to be integrated by
the backward tower.

Backward conditioning now bounds every product of positive half-line
factors followed by one negative half-line factor by
$C^j\prod_{l\leq j}M_lp_l$, and the fully surviving branch by
$C^{m-1}p_m\prod_{l<m}M_lp_l$. For completeness set
$a_j=M_jp_j$ for $j<m$, $a_m=p_m$, $r_j=\sigma_j/\sigma_1$, and
\[
 B_0=\sum_{j\leq m}r_j\log a_j,\quad
 \theta_j=r_j^{-1}\sum_{l>j}r_l\log a_l,\quad
 \xi_j=X/r_j+\theta_j.
\]
Stop the actual projected route at the first $\eta_j\leq\xi_j$.
The original capacity is $C_H\pi_G(q)e^{P_j}$, and the carry identity
gives on this branch
\[
 e^{P_j}=e^{X+c_j}e^{\zeta_j}
             \prod_{l<j}e^{-d_l\zeta_l},\qquad
 c_j=\theta_j-\sum_{l<j}d_l\theta_l
     =B_0-\sum_{l\leq j}\log a_l.
\]
The terminal branch has $c_m=-\sum_{l<m}d_l\theta_l$ and the same
last expression. Summing stopped capacities and using the
backward estimates proves for a surviving set $\mathcal S\subseteq
\bigcap_jE_j$ that
\[
 I(\mathcal S)\leq C_H
 \min\{1,e^X\prod_ja_j^{r_j}\},\qquad
 (\prod_ja_j^{r_j})^{\sigma_1}
 =\prod_{j<m}M_j^{\sigma_j}\prod_jp_j^{\sigma_j}.
\]
If a $p_j$ vanishes, the conditional bound makes the finite surviving
support empty, and no logarithm is required. For $m=1$ the direct
full-word capacity proves the assertion. This calculation preserves
the actual descendant lists and is the simple-plateau tower used in
the causal proof; hard plateaux supply their own three conditional
kernels in Lemma~\ref{upper:hard-kernels}.

\subsubsection{The ordinary rectangle and the same-count root integral}
\label{updetail:ordinary-root}
We prove Proposition~\ref{upper:root-contract}. The ordinary factor
has two sources: a local root atom and a ballot denominator from the
largest-block rectangle. Both depend on the reservoir count, so we
estimate them jointly before averaging outside counts. Positive layer
integration then combines the rectangle with an arbitrary prefix
translate and with the polynomial outgoing cover profile.

The proof proceeds through three operations: construct the rectangle
minimum, establish two Poisson mode bounds on its largest-block
count, and sum the translated root lattice in each layer. Write the unread original
suffix as blocks with $h_1>\cdots>h_m\geq2$, $w_i=\log h_i$,
$c_i=h_i-1$, lengths $L_i\geq0$, and $U=\sum_iL_i$.
Let $0<t\leq s<1$, $r=t/s$, in the fixed compact ranges.
With the entire prefix fixed, take arbitrary $D>0$ and $\kappa\in\R$,
and set
\[
 Z=\sum_i(w_iN_i-c_iL_i),\qquad X=\kappa+rZ.
\]
After the positive enlargement, the $N_i$ are independent Poisson
counts with means comparable to $L_i$. The natural means are
$h_i^tL_i$. Conditional on each count there are its original uniform
positions, with all $n_i+1$ gaps. Completed harmonic-cell budgets are
used consistently in $Z$, and their bounded difference from physical
budgets is included in $\kappa$, keeping $X$ unchanged.

Choose a largest original block $M=L_{i_*}$ and put
\[
 A=\sum_{i<i_*}L_i,\quad B=\sum_{i>i_*}L_i,\quad
 B_{\rm act}=\sum_{i>i_*}(w_iN_i-c_iL_i),\quad
 A_{\rm act}=-\sum_{i<i_*}(w_iN_i-c_iL_i).
\]
Then $Z=B_{\rm act}+Z_*-A_{\rm act}$ and $M\leq U\leq mM$.
The two outside sums are independent and retain all their counts.

\emph{The rectangle minimum.} Three actual rectangles are used before enlargement. A threshold at
the beginning of the suffix assigns its primes freely and bounds
earlier contributions by their full original rectangles, giving
$I\leq Ce^Z$. A threshold within the largest block, with its $j$
smallest prime logarithms retained, gives
$I\leq Ce^{B_{\rm act}}W_{*,N_*}$, where $W_{*,n}$ is the capped
ordered-sum rectangle of \eqref{ordsum:rectangle}. To verify this,
the $h_*-1$ unresolved widths are bounded by the prefix scale times
$1+\sum_{l\leq j}e^{(w_*/c_*)\operatorname{cell}_l}$, whereas
the free later labels contribute $h_*^{-j}$ after normalization.
Minimize over $j$, and use the right endpoint rectangle for the cap
one. The remaining rectangle is $I\leq C$.
Thus, together with a prefix cap $I\leq CDe^X$, the same tuple obeys
\begin{equation}
 I\leq C\widehat V,\qquad
 \widehat V=\min\{1,e^Z,e^{B_{\rm act}}W_{*,N_*},De^X\}.
 \label{updetail:ordinary-envelope}
\end{equation}
For every $n\geq0$ and $\ell\geq0$,
Lemma~\ref{ordsum:rectangle-tail} gives
\[
 \mathbb P(W_{*,n}>e^{-\ell}\mid n)
 \leq\min\left\{1,
 \frac{C(1+\ell)(C_1+Z_*+\ell)_+}{1+n}\right\}.
\]
For negative $\ell$ the event is empty.

\emph{The root atom with the ballot denominator.}
Fix all outside counts and restrict $Z$ to an interval
$[E,E+W]$ of fixed width. There are at most $1+W/\log2$ possible
$N_*$. The two full Poisson mode bounds
\begin{equation}
 \sup_n p_\mu(n)\leq C(1+\mu)^{-1/2},\qquad
 \sup_n\frac{p_\mu(n)}{1+n}\leq C(1+\mu)^{-3/2}
 \label{updetail:poisson-modes}
\end{equation}
follow from Stirling near the mode and the elementary Poisson tails;
they include $n=0$ and all noncentral counts. In the event $e^{B_{\rm act}}W_{*,N_*}>e^{-\ell}$, the left reserve is
$1+\ell+B_{\rm act}$ and the right reserve is $C_1+Z+\ell+A_{\rm act}$. The endpoint rectangle also requires
$Z+\ell\geq0$. Apply the two bounds in
\eqref{updetail:poisson-modes} separately, then average the independent
sides. Since $\mathbb E(B_{\rm act})_+\leq CB$ and
$\mathbb E(A_{\rm act})_+\leq CA$, this gives
\begin{align*}
 &\mathbb P\{Z\in[E,E+W],\ e^Z>e^{-\ell},\
                 e^{B_{\rm act}}W_{*,N_*}>e^{-\ell}\}\\
 &\qquad\leq C(1+U)^{-1/2}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{(1+\ell+B)(1+(E+\ell)_++A)}{1+M}\right\}.
\end{align*}
The root atom and ballot denominator have already been obtained
from the same $N_*$.

\emph{Layer integration at the translated root.}
Put $H_0=(-\log D-\kappa)/r$ and $w=Z-H_0$. Then
$e^{-sX}=D^se^{-tw}$ and $De^X=e^{rw}$. Positive layer cake in
\eqref{updetail:ordinary-envelope} gives
\begin{align*}
 D^{-s}\mathbb E[e^{-sX}\widehat V]
 =\int_0^\infty e^{-\ell}\,
 \mathbb E\big[e^{-tw}1_{\{w>-\ell/r\}}
 1_{\{Z+\ell\geq0\}}
 1_{\{W_*>e^{-\ell-B_{\rm act}}\}}\big]\,d\ell.
\end{align*}
At fixed outside counts, $a=w+\ell/r>0$ runs along a translated
lattice with spacing $w_*$. Moreover
$Z+\ell=H_0+a-(1/r-1)\ell$, so its nonnegativity forces
$a\geq-H_0$ up to a fixed geometric translation. Uniformly over
the lattice translate and $b\geq0$,
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{a>0,\ a\geq-H_0-C}e^{-ta}&\leq Ce^{-t(H_0)_-},\\
 \sum_{a>0,\ a\geq-H_0-C}e^{-ta}(C+H_0+a+b)_+
 &\leq Ce^{-t(H_0)_-}(1+(H_0)_++b).
\end{align*}
For $H_0<0$, shifting the lattice by $(H_0)_-$ gives the displayed
exponential factor. For $H_0\geq0$, the sum begins at zero. The
negative deficit thus appears only in that exponential factor.
Using first the first mode bound and then the second with the ballot
tail bounds the conditional integrand before $e^{-\ell}$ by the
minimum of
\[
 Ce^{s\ell-t(H_0)_-}(1+M)^{-1/2},\qquad
 Ce^{s\ell-t(H_0)_-}(1+M)^{-3/2}
 [1+\ell+(B_{\rm act})_+][1+(H_0)_++(A_{\rm act})_+].
\]
Average the independent sides separately in these two bounds, then
take their minimum. Since $1-s$ has a fixed positive lower bound,
integration against $e^{-(1-s)\ell}$ yields
\begin{equation}
 \mathbb E[e^{-sX}\widehat V]
 \leq CD^se^{-t(H_0)_-}(1+U)^{-1/2}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{(1+B)(1+(H_0)_++A)}{1+M}\right\}.
 \label{updetail:joint-root}
\end{equation}
Missing sides contribute exactly one; an empty suffix is treated by
the deterministic minimum with the same $1+$length conventions.

\emph{The polynomial outgoing profile.}
The outgoing profile needed in the causal theorem is
$J_\beta(X+\log D)$ instead of $De^X$, where
$J_\beta(v)=\min\{1,C_\beta e^v(1+(-v)_+)^\beta\}$ and
$\beta\geq0$ is fixed. If $J_\beta(v)>e^{-\ell}$, then
\[
 v>-L_\beta(\ell),\qquad
 L_\beta(\ell)=\ell+2\beta\log(2+\ell)+C_\beta'.
\]
Indeed $(1+u)^\beta\leq Ce^{u/2}$ first gives
$u=(-v)_+\leq2\ell+C$, which substituted back gives the stated
bound. Now set $q=r(Z-H_0)+L_\beta(\ell)>0$. The tilt becomes
$D^se^{sL_\beta(\ell)}e^{-sq}$ and
$Z+\ell\leq H_0+q/r$. The endpoint cap still forces
$q\geq r(H_0)_-$ up to a fixed translation. The same lattice sums
give $e^{-t(H_0)_-}$ and the same right reserve. The only change in
the layer integration is the weight
\[
 e^{-\ell+sL_\beta(\ell)}
 \leq Ce^{-(1-s)\ell}(2+\ell)^{2s\beta},
\]
whose integral, also multiplied by $1+\ell$, is uniformly finite.
This proves \eqref{updetail:joint-root} with the polynomial profile
and hence Proposition~\ref{upper:root-contract}.

\emph{Averaging the prefix deviation.}
For the natural suffix put
$D_{\rm mean}=\sum_iL_i(h_i^t\log h_i-(h_i-1))\geq0$ and
\[
 \mathcal B_I=(1+U)^{-1/2}
 \min\{1,(1+B)(1+D_{\rm mean}+A)/(1+M)\}.
\]
The preceding bound also gives
\[
 \mathbb E[e^{-sX}\widehat V]
 \leq CD^s\mathcal B_Ie^{-t(H_0)_-}
 \left[1+\frac{(H_0-D_{\rm mean})_+}{1+D_{\rm mean}+A}\right].
\]
The root identity is
$\kappa=-rD_{\rm mean}+\Delta_{\rm pre}$, so
$H_0-D_{\rm mean}=-(\Delta_{\rm pre}+\log D)/r$.
This is the explicit prefix deviation weight used in the final upper
