expectation. It remains together with $D^s$ under that expectation;
the conditional estimate allows arbitrary correlation among prefix
costs, counts and geometric sums.


\subsection{Conditional plateau tower, normalized capacities and shot moments}
\label{supp:causal-tower}
For clarity, we isolate the finite conditional mechanism behind the
ordered cover. Half-line kernels compose by backward conditioning;
the chosen offsets make every stopping capacity have the same pooled
cost; and polynomial floors place a hard right stop after the middle
of its block. A relative Poisson--Mecke argument then attaches the
shared shots while preserving each plateau's power.

\subsubsection{The conditional plateau filtration}

Fix the whole uncolored environment \(G\). Let \(\pi_{G}\) be its product fine-label law, \(Q_{0} \subset \ldots \subset Q_{m}\) its plateau-route
filtration, and

\[
 \sigma_1>\cdots>\sigma_m>0,\quad
 r_j=\sigma_j/\sigma_1,\quad
 d_j=r_j/r_{j+1}-1\quad(j<m).
\]

Let the grouped outputs \(Z_{j}\) be \(Q_{j}\)-measurable and define

\[
 \eta_j=\sum_{l\le j}\frac{r_l}{r_j}Z_l,\qquad
 P_j=\sum_{l\le j}Z_l,\qquad
 X=\sum_{l\le m}r_lZ_l.
\]

Assume \(X\) is uncolored and thus fixed under \(\pi_{G}\). Directly expanding
the sums gives the identities

\[
 P_j=\eta_j-\sum_{l<j}d_l\eta_l,\qquad
 P_m=X/r_m-\sum_{l<m}d_l\eta_l.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

For thresholds \(\xi_{j}\) fixed by \(G\), put \(\zeta_{j} = \eta_{j} - \xi_{j}\). Let
\(E_{j}\) be the current plateau mask. Suppose the following bounds hold on
every preceding plateau atom:

\[
 \begin{split}
 \mathbb E_{\pi_G}
   [e^{\zeta_j}\mathbf1_{\zeta_j\le0}\mathbf1_{E_j}\mid Q_{j-1}]
       &\le Cb_j,\\
 \mathbb E_{\pi_G}
   [e^{-d_j\zeta_j}\mathbf1_{\zeta_j>0}\mathbf1_{E_j}\mid Q_{j-1}]
       &\le Cb_j,
 \end{split}\qquad j<m,
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

and \(\mathbb{P}_{\pi} ( E_{m} | Q_{m - 1} ) \le Cb_{m}\). All \(b_{j} = b_{j} ( G )\) are fixed uncolored
numbers. Then any product of positive half-line factors followed by
one negative half-line factor has expectation at most
\(C^{j} \prod_{l \le j} b_{l}\). The fully continuing terminal branch is at
most \(C^{m} \prod_{l \le m} b_{l}\).

\textbf{Proof.} Write the terminal negative factor as \(g_{j}\) and the earlier
positive factors as \(f_{l}\). Since \(\prod_{l < j} f_{l}\) is
\(Q_{j - 1}\)-measurable, the tower property gives

\[
 \mathbb E\left[g_j\prod_{l<j}f_l\right]
   =\mathbb E\left[\mathbb E(g_j\mid Q_{j-1})\prod_{l<j}f_l\right]
   \le Cb_j\,\mathbb E\prod_{l<j}f_l.
\]

Apply the second bound of (2) successively in reverse plateau order.
The same calculation starts from \(\mathbf{1}_{E_{m}}\) for the terminal branch.
Throughout this calculation the uncolored environment stays fixed
under its original law. A future mask is bounded uniformly before the
current middle is integrated, leaving that middle with its original
binomial law on each preceding atom. \qed

The local product law on preceding atoms, required in the
simple-plateau kernel, is also exact. Original block \(i\) can
assign its primes only to names with indices \(c \ge i\) or to the unused
name. If it is local to plateau \(j\), all preceding exterior names have
smaller indices and are ineligible. Therefore all their routes are
deterministically child on those slots. Conditioning any preceding atom
does not observe a random label in a current local block; it leaves
its original categorical product law. This supplies the local-law assertion used in the simple kernels of
Section~\ref{upper:section}.

\subsubsection{Offsets and stopping capacities}

The offsets distribute the future pool costs among the current
thresholds. Their telescoping identity makes each stopping branch
carry exactly the pool factors already encountered.

Choose arbitrary positive uncolored pools \(a_{j}\) and set

\[
 B=\sum_jr_j\log a_j,\qquad
 \theta_j=r_j^{-1}\sum_{l>j}r_l\log a_l,\qquad
 \xi_j=X/r_j+\theta_j.
\]

Define

\[
 c_j=\theta_j-\sum_{l<j}d_l\theta_l\quad(j<m),\qquad
 c_m=-\sum_{l<m}d_l\theta_l.
\]

Then an exact coefficient calculation gives

\[
 c_j+\sum_{l\le j}\log a_l=B\quad(1\le j\le m).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

Indeed \(d_{l} / r_{l} = 1 / r_{l + 1} - 1 / r_{l}\); summing this identity determines
the coefficient of every \(\log a_{l}\) on the left to be exactly \(r_{l}\).
Using (1), a complete first stop at plateau \(j < m\) has exponent

\[
 P_j=X+c_j+\zeta_j-\sum_{l<j}d_l\zeta_l.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

If each complete projected atom has geometric capacity at most
\(C \pi_{G} ( atom ) \exp ( P_{j} )\), (2) and (4) bound the total capacity of that
branch by

\[
 Ce^{X+c_j}\prod_{l\le j}b_l.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

For the fully continuing terminal branch the same bound follows from
\(P_{m} = X + c_{m} - \sum_{l < m} d_{l} \zeta_{l}\) and its terminal mask estimate.

A hard internal stop has the same conclusion whenever its established
conditional capacity bound on the preceding atom is

\[
 C\pi_G(\alpha)e^{P_{j-1}+x_j}b_j,
 \qquad x_j=\xi_j-\eta_{j-1}/u_{j-1}.
\]

This is because

\[
 P_{j-1}+x_j=X+c_j-\sum_{l<j}d_l\zeta_l.
\]

The preceding positive half-line kernels are then applied on the
original ancestor fibers, exactly as for a complete stop.

Suppose all left-failure covers have total capacity at most
\(CS \exp ( - h )\), and \(b_{j} ( h ) \le a_{j} ( 1 + h )^{\beta}\). There are only
$C_H$ complete or internal branch types. Equations (3)--(5)
then prove

\[
 I_{\rm actual}\le C\min\{1,
       Se^{-h}+e^{X+B}(1+h)^{m\beta}\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

This is the passage to \eqref{upper:pre-profile}. The geometric
capacities provide the branch exponents; the conditional tower
integrates their private masses on the original fibers.

\subsubsection{Choice of the gate from preceding data}

A right stop must occur late enough to leave deterministic end banks
and a count middle. The offset identity removes all future pool
scales from the stopping level, so the gate can be chosen from the
current and preceding lengths alone.

Let \(L_{S} = 1 + \log ( 2 S )\), \(\beta_{*} \ge m \beta\),
\(D = L_{S}^{\beta_{*}} \exp ( B )\), and \(w_{0} = X + \log D\). When \(w_{0} < 0\), take

\[
 h=\lceil\log(2S)-w_0\rceil.
\]

At a hard plateau whose earlier routes continued, \(\zeta_{l} > 0\). Its dual
left reserve is \(h_{\mathrm{eff}} = h + \min ( P_{j - 1} , 0 )\). Hence

\[
 h_{\rm eff}+x_j
  \le h+P_{j-1}+x_j
  =h+X+c_j-\sum_{l<j}d_l\zeta_l
  \le h+X+c_j.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

Since \(h + X + B \le \log ( 2 S ) + 1\), (3) and \(\log \alpha_{h} \le 0\) imply

\[
 h_{\rm eff}+x_j+\log\alpha_h-\log S
    \le C-\sum_{l\le j}\log a_l.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

A floor \(a_{l} \ge ( 2 + T_{l} )^{- D_{l}}\) gives a bound involving \emph{only prior
and current lengths}. If the hard-edge geometric dominance gives
\(T_{l} \le C M\) for every \(l \le j\), the right side of (8) is at most
\(C + D_{\mathrm{gate}} \log ( 2 + M )\).

For \(0 \le w \le M / 2\), the right wall lies below the left wall whenever

\[
 h_{\rm eff}+x_j+\log\alpha_h-\log S
    \le A_1\log(1+M-w)-A_0\log(1+w).
\]

The right side is at least \(( A_{1} - A_{0} ) \log ( 1 + M / 2 )\). Since
\(\log ( 2 + M ) / \log ( 1 + M / 2 )\) is bounded for \(M \ge 1\), choosing \(A_{1}\) once
larger than \(A_{0} + C D_{\mathrm{gate}} + C '\) proves that a right-governed first hit
cannot occur before \(M / 2\). The scalar polynomial exponent \(K\) and
pool exponent \(\beta\) may then be chosen after \(A_{1}\); they do not occur
in (8) except through the already eliminated nonnegative
\(\beta_{*} \log L_{S}\). The floors come from the numerical profile's polynomial lower bounds
and can be chosen before \(A_{1}\). This gives the stated order of the
constants.

Using this admissible \(h\) in (6),

\[
 Se^{-h}\le\tfrac12e^{w_0},\qquad
 e^{X+B}(1+h)^{m\beta}
  \le Ce^{w_0}(1+(-w_0)_+)^{\beta_*}.
\]

For \(w_{0} \ge 0\), the cap \(I_{\mathrm{actual}} \le C\) suffices. This proves the claimed
polynomial rising profile once its local geometric capacities and
half-line kernels are available.

\subsubsection{Relative Poisson shot attachment preserves plateau powers}

The shared shot may read the same clocks as the rare local events.
To preserve their profile factors, we need insertion bounds relative
to those events. Expanding a fixed-degree shot into occurrence
partitions and applying Mecke supplies exactly such bounds.

Let independent Poisson restrictions \(N_{j}\) represent disjoint local
plateau banks, with deterministic intensity measures. Suppose a
nonnegative functional \(f_{j} ( h , N_{j} )\) satisfies, for every fixed number
\(q\) of inserted occurrences and all their deterministic positions,

\[
 f_j(h,N_j+\text{insertions})^{\sigma_j}
      \le C_q f_j(h+C_q,N_j)^{\sigma_j},
 \quad
 \mathbb E f_j(h,N_j)^{\sigma_j}
      \le C(1+h)^K F_j.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

Finite sums of deterministic bank-position expressions are permitted:
apply fractional subadditivity before their deterministic position sums.
Assume a nonnegative shot \(S\) is a finite-degree positive polynomial
in integrable Poisson shot sums, with the integrals of every occurrence
partition of the required degree bounded uniformly in the physical
lengths. Then for every fixed \(p \ge 0\) and every plateau subset \(J\),

\[
 \mathbb E\left[S^p\prod_{j\in J}f_j(h_j,N_j)^{\sigma_j}\right]
       \le C_p\prod_{j\in J}(1+h_j)^K F_j.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

\textbf{Proof.} Put \(r=\lceil p\rceil\). By \(S^p\le1+S^r\), it is enough
to estimate the zeroth moment and one integer moment. Expand the
positive polynomial for that moment. In each monomial, partition the
occurrence indices according to equality of Poisson points. The number
of partitions is finite, and each uses a bounded number \(q\) of
distinct points. The
multivariate Mecke identity changes its expectation into an integral
over these \(q\) deterministic inserted positions of the original
expectation of the product of functionals with those insertions. Apply
(9) to each plateau, then independence of the original disjoint local
restrictions. The product expectation is bounded by
\(C_{q} \prod ( 1 + h_{j} )^{K} F_{j}\); the fixed reserve enlargement does not
change this order. Every remaining partition integral is bounded by the
shot hypothesis. Summing the finitely many positive terms proves the bound at the
original plateau powers. \qed

The actual shots in Section~\ref{app:upper-details} have the form

\[
 Z(v)=1+\sum_{x\le v}e^{x-v},\qquad
 S=\sum_v\omega(v)Z(v)^d\prod_cZ(\tau_c).
\]

The local Poisson intensity is bounded on unit intervals, including
atomic prime intensities. Every occurrence-partition integral of a
product of the exponential kernels is bounded: integrate one kernel
against its bounded-unit-mass intensity and sum its exponentially
decreasing unit-interval tails. The outside endpoint locations are
deterministic; \(\sum_{v} \omega ( v )\) is bounded for the stated sufficiently
large fixed decay exponent. Products and finite moments are handled
by positive expansion and Minkowski before the position sums. This verifies the occurrence-partition integrability required in
(10), in addition to the ordinary bound \(\mathbb{E} S^{p} \le C\).

A raw prefix count \(N_{\mathrm{pre}}\) is attached by one additional Mecke point.
Its intensity integral is its mean, bounded by \(C V_{\mathrm{pre}}\). This proves
the corresponding bound with \(1 + N_{\mathrm{pre}}\) and factor \(C ( 1 + V_{\mathrm{pre}} )\).

For a count middle overlapping an intermediate reserve, use a decreasing
weight \(f ( N )\) and increasing reserve bound \(g ( N )\).
Their covariance inequality holds for every distribution of \(N\):
with an independent copy \(N '\),

\[
 2\operatorname{Cov}(f(N),g(N))
 =\mathbb E[(f(N)-f(N'))(g(N)-g(N'))]\le0.
\]

After this extraction the other deterministic bank inputs are disjoint.
This justifies the product-moment step because the proved rank-separation geometry gives that each middle lies in at most one intermediate
reserve group. The required insertion estimates are obtained by
conditioning the finitely many inserted private marks and deleting
those occurrences at a bounded reserve enlargement; middle inverse
count factors decrease under insertion. In a fixed-width band the
original middle marks may remain unobserved, so its maximum atom is
unchanged. Arbitrary band centers have already disappeared from the
max-atom bound.



\section{Scalar large deviations of conditional survival}
\label{fp:app:ldp}

The positive persistence spectrum describes Laplace transforms of the
conditional survival cost. To describe the cost itself, we also need
inverse survival moments. Their finite domain has a boundary determined
by the environmental-to-private variance ratio. We prove existence and
regularity of the limiting pressure throughout that domain, show that
its derivative reaches every positive cost, and then derive the full
scalar large-deviation principle by a direct change of measure.

There are two new ingredients beyond the positive-order theory.
Reverse hypercontractivity identifies the inverse-moment domain, and
a covariance interpolation supplies the product inequality needed
for existence at those orders. Convex Gaussian curvature controls the
tilted variance. These bounds also identify the almost-sure conditional
cost and the scalar value selected by each environmental tilt.

\subsection{Pressure and the rate function}

Throughout this appendix, $0<\rho<1$ is fixed and $X,Y$ are the
independent stationary standard OU processes of \eqref{pr:defF}.
Put
\[
 \beta^2=\frac\rho{1-\rho},\qquad
 S_t=-\log q_t(X),\qquad \theta_c=\beta^{-2}.
\]
Stationarity at time zero and equality of the two covariance
functions are part of the model throughout this appendix. They permit
the common whitening and the endpoint comparison used below. Every continuous environmental path is bounded
on $[0,t]$, and a private OU path in a sufficiently high fixed tube has
positive probability. Consequently $q_t>0$ almost surely. The initial
constraint gives $q_t\le\Phi(\beta X_0)<1$, so $0<S_t<\infty$.

\begin{theorem}[Pressure and full scalar large deviations]
\label{fp:thm:scalar-ldp}
For every $\theta<\theta_c$, the finite limit
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:Lambda}
 \Lambda_\rho(\theta)=
 \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\log\EE e^{\theta S_t}
\end{equation}
exists. It is nondecreasing, convex and belongs to
$C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(( -\infty,\theta_c))$. For every $t>0$,
$\EE e^{\theta S_t}=\infty$ precisely when $\theta\ge\theta_c$.
Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:Lambda-boundaries}
 \Lambda_\rho(\theta)\longrightarrow\infty,
 \quad\Lambda_\rho'(\theta)\longrightarrow\infty
 \quad(\theta\uparrow\theta_c),\qquad
 \Lambda_\rho'(\theta)\longrightarrow0
 \quad(\theta\to-\infty).
\end{equation}
The variables $S_t/t$ satisfy a full large-deviation principle at speed
$t$, with good convex rate function
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:rate}
 I_\rho(y)=\sup_{\theta<\theta_c}
                 \{\theta y-\Lambda_\rho(\theta)\}.
\end{equation}
Thus, for every Borel set $B\subset\R$,
\begin{align}\label{fp:eq:full-ldp}
 -\inf_{B^\circ}I_\rho
 &\le\liminf_{t\to\infty}t^{-1}\log\PP(S_t/t\in B)\notag\\
 &\le\limsup_{t\to\infty}t^{-1}\log\PP(S_t/t\in B)
 \le-\inf_{\overline B}I_\rho.
\end{align}
The rate is finite for every $y>0$ and infinite for $y\le0$.
Its unique zero is $\gamma_\rho=\Lambda_\rho'(0)$, and
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:tail-slope}
 \lim_{y\to\infty}\frac{I_\rho(y)}y=\frac{1-\rho}{\rho}.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}

\subsection{The inverse-moment domain}

Whitening turns the finite-grid survival constraint into a convex cone.
Reverse hypercontractivity then bounds its negative moments in terms
of ordinary survival. The initial-time constraint gives the matching
obstruction at the domain boundary. We keep this finite-time domain
calculation separate from the later extensive lower bound for pressure.

On a finite ordered grid let $\Sigma$ be its OU covariance matrix.
Simultaneously whitening the environmental and private vectors gives
the convex cone $C=\Sigma^{-1/2}\R_+^n$ and
\[
 q(x)=\PP\{Z+\beta x\in C\}=T_{\sqrt\rho}\ind_C(x),
 \qquad x,Z\sim N(0,I_n),
\]
where $T_rf(x)=\EE f(rx+\sqrt{1-r^2}Z)$. The second equality uses
the cone property. The Gaussian reverse-hypercontractive inequality
\cite[Section~3.3, equation~(3.14)]{CDP} states
\[
 \|T_rf\|_s\ge\|f\|_p,
 \qquad s<p<1,\quad r^2\le\frac{1-p}{1-s}.
\]
For $s<0$ the convention is
$\|f\|_s=(\EE f^s)^{1/s}$, with zero values handled by positive
approximation. For $0<\theta<\theta_c$ choose
$s=-\theta$ and $p=1-\rho(1+\theta)>0$. Raising the norm inequality
to the negative power gives
\[
 \EE q_{\mathrm{grid}}^{-\theta}
 \le a_{\mathrm{grid}}^{-
           \theta/[1-\rho(1+\theta)]},
 \qquad a_{\mathrm{grid}}=\EE q_{\mathrm{grid}}.
\]
Nested dense grids give $q_{\mathrm{grid}}\downarrow q_t$ and
$a_{\mathrm{grid}}\downarrow a(t)>0$ by continuity. Monotone
convergence and \eqref{pr:ordinaryOU} therefore prove
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:neg-bound}
 \EE e^{\theta S_t}
 \le a(t)^{-\theta/[1-\rho(1+\theta)]},
 \qquad
 \limsup_{t\to\infty}t^{-1}\log\EE e^{\theta S_t}
 \le\frac{\theta}{2[1-\rho(1+\theta)]}.
\end{equation}
Nonpositive orders are finite since $S_t\ge0$.

Conversely, $q_t\le\Phi(\beta X_0)$. The elementary Gaussian bound
$\Phi(-z)\le(2\pi)^{-1/2}z^{-1}e^{-z^2/2}$ for $z>0$ shows that
$\EE\Phi(\beta X_0)^{-\theta}$ dominates a positive constant times
\[
 \int_1^\infty x^\theta
       \exp\{(\theta\beta^2-1)x^2/2\}\,dx.
\]
This is infinite for $\theta\ge\theta_c$, including equality.
This identifies the finite-time moment domain. Divergence of the
limiting pressure requires a lower bound proportional to the horizon,
which we prove below using a fixed-density time grid.

\subsection{A covariance interpolation for existence}

For inverse moments we need a product comparison in the direction
opposite to the positive-order association bound. We interpolate the
single OU correlation joining two blocks. The MTP$_2$ property of the
Gaussian distribution function controls the sign of the resulting
derivative throughout the full moment domain.

Divide an ordered finite OU grid
into two consecutive nonempty blocks. Its Markov representation is
\[
 U_{j+1}=r_jU_j+\sqrt{1-r_j^2}\,G_{j+1},\qquad
 0<r_j<1,
\]
with independent standard Gaussian innovations and stationary $U_1$.
Replace only the correlation joining the blocks by $vr_j$,
$0\le v\le1$, and denote the resulting covariance by $\Sigma_v$.
Within-block covariances are unchanged, cross-block covariances are
multiplied by $v$, and hence
\[
 \dot\Sigma_{ii}=0,\qquad\dot\Sigma_{ij}\ge0\quad(i\ne j).
\]
The precision matrix remains tridiagonal with nonpositive
off-diagonal entries. Its Gaussian density is therefore MTP$_2$;
see \cite[Section~4.1]{Fallat}.

Let $u_v(z)=\PP\{N(0,\Sigma_v)\le z\}$. Its derivatives satisfy
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:cdf-mtp}
 u_i\ge0,\qquad \partial_{ij}\log u\ge0\quad(i\ne j).
\end{equation}
For the second assertion, the relation $w_i\le z_i$ for all $i$ is
closed under coordinatewise minimum and maximum, so its indicator
times the Gaussian density in $w$ is MTP$_2$ in $(w,z)$.
Insert any positive product Gaussian density in $z$ to make the joint
integral finite, apply MTP$_2$ marginalization
\cite[Proposition~3.4(ii)]{Fallat}, and cancel that product density.
Thus $u_v$ is MTP$_2$. Since it is positive and smooth, its
two-coordinate lattice inequality gives the second derivative
inequality in \eqref{fp:eq:cdf-mtp}.

For $\eta>-\theta_c$ put
$H_\eta(v)=\EE_{U\sim N(0,\Sigma_v)}u_v(\beta U)^\eta$.
Differentiation of the environmental Gaussian integral and the
private Gaussian heat equation give
\begin{align}\label{fp:eq:interpolation}
 H_\eta'(v)=\frac\eta2\sum_{i,j}\dot\Sigma_{ij}
 \EE\bigl[u^{\eta-2}
 \{(1+\beta^2)u u_{ij}
       +\beta^2(\eta-1)u_i u_j\}\bigr].
\end{align}
Here all derivatives of $u=u_v$ are evaluated at $\beta U$.
The expression in braces is exactly
\[
 (1+\beta^2)u^2\partial_{ij}\log u
             +(1+\eta\beta^2)u_i u_j.
\]
It is nonnegative for $i\ne j$, by \eqref{fp:eq:cdf-mtp} and
$\eta>-\beta^{-2}$. Consequently $H_\eta$ increases for $\eta>0$
and decreases for $-\theta_c<\eta<0$.

To justify differentiation at negative orders, we use a slightly
larger inverse moment to dominate the derivative integrands. On this fixed grid the covariance path is uniformly
positive definite. Lemma~\ref{fp:lem:curvature}, after whitening,
bounds $D^2\log u_v$ uniformly; its gradient is therefore bounded
by a fixed multiple of $1+|z|$, uniformly in $v$. Values and
gradients at zero are bounded by compactness of the covariance path.
Choose $-\eta<\theta'<\theta_c$. The reverse-hypercontractive
bound at order $\theta'$ is uniform in $v$: the corresponding
orthant probabilities are positive and have a positive minimum
on this compact path. H\"older then bounds all polynomial-weighted
integrands in \eqref{fp:eq:interpolation}. This justifies Gaussian
integration by parts and removal of spatial cutoffs. For $\eta>0$
the same derivative bounds and $u^\eta\le1$ suffice.

We now pass from the finite interpolation to the continuous product
inequalities. At $v=0$ the blocks are independent. In two adjacent
continuous
intervals choose dense grids with no repeated common endpoint;
points approaching the endpoint from either side impose it in each
marginal limit. For negative powers use monotone convergence and
\eqref{fp:eq:neg-bound}; positive powers use bounded convergence.
Writing $M_\theta(t)=\EE e^{\theta S_t}$ gives
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:pressure-products}
 M_\theta(s+t)\le M_\theta(s)M_\theta(t)
 \quad(0<\theta<\theta_c),\qquad
 M_\theta(s+t)\ge M_\theta(s)M_\theta(t)
 \quad(\theta<0).
\end{equation}
For positive $\theta$, \eqref{fp:eq:neg-bound} bounds
$0\le\log M_\theta(t)\le C_\theta(t+1)$.
For negative $\theta=-p$, Jensen and $q^p\ge q$ when $p\le1$
give
\[
 -\max(1,p)[t/2+\log\pi]\le\log M_{-p}(t)\le0.
\]
The continuous-parameter subadditivity and superadditivity arguments
applied to \eqref{fp:eq:pressure-products} now prove existence and
finiteness in \eqref{fp:eq:Lambda}; specifically,
\[
 \Lambda_\rho(\theta)=
 \begin{cases}
  \inf_{t>0}t^{-1}\log M_\theta(t),&0<\theta<\theta_c,\\
  0,&\theta=0,\\
  \sup_{t>0}t^{-1}\log M_\theta(t),&\theta<0.
 \end{cases}
\]
The displayed linear bounds control the remainder in $T=nt+r$,
$0\le r<t$, giving the continuous-parameter limiting slope. Convexity
and monotonicity pass from the finite-time log moment generating
functions to their limit.

\subsection{Pressure regularity}

Throughout the inverse-moment domain, the negative-order tilt is
strongly log-concave. The curvature bound from
Lemma~\ref{fp:lem:curvature} therefore gives a dimension-free variance
estimate under every interior tilt. This supplies uniform control of
the pressure derivatives as both the time grid and horizon vary.

On a whitened grid write $A=-\log q$ and
$d\nu_\theta=e^{\theta A}d\gamma/\EE e^{\theta A}$.
The potential $V_\theta=|x|^2/2-\theta A(x)$ has
\[
 D^2V_\theta\succeq\kappa_\theta I,
 \qquad \kappa_\theta=
 \begin{cases}1,&\theta\le0,\\1-\theta\beta^2,&0<\theta<\theta_c.
 \end{cases}
\]
The Brascamp--Lieb variance inequality used in
Lemma~\ref{fp:lem:curvature} and its gradient estimate yield
\[
 \Var_{\nu_\theta}(A)
 \le\kappa_\theta^{-1}\EE_{\nu_\theta}|\nabla A|^2
 \le\frac{2\beta^2}{\kappa_\theta}\EE_{\nu_\theta}A.
\]
Thus, with $L_{t,\mathrm{grid}}(\theta)
=t^{-1}\log\EE e^{\theta A}$,
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:Lambda-curvature}
 0\le L_{t,\mathrm{grid}}''(\theta)
 \le\frac{2\beta^2}{\kappa_\theta}
              L_{t,\mathrm{grid}}'(\theta).
\end{equation}
For $t\ge1$, the preceding moment bounds control
$L_{t,\mathrm{grid}}$ uniformly on every compact subinterval of
$(-\infty,\theta_c)$, independently of the grid:
$a_{\mathrm{grid}}\ge a(t)$ in the inverse-moment bound, and the
same inequality applies to the positive-order bound.
Convex secants on a slightly larger compact interval bound
$L_{t,\mathrm{grid}}'$ uniformly. Therefore
\eqref{fp:eq:Lambda-curvature} bounds its second derivative uniformly.

For any fixed $t$ and compact order interval, an interior neighboring
order $\theta'$ larger than all its orders dominates
$A^j e^{\theta A}$, $j=0,1,2$. If $\theta'>0$,
$\EE e^{\theta'S_t}<\infty$ by \eqref{fp:eq:neg-bound}; if
$\theta'\le0$, the polynomial factors are bounded using the strict
order margin. Dominated convergence passes the first two derivatives
to the continuous-time function
$L_t(\theta)=t^{-1}\log M_\theta(t)$.
Its first derivatives are thus locally uniformly bounded and
equicontinuous for $t\ge1$. Arzel\`a--Ascoli, pointwise convergence of
$L_t$, and
$L_t(b)-L_t(a)=\int_a^bL_t'(\theta)\,d\theta$ prove
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:Lambda-derivative-limit}
 \Lambda_\rho\in C^{1,1}_{\mathrm{loc}}(( -\infty,\theta_c)),
 \qquad L_t'\longrightarrow\Lambda_\rho'
          \quad\hbox{locally uniformly}.
\end{equation}
In particular the tilted variance of $S_t/t$ is $O(t^{-1})$ on
each compact order interval. The conclusion controls the first
derivative by a local Lipschitz bound; it does not require a limiting
second derivative.

\subsection{Both pressure boundaries}

To obtain a full scalar LDP, the derivative of the pressure must cover
all positive costs. At the finite right boundary we prove an extensive
lower bound on inverse moments. At the left boundary we force a high
environmental tube, where private survival is arbitrarily likely.
These two constructions give the derivative limits needed for the
change-of-measure argument.

Take $n=\lfloor t\rfloor+1$ unit-spaced grid points in $[0,t]$.
Their covariance is $\Sigma_{ij}=r^{|i-j|}$, $r=e^{-1/2}$, and
write $Q=\Sigma^{-1}$. The eigenvalues of both matrices lie in
$[K^{-1},K]$ for $K=(1+r)/(1-r)$. This follows directly from the
tridiagonal OU precision matrix and its row sums.
For an environmental vector $x$ with $Qx\le0$, put
$h=-\beta Qx\ge0$. Markov's inequality for $e^{h^TZ}$ gives
\[
 q_{\mathrm{grid}}(x)=\PP\{Z\ge-\beta x\}
 \le\exp\{\beta h^Tx+h^T\Sigma h/2\}
 =\exp\{-\beta^2x^TQx/2\}.
\]
Since $q_t\le q_{\mathrm{grid}}$, for
$\delta=1-\theta\beta^2>0$ we obtain
\[
 M_\theta(t)\ge
 \int_{\{Qx\le0\}}e^{\theta\beta^2x^TQx/2}
                  \,dN(0,\Sigma)(x)
 =\delta^{-n/2}\PP\{QX\le0\}.
\]
The last equality uses homogeneity of the cone and Gaussian scaling.
Now $QX\sim N(0,Q)$. Its density on $[-1,0]^n$ is at least
$(2\pi K)^{-n/2}e^{-Kn/2}$. Hence
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:boundary-divergence}
 \Lambda_\rho(\theta)\ge
       \frac12\log\frac1{1-\theta\beta^2}-C,
       \qquad0<\theta<\theta_c,
\end{equation}
where $C$ is an absolute constant for this fixed unit grid.
This proves pressure divergence at the finite boundary, and convexity
then forces $\Lambda_\rho'(\theta)\to\infty$ there.

At the left boundary, a high environmental tube supplies moments
whose logarithmic cost per order can be made arbitrarily small.
Fix $a>0$ and set
\[
 p_a=\PP\{X_s\ge a:0\le s\le1\},\qquad
 r_a=\PP\{Y_s\ge-\beta a:0\le s\le1\}.
\]
These numbers are positive, and $r_a\uparrow1$ as $a\to\infty$.
Association on consecutive unit intervals implies
\[
 M_{-p}(t)\ge p_a^{\lceil t\rceil}
                   r_a^{p\lceil t\rceil},\qquad p>0.
\]
Consequently
$0\le\Lambda_\rho(-p)/(-p)
\le-\log r_a-(\log p_a)/p$.
Letting $p\to\infty$ and then $a\to\infty$ gives
$\Lambda_\rho(-p)/(-p)\to0$. For a nondecreasing convex function
finite on a left half-line, this sublinear asymptotic implies
$\Lambda_\rho'(-\infty)=0$.

\subsection{The full LDP bounds}

We prove the lower bound by tilting to each prescribed positive
cost. The tilted variance estimate gives concentration there.
For the upper bound, local Chernoff estimates cover compact sets and
exponential tightness removes compactness. We then verify the rate
at the nonpositive endpoint and its large-cost slope.

Choose
$0<\theta_0<\theta_c$. Since $S_t/t\ge0$, Chernoff's bound
\[
 \limsup_{t\to\infty}t^{-1}\log\PP(S_t/t>R)
 \le\Lambda_\rho(\theta_0)-\theta_0R
\]
proves exponential tightness.
The continuous derivative and its limits in
\eqref{fp:eq:Lambda-boundaries} show that every $y>0$ equals
$\Lambda_\rho'(\theta)$ for an interior $\theta$.
Convexity gives $I_\rho(y)=\theta y-\Lambda_\rho(\theta)<\infty$.
Under the tilted environmental law
\[
 \frac{d\PP_{\theta,t}}{d\PP}
       =e^{\theta S_t-tL_t(\theta)},
\]
the mean of $S_t/t$ tends to $y$, by
\eqref{fp:eq:Lambda-derivative-limit}, and its variance is
$L_t''(\theta)/t=O(t^{-1})$. It follows that
$\PP_{\theta,t}(|S_t/t-y|<\epsilon)\to1$.
Changing measure back gives
\[
 \liminf_{t\to\infty}t^{-1}\log
          \PP(|S_t/t-y|<\epsilon)
 \ge-I_\rho(y)-|\theta|\epsilon.
\]
For any open set containing $y$, let $\epsilon\downarrow0$
inside that set and then optimize over its positive points.

At $y<0$, the sublinear left asymptotic of $\Lambda_\rho$ makes
$I_\rho(y)=\infty$. Also
$I_\rho(0)=\sup_{p>0}\chi(p,\rho)=\infty$, by the unboundedness
of the positive spectrum proved in Theorem~\ref{fp:thm:regularity}.
Thus the rate is infinite at every nonpositive point, and the open-set
lower bound is completely determined by the positive points.

For the upper bound, fix a compact set $K$ and a number
$a<\inf_K I_\rho$. At each $y\in K$ choose an interior parameter
$\theta_y$ with $\theta_yy-\Lambda_\rho(\theta_y)>a$.
The strict inequality persists on a sufficiently small neighborhood
of $y$. Chernoff's bound on that neighborhood has upper rate at most
$-a$. A finite subcover proves the compact-set upper bound.
Exponential tightness extends it to every closed set, including
those with infinite rate infimum. The function $I_\rho$ is convex
and lower semicontinuous; for $y\ge0$ it dominates
$\theta_0y-\Lambda_\rho(\theta_0)$, while it is infinite on
$y\le0$. Its sublevel sets are therefore compact. This proves the
full LDP in \eqref{fp:eq:full-ldp}.

Finally, differentiability at zero shows that $I_\rho$ has its unique
zero at $\gamma_\rho=\Lambda_\rho'(0)$. For $y\ge\gamma_\rho$,
convexity gives $\Lambda_\rho(\theta)\ge\gamma_\rho\theta$, so
negative $\theta$ cannot improve the dual value at zero.
For $0\le\theta<\theta_c$, $\Lambda_\rho(\theta)\ge0$;
therefore $I_\rho(y)\le\theta_cy$. Every fixed
$\theta<\theta_c$ gives
$I_\rho(y)/y\ge\theta-\Lambda_\rho(\theta)/y$.
Let $y\to\infty$ and then $\theta\uparrow\theta_c$ to prove
\eqref{fp:eq:tail-slope}.

\subsection{Quenched slope, scalar duality and entropy}

Differentiability at zero identifies the ordinary conditional cost,
and the exponential concentration bounds strengthen convergence in
probability to almost-sure convergence. More generally, each interior
order tilt selects the corresponding pressure derivative. Convex
duality describes this selection and expresses its relative entropy
as a scalar large-deviation cost.

\begin{corollary}\label{fp:cor:scalar-consequences}
The quenched exponent satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:quenched-derivative}
 \frac{S_t}{t}\longrightarrow\gamma_\rho
 \quad\hbox{almost surely},\qquad
 \frac{\EE S_t}{t}\longrightarrow\gamma_\rho,
 \qquad
 \frac12+\frac\rho{16\pi}\le\gamma_\rho
          \le\frac1{2(1-\rho)}.
\end{equation}
Define the extended spectrum by
$\widetilde\chi(p,\rho)=-\Lambda_\rho(-p)$ for $p>-\theta_c$;
it agrees with $\chi$ for $p>0$ and vanishes at $p=0$.
Then
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:duality-extended}
 \widetilde\chi(p,\rho)
   =\inf_{y\ge0}\{I_\rho(y)+py\},\qquad
 I_\rho(y)=\sup_{p>-\theta_c}
          \{\widetilde\chi(p,\rho)-py\}.
\end{equation}
The infimum has the unique minimizer
$y_p=\Lambda_\rho'(-p)=\partial_p\widetilde\chi(p,\rho)>0$.
Under the pure environmental tilt
$d\nu_{p,t}=q_t^p d\PP/\EE q_t^p$, the variables $S_t/t$
have the full LDP with good rate
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:tilted-rate}
 I_{p,\rho}(y)=I_\rho(y)+py-\widetilde\chi(p,\rho).
\end{equation}
Moreover,
\begin{equation}\label{fp:eq:scalar-entropy}
 \lim_{t\to\infty}\frac1t\KL(\nu_{p,t}\Vert\PP)
 =I_\rho(y_p)
 =\widetilde\chi(p,\rho)-p\partial_p\widetilde\chi(p,\rho).
\end{equation}
\end{corollary}
\begin{proof}
We first identify the quenched slope and its bounds, then establish
the dual variational formulas. The tilted LDP follows by shifting the
pressure, and the entropy identity follows from its order derivative.

The mean convergence is \eqref{fp:eq:Lambda-derivative-limit} at
zero. Differentiability there and Chernoff's bound with small positive
and negative orders give, for each $\epsilon>0$, a constant
$c_\epsilon>0$ such that
$\PP(|S_t/t-\gamma_\rho|>\epsilon)\le e^{-c_\epsilon t}$
for all sufficiently large $t$. Borel--Cantelli proves convergence
along integers. Monotonicity of $S_t$ supplies the continuous-time
conclusion. Jensen and \eqref{pr:ordinaryOU} give
$\gamma_\rho\ge1/2$; the upper bound follows by taking the right
derivative at zero in \eqref{fp:eq:neg-bound}. For $0<p\le1/2$,
Theorem~\ref{fp:thm:annealing} gives
$\chi(p,\rho)/p\ge1/2+\rho/(16\pi)$; let $p\downarrow0$.

For any interior $\theta=-p$, the supporting-line inequality for
$\Lambda_\rho$ gives
$I_\rho(\Lambda_\rho'(\theta))
=\theta\Lambda_\rho'(\theta)-\Lambda_\rho(\theta)$.
It also proves that this value is the unique minimizer in the first
formula of \eqref{fp:eq:duality-extended}: equality forces $y$ into
the singleton subgradient of $\Lambda_\rho$ at $\theta$.
The second formula is just \eqref{fp:eq:rate} with $\theta=-p$.
For $p>0$, positivity of $y_p$ follows from strict increase of the
positive spectrum; for $p\le0$, it follows from
$\Lambda_\rho'(-p)\ge\gamma_\rho>0$.

The tilted limiting cumulant is
\[
 \Lambda_{p,\rho}(\theta)
     =\Lambda_\rho(\theta-p)-\Lambda_\rho(-p),
       \qquad\theta<\theta_c+p.
\]
It has the same regularity, variance bounds and derivative boundary
limits as the pressure already treated, and its finite right boundary
is positive. The identical exponential-tightness and tilt argument
therefore gives a full LDP. Taking its convex dual yields
\eqref{fp:eq:tilted-rate}. Finally the exact finite-time identity is
\[
 \KL(\nu_{p,t}\Vert\PP)
      =-p\EE_{\nu_{p,t}}S_t-\log\EE q_t^p.
\]
Derivative convergence proves \eqref{fp:eq:scalar-entropy}.
This entropy rate belongs to the pure environmental OU tilt. The
arithmetic accepting measures are constructed separately and are
outside the scope of this identity.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[Brownian normalization]
The Lamperti representation
$X_u=e^{-u/2}B^X_{e^u}$, $Y_u=e^{-u/2}B^Y_{e^u}$
transfers these statements to Brownian random-wall survival on
$[1,R]$, with speed $\log R$. The law at the left endpoint is
the one induced by Brownian time $1$; the appendix does not assert
the same finite-time moment domain for prescribed deterministic
initial values.
\end{remark}

\section{Constants and the length threshold}\label{appendix:constants}
The profile uses a single length threshold depending only on the
dimension. This appendix makes that choice explicit and checks that
all earlier geometric, probabilistic, and arithmetic requirements can
be met in a consistent order. The constants are deliberately generous;
their role is to establish uniform dependence on the dimension.
Harmonic stability then extends the estimate to vanishing lengths.

The verification has three stages. First we bound the primitive
coefficients, history sums, and exponent sensitivity. Next we choose
the proof parameters, followed by the regularity intercept, endpoint
reserve, arithmetic grid, and final length. Finally we explain why the
ordered-sum constant enters only the output comparison and prove the
equivalence of the lifted and original harmonic profiles.

\subsection{Coefficient bounds, scalar sensitivity and pivot sums}
\label{supp:finite-history-constants}
The following majorants organize the deterministic coefficients.
They also distinguish polynomial degrees from multiplicative
probability constants: a large comparison constant need not enlarge
the degree of a history weight.

Put \(H = k + 1\),

\[
 A_H=10^6H^{3H+30},\quad
 B_0=10H,\quad B_{j+1}=A_H(B_j+1)\ (j<H^2),
\]

\[
 U_H=\max\{(10H)^{10H},(2A_H)^{H^2+1}\},\quad
 Q_H=(100U_H)^{16^{100H^4}},\quad
 M_0=2^{\,2^{10000H^5}},\quad M_1=M_0^{1000}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
\]

For \(H \ge 2\), elementary logarithms give \(Q_{H} < M_{0}\).
Indeed \(\log U_{H} \le 100 H^{3} \log ( 10 H )\) and
\(\log_{2} ( 16^{100 H^{4}} ) = 400 H^{4}\), while
\(10000 H^{5} > 400 H^{4} + \log_{2} [ 100 H^{3} \log ( 10 H ) + \log 100 ]\).
The double exponential in (1) dominates the finite sequence of powers
arising from repeated applications of Young's inequality.

\subsubsection{Primitive constants}

The table records uniform lower bounds for positive coefficients and
upper bounds for their sizes. Its denominators involve only the
dimension, so the bounds remain valid when lengths or strict plateau
gaps have very different scales.

\begin{longtable}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.46\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{0.46\textwidth}}
\toprule
Calculation and location & Explicit bound \\
\midrule
Fine probabilities and transported coefficients, Section~\ref{profile:definition}, Section~\ref{paper:geometry} & \(p_{*} \ge H^{- H}\), \(\kappa_{*} \ge H^{- H - 1}\), rates at most \(H\) \\
Product compactness, Section~\ref{paper:geometry} & \(\sigma \ge \alpha_{2} > 1 / 2\), \(1 - \sigma \ge 1 / ( 10 H^{3} )\) \\
Nondegenerate proper child, Section~\ref{profile:definition} & \(z \ge \sqrt{2}\), \(z \le H - 1\), \(\log z > 1 / 3\) \\
Split/loss coefficients, Section~\ref{app:history-details} & absolute loss at most \(H \log H\); absolute contrast at most \(3 H \log H\) \\
Complete reference, Section~\ref{paper:ep-reference} & nonnegative complete comparison costs; local/old rank capacities are integers in \([ 1 , H ]\) \\
Clipped-prefix derivative and charge, Section~\ref{paper:ep-prefix-guards} & \(d_{0} \ge 1 / ( 100 H^{H + 6} )\), \(c_{\mathrm{ref}} \ge 1 / ( 1000 H^{H + 6} )\) \\
Local hierarchy, Section~\ref{paper:geometry} & \(V_{\mathrm{old}} \le 16 H^{6} T_{\mathrm{local}}\) \\
Proper nontrivial mixed entropy, Section~\ref{app:history-details} & per-slot gap at least \(2 H^{- 4 H}\), rate gap at least \(2 H^{- 5 H}\) \\
Pure child lifetime, Section~\ref{app:history-details} & \(\gamma_{z} > 1 / ( 4 H )\), resulting linear gap at least \(H^{- H - 1} / ( 4 H )\) \\
Terminal float, Section~\ref{app:history-details} & rank second difference at least \(H^{- H - 2}\); retained slope at least \(H^{- H - 1} / ( 2 H )\) \\
Atomic spread, Section~\ref{app:history-details} & curvature charge at least \(H^{- H - 1} / ( 2 H )\) times the spread \\
Original pivot reassignment, Section~\ref{app:history-details}; independent token proof & at most \(H - 1\) tokens, depth inflation coefficient at most \(H^{2}\) \\
Positive endpoint representative, Section~\ref{app:history-details} & representative weight at least \(( H + 1 )^{- H}\), marginal at least \(1 / ( H + 1 )\) \\
\bottomrule
\end{longtable}

Every positive entry and its reciprocal is bounded by \(U_{H}\).
Within an eligible cell, a retained fine letter has conditional
probability \(p_c/\mathbb P(\text{cell})\ge p_c\), so the same
lower bound \(H^{-H}\) applies.
None of these bounds uses a strict adjacent-product gap.

The pure lifetime row uses
\(( z - 1 ) \log ( 1 + 1 / z )\) with \(z \ge \sqrt{2}\), \(z \le H\); since
\(\sqrt{2} - 1 > 2 / 5\), \(\log ( 1 + 1 / H ) \ge 1 / ( H + 1 )\), and
\(H / ( H + 1 ) \ge 2 / 3\), its lower bound exceeds
\(4 / ( 15 H ) > 1 / ( 4 H )\). The \(U_{H}\) bound therefore covers the
quarter coefficient without relying on a limiting estimate.

\subsubsection{Selected local and old weak edges}

The endpoint formulas in Section~\ref{paper:ep-reference} give the
following explicit weak-edge bounds. In its notation use \(e_{0} = \epsilon_{H} \ge 1 / ( 10 H^{3} )\) and

\begin{align*}
 \nu&=e_{0}/H\ge1/(10H^4),\qquad \eta=1/(4H^2),\\
 \gamma_w&=\log2/(48H^2)\ge1/(100H^2),\\
 \mu&=\min(\nu,\gamma_w)\ge1/(100H^4).
\end{align*}

The wrong-output constants obey

\[
 c_{\rm curv}=\frac{\min(1,2\nu/\log H)}{2H^2}
                         \ge1/(10H^7),
\]

\[
 c_{\rm wrong}=
 \frac{7\min(1,\mu/[2H(1+\log H)+\log H])}{16H^2}
                         \ge1/(2000H^8).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

The proper-input two-cut exchange pays \(L_{i} / ( 4 H^{2} )\).
The local weak threshold can be at least \(1 / ( 1000 H^{4} )\) by
the explicit entropy formulas above. Choose the even smaller threshold \(\epsilon_{w} = M_{1}^{- 100}\). Then every nonexceptional
local weak edge has both reference endpoints at least
\(L_{i} / ( 2000 H^{8} )\). The possible local exception is exactly the
full-input, deepest-output edge; its actual source wall is
retained, so no inverse of its vanishing drift is taken.

For old edges, the same comparison gives
\(\beta_{H} = 1 / [ 4 H ( 1 + \log H )^{2} ] \ge 1 / ( 16 H^{3} )\).
Its full-input charge is at least \(V_{\mathrm{old}} / ( 32 H^{3} )\); its
proper-input charge is at least \(H^{- H - 1} L_{i} / ( 4 H )\).
The same \(\epsilon_{w}\) is below both required thresholds
\(\beta_{H} / 4\) and \(\kappa_{*} / ( 8 H )\).
Nonweak edges are charged from the favorable endpoint with
gap at least \(\epsilon_{w}\). These bounds keep the selected-edge constants uniform as a local
critical drift, output drift, or adjacent saddle-product difference
tends to zero.

The local weak-order comparison is an integer-capacity/secant
comparison, with normalized-secant derivative at least
\(1 / ( 24 H^{2} )\); zero-output proper edges use \(z \ge \sqrt{2}\).
The sole terminal zero-output edge is ordinary and is omitted.

\subsubsection{Endpoint/count coefficients and root-separated chords}

The count recurrence bounds the errors at every exposed group.
Reference charges absorb those errors and leave a definite fraction
of each intrinsic chord. The root keeps coefficient one throughout
this comparison.

On the coupled source the own-group count errors are bounded
by the recurrence in (1). Each count step has at most \(H\)
eligible labels and at most \(H\) earlier groups. Its smallest
unread split variance is at least
\(H^{- ( H + 1 )} T / 16\), and the hierarchy bounds the old error by
\(4 H^{4} B_{j} \sqrt{T}\). The split coefficient is at least
\(( \log 2 ) / 2\); therefore the factor \(A_{H}\) covers each diagonal
selection and each displaced-count adjustment. At most \(H^{2}\)
such steps occur. The binomial/multinomial probabilities are
evaluated separately by Stirling; they are not denominators
in the deterministic endpoint coefficient bounds.

The shifted intrinsic common-pair coefficient can be taken at least
\(M_{0}^{- 20}\), with upper coefficient at most \(M_{0}^{20}\),
after the fixed reserve exceeds \(M_{0}^{20}\). This follows from
the exact early/tail cancellation, the good-group displacement,
and one Young inequality against \(c_{\mathrm{ref}}\) per exposed group;
there are at most \(H\) groups. The all-zero and full-deadline
rows are exact. These inputs are proved in Section~\ref{paper:ep-intrinsic-section}, including the terminal unread-suffix refinement.
Its scales are the \(h\)-leading \(S_{v}^{I}\), not the physical
profile's leading-one scales. The two selections and their final
comparison are made explicit in Section~\ref{supp:selected-weak-edge}:
the lower imposes every weak canonical wall, including saturated
ones; the upper's rare cutoff is fixed before \(h\). All physical
count compactness and correlation replacement bounds are proved
there without a reciprocal \(h\)-dependent rarity threshold.

The root is retained with coefficient one in Section~\ref{app:history-details}. Its bounded
rounding is divided by \(r_{j} \ge 1 / 2\), never by a strict product
gap. For allowed targets \(y_{j} \le D_{0} \log ( 2 + T_{j} )\) the root-prefix
representative comparison may use an extra polynomial in
\(D_{0}\), because its reserve difference is at most
\(2 HD_{0} \log ( 2 + V_{\mathrm{pre}} )\). The old-input reference charges just
listed pay that difference. The coefficient therefore includes this dependence on \(D_{0}\).

With \(D_{0} = M_{1}^{10}\), its additional coefficients are below
\(M_{1}^{100}\). Choose

\[
 \theta_{\rm intr}=\epsilon_{\rm mix}=M_1^{-M_1},
 \quad\theta_{\rm glob}=1/(4H^2).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

These choices are below the partial-child/root-separated
chord fraction times \(\theta_{\mathrm{glob}}\), including the \(D_{0}\) factor.
The partial-child alternatives in Section~\ref{supp:chord-comparison} use either a
linear \(cL_{i}\) vertex charge or this actual intrinsic chord;
the same empirical bridge is used in each branch. The
maximum-weight vertex step costs only \(( H + 1 )^{H}\). After all
finite shares, the retained positive coefficient can safely
be bounded below by

\[
 \delta_H=M_1^{-M_1^2}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

Its actual primitive positive factors involve at most \(H^{3}\)
entries from the primitive-constant table and at most \(H^{3}\) source/mixing/bank
shares, each with reciprocal at most \(M_{1}^{10 M_{1}}\).
Their product inverse is smaller than \(M_{1}^{20 H^{3} M_{1}}\),
which is below \(M_{1}^{M_{1}^{2}}\). Thus (4) is conservative even
without assuming that only a few tiny shares are multiplied.
A parameter approaching
a merge face causes no denominator in this calculation.

\subsubsection{Explicit control of all REG/interpolation errors}

We next absorb the regularity and interpolation errors into the
available linear and inward-curve charges. The important point is
that the number of coefficient operations along a dependency branch
is bounded in terms of the dimension, even though pivot locations
range over a long interval.

The shorter-end REG calculation bounds one
empirical bridge by

\[
 |\mathcal E_e(t)|\le
      4H^2\log H\{\vartheta d(t)+K[1+d(t)^\zeta]\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

For the mixed contrast, at most \(2 H\) constant-partition
intervals per plateau occur, with each per-label coefficient
at most \(3 H \log H\); its error coefficient is at most
\(12 H^{3} \log H\). Projection moves at most \(H - 1\) original
boundaries and token depth gains have coefficient at most
\(H^{2}\); concavity of the powers propagates these factors
without any endpoint-sized count. Synchronization changes
maxima/minima by the sum of at most \(H^{2}\) spreads. Thus
every coefficient of \(\vartheta \cdot \mathrm{length}\) or \(K \cdot \mathrm{depth}^{\zeta}\)
before finite budget shares is below \(U_{H}^{4}\).

Take \(\zeta = 1 / 16\), \(\gamma = 1 / 8\) and
\(\vartheta = M_{1}^{- M_{1}^{3}}\). It is less than one hundredth of
every retained linear charge divided by its regularity coefficient.
The concrete absorption formulas are

\[
 av^{1/16}\le\tfrac12 bv^{1/8}+a^2/(2b),
 \qquad
 av^{1/16}\le\tfrac12 bv+4b(1+a/b)^2,
\]

\[
 a\sqrt v\le\tfrac14bv+a^2/b.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

The middle bound follows from \(v^{1 / 16} \le 1 + \sqrt{v}\)
and \(a \sqrt{v} \le b v / 4 + a^{2} / b\): its remainder
\(a + a^{2} / b\) is bounded by the displayed constant for all
\(a , b > 0\). Source and target inequalities use at most
\(H^{3}\) group/boundary charges; applying these absorptions
successively never creates a new depth exponent. The original
pure-lifetime \(\zeta\)-power versus a linear charge
uses exponent \(16 / 15 < 2\); original depth transfer into inward
\(\gamma\) uses exponent 2. Even allowing power 16 at every
step is therefore safe for the bound \(Q_{H}\) in (1).

Here the finite-operation count is per coefficient formula, not
the number of lawful endpoint contexts. Each original history has
at most \(H - 1\) cuts; projection moves at most \(H - 1\) tokens; each of at
most \(H\) plateaux has at most \(H\) physical groups. Synchronization,
partial-child alternatives, endpoint budget shares and original
depth transfer therefore require at most \(100 H^{4}\) coefficient
operations along any dependency branch. Different lawful contexts
are bounded by the same branchwise maximum. Taking their maximum
does not raise the bound to another power. A sum over the at most
\(H ! H^{H} 2^{H}\) endpoint templates contributes only that dimension-only
multiplier, already below \(U_{H}\). Original pivot position summation is
the separate convergent one-dimensional series, not an iteration
of coefficient definitions indexed by its number of terms.

After the small proof parameters are installed, their reciprocals
are at most \(M_{1}^{M_{1}^{4}}\). If a branch starts from
\(100 M_{1}^{M_{1}^{4}} ( 1 + K ) ( 1 + h )\) and each of its at most \(100 H^{4}\)
steps raises the running majorant to at most power 16, its final
bound is at most

\[
 [100M_1^{M_1^4}(1+K)(1+h)]^{16^{100H^4}}
                  <(M_1Kh)^{M_1^{10}},
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6a}
\]

for \(K\),\(h \ge 2\). The inequality follows by comparing exponents:
\(( M_{1}^{4} + 10 ) 16^{100 H^{4}} < M_{1}^{10}\). It also includes the inverse
retained charge \(\delta_{H}^{- 1}\) and the inverse upper rare cutoff
\(\tau_{0}^{- 1} \le 4 H M_{1}^{100} + 800 H^{5}\); no \(h\)-dependent rare cutoff
is used. Applying (6a) without the final \(h\) gives the REG-only
bound below. Thus the final intercept is bounded by the displayed finite
arithmetic recurrence.

The terminal flag error is
\(A \log ( 2 + T ) d / L\). At \(L \ge T / 4\) its coefficient of \(d^{\gamma}\)
is at most \(A \log ( 2 + 4 L ) L^{- \gamma}\). At \(L < T / 4\), the
clipped-reference charge is at least \(c_{\mathrm{ref}} T / 4\) and pays
\(A\log(2+T)\). For \(t\ge1\),
\(\log(2+4t)\le100t^{1/16}\). The first coefficient is therefore
below \(\delta_H/100\) whenever
\[
 L\ge(10^4A/\delta_H)^{16}.
\]
The second reference share is available whenever
\[
 T\ge(4\cdot10^4A/(\delta_Hc_{\rm ref}))^{16/15}.
\]
With \(A\le2HD_0\), \(D_0=M_1^{10}\), and
\(\delta_H=M_1^{-M_1^2}\), the logarithms of both cutoffs are below
\(M_1^{100000}\). Thus both cutoffs are at most \(M_2\).

\subsubsection{Target recoloring and the final intercept bound}

Recoloring contributes a second kind of error: the target displacement
can depend on the preceding data. The deterministic cascade below
bounds that displacement for every admissible target, so it remains
valid for adaptive choices.

The exact target cascade in Section~\ref{paper:ep-cascade} has
\(b_{j} e_{j} - A_{j} e_{j - 1} = y_{j} + \delta_{j}\), \(0 \le \delta_{j} < b_{j}\),
with \(b_{j} > 1 / 3\), \(A_{j} \le H\). Hence

\[
 e_j\le(4H)^H\{H+D_0H\log(2+T_j)\}
                  \le M_1^{100}\log(2+T_j).
 \tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\]

For \(i<j\), the hierarchy gives \(T_i\le C_HT_j\), so
\[
 \log(2+T_i)\le\log(2+T_j)+\log C_H.
\]
At the specified lift, \(\log C_H\le\tfrac14\log(2+T_j)\).
The recurrence with \(b_j^{-1}<3\) and \(A_j\le H\) then gives
the factor \((4H)^H\) in (7). It is a deterministic bound for every
admissible target vector, including one chosen from the prefix data.
Each flip changes any loss by at most \(4H\log H\).
The deep-bank margin may be chosen as the smaller fraction
\(\rho_{\mathrm{bank}} = M_{1}^{- 10 M_{1}}\). Image regularity only uses (7), the
linear macro-length margin or \(\rho_{\mathrm{bank}}^{\zeta}\) endpoint-depth
margin; all have explicit coefficients at least powers of
\(M_{1}^{- 10 M_{1}}\). The scalar cost cutoff/penalty can use
\(b_{0} = M_{1}^{- M_{1}^{3}}\), \(C_{\mathrm{cut}} = M_{1}^{M_{1}^{4}}\).
All these requirements are paid at the final lift in the
fixed-lift rule in Section~\ref{supp:explicit-fixed-lift-rule}.

Set \(M_{2} = \exp ( M_{1}^{100000} )\),
\(K = \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{5000} ) )\) and scalar reserve
\(h = \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{6000} ) )\), as in that rule. Combining
the preceding coefficient estimates and (6), every deterministic error coefficient
or intercept excluding the added reserve is bounded by
\(( M_{1} K )^{M_{1}^{10}}\). Thus it is below
\(h_{W} = \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{5500} ) )\). Terms that read the added
reserve, including root-separated endpoint shifts, are instead
bounded by \(( M_{1} Kh )^{M_{1}^{10}}\), which is below the explicit

\[
 C_{\rm geom}^{\rm final}=\exp\{\exp(M_2^{6500})\}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

The final source intercept includes terms depending on \(h\), whereas
\(h_{W}\) bounds only the regularity terms chosen earlier. The geometric
argument carries the logarithmic density cost of the larger intercept. At the fixed lift
\(\Lambda = \lceil \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{10000} ) ) \rceil\), (8) is smaller than
\(\delta_{H} \sqrt{\Lambda} / 100\). The numerical grid defect is
at most \(M_{2}^{7000}\), and the same inequality pays it.

The probability choices precede this geometric intercept. Path and
regularity retention are fixed at each exact type before target
transport and the arithmetic first-mass argument, using the constants
of the scalar estimates. Thus these choices do not depend on the
rare arithmetic acceptance probability that they help to estimate.

The displayed tables and inequalities bound the coefficients in the source, classification, and history comparisons proved above. They supply the finite deterministic inputs to the explicit fixed-lift construction.

\subsubsection{Scalar exponent sensitivity uses the physical margin}

The exponent sensitivity is controlled by the physical variance
margin. This calculation keeps the degree of the depth polynomial
separate from the large multiplicative probability constant \(M_{2}\).
For a finite whitened Gaussian grid write \(q = T_{s} f\),
\(\exp ( - s ) = \sqrt{\rho}\), \(0 \le f \le 1\). The one-dimensional Gaussian
rearrangement bound gives

\[
 |\nabla q|\le\sqrt{\rho/(1-\rho)}
                         \phi(\Phi^{-1}(q)).
\]

For every \(0 < q < 1\),

\[
 \phi(\Phi^{-1}q)^2\le2q^2(1-\log q).                     \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

One direct proof puts \(q = Q ( t )\), \(m ( t ) = \phi ( t ) / Q ( t )\). The truncated
normal variance gives \(m ' ( t ) = m ( t ) ( m ( t ) - t ) \le 1\). Hence the derivative
of \(2 ( 1 - \log Q ( t ) ) - m ( t )^{2}\) is \(2 m ( t ) ( 1 - m ' ( t ) ) \ge 0\); its limit at
minus infinity is 2. This proves (9) without an unspecified Mills
constant.

For the plateau range $0<\eta<1$, let \(F = \mathbb{E} q^{\eta}\).
Noise differentiation, Gaussian integration by
parts, and convexity of \(\log \mathbb{E} q^{\eta}\) in \(\eta\) give

\[
 0\le\partial_s\log F
 \le\frac{2(1-\eta)\rho}{1-\rho}
                              (\eta-\log F),
 \qquad
 -\partial_\eta\log F\le-\log F/\eta.
\]

Since \(\,\mathrm{d}s / \,\mathrm{d}\rho = - 1 / ( 2 \rho )\), divide by the horizon, use the exact
ordinary OU survival comparison, and pass to the infinite-horizon
rate. The resulting local Lipschitz inequalities (derivatives when
they exist, otherwise their corresponding increment bounds) are

\[
 |\partial_\rho\chi|\le
          \frac{(1-\eta)\chi}{1-\rho},\qquad
 |\partial_\eta\chi|\le\chi/\eta.                          \tag{\papertagprefix.10}
\]

For plateau powers $1/2\le\eta<1$, these bounds are at most \(1 / [ 2 ( 1 - \rho ) ]\) and 1.
Finite-grid approximation is monotone; the bounds are uniform in
the grid dimension. The additive \(\eta / \mathrm{horizon}\) term tends to zero.


At a selected actual local type the count compactness gives
\(p \in [ 1 / ( 2 H ) , 1 - 1 / ( 2 H ) ]\), \(\tau \in [ 1 / ( 2 H ) , 2 ]\),
\(b \ge \log ( 2 ) / 2\), \(b \le \log H\). Both original and contracted speeds
are in \([ 1 / ( 4 H ) , 2 H \log H ]\). Thus the environmental variance is
at least \(1 / ( 64 H^{4} )\), the private variance is at least
\(1 / ( 100 H )\), and their sum is at most \(20 H^{2} ( 1 + \log H )^{2}\).
Consequently both \(\rho\) and its complement are at least

\[
 \epsilon_{\rm phys}=1/(10^5H^{10}).                       \tag{\papertagprefix.11}
\]

This conservative floor covers the contracted case as well as the
canonical centered model. Equations (10)--(11) bound the physical
exponent sensitivity by \(10^{5} H^{10} < U_{H}\); the type-error constants
come from the deterministic count recurrence and are bounded by
\(U_{H}\). In particular the replacement \(O ( T + ( 1 + d ) / n )\) has an explicit
coefficient below \(U_{H}^{4}\). The log-ratio contribution is a fixed
constant, using \(T | \log T | \le 1 / e\) and
\(\log ( 2 + n ) / \sqrt{1 + n} \le 2\). Its dependence on \(d\) comes only from
\(( 1 + X + d ) ( 1 + Y + d ) \le ( 1 + d )^{2} ( 1 + X ) ( 1 + Y )\) and the finite history
polynomial weights. Their degree is covered by \(Q_{H} < M_{0}\), hence by
\(M_{1}\). The very large one-end probability comparison constant is
not a power of (\(1 + d\)) and is not assigned to \(D_{0}\).

\subsubsection{Original-pivot series and the active-depth cutoff}

The token reduction leaves one convergent series for each original
pivot. We bound these series explicitly, then verify that the active
depth cutoff lies inside the permitted bank. For \(0 < b \le 1\), \(B \ge 0\), \(\gamma = 1 / 8\), monotone interval comparison
and \(u = t^{1 / 8}\) give

\[
 \sum_{m\ge0}(1+m)^B e^{-b m^{1/8}}
 \le 2^{B+10}(1+b^{-8(B+1)})
                   \Gamma(8(B+1)+1).                     \tag{\papertagprefix.12}
\]

For noninteger \(B\) use the larger integer ceiling before this bound.
The elementary Gamma inequality
\(\Gamma ( v + 1 ) \le 2 ( v + 1 )^{v + 1}\) for \(v \ge 1\) follows by writing its
integrand as \(( t^{v} \exp ( - t / 2 ) ) \exp ( - t / 2 )\): the first factor is
maximized at \(2 v\) and is \(( 2 v / e )^{v}\), and the integral of the
second factor is 2. Since \(2 / e < 1\), this proves the stated bound.
One can also use the integer factorial inequality after taking
another ceiling. Thus the logarithm of (12) is at most

\[
 100(B+1)\{1+\log(B+2)+\log(1/b)\}.                        \tag{\papertagprefix.13}
\]

Original unit-strip occupancies have an extra finite prefactor,
bounded by a fixed power of \(( M_{1} K h )\) by (5). They do not change
the degree \(B\) in (12). There are at most \(H - 1\) original tokens and
at most \(H\) plateaux, so at most $C_H$ products of (12) exhaust
original pivot multiplicities, including repeated pivots.
For \(B \le M_{1}^{2}\) and \(b \ge b_{0} / 100 = M_{1}^{- M_{1}^{3}} / 100\), the entire
logarithmic core-series cost is below \(M_{1}^{100}\). The additional
occupancy prefactor is covered by (6a), including its dependence
on \(h\). The original-pivot series is therefore bounded by a dimension-dependent
constant, independently of the endpoint size and rare acceptance
probability.

For the envelope tail let \(\eta \ge 1 / 2\), \(B \le M_{1}^{2}\) and
\(r_{0} = C_{\mathrm{cut}} \log ( 2 + n )\). Substitution \(r = d^{1 / 8}\) in its integral
gives a polynomial of degree at most \(8 B + 8\) times
\(\exp ( - b_{0} \eta r )\). Since \(\log r \le \sqrt{r}\) for \(r \ge 1\), the polynomial
is at most \(\exp ( b_{0} r / 4 )\) as soon as

\[
 r\ge [100(B+1)/b_{0}]^2.
\]

The explicit \(C_{\mathrm{cut}} = M_{1}^{M_{1}^{4}}\) exceeds that threshold and also
\(100 D_{0} / b_{0}\), where \(D_{0} = M_{1}^{10}\). Hence the summed tail, including
its fixed integral prefactor, is bounded by
\(( 2 + n )^{- 10 D_{0}}\) for \(n\ge\Lambda_k/(4H)\). The nontrivial plateau power
can therefore be retained; a common final power is not substituted.
Also \(D_{0} \eta > 1\) makes the \(( 2 + n )^{- D_{0}}\) floor smaller
than the least possible persistence factor, which is of order
\(( 2 + n )^{- 1}\). The active depth is precisely
\([ C_{\mathrm{cut}} \log ( 2 + n ) ]^{8}\), already checked to be inside
\(\rho_{\mathrm{bank}} n / 100\) at the specified lift.

The sensitivity bounds and the convergent original-pivot series give
the stated coefficient bounds. The ordinary bridge, causal cover, and
correlated arithmetic estimates use these same constants.


\subsection{An explicit length threshold}
\label{supp:explicit-fixed-lift-rule}
For a fixed integer \(k \ge 1\), put \(H = k + 1\). Here is one explicit
rule containing only arithmetic, exponentials and a ceiling:

\[
 M_0=2^{\,2^{10000H^5}},\qquad M_1=M_0^{1000},\qquad
 M_2=\exp(M_1^{100000}),
\]

\[
 \boxed{\displaystyle
 \Lambda_k=\left\lceil\exp\{\exp(M_2^{10000})\}\right\rceil .}
 \tag{\papertagprefix.1}
 \label{new:lift}
\]

The rule has fixed depth and depends only on the dimension.
The subsections below verify the geometric margins, count boxes,
probability and regularity parameters, and arithmetic grid, in that
order. Their final inequalities show that this one threshold meets
all the requirements simultaneously.

\subsubsection{Numerical complete-chain physical bounds}

We begin with the compact ranges for saddle coordinates, fine-label
probabilities, and binary variances. These bounds are the common
inputs to the endpoint and scalar estimates.

At the actual ordered optimizer, every product is in
\([ \alpha_{2} , 1 - \epsilon_{H} ]\), where

\[
 \epsilon_H=\frac{2\log2-1}{2H(\log H)^2}
                         \ge\frac1{10H^3}.
\]

Every original fine-leaf probability is at least \(H^{- H}\); the
conservative transported reference-coefficient floor is \(H^{- H - 1}\).
Indeed each route has at most \(H - 2\)
factors \(\beta \ge 1 / 2\), followed by a factor at least \(1 / H\);
the all-child final route is no smaller. Local coefficients
\(( r + z )^{\sigma - 1}\) are at least \(H^{- 1 / 2}\). Fine probabilities,
reference intensities, and original Poisson rates are at most
\(H\). Every split log coefficient has absolute value at most
\(H \log H\), including a routed original fine split.

For a canonical nondegenerate local edge,
\(a = \log ( r + z )\), \(b = \log ( q + z )\), \(p = ( q + z ) / ( r + z )\). A proper child
has \(z \ge \sqrt{2}\) because \(G_{b + 1} \ge \alpha_{2} \log 2\) and \(\sigma \le 1\).
The terminal nondegenerate edge has \(q \ge 1\). Hence

\[
 b\ge\tfrac12\log2,\quad
 a-b\ge\log\frac H{H-1}\ge H^{-1},\quad
 H^{-1}\le p\le1-H^{-1},
\]

\[
 m=a-pb\ge\frac{\log2}{H},\qquad
 \frac1{100H^6}\le\rho_e\le1-\frac1{100H^6}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.2}
\]

Here \(\rho_{e} = m^{2} / ( m^{2} + b^{2} p ( 1 - p ) )\); the upper denominator is
at most \(5 ( \log H )^{2} / 4\). The natural local risk speed is the
integer \(r - q\), in \([ 1 , H ]\). On own-scale central counts its
clock mean is in \([ 1 / ( 2 H ) , 2 ]\). The contracted speed
\(\theta c + ( 1 - \theta ) A / P\) also lies in \([ 1 / ( 4 H ) , 2 H \log H ]\)
for every \(0 \le \theta \le 1\): the total jump rate \(A / P\) has this
lower bound on central original counts. Thus making the reserve
allocation small does not make the clock speed degenerate.
The rare branch uses a threshold \(t_{0} = M_{1}^{- 100}\). Its actual
type and centered type remain in the compact bounds (2), with
\(100 H^{6}\) replaced by \(M_{1}\), once the own-scale count and
score bounds below hold. This follows from
\(\max ( X , Y ) / n \le t_{0} / \min ( X , Y )\) and the exact type increment.
These bounds remain uniform when a strict product gap tends to zero.

\subsubsection{Numerical strict reference charges and suffix thresholds}

The next bounds control the charges used to absorb count and path
errors. The terminal suffix also needs a definite separation between
successive ordinary thresholds.

The hierarchy bound in Theorem~\ref{hier:thm:hierarchy} is

\[
 V_{\rm old}\le C_HT_{\rm local},\qquad
 C_H=2H^3(1+\log H)^3\le16H^6.
\]

The explicit old transition constant in Section~\ref{paper:ep-prefix-guards}
is

\[
 d_* =\min\left\{\frac{\epsilon_H}{H^2},
 H^{-H-1}[1-(1-H^{-1})^{\epsilon_H}]\right\}
                      \ge\frac1{20H^{H+5}}.
\]

Use \(1 - e^{- v} \ge v / 2\) for \(0 \le v \le 1\). The local secant
derivative is at least \(1 / ( 24 H^{2} )\) and the alternative branch
at least \(\log ( 2 \log 2 ) / ( H \log^{2} H )\). Thus the clipped-reference
gap and charge can be set to

\[
 d_0\ge\frac1{100H^{H+6}},\qquad
 c_{\rm ref}=1-2^{-d_0/3}\ge\frac1{1000H^{H+6}}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.3}
\]

Local and terminal rank curvature is at least $H^{-H-2}$.
The bad-group charge is at least $H^{-H-1}/(2H^2)$, and the
nontrivial mixed entropy gap is at least $2H^{-4H}$. Each bound
exceeds $M_0^{-1}$. Reference integrands and their first two
derivatives are bounded in absolute value by $M_0$: their
denominators involve at most $H$ positive rates or probabilities
bounded below by $H^{-H}$, or logarithms at least $(\log2)/2$.
There are at most $H!H^H2^H$ physical endpoint histories, fewer than
$M_0$. These estimates also cover ties and zero first-root templates;
they use no inverse of a strict product difference.

For the ordinary suffix one also needs an explicit separation of
the thresholds \(\alpha_{h}\). Put \(z = ( \log h ) / 2\) and
\(R ( z ) = z \coth z - 1 - \log ( \sinh z / z )\). Since
\(\sinh^{2} u - u^{2} \ge u^{4} / 3\) and \(\sinh u \le u e^{u}\),

\[
 R'(u)\ge ue^{-2u}/3,
 \quad R(z)\ge z^2e^{-2z}/8,
 \quad \alpha_h'\ge1/(32h^2).
\]

Integrating gives \(\alpha_{h + 1} - \alpha_{h} \ge 1 / ( 32 H^{2} )\).
Consequently the suffix threshold in Section~\ref{profile:definition}
can be retained with

\[
 \tau\ge1/(128H^5),
\]

and every positive tail drift separated from its weak window
is at least \(1 / ( 400 H^{5} )\). The first-plateau transport gap
\(1 - q_{+}\) is at least \(\epsilon_{H} / ( 2 H )\), so every effective-time
comparison coefficient lies between \(M_{0}^{- 1}\) and \(M_{0}\).

\subsubsection{Explicit count-box estimates}

We now quantify the count boxes from
Section~\ref{paper:ep-prefix-guards} and the fresh-name displacement
from Section~\ref{app:endpoint-details}. The recurrence bounds the
centrality constants before transport; a final estimate includes all
transport displacements.
Start the uncolored Poisson windows at width \(10 H \sqrt{\mu}\).
On the pair-coarsened event give every coarse category an
own-scale window of width \(10 H \sqrt{n}\). Chebyshev and a union
bound over at most \(H^{2}\) categories retain probability at least
\(9 / 10\). Require original counts at least \(M_{0}^{100}\) so these
windows also make every selected two-name bank total at least
\(H^{- H} T / ( 4 H )\). These conditions concern unread splits only.

For a bound on successive centrality constants set

\[
 A=10^6H^{3H+30},\quad B_0=10H,\quad
 B_{j+1}=A(B_j+1),\qquad0\le j<H^2.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.4}
\]

The \(H^{2}\) upper bound covers all proper split selections, their
successive count adjustments, and the terminal-prefix completion.
Every such operation uses at most \(H\) earlier groups; the hierarchy
turns their summed square-root errors into at most
\(4 H^{4} B_{j} \sqrt{T}\). Its entropy coefficients are at most
\(H \log H\), its exit coefficient is at least \(( \log 2 ) / 2\), and
its bank standard deviation is at least
\(H^{- ( H + 1 ) / 2} \sqrt{T} / 4\). Their product and quotient are bounded
by the factor \(A\) in (4), including integer rounding and the
width floor \(R_{j} \le \sqrt{T}\). A count transport changes at most
\(H\) exterior categories, with displacement chosen below; its
new own-scale centrality is covered by the same recurrence.
Since \(( 2 A )^{H^{2} + 1} \le M_{0}\), all these centrality constants can
therefore be taken below \(M_{0}\).

Choose the fresh displaced box width
\(\epsilon_{\mathrm{box}} = 1 / ( 100 H )\) and displacement
\(K_{\mathrm{box}} = 100 H^{3} ( B_{H^{2}} + 1 ) \le M_{0}^{2}\).
When \(N \ge M_{0}^{100}\), every nonshallow interval
\(N / r - K_{\mathrm{box}} \sqrt{N} + [ - \epsilon_{\mathrm{box}} , \epsilon_{\mathrm{box}} ] \sqrt{N}\)
is interior, contains at least \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{box}} \sqrt{N}\) integers,
and its determined shallow count is also interior. Elementary
Stirling at these central points gives its simultaneous mass
at least \(\exp ( - M_{0}^{10} )\). For smaller \(N\), the all-shallow
target mass is at least \(H^{- M_{0}^{100}}\); it has wider central
constant at most \(M_{0}^{51}\). Such small original groups are
absent in the fixed-lift source, whose original means and
retained counts exceed \(M_{0}^{100}\). The finite bounded-support
convention therefore need not be used in (1).

These count transports preserve the preceding coarse words and the
finer child word. The binary errors used in the next plateau selection
therefore retain the pretransport bound \(B_{H^2}\). Each of at most
\(H\) transports changes a final fine-leaf count by at most
\(2HK_{\rm box}\sqrt{N_g}\), where \(N_g\le2HL_g\) at the fixed lift.
Consequently
\[
 B_{\rm final}\le B_{H^2}+4H^3K_{\rm box}
 \le500H^6(U_H+1)<M_0.
\]
The last inequality follows from
\(\log U_H\le100H^3\log(10H)\) and
\(\log M_0=(\log2)2^{10000H^5}\). Multiplication by the finitely many
split coefficients bounds the endpoint errors by
\(M_0^5\sqrt{L_g}\). Since \(c_{\rm ref}^{-1}<M_0\), their Young
remainders are at most \(M_0^{12}\).

The full proper/terminal count source uses at most \(H^{2}\) such
steps. Its fixed normalizing density bound is at most
\(\exp ( M_{0}^{12} )\), its own-group count centrality at most
\(M_{0}^{10}\), and its remaining box mass at least
\(\exp ( - M_{0}^{12} )\) times the proper-band mass.
The coefficient-one endpoint cancellation is exact. The
square-root errors are at most \(M_{0}^{5} \sqrt{L}\);
Young's inequality against (3) costs at most \(M_{0}^{12}\).
Thus intrinsic common-pair comparisons may use

\[
M_0^{-20}S_v\le K_v+h\le M_0^{20}S_v,
\quad S_v=S_v^I,
                         \qquad h\ge M_0^{20}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.5}
\]

The terminal-prefix count box is retained; only unread
suffix terminal names are filled at the later positive root.
Its type increments use that actual root count. In particular
the exceptional complete-deadline and all-zero rows acquire
no nominal reference defect.

Here \(S_{v}^{I}\) is the shifted intrinsic score, with leading term \(h\),
as defined in Section~\ref{supp:selected-weak-edge} (4). It is not the
profile's leading-one score. Comparing the two costs only a final
factor at most \(1000 H^{2} ( 1 + h )\) per endpoint. The lower selects every
canonical weak edge, including saturated ones, so all source weak
walls are imposed. The upper retains only \(T_{e} < \tau_{0}\), with the
explicit \(h\)-independent \(\tau_{0}\) in Section~\ref{supp:selected-weak-edge}, (11). All omitted factors
are bounded below by a fixed constant. Actual-type compactness is
proved directly from weak drift and own-scale central counts in
that section, (7)--(10), before \(h\) is chosen; no inverse of an
\(h\)-dependent rarity threshold enters the scalar estimates.

\subsubsection{Fixed proof parameters and their finite inequalities}

With (2)--(5) fixed, choose the curve exponents, budget fractions,
regularity slope, bank fraction, and depth cutoff as follows:

\[
 \gamma=1/8,\quad\zeta=1/16,\quad
 \theta_{\rm glob}=1/(4H^2),\quad
 \theta_{\rm intr}=M_1^{-M_1},\quad
 \epsilon_{\rm mix}=M_1^{-M_1},
\]

\[
 \vartheta=M_1^{-M_1^3},\quad
 b_0=M_1^{-M_1^3},\quad
 \rho_{\rm bank}=M_1^{-10M_1},\quad
 D_0=M_1^{10},\quad C_{\rm cut}=M_1^{M_1^4}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.6}
\]

Actual banks are much larger than \(\rho_{\mathrm{bank}}\); using a smaller
bank merely fixes a still positive allowed fraction. The scalar
floor power \(D_{0}\) exceeds every compact plateau exponent and every
finite history polynomial. \(C_{\mathrm{cut}}\) exceeds its required quotient
by the stretched-exponential penalty \(b_{0}\).

For named refinement slopes start below
\(\vartheta M_{1}^{- 10 H - 20}\) and enlarge each successive level by
at most \(M_{1}^{10}\). All final original fine-name slopes remain
below \(\vartheta / 4\); allow target slopes below \(\vartheta / 2\).
There are at most \(H\) levels. Every Chernoff coefficient on
these fixed original laws is then at least \(M_{2}^{- 1}\).

The primitive geometric coefficients before the weak cutoff,
small proof parameters and regularity intercept are installed can be
bounded by \(M_{1}\), with primitive positive fractions at least
\(M_{1}^{- 1}\). The cutoff \(\epsilon_{w} = M_{1}^{- 100}\) is then included
among the explicit small proof parameters; the primitive lower
bound \(M_{1}^{-1}\) is applied before that cutoff is introduced. The finite
number of reference, rank, projection, and carry operations is
at most \(H^{3}\), each uses the explicit primitive rates and
the charges (3), and its Young exponents are 2 or fixed powers
at most 16. Even repeated raising to power 16 over \(H^{3}\)
algebra steps has logarithm below \(2^{10000 H^{5}}\); this is why
\(M_{0}\) uses the extra exponential. After (6), use the safer
positive-fraction floor \(M_{1}^{- M_{1}^{2}}\) and bound every finite
error intercept that does not read the added reserve by
\(( M_{1} K_{\mathrm{REG}} )^{M_{1}^{10}}\). An endpoint shift that reads the
added reserve can instead cost \(( M_{1} K_{\mathrm{REG}} h )^{M_{1}^{10}}\);
the larger final intercept below pays this separately. These estimates bound the deterministic coefficients in the
selected-edge and source-history inequalities.

The asymmetric ordinary continuation uses compact parameter
$M_1$ and height times drift at least $M_1^{-20}$.
The half-Poisson upper density is at most 25; at deviations
\(K \sqrt{n_{i}}\), its lower density is at least
\(( 1 / 16 ) \exp ( - 4 - 8 K^{2} )\) for \(n_{i} \ge 16 K^{2}\).
With \(\kappa = M_{1}^{- 3} \exp ( - M_{1} )\), choose
\(K = 4 M_{1}^{12} \exp ( M_{1} )\) and
\(R_{\mathrm{asy}} = \exp ( 1000 M_{1}^{2} )\). The first-half and late-half inequalities of
Section~\ref{supp:exact-type-continuation} then hold. The fixed
asymmetry cutoff and the scaled drifts in the one-end Gaussian
experiment are below $M_2$.

Use the scalar estimates with this \(M_{2}\). Its proved OU
constant is at most \(2^{80} M_{2}^{2}\), its positive-box loss is at
least \(\exp ( - M_{2}^{100} )\), and its exact middle constants are
the displayed formulas in Section~\ref{supp:explicit-middle-continuation}.
The relative bad construction for the binary construction is
\(C_{\mathrm{bad}} = \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{300} ) )\),
\(L_{0}^{\mathrm{bin}} = \lceil \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{400} ) ) \rceil\). The
ordinary one-channel estimates have \(L_{0}^{\mathrm{ord}} = \lceil \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{2300} ) ) \rceil\),
\(h_{\mathrm{ord}} = \lceil \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{3000} ) ) \rceil\),
\(K_{\mathrm{ord}} = \lceil \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{3500} ) ) \rceil\), and
\(C_{\mathrm{ord}} = \exp ( \exp ( M_{2}^{4000} ) )\); see Section~\ref{supp:explicit-ordinary-construction}
. These constants do not use
the binary theorem at \(\rho = 1\). Define

\begin{equation}
\begin{aligned}
 K_{\rm REG}&=\exp\{\exp(M_2^{5000})\},\qquad
 h_W=\exp\{\exp(M_2^{5500})\},\\
 h&=\exp\{\exp(M_2^{6000})\},\qquad
 C_{\rm geom}^{\rm final}=\exp\{\exp(M_2^{6500})\},\\
 R_0&=100H^2.
\end{aligned}\tag{\papertagprefix.7}
\end{equation}

These choices make the Chernoff and refinement tails smaller than
the preceding relative retention losses: their first exponent exceeds
\(K_{\mathrm{REG}} / M_{2}\), whereas the logarithm of every preceding inverse
retention is at most \(\exp ( M_{2}^{4500} )\), including the ordinary
\(\log C_{\mathrm{ord}} = \exp ( M_{2}^{4000} )\). Fixed grid-pair series
have powers at most \(M_{1}^{1000}\); their integral bounds are
also swallowed by that exponent. This fixes REG before lengths
are inspected.

Take the strong curve amplitude to be one. Its history errors
are paid by the explicit inequality

\[
 C_K d^{1/16}\le\tfrac12 g_0d^{1/8}
                          +\frac{C_K^2}{2g_0},
\]

where \(g_{0} \ge M_{1}^{- M_{1}^{2}}\) and
\(C_{K} \le ( M_{1} K_{\mathrm{REG}} )^{M_{1}^{10}}\). The last constant is below
\(h_{W}\): its logarithm is at most
\(4 M_{1}^{10} \exp ( M_{2}^{5000} ) < \exp ( M_{2}^{5500} )\). This also pays the
finite repeated Young absorptions. The strong-wall amplitude can therefore be fixed before the
regularity intercept is enlarged. The minimum reserve \(h\) dominates \(h_{W}\), all OU endpoint
boxes divided by their allocation fractions,
\(100 M_{2} \max ( L_{0}^{\mathrm{bin}} , L_{0}^{\mathrm{ord}} )^{2}\),
and every strong-wall/relative-coupling initial reserve.

\subsubsection{Arithmetic, grid, and the final length inequalities}

The last choice is the prime grid. Its total clock defect is bounded
in terms of the parameters already fixed. The final length then makes
this defect and every remaining intercept small relative to the
available count and reference margins.

Set \(A_{0} = A_{1} = hM_{1}^{100000}\) and use the exact numerical
\(Q\) from Section~\ref{supp:explicit-arithmetic-grid}, equation (2). This
dominates every actual named regularity linear occupancy tube and gives
pointwise squarefree supply at least \(e^{- 1 / 2}\). Its elementary
bound is \(Q \le h^{4} M_{1}^{300000}\). Consequently

\[
 R=k(\log\log Q+100)\le M_2^{7000}.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.8}
\]

At the value of \(\Lambda_k\) in (1), the following inequalities hold:

\[
 \Lambda_k>100M_1^{100000}h^2,
 \quad\Lambda_k>100M_1^{100000}R_0^2,
 \quad\Lambda_k>100M_1^{100000}(1+R)^2,
 \quad\Lambda_k>M_0^{1000},
\]

\[
 M_1\{\log(2+T)\}^{M_1^{10}}
               <M_1^{-M_1^3}T^{1/16}\quad(T\ge\Lambda_k),
\]

\[
 [C_{\rm cut}\log(2+n)]^8
                     <\rho_{\rm bank}n/100
                                  \quad(n\ge\Lambda_k/4H),
\]

\[
 \max(M_1R,C_{\rm geom}^{\rm final})
                 <M_1^{-M_1^2}\sqrt{\Lambda_k}/100.
 \tag{\papertagprefix.9}
\]

For the logarithm inequalities, the relevant functions
\(\log ( 2 + t )^{a} / t^{b}\) are decreasing once
\(\log ( 2 + t ) > 2 a / b\); substitute \(t = \Lambda_{k} / ( 4 H )\) and use the
strict power gap \(10000 > 7000 > 6500 > 6000 > 5500 > 5000 > 400\). This verifies
them for every later length, without endpoint enumeration.
The first line of (9) makes every actual width band interior
and pays the central root/grid count translates. The last
line pays every nonexceptional square-root reference charge;
the two exceptional rows are exact. The middle lines pay all
logarithmic recoloring/image-REG margins and keep every active
bank cutoff inside its allowed local block. Affine grid maps
lose at most \(R\) by (8), so all original groups remain present.



\subsection{Harmonic stability and equivalent profiles}
\label{supp:fixed-lift-constant-dependencies}
Two points complete the dependence check. The ordered-sum estimate
changes only the final upper comparison constant. Harmonic stability
then compares the given vector with its lift, including zero lengths.

\subsubsection{The ordered-sum constant enters only the final upper bound}

Let
\[
 C_H^{\mathrm{os}}=\max_{2\le h\le H}C_{h^{1/(h-1)}}.
\]
This is finite by Corollary~\ref{ordsumadjustment:a0}. Its value enters
only the multiplicative upper constant. To see this directly, fix the geometric constant $C_0$
before applying the ordered-sum bound and put
\[
 C_1=1+\log C_0+(H-1)\log2+\log H,
 \qquad C_{\mathrm{tail}}=
 1+\frac{2C_H^{\mathrm{os}}C_1}{(\log2)^2}.
\]
In the notation of Section~\ref{ordsumadjustment:section},
\begin{align*}
 \gamma+1
 &=\frac{Z+\ell+\log C_0+(h-1)\log2+\log h}{\log h}
 \le\frac{C_1+Z+\ell}{\log2},\\
 \gamma-n+v+1&\le\frac{C_1(1+\ell)}{\log2}.
\end{align*}
On a nonempty event with $n=0$ one has $C_1+Z+\ell>1$. Thus the
all-count conclusion, including $n=0$, is
\[
 \PP(W_n>e^{-\ell}\mid n)
 \le\min\left\{1,
 \frac{C_{\mathrm{tail}}(1+\ell)(C_1+Z+\ell)_+}{1+n}\right\}.
\]
The constant $C_H^{\mathrm{os}}$ occurs only in $C_{\mathrm{tail}}$.
It changes neither the event nor its root translate, count reservoir,
geometric prefix cap, plateau powers, or all-count hypotheses. The two
Poisson mode bounds in Section~\ref{app:upper-details} multiply this
estimate by fixed factors and retain the same-count minimum. Subsequent
layer integrals have already fixed $1-s$, the root span, and the pool
exponent. Consequently enlarging $C_{\mathrm{tail}}$ only enlarges the
output upper constant.

The pool gate in Section~\ref{upper:section} is chosen earlier from
past inverse floors and physical linear information. It does not use
the ordered-sum estimate. The root estimate concludes
